26 September 2026 — One homogeneous operator ideal contains every order of a threshold row

Working theorem: a monic-factor intersection, an explicit polynomial connection, and a finite all-order Gröbner certificate in characteristic zero. Generic-orbit localization erases the positive first-step degree obstruction. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and outcome. Open statement 3 still needs the first nonzero parameter degree. The Hankel test rejected one matrix pattern, not the broader operator description. After reading both desingularization sources in full, I constructed an exact model over the polynomial parameter ring: all orders are slices of one homogeneous Ore ideal, given as an intersection of powers of monic first-order operators. It also has a polynomial connection over the symmetric ring whose divided iterates are the existing coefficient matrix. A homogeneous Gröbner basis would therefore certify the entire order row at once. No such basis in general degree, and hence no new numerical threshold formula, is claimed. The tempting reduction to a rational coefficient field loses the obstruction: the proper first-step ideal becomes the unit ideal on a generic reciprocal-coordinate orbit.

The fixed all-order ideal

Theorem (thm:cube-polynomial-ore-model). Let \(F\) have characteristic zero, \(n\ge1\), \(d\ge0\), and put \[R=F[a_1,\ldots,a_n],\qquad \delta=-\sum_i a_i^2\partial_{a_i},\qquad \mathscr A=R[\partial;\delta].\] Thus \(\partial f=f\partial+\delta f\), in particular \(\partial a_i=a_i\partial-a_i^2\). Give \(a_i\) and \(\partial\) degree one. For every subset \(S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) with \(|S|\le d\), define \[\lambda_S=\tfrac12\sum_{i\in S}a_i,\qquad k_S=\lfloor(d-|S|)/2\rfloor+1,\qquad \mathscr J_{n,d}=\bigcap_{|S|\le d}\mathscr A(\partial-\lambda_S)^{k_S}.\] This is a homogeneous left ideal depending only on \(n,d\), not on the order cutoff. The dictionary \[W=(W_0,\ldots,W_m)\longmapsto P_W=\sum_{c=0}^m\frac{W_c}{c!}\partial^c\] identifies the full cube solution module \(K_{n,d,m}\) with the order-at-most-\(m\) part of \(\mathscr J_{n,d}\). A solution of excess \(\ell\) corresponds to total degree \(\ell+m\). Its nonzero top coordinate corresponds to exact order \(m\), and equals \(m!\) times the leading coefficient in the usual left-coefficient convention.

Put \(N=N_{2,n}(d)\). For the primitive boundary generator \(G\), the operator \(\mathscr L=P_G\) has order \(N\), and \[\mathscr J_{n,d}=\operatorname{Frac}(R)[\partial;\delta]\mathscr L\ \cap\ \mathscr A.\] Left multiplication by \(\partial\) corresponds exactly to the negative of the recorded order-raising operator. The first-step slice therefore recovers the single-division presentation; this compatibility is not a stronger first-step threshold bound.

There exists a finite homogeneous left Gröbner basis \(\mathcal G\) of \(\mathscr J_{n,d}\) for the PBW order described below. For each nonzero \(g\in\mathcal G\), put \(r_g=\operatorname{ord}_\partial g\) and \(e_g=\deg g-r_g\ge0\). Then, for every \(m\ge0\), \[\boxed{\ell_0(d+1,m)=\min\{e_g:g\in\mathcal G,\ r_g\le m\}}\] with empty minimum infinity. This is a finite certificate for all orders at a fixed \(n,d\), not an evaluated formula uniformly in \(n,d\).

The exact differential dictionary

Proof. In the fraction field set \[x=a_1^{-1},\qquad b_i=a_i^{-1}-a_1^{-1}\ (i\ge2),\qquad b_1=0.\] Then \(\delta x=1\), \(\delta b_i=0\), and \(a_i=1/(x+b_i)\). In a differential algebraic extension let \(g_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}(x+b_i)^{1/2}\). Its logarithmic derivative is \(\lambda_S\). The ratio \[g_S(x+T)/g_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}(1+a_iT)^{1/2}=w^S(T)\] gives the original character rows. Set \[E_j=g_S^{-1}\sum_{c\ge j}W_c\frac{g_S^{(c-j)}}{(c-j)!}.\] The row constraint for \(T^jw^S\) is \(E_j=0\). By Leibniz, \[P_W(x^qg_S)=g_S\sum_{j=0}^q\binom qj x^{q-j}E_j.\] This triangular transformation has diagonal one. Thus vanishing of all original rows \(0\le q

Since \((\partial-\lambda_S)(x^qg_S)=q x^{q-1}g_S\), the monic operator \((\partial-\lambda_S)^{k_S}\) annihilates all these functions. Conversely, right division of a polynomial-coefficient operator by this monic operator stays inside \(\mathscr A\). Its remainder has order less than \(k_S\). Conjugating by \(g_S\), a remainder annihilating \(g_S,xg_S,\ldots,x^{k_S-1}g_S\) becomes an operator \(\sum_{j

The generic-normality lemma gives no nonzero solution of order below \(N\) over \(\operatorname{Frac}R\); for \(d=0\) this is simply the row \(1\). The primitive boundary vector supplies an order-\(N\) annihilator. Right Euclidean division by \(\mathscr L\) over the fraction-field Ore algebra leaves a remainder of smaller order annihilating the same functions, hence zero. Therefore all rational-coefficient annihilators form its left ideal, and the polynomial intersection gives precisely the asserted contraction.

The grading follows from \(\deg W_c=\ell+m-c\); the Ore relation is homogeneous because \(\delta\) raises parameter degree by one. Left multiplication gives coefficient vector \[(W'_c)_{c=0}^{m+1}=(\delta W_c+cW_{c-1})_{c=0}^{m+1}=-(\mathcal L_mW)_c,\] with missing endpoint coordinates zero. For \(f=G_N\) and \(B=-\mathcal L_NG/(N+1)\), the already-proved first-step expression \(W=(a(G,0)+bB)/f\) becomes the left multiple \[P_W=\left(\frac a f+\frac{b}{(N+1)f}\partial\right)\mathscr L.\] In particular, its denominators and parameter degrees are still explicit.

Why one Gröbner basis gives every order

Use PBW monomials \(\partial^r a_1^{\alpha_1}\cdots a_n^{\alpha_n}\), with \(\partial\) on the left, and lexicographic order on \((r,\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n)\). The relation \(a_i\partial=\partial a_i+a_i^2\) has a strictly smaller correction in this order. Thus leading exponents add under multiplication, with coefficient one for products of monomials. The leading exponents of a left ideal are closed under addition by \(\mathbb N^{n+1}\); Dickson's lemma gives finitely many minimal exponents. Choose representatives of those leading monomials in the ideal. Since the ideal is homogeneous, choose their homogeneous components containing the leading term. These representatives form a finite homogeneous left Gröbner basis.

For a nonzero homogeneous operator of exact order \(m\) and total degree \(\ell+m\), the highest-order coefficient has parameter degree \(\ell\). Its leading monomial is left-divisible by the leading monomial of some \(g\in\mathcal G\). Hence \(r_g\le m\) and \(e_g\le\ell\). Conversely, \(\partial^{m-r_g}g\) has exact order \(m\) and excess \(e_g\), so it attains this value. Changing between right and left coefficient PBW conventions changes only lower-order terms and preserves total degree, so the highest-order coefficient is unaffected. The factorial dictionary then proves the boxed equality. \(\square\)

A polynomial connection over the symmetric ring

The theorem also has an explicit implementation over \(B=F[e_1,\ldots,e_n]\), \(\deg e_j=j\), without generating a separate row matrix at every order. Here \[\delta_B(e_j)=(j+1)e_{j+1}-e_1e_j,\qquad e_{n+1}=0.\] Use the companion module \(V=B[z]/(z^n-e_1z^{n-1}+\cdots+(-1)^ne_n)\), multiplication matrix \(Z\), and shifted exterior modules \(V_s\) of the descent theorem. For an endomorphism \(U\), write \(U^{[s]}\) for its additive exterior action, the coefficient of \(t\) in \(\bigwedge^s(1+tU)\), not its multiplicative exterior power. Put \[B_0=-Z\operatorname{diag}(0,1,\ldots,n-1),\qquad M_s=B_0^{[s]}+(s-\tfrac12)Z^{[s]},\qquad \nabla_s=\delta_B+M_s.\] Each connection raises weighted degree by one. For \(k_s=\lfloor(d-s)/2\rfloor+1\), take \[\mathcal M=\bigoplus_{0\le s\le\min(n,d)}V_s\otimes B[u]/(u^{k_s}),\qquad \nabla|_s=\nabla_s+u,\qquad \delta_Bu=0,\quad\deg u=1.\] It is free of rank \(N\) over \(B\). Its distinguished vector is \(v=(v_s\otimes1)_s\), where \(v_s=1\wedge z\wedge\cdots\wedge z^{s-1}\). The \(u^q\) coordinate of \(\nabla^cv/c!\) is \[\frac1{q!}[T^{c-q}]H_s(T)v_s.\] Thus its divided iterates reproduce the complete weighted coefficient matrix, up to the nonzero row scalars \(q!\). Its polynomial annihilator recovers \(K_B\) at every order. The vector is generically cyclic, by normality, but is not asserted to generate \(\mathcal M\) over \(B\) by its iterates.

Connection proof. The identity for \(\delta_B e_j\) follows by expanding \(e_1e_j\): the terms with a repeated variable sum to \(\sum_i a_i^2\partial_{a_i}e_j\), and the others give \((j+1)e_{j+1}\). For the evaluation matrix \(E=(a_i^j)\), \(\delta E=EB_0\). On the subset \(S\), the Vandermonde satisfies \[\delta\Delta_S=-(s-1)(\textstyle\sum_{i\in S}a_i)\Delta_S,\qquad \delta g_S=\tfrac12(\textstyle\sum_{i\in S}a_i)g_S.\] Therefore the injective evaluation map \(\Psi_s=\operatorname{diag}(g_S/\Delta_S)\bigwedge^sE\) intertwines \(\nabla_s\) with \(d/dx\). It sends \(v_s\) to the vector \((g_S)_S\). Taylor expansion of \(g_S(x+T)/g_S(x)\), and the companion square-root identity, give \(\nabla_s^cv_s/c!=[T^c]H_sv_s\). Finally \(u\) commutes with \(\nabla_s\), so binomial expansion of \((\nabla_s+u)^c/c!\) gives the asserted \(1/q!\) factor. The basis weight \(\sum i_j-s(s-1)/2+q\) gives coefficient degree \(c-q-\sum i_j+s(s-1)/2\), exactly the prior matrix grading.

Encoding audit. The exact Macaulay2 audit independently constructs the exterior square roots and the polynomial-connection iterates for every \(1\le n\le4\), \(0\le s\le n\), coefficient \(0\le c\le6\), and every nilpotent-jet coordinate needed at \(d\le4\). Its inventory is 14 blocks and 203 divided-iterate identities; the largest exterior block is \(6\times6\). It checks the elementary-symmetric derivation, all identities and coordinate degrees. Replacing the correction \(s-1/2\) by \(1/2\) fails in every block with \(s\ge2\), so the Vandermonde correction is a nonvacuous control. The full output passes. No threshold value or all-parameter conclusion is inferred from this finite audit; those follow only from the displayed proofs where stated.

Why the generic-orbit answer loses the threshold

Observation (obs:cube-orbit-localization-degree-loss). For \(n=4\), characteristic zero and every \(d\ge2\), the proper first-step ideal \(I_d=I^{(d+1)}_{8d-3}\) becomes the unit ideal after the reciprocal-coordinate localization \[R\longrightarrow F(b_2,b_3,b_4)[x,S(x)^{-1}],\qquad S(x)=\prod_{i=1}^4(x+b_i).\] Its original initial degree is nevertheless positive.

Proof. Inverting all \(a_i\) identifies \(R[(\prod a_i)^{-1}]\) with \(F[x,b_2,b_3,b_4,S^{-1}]\). The pure-curve theorem gives height two and properness in \(R\). On this reciprocal open the zero locus therefore has dimension at most two, possibly empty. It cannot dominate the three-dimensional \(b\)-space. Algebraically, for each minimal prime of the localized ideal the images of the three \(b_i\) are algebraically dependent, so its contraction to \(F[b_2,b_3,b_4]\) contains a nonzero polynomial. Multiplying one such polynomial for each of the finitely many minimal primes gives a nonzero element of the radical of the localized ideal. A power belongs to the ideal itself. Inverting all nonzero polynomials in \(F[b_2,b_3,b_4]\) therefore makes the ideal the unit ideal. If the reciprocal zero locus is already empty, the same conclusion is immediate. Original properness and homogeneity imply positive initial degree. \(\square\)

Source audit and implication. Both Chen–Jaroschek–Kauers–Singer (2013), all eight pages, and Chen–Kauers–Singer (2014), all eleven pages, were read, including proofs. The 2013 Theorem 9 derives a univariate coefficient-degree bound from removable leading factors. The 2014 Theorem 6 uses a generic auxiliary operator of a specified order to remove the factors removable at that order; it does not supply that order bound. These theorems concern a polynomial ring in one variable over a constant field. Taking that field to be \(F(b)\) gives the preceding localized situation. The proofs' univariate degree bounds do not measure the original homogeneous degree in all \(a_i\). Consequently, a generic-orbit factor-removal computation alone cannot prove our threshold. This is not a refutation of the source theorems or of polynomial-parameter Ore contraction: the monic intersection and connection above retain the lost information and are the versions to develop.

General statement. thm:cube-polynomial-ore-model holds for every \(n\ge1,d,m\ge0\) in characteristic zero and provides one finite all-order certificate per \(n,d\). obs:cube-orbit-localization-degree-loss identifies the lost obstruction for every dimension-four first step. No small-prime statement follows from ordinary differential operators or factorial division.

Verification gate. Re-read the threshold system, Hermite–Padé form, generic normality, transport, single division, symmetric descent and pure-curve result. A medium-reasoning pre-proof reviewer checked the differential dictionary, monic division, connection signs and grading, finite-staircase extraction and localization scope. Its correction is included: the reciprocal zero locus can be empty, and the vector is distinguished rather than claimed polynomially cyclic. The full bounded connection audit passed. A fresh-context medium-reasoning correctness reviewer checked every part of the operator theorem, connection, grading and localization proof, and inspected the script and complete output without rerunning. It found no gap or unused substantive hypothesis. The localization observation now uses only positivity from its cited pure-curve dependency; it does not need a numerical threshold.

Assessment and next step. The uniform model now keeps all orders and the original parameter grading in one ideal generated by an explicit finite intersection. The missing numerical implication is its homogeneous Gröbner staircase, not generic divisorial removability. Next implement the polynomial-parameter left-ideal intersection and certify a complete staircase on a solved control before applying it to the retained first-step example; the purpose is one all-order calculation, not a larger list of separately computed kernels. The all-dimensional and small-prime goals remain open.

Process. Reading the source proofs exposed the coefficient-field loss before an uninformative factor-removal run; the polynomial connection was checked against the existing exact encoding instead. No dependency installation or larger parameter sweep was needed.

26 September 2026 — Polynomial operator certificates pass the solved control; dimension four remains computationally unresolved

Working implementation lemma and exact rational control: direct intersection and symmetric connection recover every order at n=3,d=2. The bounded dimension-four attempts do not finish. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and outcome. Open statement 3 requires the actual first parameter degree, not only an equivalent operator ideal. The previous theorem suggested computing one complete homogeneous left Gröbner basis for the entire order row. I implemented both its monic-factor intersection and its polynomial connection. On the smallest solved control with nonzero boundary excess, \(n=3,d=2\), both recover the complete known row from just two basis operators. In dimension four, neither the raw intersection nor the symmetric module preimage finishes within the bounded runs below. Thus this cycle validates the encoding and exposes a computational obstacle; it does not determine a new dimension-four threshold or a uniform staircase.

The connection as a polynomial module presentation

Implementation lemma (lem:cube-connection-presentation). Let \(B\) be a commutative ring with derivation \(\delta\), \(A=B[D;\delta]\), and \(C\) an \(N\times N\) matrix over \(B\). Give \(M=B^N\) the left \(A\)-action \(D\cdot w=\delta(w)+Cw\). For formal basis vectors \(b_j\), let \(L\subset A^N\) be the left submodule generated by

\[D b_j-\sum_i C_{ij}b_i.\]

Then \(A^N/L\cong M\) as left \(A\)-modules, by the map taking \(b_j\) to the ordinary basis vector. In particular, for \(v\in B^N\),

\[\operatorname{Ann}_A(v)=\{P\in A:Pv\in L\}.\]

Proof. The proposed connection is an \(A\)-representation because \([\delta+C,f]=\delta(f)\) for every \(f\in B\). Its evaluation map kills the displayed generators of \(L\). Conversely, reduce a vector in \(A^N\), starting at its largest \(D\)-order, using these monic relations. Reordering a coefficient past \(D\) adds only terms of lower \(D\)-order, so this process ends at a vector with entries in \(B\). The actual connection representation sends that vector to itself. Therefore a vector in its kernel reduces to zero and lies in \(L\). This proves both assertions. No characteristic restriction, generic cyclicity or nonnegative grading assumption is needed for this elementary presentation. \(\square\)

Application with the precise grading. For every \(n\ge1,d\ge0\) in characteristic zero, use the polynomial connection of the previous theorem over \(B=F[e_1,\ldots,e_n]\), with \(\deg e_j=j\) and \(\delta e_j=(j+1)e_{j+1}-e_1e_j\). Its shifted basis degrees \(t_j\) make \(C_{ij}\) have degree \(1+t_j-t_i\), and its distinguished vector has degree zero. Thus the displayed presentation is homogeneous and its preimage is the exact polynomial annihilator. The flat symmetric descent identifies its minimum excess with that of the original root-parameter kernel. For a homogeneous left Gröbner basis \(\mathcal G\) in such a \(D\)-first order,

\[\ell_0(d+1,m)=\min_{g\in\mathcal G,\ \operatorname{ord}_Dg\le m}\bigl(\deg_{\mathrm{wt}}g-\operatorname{ord}_Dg\bigr).\]

The proof from the previous theorem works with any global parameter monomial order after the first \(D\)-order block. Indeed, in \(e_jD=De_j-\delta e_j\) the correction has lower \(D\)-order. Leading exponents therefore add, Dickson's lemma gives a finite homogeneous basis, and leading-term divisibility bounds weighted excess. Multiplication by \(D\) increases exact order and preserves excess, giving the reverse inequality. This is a presentation of the already proved connection, not a new uniform numerical threshold theorem. Characteristic zero is retained here for the divided-iterate threshold dictionary.

The nontrivial solved control

Exact finite check (check:cube-operator-staircase-control). Over \(\mathbb Q\), for \(n=3,d=2\), the direct polynomial ideal has seven factors:

\[A D^2\ \cap\ \bigcap_{i=1}^3 A(D-a_i/2)\ \cap\ \bigcap_{1\le i<j\le3}A(D-(a_i+a_j)/2).\]

The empty subset contributes \(D^2\), so the sum of the factor orders is eight. A completed left Gröbner calculation gives two homogeneous operators, with \((D\text{-order},\text{excess})=(8,3),(9,0)\). Hence the entire row is

\[\ell_0(3,m)=\begin{cases}\infty,&m<8,\\3,&m=8,\\0,&m\ge9.\end{cases}\]

This agrees with the solved dimension-three theorem. Independently, the rank-eight symmetric connection presentation gives two operators with the same order/excess pairs, for both lexicographic and weighted reverse-lexicographic parameter blocks. All runs retain complete basis polynomials. The direct implementation checks every defining Ore relation, homogeneity, membership of each final operator in every monic factor, and the final Buchberger pair. The symmetric implementation checks weighted homogeneity and its final Buchberger pair. Its exporter independently checks every jet column through coefficient six against the exterior square-root encoding, as well as every nonzero connection-entry degree. The control is nonvacuous: dropping the boundary factor, confusing left and right multiplication, or treating weighted parameter degree as ordinary degree would change what is being certified.

Completeness and software scope. The equality with the full ideal comes from Singular's complete intersect and modulo computations and the proved presentation. Membership witnesses and critical-pair reductions by themselves do not prove that equality. The installed nctools.lib implements right preimages by taking opposite rings before invoking modulo; dmodapp.lib's isFsat explicitly uses modulo for the kernel of right multiplication by a fixed element into a left-module quotient. This confirms the required left preimage \(P\mapsto Pv\). No parameter is put into the coefficient field, and no degree truncation is used.

What failed in dimension four

The target comparison was the retained row \(15,12,11,6,5,2,2,0\) at \(m=12,\ldots,19\), previously computed over \(\mathbb F_{32003}\) (record). A rational whole-row certificate would be new evidence; the modular row alone does not give rational upper bounds.

The first raw \(n=4,d=2\) run intersected all singleton factors first and stalled at the first pair factor. It was stopped when a better ordering was available. A second run completed each lower-dimensional subcube first, reached the two-generator dimension-three ideal, then timed out after 180 seconds while adding the fourth singleton. The symmetric rank-twelve presentation passes its encoding and grading checks, but its rational preimage calculation also times out after 180 seconds. Replacing pure parameter lexicographic order with a weighted reverse-lexicographic block preserves the solved control but the dimension-four preimage again reaches the 180-second limit. These failures show the limits of these implementations and budgets, not a mathematical obstruction to the operator model or evidence against a conjectured threshold.

Evidence. Scripts: direct intersection, audited connection exporter, and weighted annihilator. Complete accepted outputs: direct control, symmetric lex control, and symmetric weighted control. Generated rank-eight and rank-twelve presentations and the full failed-run logs are retained with the session. Two Singular runs initially used reserved identifiers and one exporter run used the wrong string-concatenation operator; these are corrected. Because Singular can return exit zero after a syntax error, successful outputs were also checked for error diagnostics and their complete audit lines.

General statement. lem:cube-connection-presentation applies to every finite free connection over a commutative differential ring. Together with thm:cube-polynomial-ore-model, it gives an exact polynomial preimage problem for every cube row in characteristic zero. The numerical result here is only the already solved \(n=3,d=2\) control; the open all-parameter thresholds are untouched.

Verification gate. Re-read the polynomial Ore theorem, its exact symmetric-descent dependency, the dimension-three endpoint and the recorded dimension-four modular row. A medium-reasoning pre-proof reviewer checked prior scope and the seven-factor control, then the connection-presentation signs and polynomial completeness. A fresh-context medium-reasoning correctness reviewer checked the full presentation argument, the scripts, generated presentations and retained control outputs. It found no mathematical gap; its scope correction is included: completeness rests on the full preimage algorithm, not the membership or Buchberger checks. Unneeded hypotheses were removed from the abstract presentation lemma. The dimension-four attempts are reported only as incomplete runs.

Assessment and next step. One computation can certify every order, as the solved control demonstrates, but these implementations have not made the open dimension-four case tractable. The next cycle is a route review: revisit the missing global-degree implication, develop the outstanding passed leads, and test a reduction using an explicit monic annihilator to bound the order before elimination. Any new computation must test an improvement that changes this bottleneck or the underlying uniform mathematics, rather than merely allowing the same Gröbner call more time.

Process. Completing lower-dimensional intersections first and passing to the audited symmetric connection reduced intermediate descriptions, but did not finish dimension four; retained full outputs and explicit syntax-diagnostic checks prevent interrupted or erroring runs from becoming certificates.

27 September 2026 — A bounded polynomial kernel certifies the complete rational row; global degree remains the uniform obstacle

Route review. Working bounded-kernel reduction; exact characteristic-zero row at n=4,d=2; no collision curve component in that first-step case; positive Euler characteristic does not imply a section. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

The line's general claim. Determine the cube per-order function in every odd characteristic and all dimensions by computing the threshold initial degrees. The characteristic-zero dimension-four boundary is proved for every degree, but open statement 3 still requires the later thresholds uniformly, and statement 2 still requires small-prime stable orders. The last six cycles produced pure-curve structure, symmetric descent, one rational resolution and an all-order operator ideal. Their value must be judged by whether they help determine the original global parameter degree.

Obstacle

For \(n=4,d\ge2\), the first unsolved order is \(m=8d-3\). We need matching vanishing and nonvanishing in the smallest homogeneous degree of \(I^{(d+1)}_m\), then analogous control of the deeper orders. An exact ideal presentation or a description on a generic curve is insufficient without that graded calculation. The generic-orbit localization even turns the proper first-step ideal into a unit ideal. The plane-section example shows that saturation does not guarantee lifting. The preceding cycle's complete operator computations passed a solved control but timed out in dimension four. This review tests a smaller exact computation and whether collision components, vector-bundle criteria or an alternating cohomological index explain the remaining difficulty.

Remove unbounded operator elimination

Lemma (lem:cube-bounded-operator-kernel). Let \(B\) be a commutative differential ring, \(A=B[D;\delta]\), and \(J=\operatorname{Ann}_A(v)\) for a vector in a left \(A\)-module. Suppose \(J\) contains a monic operator \(H\) of order \(U\). Then

\[J=AH\oplus_B K_{<U},\qquad K_{<U}=J\cap\{P:\operatorname{ord}_D P<U\}.\]

This is a decomposition of \(B\)-modules; \(K_{<U}\) need not be an \(A\)-submodule. It is the kernel of the \(B\)-linear map

\[B^U\longrightarrow M,\qquad (b_0,\ldots,b_{U-1})\longmapsto\sum_{c=0}^{U-1}b_cD^cv.\]

When \(B\) is Noetherian, this kernel is finitely generated. Its \(B\)-generators, together with \(H\), generate \(J\) as a left ideal.

Proof. Right division by a monic operator stays in \(A\): cancel the highest \(D\)-term successively to obtain uniquely \(P=QH+R\), \(\operatorname{ord}R<U\). Coefficient commutations introduce only lower-order terms. If \(P\) annihilates \(v\), then \(R\) does too. Conversely every displayed summand annihilates \(v\). A nonzero \(QH\) has order \(\operatorname{ord}Q+U\), even if \(B\) has zero divisors, because the leading coefficient of \(H\) is one. Thus the intersection is zero and division is unique. The kernel description follows by writing left coefficients, and Noetherianity gives finite generation inside \(B^U\). \(\square\)

Graded extraction. Suppose now that \(B\) is a polynomial ring over a field with positive parameter weights, \(D\) and \(\delta\) have degree one, the action is homogeneous, \(v\) has degree zero, and \(H\) is homogeneous of degree \(U\). Choose a homogeneous \(B\)-module Gröbner basis \(\mathcal G\) of \(K_{<U}\) in a position-first order where the greatest nonzero coefficient index is leading. Let \(r_g\) be that index and \(e_g\) the weighted degree of its coefficient. The least top coefficient degree is

\[\ell_0(m)=\begin{cases}\min_{r_g\le m} e_g,&m<U,\\0,&m\ge U,\end{cases}\]

with empty minimum infinity. For the lower bound at \(m<U\), the leading term of an exact-order-\(m\) vector is divisible by a basis leading term in position \(m\); weighted degree can only increase under a polynomial multiplier. For the upper bound, \(D^{m-r_g}g\) has exact order \(m\), the same excess, and still belongs to the bounded kernel. The monic operator and its left \(D\)-multiples prove the last case. Positivity excludes negative coefficient degrees.

The cube cutoff is already known. In characteristic zero, the product-and-raising bound gives \(I^{(d+1)}_U=R\) for \(n=4,d\ge2,U=20d-21\). The symmetric descent makes the top ideal over \(B=F[e_1,e_2,e_3,e_4]\) the unit ideal too, by faithful flatness. A homogeneous lift of its degree-zero element \(1\) gives a symmetric solution with \(W_U=1\). In the operator dictionary \(P_W=\sum W_cD^c/c!\), scaling by \(U!\) makes it monic. Thus one bounded \((8d-4)\times(20d-21)\) commutative kernel suffices to represent every order in the row. This does not evaluate that kernel uniformly in \(d\).

The whole degree-two row over the rationals

Exact certificate (check:cube-degree-two-rational-row). For \(n=4,d=2\), the bounded cutoff is \(U=19\). The complete \(12\times19\) kernel over \(\mathbb Q[e_1,e_2,e_3,e_4]\), with weights \(1,2,3,4\), and its position-first Gröbner basis give

Order \(m\)\(<12\)12131415161718\(\ge19\)
\(\ell_0(3,m)\)\(\infty\)15121165220

The script computes one full kernel and one position-first module basis, without a degree cutoff or separate kernel for each order. The complete kernel took 3.12807 CPU seconds; the basis extraction, full output and checks took 23.2545 CPU seconds in total. All 118 basis vectors are retained in the full rational certificate. The exact matrix residual is zero, every vector is homogeneous, and each leading position is its highest nonzero coefficient index. Here position means the coefficient of \(D^c\), not a target connection row.

The implementation uses the original solution coordinates \(W_c\); the abstract lemma uses \(W_c/c!\). This invertible diagonal constant change preserves weighted degrees, leading positions and divisibility, hence the module Gröbner argument. Completeness comes from the exact kernel and gb computations; residual and degree assertions check the returned encoding. The value at 19 is supplied by the previous monic-existence bound, not by a newly computed order-19 operator. Its multiples give every larger order. Flat field extension and symmetric descent give the same row over every characteristic-zero field. No positive-characteristic or other-degree row follows.

The same bounded method was first tested on the retained \(n=3,d=2,U=9\) control. Its \(8\times9\) kernel has one generator, of order eight and top coefficient \(4096(e_1^3-4e_1e_2+8e_3)\), matching the previous full operator basis. The control output contains the complete vector. The new rational dimension-four row agrees with the archived modular row; unlike that earlier evidence, the present calculation provides rational witnesses. This is a successful test of an all-order computation, not a general formula inferred from agreement.

Two diagnostics from the actual first-step scheme

Fixed-case consequence (check:cube-first-step-collision-closure). For \(n=4,d=2\) over every characteristic-zero field, put \(I=I^{(3)}_{13}\) and \(\Delta=\prod_i a_i\prod_{i<j}(a_i-a_j)\). Then

\[I:\Delta^\infty=I.\]

Thus there is no collision-supported curve component, and the scheme is the scheme-theoretic closure of its own collision-free restriction. This does not assert radicality or identify it with a reduced effectivity locus.

Proof and exact test. Use the four retained full branch-invariant generators of weights \(12,13,14,15\), whose equality with the actual ideal was previously certified. On the collision hyperplane \(a_1=0\), the five branch roots are \((0,0,u,v,w)\). Center them by their mean and substitute their elementary invariants. The four complete restrictions, of degrees \(12,13,14,15\), have gcd one in \(\mathbb Q[u,v,w]\). If an associated height-two prime of \(R/I\) contained \(a_1\), its image in \(R/(a_1)\) would be a height-one prime, hence generated by an irreducible common divisor of the restrictions. This contradicts the gcd. The unmixedness theorem excludes associated primes of other heights, and full \(S_5\)-symmetry gives the same result on all ten collision hyperplanes. None of their equations is a zero divisor modulo \(I\), so neither is their product. This proves saturation by every power of \(\Delta\), which is the affine contraction defining the indicated closure. Field extension preserves this injection. \(\square\)

The two codimension-two flat types were also tested. Neither the triple-root pattern \((0,0,0,u,v)\) nor the two-pair pattern \((0,0,u,u,v)\) lies entirely in the ideal's zero set. Their restrictions can still have common zeros, and do: those are intersections with the scheme, not whole collision-line components. The full restrictions and gcds are retained. No all-degree collision assertion is made.

Actual cohomological obstruction (obs:cube-first-step-index-obstruction). The normalized first-step reflexive sheaf at \(d=2\), \(\mathcal E=\widetilde K(7)\), satisfies \(h^0(\mathcal E)=0\) but \(\chi(\mathcal E)=280\). Its first section is at twist five, and its Chern classes are \(c_1=0,c_2=71H^2,c_3=840H^3\); in particular it is not locally free of rank two.

Proof. The retained exact resolution gives

\[0\longrightarrow\mathcal O(-10)\oplus\mathcal O(-11)\oplus\mathcal O(-12)\longrightarrow\mathcal O(-5)\oplus\mathcal O(-6)\oplus\mathcal O(-7)^2\oplus\mathcal O(-8)\longrightarrow\mathcal E\longrightarrow0.\]

Write \(b(t)=\binom{t+3}{3}\) for \(t\ge0\), and \(b(t)=0\) otherwise. Since the first and second cohomology of every line bundle on \(\mathbb P^3\) vanish, \(H^1(\mathcal E(t))=0\) for every integer \(t\), and

\[h^0(\mathcal E(t))=b(t-5)+b(t-6)+2b(t-7)+b(t-8)-b(t-10)-b(t-11)-b(t-12).\]

This is zero for \(t<5\) and one for \(t=5\). Using the Euler polynomial of each line bundle instead gives

\[\chi(\mathcal E(t))=2\binom{t+3}{3}-71(t+2)+420,\]

where the binomial on this line is a polynomial for every integer \(t\). Expansion of the Chern character of the displayed resolution yields the claimed Chern classes. A locally free rank-two sheaf has no third Chern class, so this one is not locally free. At twist zero the derived global-section complex has a space of dimension \(84+120+165=369\) in cohomological degree two mapping to a space of dimension \(4+10+20+20+35=89\) in degree three, with no degree-zero space. Its Euler characteristic is 280, entirely compatible with no global sections. \(\square\)

Outside leads

  • Ore monic division and bounded module elimination. The lemma replaces unbounded noncommutative elimination by a finite polynomial kernel, using the already proved order-zero cutoff. The mathematical input is monic division, proved above; it retains every parameter degree and does not require a new generic-orbit theorem. The solved control and the complete rational dimension-four row test the actual target. Test. Passed: the new method completes the previously stalled row. Answers. A uniform description of these bounded kernels would determine all graded thresholds; the linear cutoff reduces the required objects but does not supply their generator degrees.
  • Kapranov's configuration compactification and collision extension. The proved configuration dictionary identifies the collision-free parameter space with \(M_{0,n+2}\). This cycle tests an actual obstruction to comparing a compactified calculation with the original ideal: extra curve components on the boundary. The full invariant generators, rather than a generic fibre model, show that they are absent at \(d=2\). No additional theorem from the unread portions of Kapranov's paper is invoked. Test. Passed for the stated first-step case: gcd one on a representative collision hyperplane and unmixedness prove \(I:\Delta^\infty=I\). Answers. Controlling this extension uniformly would permit a boundary-aware graded-section calculation; absence of curve components alone still does not determine section degree or boundary multiplicities.
  • Bernstein–Gelfand–Gelfand and graded global cohomology. The full three-page BGG note was reread, including its stable-category equivalence and proof sketch. Its coherent-sheaf formulation applies even though the actual normalized sheaf is not a vector bundle. This cycle constructs its derived global-section complex from the retained resolution and computes its graded section function; it does not claim an explicit exterior-module presentation in all degrees. Test. Passed: the actual degree-two sheaf has first section at twist five, while its untwisted Euler characteristic is 280. Answers. The grading and the correct cohomological sector recover the threshold exactly; a uniform complex with controlled low-degree cohomology could provide the needed vanishing and nonvanishing. Rank, Chern numbers or an ungraded index cannot replace it.

Absurd bridges

  • Supersymmetric ground states and the Witten index. Translate a finite complex computing derived global sections into a graded state space, with supercharge its differential \(Q\) and, over \(\mathbb C\), Hamiltonian \(QQ^*+Q^*Q\) after choosing Hermitian inner products. Its alternating index is the sheaf Euler characteristic; our target is specifically the cohomological degree-zero sector. Unlike the earlier bare exterior-space shortcut, the test now uses the actual constrained complex \(\mathbb C^{369}\to\mathbb C^{89}\) in degrees two and three. Test. Falsified for inferring a target section from a positive index: the index is 280 but the degree-zero space is absent. Answers. Keeping the cohomological sector, twist and differential repairs the translation and gives exactly the section problem, as the explicit resolution demonstrates. Supersymmetric or BGG methods themselves are not excluded; an alternating index alone cannot answer the obstacle.
  • Finite-state chemical kinetics and Cayley–Hamilton closure. Treat the polynomial connection as a linear concentration-response system with varying rates; one inert state and one autocatalytic state already give the actual \(n=1,d=1\) test \(C=\operatorname{diag}(0,a/2)\), \(v=(1,1)\), and rate evolution \(\delta a=-a^2\). Cayley–Hamilton gives \(C^2-(a/2)C=0\), suggesting an order-two frozen-rate closure. But the actual covariant derivative is \(\nabla=\delta+C\), and direct calculation gives \((\nabla^2-(a/2)\nabla)v=(0,-a^2/2)\), whereas \((\nabla^2+(a/2)\nabla)v=0\). Test. Falsified for replacing covariant iterates by powers of the instantaneous rate matrix; the exact residual and repaired monic operator are in the audit. Answers. A faithful finite polynomial state module and a uniform bound on its graded cyclic relations would control both order and excess. The connection and bounded-kernel construction develop that repaired encoding; ordinary state count or a frozen characteristic polynomial loses the derivative terms.

Bridge follow-up

  • Renewal-reward. The propagated product bound now supplies the finite cutoff \(U=20d-21\) for the entire characteristic-zero row, and the new kernel calculation uses it rather than guessing optimality from repeated blocks. Follow-up. Developed as an upper cutoff; continuing on the missing matching order-zero lower bound. The new row has the old endpoint 19 and does not establish renewal optimality in all degrees.

Lead follow-up

  • Invariant order-zero solutions. Faithful symmetric descent turns the proved unit top ideal into a homogeneous invariant solution and hence a monic operator of the same order. Follow-up. Developed: this supplies the cutoff over the correct weighted coefficient ring. No new all-degree optimal endpoint is asserted.
  • Hermite–Padé. The exact character-row encoding is now evaluated jointly across the full rational degree-two row, through one bounded kernel rather than separate order scans. Follow-up. Developed for characteristic-zero graded approximation; continuing for the small-prime stable-order obligation, where factorial division is unavailable.
  • Horrocks and lifting. The actual normalized sheaf has \(H^1(\mathcal E(t))=0\) in every twist but \(c_3=840H^3\), so it is not a vector bundle to which a splitting criterion can simply be applied. Its complete section function is instead obtained from the exact resolution. Follow-up. Developed; retain degree-specific global cohomology as the endpoint, not blanket local-freeness or splitting assumptions.
  • Polarized Humbert decomposition. Compared the descended theta description with the actual first-step ideal: the collision-saturation calculation removes extra boundary curve components at \(d=2\), one obstruction to extending a collision-free description. Radicality and comparison with the reduced theta/effectivity locus remain unproved. Follow-up. Continuing with this exact scope; a set-theoretic theta test still cannot determine the scheme's first parameter degree.

27 September 2026 — Added jets have a fixed-rank obstruction; lifting one smallest old operator misses the boundary

Working all-parameter added-jet map in characteristic zero. Exact family certificate: no single homogeneous degree-19 operator for n=4,d=2 reaches the d=4 boundary by a left multiple. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and outcome. Open statement 3 needs a uniform argument for the first graded relation, beyond the certified degree-two row. The connection blocks are fixed while their nilpotent jet lengths grow. This cycle identifies the exact map measuring that growth: its target has rank at most \(2^n\), independent of \(d\). It then tests the proposed shortcut of propagating one smallest old operator. In dimension four, every homogeneous old operator of minimal total degree fails to reach the next degree-two increment's boundary by a single left multiple. The test covers the complete family, not one chosen representative. Sums involving several old relations and the full polynomial obstruction map remain available; no new numerical threshold formula is claimed.

The formal derivative criterion

Lemma (lem:cube-added-jet-obstruction). Work over a characteristic-zero field, with \(R=F[a_1,\ldots,a_n]\), \(\delta=-\sum a_i^2\partial_{a_i}\), and \(\mathscr A_R=R[D;\delta]\). Let \(\partial_D\) fix \(R\) and send \(D\) to one. Put \(\lambda_S=\frac12\sum_{i\in S}a_i\), \(k_s(d)=\max(0,\lfloor(d-s)/2\rfloor+1)\), and use the polynomial annihilator \(\mathscr J_d\). Then

\[\mathscr J_{d+2}=\{P\in\mathscr J_d:\partial_DP\in\mathscr J_d\}\ \cap\!\bigcap_{d<|S|\le\min(n,d+2)}\mathscr A_R(D-\lambda_S).\]

The last intersection is absent for \(d\ge n\). On \(\mathscr J_d\), the map \(P\mapsto\partial_DP\bmod\mathscr J_d\) is left \(\mathscr A_R\)-linear. It has homogeneous degree minus one, and for a nonzero operator of positive order it decreases order by one while preserving excess. In the original coordinates \(P_W=\sum_c W_cD^c/c!\), it is the shift \(W'_c=W_{c+1}\).

Proof. Formal differentiation kills the relation \(Df-fD-\delta f\), so it is a derivation of the Ore algebra. For an old subset put \(t=D-\lambda_S\), \(k=k_s(d)>0\). The change of generator from \(D\) to \(t\) leaves the coefficient derivation unchanged. Every \(P\in\mathscr A_Rt^k\) has a unique left-coefficient expansion \(P=\sum_{j\ge k}b_jt^j\). Differentiation gives \(\sum_{j\ge k}j b_jt^{j-1}\). This belongs to \(\mathscr A_Rt^k\) exactly when \(kb_k=0\), hence when \(b_k=0\), because \(k\) is invertible. This is exactly membership in \(\mathscr A_Rt^{k+1}\). Every old exponent increases by one; newly appearing subsets have exponent one and must be imposed separately. For \(Q\in\mathscr A_R\), the product-rule error \((\partial_DQ)P\) belongs to the left ideal \(\mathscr J_d\), proving linearity of the induced map. Homogeneity and the coordinate shift follow by differentiating \(W_cD^c/c!\). \(\square\)

In particular, once every subset is present, iterating the criterion gives \(\mathscr J_{d+2r}=\{P:\partial_D^jP\in\mathscr J_d\text{ for }0\le j\le r\}\). This is a differential condition on a left ideal, not a statement that ordinary ideal powers or operator powers add the required jets.

The polynomial target has bounded rank

Let \(B=F[e_1,\ldots,e_n]\), with \(\deg e_j=j\), and \(\mathscr A_B=B[D;\delta_B]\), where \(\delta_Be_j=(j+1)e_{j+1}-e_1e_j\). The previous theorem constructs \(V_s\), its connection \(\nabla_s\), basis weights \(w_I=\sum i_j-s(s-1)/2\), and distinguished vector \(v_s\). Write

\[\mathcal M_d=\bigoplus_{s\le\min(n,d)}V_s\otimes B[u]/u^{k_s(d)},\qquad D|_s=\nabla_s+u.\]

The natural projection \(\mathcal M_{d+2}\to\mathcal M_d\), sending new blocks to zero, has kernel

\[\mathcal L_d=\bigoplus_{s\le\min(n,d+2)}u^{k_s(d)}V_s,\qquad \operatorname{rank}_B\mathcal L_d=\sum_{s=0}^{\min(n,d+2)}\binom ns\le2^n.\]

Its basis shifts are \(k_s(d)+w_I\); multiplication by \(u\) is zero on this kernel, so its connection is the shifted \(\nabla_s\). The rank is already \(2^n\) when \(d+2\ge n\), although absence of new blocks requires \(d\ge n\). There is an exact kernel description

\[\rho_d:\mathscr J_d^B\longrightarrow\mathcal L_d,\qquad P\longmapsto Pv_{d+2},\qquad \ker\rho_d=\mathscr J_{d+2}^B,\]

where \(\mathscr J_d^B=\operatorname{Ann}_{\mathscr A_B}(v_d)\). The map is left \(\mathscr A_B\)-linear and has homogeneous degree zero. On a block with \(k=k_s(d)\), its coefficient is

\[\rho_{d,s}(P)=\frac1{k!}(\partial_D^kP)(\nabla_s)v_s.\]

For an old block, \((\partial_DP)v_d\) is supported only at its top old jet, with coefficient \(k\rho_{d,s}(P)\). New blocks have \(k=0\), contribute \(P(\nabla_s)v_s\), and are invisible in that derivative acting on the old module.

Proof. Each included jet length increases by exactly one. The projection respects the connection, hence sends \(Pv_{d+2}\) to \(Pv_d=0\). Its kernel and grading are the displayed ones, and acting on the distinguished vector proves linearity and the asserted kernel. Since \(u\) commutes with \(\nabla_s\), the coefficient of \(u^k\) in \(P(\nabla_s+u)v_s\) is the displayed formal derivative. Differentiating the polynomial in \(u\) gives the old-top-jet identity; lower coefficients vanish because \(P\) annihilates \(v_d\).

The image has full generic rank. Indeed, over \(K=\operatorname{Frac}B\), generic normality makes \(v_{d+2}\) cyclic in \(K\otimes_B\mathcal M_{d+2}\). Any vector of the kernel layer is therefore \(Pv_{d+2}\) for an operator over \(K[D;\delta_B]\); its projection says \(Pv_d=0\). Clearing a common coefficient denominator on the left identifies this localized annihilator with \(K\otimes_B\mathscr J_d^B\). Thus the localized map is onto. This does not prove polynomial surjectivity, control of its cokernel, or the first degree in its kernel. \(\square\)

Why powers and a single smallest operator are insufficient

A direct control for powers. For \(n=1,d=1\), set \(x=1/a\) and \(H_2=D^2+(a/2)D\). It annihilates \(1,\sqrt{x}\), but \(H_2(x)=a/2\) and \(H_2^2(x)=3a^3/4\ne0\). Squaring therefore misses an added jet. The actual next operator

\[H_4=D^4+3aD^3+\tfrac34a^2D^2=(D^2+\tfrac52aD+\tfrac12a^2)H_2\]

satisfies \(\partial_DH_4=(4D+7a)H_2\). Direct multiplication using \(Da=aD-a^2\) also gives \(H_4=(D^2+3aD+\frac34a^2)D^2=(D^2+4aD+2a^2)(D-a/2)^2\), verifying the next intersection. This falsifies the power shortcut, not the derivative criterion.

Family obstruction (obs:cube-minimal-degree-single-lift-obstruction). In the characteristic-zero four-dimensional cube, every nonzero homogeneous operator in \(\mathscr J_2\) of minimal total degree 19 fails to reach \(\mathscr J_4\) at order 28 by a single nonzero left multiple, even allowing rational parameter coefficients in that multiplier. This includes every homogeneous monic order-19 choice. Generic normality gives the new boundary order \(N_{2,4}(4)=28\), so the shortcut misses a required part of the row. The assertion does not exclude sums of multiples of several old relations, nonhomogeneous choices or other old degrees.

Classify the whole homogeneous family. The complete retained bounded kernel has no operator of total degree below 19, and exactly one degree-19 basis vector \(G\), of order 17 and excess two. The exact matrix, not only the threshold table, was read to check this inventory. A new polynomial solve gives a degree-19 order-19 vector \(H\) with \(W_{19}=1\), verifying all old rows and degrees. Thus the degree-19 annihilator space is \(F H+F G\): all other operators at that degree have order below 19, and the homogeneous bounded kernel at that degree is one-dimensional. Positive weights prohibit a contribution from higher-degree generators. Graded free symmetric descent gives the same classification in the root ring: its nonconstant Artin basis elements have positive degree and cannot multiply a nonexistent lower-degree kernel component.

In these \(W\)-coordinates the operator's leading coefficient is \(1/19!\). Scaling both \(H\) and \(G\) by \(19!\) puts the family \(H+\alpha G\) in monic convention without affecting any rank or resultant below. The parameter \(\alpha\) belongs to the constant field, including arbitrary characteristic-zero field extensions; it is not a parameter-dependent rational function.

The first response test. For \(d=2\to4\), the new layer has block ranks \(1,4,6,4,1\), with old jet lengths \(2,1,1,0,0\). After symbolic differentiation, specialize the roots to \((1,2,3,5)\), so the elementary invariants are \((11,41,61,30)\), and reduce modulo 32003. Every rational coefficient denominator survives this reduction. The matrix \(A=[\rho(H),\nabla\rho(H),\ldots,\nabla^{15}\rho(H)]\) has determinant 10034. This proves generic characteristic-zero cyclic rank 16, not merely numerical rank at an assumed generic point: the corresponding rational determinant polynomial is nonzero. Hence no nonzero left multiplier of this \(H\) of order below 16 annihilates its response, and its first possible order in \(\mathscr J_4\) is at least 35.

Exclude every monic choice. Let \(B_0\) be the corresponding 16-column matrix for \(G\). The two ten-by-ten minors of \(A+zB_0\) using columns \(0,\ldots,9\) and rows \(0,\ldots,9\), respectively \(1,\ldots,10\), are

\[\begin{aligned}f(z)={}&-7222z^{10}+2782z^9-3584z^8+5973z^7+3149z^6+7148z^5\\&-11913z^4-6205z^3+8511z^2-8417z+6606,\\g(z)={}&-9707z^{10}+13802z^9-5526z^8-2385z^7+14656z^6+4608z^5\\&-1981z^4+14547z^3-3017z^2-7487z+10361\end{aligned}\]

over \(\mathbb F_{32003}\). Both have degree ten and their resultant is 12223, not zero. Their degree-ten homogenizations have no common projective root; the nonzero leading coefficients also exclude infinity. Since the rational coefficients are integral at this prime and both degrees are preserved, the characteristic-zero resultant is nonzero too. No constant-field choice of \(\alpha\) can make both rational specialized minors vanish. Thus the first ten generic response iterates are independent for every monic family member. A nonzero multiplier of order at most nine would contradict this independence. Every such left multiple entering \(\mathscr J_4\) therefore has order at least \(19+10=29\), which already misses 28.

The pure \(G\) direction has \(\det B_0=-10810\ne0\pmod{32003}\). Its generic cyclic rank is 16, so a nonzero left multiple entering \(\mathscr J_4\) has order at least \(17+16=33\). Together these cover every nonzero vector \(cH+bG\) of the old minimal total degree. \(\square\)

Exact evidence and scope

The first script solves for \(H\) over \(\mathbb Q\), checks its old equations and degrees, and constructs the added-layer response. The family script reads the complete old basis, verifies the one-dimensional lower-order degree-19 space, checks every denominator, forms both symbolic response matrices before root evaluation, and computes the two minors and resultant. Complete outputs retain \(H\) and its response and \(G\), both matrices and the resultant.

The independent Taylor audit uses \(a_i(t)=a_i/(1+a_it)\), literal square-root characters and the factor \(g_S(x+t)/g_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}(1+a_it)^{1/2}\), modulo \(t^{16}\). It compares every entry of both matrices after the explicit Vandermonde frame change \(\Theta_s=\operatorname{diag}(1/\Delta_S)\bigwedge^s(a_i^j)\). All 512 identities pass; the frame determinant is \(-4082\pmod{32003}\). Omitting the character factor fails all 30 nonempty-character first-derivative comparisons. The full audit also records both determinants. This checks the fixed modular certificate's encoding; the all-parameter map is justified by the displayed proof, not by extrapolating the finite audit.

General statement. lem:cube-added-jet-obstruction gives the exact derivative recurrence and bounded-rank polynomial layer map for every \(n\ge1,d\ge0\) in characteristic zero. obs:cube-minimal-degree-single-lift-obstruction refutes propagation by a single minimal-total-degree old operator already at \(n=4,d=2\to4\), including its complete homogeneous family. The remaining uniform implication is control of the full map's graded kernel, not of a generic scalar annihilator alone.

Verification gate. Read the exact Ore/connection theorem, generic normality, symmetric descent and bounded-kernel proof, with reviewed dependency links. A medium-reasoning pre-proof reviewer checked the derivative recurrence, new blocks, fixed-rank map and family scope. A fresh-context medium-reasoning correctness reviewer inspected the proofs, all three scripts and bounded certificate excerpts without rerunning. It found no gap and accepted the pure-\(G\) strengthening. Its qualifications are retained: generic surjectivity is not polynomial surjectivity; the family parameter is constant; monic normalization uses \(19!\); exclusions concern nonzero multipliers; and the independent audit verifies this finite encoding rather than all parameters.

Assessment and next step. The uniform growth problem now has an explicit target whose rank stays fixed with \(d\), and the complete minimal-degree family test rules out one tempting way of avoiding its coupled relations. This does not evaluate the uniform threshold. Next investigate the support and graded structure of the polynomial cokernel of \(\rho_d\), retaining the operator-order filtration: distinguish an obstruction from collision parameters from failure to lift within the required order and excess. Use the whole old relation module, since a single minimal-degree relation has now been tested and excluded at the first nontrivial increment.

27 September 2026 — The cyclic defect has an explicit collision divisor, but height-one data miss an actual defect

Working all-parameter support and divisorial formula in characteristic zero. Exact solved control: the n=3,d=2 cyclic image is nonreflexive at a two-pair collision. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and outcome. The added-jet map has fixed target rank, but open statement 3 still needs the first degree of its polynomial kernel. This cycle determines where its unfiltered polynomial cokernel can live, and computes its codimension-one multiplicities using the existing Smith theorem. It also tests the suggested reconstruction from local data along collision divisors. That reconstruction fails for the actual cyclic image already in the solved three-dimensional control: a height-two defect survives. The result locates two different costs, without pretending that divisor multiplicities alone give the global threshold.

Cyclic images and bounded lifting off collisions

Proposition (prop:cube-cyclic-collision-defect). Work in characteristic zero. In the symmetric polynomial connection, write

\[\mathcal N_d=\mathscr A_Bv_d\subseteq\mathcal M_d,\qquad \mathcal C_d=\mathcal M_d/\mathcal N_d,\qquad \mathcal T_d=\operatorname{coker}\rho_d.\]

Here \(\mathcal N_d\) is the \(B\)-span of all iterates, not the threshold kernel. It is finite over the Noetherian ring \(B\), as a submodule of the finite free \(\mathcal M_d\). Let

\[p(z)=z^n-e_1z^{n-1}+\cdots+(-1)^ne_n,\qquad \mathfrak d=\operatorname{Disc}(p),\qquad q=e_n\mathfrak d,\]

with \(\mathfrak d=1\) when \(n=1\). Then for every \(n\ge1,d\ge0\):

  • \(\mathcal C_d[q^{-1}]=0\); in fact the iterates through order \(2^{n-1}d\) already generate \(\mathcal M_d\) after this localization.
  • \(\rho_d\) is onto after inverting \(q\), even when its source is restricted to old annihilators of order at most \(2^{n-1}(d+2)\).
  • There is an exact sequence of finite torsion \(B\)-modules \[0\longrightarrow\mathcal T_d\longrightarrow\mathcal C_{d+2}\longrightarrow\mathcal C_d\longrightarrow0.\]

Proof of the support and order bound. Extend the field to an algebraic closure and specialize at any point with \(q\ne0\). Its roots \(a_i\) are distinct and nonzero. On the smooth root cover \(w_i^2=1+a_iT\), the \(2^{n-1}\) points at infinity form \(H_\infty\); each \(w_i\) has a simple pole there and \(T\) a double pole. The functions \(T^Qw^S\), \(2Q+|S|\le d\), are independent by the Kummer character basis. Each has pole divisor bounded by \(dH_\infty\), of degree \(L=2^{n-1}d\). Thus a nonzero linear combination cannot vanish at the unramified marked point \(T=0,w_i=1\) to order \(L+1\). The coefficient matrix through order \(L\) has full row rank at every such parameter point.

The companion frame is invertible off collisions, and its coefficient columns differ from the connection iterates only by invertible characteristic-zero factorial normalizations. Hence this finite column matrix is onto at every closed point of \(B[q^{-1}]\). Its finite cokernel is zero by Nakayama and the fact that this ring is Jacobson. Faithful scalar extension descends the conclusion to the original field. This argument requires only the independent functions and their pole bound; it does not require that they fill a complete Riemann–Roch space or the older restriction \(d>n-3\).

Apply the same argument to \(d+2\). Every vector of the new layer can be lifted through the new column matrix by an operator of order at most \(2^{n-1}(d+2)\). Its projection to \(\mathcal M_d\) is zero, so that operator belongs to the localized old bounded annihilator kernel. Localization of this finite matrix kernel is exact. Finally, the projection sends \(v_{d+2}\) to \(v_d\), hence \(\mathcal N_{d+2}\) onto \(\mathcal N_d\). Its intersection with the kernel layer is precisely \(\rho_d(\mathscr J_d^B)\). The quotient diagram gives the displayed torsion sequence. \(\square\)

This is a localized order bound, not a bound on the powers of \(q\) needed to clear a lift's coefficients. Those denominators and the operator-order filtration remain part of the global-degree problem.

The codimension-one Fitting divisor

For \(n\ge2\), put

\[E_n(d)=\sum_{s=0}^{\min(n-1,d)}\binom{n-1}{s}\left\lfloor\frac{(d-s+1)^2}{4}\right\rfloor,\qquad A_n(d)=\sum_{s=0}^n k_s(d)\binom{n-2}{s-1},\]

where \(k_s(d)=\max(0,\lfloor(d-s)/2\rfloor+1)\) and out-of-range binomial coefficients are zero. The codimension-one divisor of the zeroth Fitting ideal of \(\mathcal C_d\) is

\[\operatorname{DivFitt}_0(\mathcal C_d)=E_n(d)[e_n=0]+\frac{E_n(d)-A_n(d)}2[\mathfrak d=0].\]

The corresponding divisor for \(\mathcal T_d\) is obtained by taking the difference between degrees \(d+2\) and \(d\). These statements concern DVR lengths, not equality of the full Fitting ideals with principal ideals.

Proof. Over \(R=F[a_1,\ldots,a_n]\), first use the raw character connection: one block \(R[u]/u^{k_{|S|}(d)}\) for each subset, with action \(\delta+\lambda_S+u\). Its divided-iterate matrix is the original character coefficient matrix up to nonzero factorial row and column factors. The change between the \(z\)-basis and the \(w\)-characters is triangular with nonzero constant diagonal. These changes preserve local elementary divisors. The existing all-truncation Smith theorem therefore gives cyclic-cokernel length \(E_n(d)\) at every raw collision hyperplane for every truncation \(m\ge N-1\). Nested full-rank images with equal finite colength over a DVR are equal, so this is also the length for the infinite cyclic image. The case \(d=0\) is trivial.

Let \(E=(a_i^j)\) be the Vandermonde evaluation matrix. The polynomial frame from companion to raw coordinates on the \(s\)-block is

\[\Theta_s=\operatorname{diag}(1/\Delta_S)\bigwedge^sE.\]

Its entries are polynomials because each alternant is divisible by the corresponding subset Vandermonde. For \(s\ge1\), the exponent of a given factor \(a_i-a_j\) in its determinant is

\[\binom{n-1}{s-1}-\binom{n-2}{s-2}=\binom{n-2}{s-1};\]

for \(s=0\), the determinant is one. There are \(k_s(d)\) copies. The full frame \(\Theta\) is injective, and the raw column image is \(\Theta(R\otimes_B\mathcal N_d)\). Thus

\[0\longrightarrow R\otimes_B\mathcal C_d\longrightarrow\mathcal C_d^{\rm raw}\longrightarrow\operatorname{coker}\Theta\longrightarrow0.\]

At \(a_i=0\) the frame is a unit generically, so the companion length is \(E_n(d)\). At \(a_i=a_j\) its determinant has valuation \(A_n(d)\), so the companion length is \(E_n(d)-A_n(d)\). The direction of this subtraction matters.

The coordinate hyperplanes form one symmetric-group orbit, and the pair-collision hyperplanes another. Their images are the irreducible divisors \(e_n=0\) and \(\mathfrak d=0\). The generic ramification index of the root-to-coefficient map is one over the first and two over the second: near a simple pair collision, the transverse root coordinate changes sign and the symmetric transverse coordinate is its square. Length under this DVR extension is multiplied by that ramification index, with no residue-degree factor. Dividing the pair-collision length by two proves the formula. The support result excludes other prime divisors. Lengths are additive in the torsion sequence, giving the claim for \(\mathcal T_d\). \(\square\)

Dimension four. For every \(d\ge2\), the existing identity \(E_4(d)=d^2+(d-1)^2\) and the two parity cases in \(A_4=k_1+2k_2+k_3\) give \(A_4(d)=2d-1\). Hence

\[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{DivFitt}_0(\mathcal C_d)&=(d^2+(d-1)^2)[e_4=0]+(d-1)^2[\mathfrak d=0],\\\operatorname{DivFitt}_0(\mathcal T_d)&=(8d+4)[e_4=0]+4d[\mathfrak d=0].\end{aligned}\]

This is an explicit composition of the known collision Smith theorem, the companion frame and the new quotient sequence. It is not a new independent confluence calculation, and it does not determine the threshold from a divisor degree.

An actual defect invisible to height-one reconstruction

Obstruction (obs:cube-cyclic-image-nonreflexive). For \(n=3,d=2\), the actual cyclic image \(\mathcal N_2\) over \(B=\mathbb Q[e_1,e_2,e_3]\) is not reflexive. Its codimension-one localizations therefore reconstruct a strictly larger module. The full zeroth Fitting ideal of \(\mathcal C_2\) has a proper height-two residual factor beyond its divisor \(e_3^4\mathfrak d_3\).

Proof and exact control. The retained complete operator control contains an order-nine annihilator with constant leading coefficient 256. Dividing by that scalar makes it monic, so all higher iterates reduce to the first nine. Therefore \(\mathcal N_2\) is exactly the image of the \(8\times9\) coefficient matrix \(\Phi\) with columns indexed \(0,\ldots,8\). Its retained complete polynomial kernel is generated by one vector \(G\), of total operator degree 11, with

\[G_8=4096(e_1^3-4e_1e_2+8e_3).\]

The vector is primitive: dividing a hypothetical common nonunit factor would give another polynomial kernel vector outside the module it generates. Thus the signed maximal minors are one polynomial times \(G\). The exact audit rebuilds \(\Phi\), verifies \(\Phi G=0\), verifies the coordinate gcd is one, and checks all nine identities

\[(-1)^j\det\Phi_{\widehat j}=c\,e_3^4\mathfrak d_3 G_j,\qquad c\in\mathbb Q^\times,\]

where

\[\mathfrak d_3=e_1^2e_2^2-4e_2^3-4e_1^3e_3+18e_1e_2e_3-27e_3^2.\]

The discriminant expression is also checked against the squared root Vandermonde. Consequently

\[\operatorname{Fitt}_0(\mathcal C_2)=(e_3^4\mathfrak d_3)\,I(G).\]

All coordinates of \(G\) vanish identically under \((e_1,e_2,e_3)=(2t,t^2,0)\). This is checked on the complete vector, not inferred from the top coordinate. Thus \(I(G)\) is contained in the height-two prime \(\mathfrak p=(e_3,e_1^2-4e_2)\), which is the image of a two-pair root collision. Primitivity gives height at least two, so the residual ideal has height exactly two and is proper.

The graded presentation

\[0\longrightarrow B(-11)\xrightarrow{G}\bigoplus_{c=0}^8 B(-c)\longrightarrow\mathcal N_2\longrightarrow0\]

becomes a minimal length-one free resolution at \(\mathfrak p\), because every coordinate lies in that maximal ideal. Over the regular local ring \(B_{\mathfrak p}\) of dimension two, its projective dimension is one. The Auslander–Buchsbaum formula gives depth one. Hence this torsion-free image fails \((S_2)\) and is not reflexive; the height-one characterization of reflexive modules then gives the strict enlargement. Both cited statements and their proofs were read. The full output retains every cofactor and the substitution check. \(\square\)

27 September 2026 — A reflexive ambient connection preserves the exact polynomial annihilator

Working general ambient lemma and exact characteristic-zero control: the nonreflexive three-dimensional cyclic image has a free hull, with its residual defect retained by the vector and connection. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and outcome. Open statement 3 needs uniform graded relations, including the marked highest-order coefficient. The previous counterexample forbids reconstructing the actual cyclic image from its height-one localizations. It does not forbid using their intersection as a larger ambient module. The lemma below proves that this ambient change preserves the entire polynomial annihilator, hence every order and excess restriction. In the actual solved control the hull is free, and an exact frame gives a polynomial connection on it. The cyclic-image quotient remains a nonzero doubled collision locus. This advances the collision-extension lead by validating the change of ambient module; it does not supply the missing uniform generator-degree law.

The connection extends without changing its polynomial source

Lemma (lem:cube-reflexive-ambient-connection). Let \(B\) be a normal Noetherian domain, \(K=\operatorname{Frac}B\), \(\delta:B\to B\) a derivation, and \(M\) a finite reflexive \(B\)-module with a \(\delta\)-connection \(\nabla\). Let \(N\subseteq M\) be a \(\nabla\)-stable submodule. Inside \(N_K\subseteq M_K\), \[N^{**}=\bigcap_{\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak p=1}N_{\mathfrak p}\subseteq M,\] and this hull is stable under the extended connection. For every \(v\in N\), its annihilators in \(A=B[D;\delta]\), computed using \(N\), \(N^{**}\) or \(M\), are equal. Thus restricting the source to a fixed order, a fixed homogeneous degree, or a specified highest-order coefficient gives exactly the same kernel in all three models. If \(B,M,N\) are graded, the inclusion is homogeneous, and \(\delta,\nabla\) raise degree by one, then the hull and its connection have the same graded structure. Freeness of the hull is not asserted.

Proof. All these finite modules are torsion-free. Normality gives \(B=\bigcap_{\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak p=1}B_{\mathfrak p}\) inside \(K\), and each height-one localization is a DVR. To see the double-dual formula directly, identify \(N^{**}\) inside \(N_K\) by evaluation against \(N^*=\operatorname{Hom}_B(N,B)\). An element of every \(N_{\mathfrak p}\) pairs into every \(B_{\mathfrak p}\), hence into \(B\), with every member of \(N^*\); it therefore belongs to \(N^{**}\). Conversely, finite presentation lets duals commute with localization, and a finite torsion-free module over a DVR is free. Thus \((N^{**})_{\mathfrak p}=N_{\mathfrak p}\), giving the reverse inclusion. Apply the same formula to the reflexive \(M\) to obtain the displayed inclusion. This is the standard height-one characterization of reflexivity, applied inside the correct generic subspace; \(N\) need not have full rank in \(M\).

The unique extension of the connection to the fraction field satisfies \[\nabla(n/s)=\nabla(n)/s-\delta(s)n/s^2.\] For \(s\notin\mathfrak p\), both terms lie in \(N_{\mathfrak p}\). Consequently the connection preserves every localization and their intersection. The three inclusions are injective maps of left \(A\)-modules. Therefore \(Pv=0\) in one if and only if it is zero in all; intersection with any specified subset of the same polynomial source preserves that equality. No operator coefficient has been localized. In the graded case the natural double dual and its injection are graded, and the induced connection remains of degree one. This also follows by taking homogeneous components of the injection into \(M\). \(\square\)

The abstract lemma needs neither characteristic zero nor generic cyclicity. Its application to the cube's ordinary differential-operator dictionary retains characteristic zero because that dictionary uses factorial division. It is a standard reflexive-hull argument composed with the polynomial connection presentation, not a new general freeness theorem. Unlike generic-orbit localization, it changes only the target of the kernel map.

The actual nonreflexive control and its doubled residual locus

Proposition (prop:cube-three-cyclic-hull). For \(n=3,d=2\) over \(\mathbb Q\), put \(B=\mathbb Q[e_1,e_2,e_3]\), \(\deg e_j=j\), and \[h=e_1^2-4e_2,\qquad f=e_1h+8e_3,\qquad I=(f,h^2).\] The actual cyclic image \(N=\mathscr A_Bv\) has graded module structure \[N\cong\bigoplus_{c=0}^6B(-c)\oplus I(-4),\qquad N^{**}\cong\bigoplus_{c=0}^6B(-c)\oplus B(-4),\qquad N^{**}/N\cong(B/I)(-4).\] In particular \(B/I\cong\mathbb Q[e_1,h]/(h^2)\), and the generic transverse length of this residual defect is two at \((e_3,h)\). The free hull embeds polynomially in the original rank-eight connection. Its basis weights are \((0,1,2,3,4,5,6,4)\), its distinguished vector is the first unit vector, and its connection matrix is polynomial. All claims extend by scalar extension to every characteristic-zero field.

Proof with exact certificate. The retained full cyclic presentation is \[0\longrightarrow B(-11)\xrightarrow{G}\bigoplus_{c=0}^8B(-c)\xrightarrow{\Phi}N\longrightarrow0.\] Its completeness uses the known monic order-nine operator; it is not inferred merely from \(\Phi G=0\). The last coordinates satisfy \[G_8=4096f,\qquad G_7=256h^2+6656e_1f.\] The complete coefficient lift in the exact output verifies that every coordinate of \(G\) belongs to \(I\). The two displayed coordinates imply the opposite ideal inclusion, so \(I(G)=I\). Dividing the last row by 4096 and replacing the next row by \(G_7/256-13e_1G_8/2048\) gives \(f,h^2\). Subtracting the retained coefficient lifts from rows zero through six gives a graded unimodular matrix \(T\) with \[TG=(0,\ldots,0,h^2,f)^t.\] Its diagonal is \((1,\ldots,1,1/256,1/4096)\); the full matrix is retained. The common factor of \(f,h^2\) is one, since \(f\) is linear in \(e_3\) with unit coefficient and \(h\) is independent of \(e_3\). Hence the map from the last two summands to \(I(-4)\), \((x,y)\mapsto fx-h^2y\), has kernel generated by \((h^2,f)\). The shifts agree because these two summands have generator degrees seven and eight. The other seven coordinates are free. This proves the first isomorphism.

The ideal \(I\) has height two: eliminate \(e_3\) using \(f\) and then \(e_2\) using \(h=e_1^2-4e_2\) to obtain the stated quotient. Therefore \(I_{\mathfrak p}=B_{\mathfrak p}\) at every height-one prime and \(I^{**}=B\). The remaining isomorphisms follow. At the generic point of \((e_3,h)\), the quotient is \(\mathbb Q(e_1)[h]/(h^2)\), of length two. This identifies the whole residual ideal, strengthening the earlier support-only calculation.

The embedded frame and connection. Set \(\Phi'=\Phi T^{-1}\). Its first seven columns remain \(\Phi_0,\ldots,\Phi_6\). The exact polynomial identities are \[\Phi'_7=f\eta,\qquad\Phi'_8=-h^2\eta,\qquad L=(\Phi_0,\ldots,\Phi_6,\eta),\qquad\det L=-2^{-35}e_3^4\operatorname{Disc}_3.\] Here \(\eta\) is polynomial, as verified by exact division and multiplication back; the full frame is in the output. Thus \(L\) is injective. Its free image contains \(N\), with quotient \((B/I)(-4)\), and agrees with \(N\) at every height-one prime. Since a free module is reflexive, the height-one formula identifies its image with the actual embedded \(N^{**}\).

Write \(C\) for the original connection matrix and \(\widetilde C\) for the matrix in this frame. The required identity, including its covariance term, is \[L\widetilde C=\delta(L)+CL,\qquad \delta(e_1,e_2,e_3)=(2e_2-e_1^2,3e_3-e_1e_2,-e_1e_3).\] The first six columns of \(\widetilde C\) have only \(\widetilde C_{j+1,j}=j+1\) for \(0\le j\le5\). Rows zero and one of its last two columns vanish. Rows two through seven of those columns are \[ \begin{pmatrix} 7e_1^2e_3/1024-63e_2e_3/256&-7e_3/16\\ 7e_1^2e_2/512-63e_2^2/128-273e_1e_3/256&-7e_2/8\\ -77e_1^3/128-63e_3/8&77e_1/2\\ -77e_1^2/32-21e_2/4&112\\ -35e_1/4&0\\ 7f/256&-7e_1/4 \end{pmatrix}. \] With \(\widetilde v=(1,0,\ldots,0)^t\), the frame satisfies \(L\widetilde v=v\). Each entry has the required degree \(1+w_j-w_i\). The covariance identity and injectivity prove equality of annihilators for all orders; the finite iterate audit is a control, not a substitute for that proof. Also \[\delta f=-\tfrac52e_1f-\tfrac12h^2,\qquad\delta(h^2)=-e_1h^2-3hf.\] These identities show explicitly how the residual ideal is preserved. The free ambient module has not made the vector polynomially cyclic: the image still has exactly the quotient above. \(\square\)
