27 September 2026 — Boundary columns determine the cyclic hull; perfection decides its freeness

Working all-degree reduction in dimension four and a general perfection criterion. Exact rational control: the degree-two cyclic hull is free with twelve explicitly determined graded shifts. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and outcome. Open statement 3 needs a uniform graded annihilator law. The ambient lemma preserves that problem in the cyclic hull, but supplies no freeness theorem. This cycle tests whether a free frame remains possible in the first unresolved dimension. Direct double duals timed out. Re-reading the stronger clause of the boundary theorem gives an all-degree reduction to a single relation. A standard homological criterion then replaces double dualization by a scalar ideal's perfection. The exact dimension-four degree-two ideal is perfect, so its hull is free. The model survives this test; a uniform ideal presentation and the filtered annihilator calculation remain missing.

An all-degree boundary presentation of the hull

Lemma (lem:cube-boundary-cyclic-hull). In dimension four, over any characteristic-zero field, let \(d\ge2\), \(r=8d-4\), and let \(M_d\) be the symmetric polynomial connection over \(B=F[e_1,e_2,e_3,e_4]\). Let \(N_d=\mathscr A_Bv_d\) be its full cyclic image and let \(L_d\) be the \(B\)-span of its divided iterates of orders \(0,\ldots,r\). Then, as submodules of \((M_d)_K\), \[L_d^{**}=N_d^{**}.\] If \(G=(G_0,\ldots,G_r)^t\) is the primitive generator of the boundary kernel, \(\lambda=10d^2-10d-5\), and \(t=r+\lambda\), then \[0\longrightarrow B(-t)\xrightarrow{G}\bigoplus_{c=0}^{r}B(-c)\longrightarrow L_d\longrightarrow0.\] Consequently \(N_d^{**}\) is the double dual of this one-relation cokernel. The boundary-column map identifies the abstract hull with the embedded one; the connection extends there by the ambient lemma. Neither \(L_d=N_d\) nor freeness is asserted.

Proof. The boundary law states that the gcd of the boundary maximal minors has no noncollision prime factor. This is an explicit part of that theorem, stronger than its numerical threshold. The all-truncation Smith theorem states that, at every collision DVR in root parameters, all truncations through order at least \(r-1\) have the same cokernel length. Nested full-rank lattices of the same finite colength over a DVR are equal. Hence the boundary-column image and the full cyclic image coincide at every root collision DVR. Away from collisions, the absence of another gcd factor says that the boundary matrix is onto at every height-one prime, so equality holds there too.

The changes between raw characters and connection columns use unit factorial row and column factors. The polynomial companion frame is injective and fixed independently of the truncation. Its determinant valuation is subtracted from both cokernel lengths, as in the cyclic divisor calculation, so the equalities transfer to the companion images. Descent from the root ring to \(B\) is faithfully flat. More explicitly, over a height-one prime of \(B\), localize at a root prime above it; the ramification index multiplies both lengths by the same positive integer (two at the generic discriminant and one at \(e_4=0\)). Thus equality upstairs implies equality of the original lengths. There is no division of the operator coefficients. We have \((L_d)_{\mathfrak p}=(N_d)_{\mathfrak p}\) at every height-one prime of \(B\). The normal-domain intersection formula proves equality of their hulls.

The boundary matrix has rank \(r\), so its kernel has generic rank one. Divide its maximal-minor vector by its coordinate gcd to obtain primitive \(G\). Over a polynomial UFD, a rational multiple of a primitive polynomial vector is polynomial only when the multiplier is polynomial; check each irreducible denominator against a coordinate not divisible by it. Hence the entire kernel is \(BG\). The top coordinate has degree \(\lambda\), so the column has total degree \(t=r+\lambda\). This proves the graded presentation and the last assertion. \(\square\)

Keeping the column of order \(r\) matters: the square prefix through \(r-1\) has a determinant with the noncollision ramification factor. Equality of collision lengths alone would not justify replacing that square prefix by the full cyclic hull. The conclusion is currently all-degree in dimension four, not all-dimensional: the corresponding absence of extra noncollision gcd factors is still open in higher dimensions.

A scalar ideal tests freeness

Lemma (lem:primitive-column-hull-perfection). Let \(B\) be a positively weighted polynomial ring over a field, \(F_0\) a finite graded free module, and \(B(-t)\xrightarrow{G}F_0\) a nonzero homogeneous primitive column. Put \(L=\operatorname{coker}G\) and \(I=(G_i)\). If \(I\ne B\), then \[L^{**}\text{ is graded free}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \operatorname{pd}_B I\le1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \operatorname{pd}_B(B/I)=2,\] that is, \(I\) is perfect of height two. If \(I=B\), the hull is graded free. A certified nonzero third Betti number of \(B/I\) therefore refutes free-hull reconstruction.

Proof. Primitivity makes \(BG\) saturated in \(F_0\), by the same irreducible-denominator argument, so \(L\) is torsion-free. Dualizing the presentation gives \[0\longrightarrow L^*\longrightarrow F_0^*\longrightarrow I(t)\longrightarrow0.\] A dual over this normal ring is reflexive: identify it with the generic functionals integral on the module, and use \(B=\bigcap_{\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak p=1}B_{\mathfrak p}\). In particular \(L^*=(L^{**})^*\). Thus \(L^{**}\) is graded free if and only if \(L^*\) is graded free. The displayed sequence gives the forward implication to \(\operatorname{pd}I\le1\). Conversely, if \(I\) has projective dimension at most one, its kernel in any surjection from a projective module is projective, by comparison with a length-one projective resolution. Hence \(L^*\) is graded projective and graded free. For the last implication one can lift a homogeneous basis modulo the positive-degree maximal ideal: graded Nakayama gives a surjection from the corresponding graded free module, projectivity splits it, and the kernel has zero reduction modulo that ideal, so is zero.

If \(I\) is proper, primitivity excludes every height-one prime containing it, so \(\operatorname{ht}I\ge2\). The sequence \(0\to I\to B\to B/I\to0\) now identifies \(\operatorname{pd}I\le1\) with \(\operatorname{pd}(B/I)=2\): projective dimension zero or one for \(B/I\) is excluded by its height. Over the regular polynomial ring this is exactly the perfect height-two condition, by the depth/projective-dimension formula. If \(I=B\), the dual sequence splits and the same graded-projective argument applies. \(\square\)

Applied to the preceding boundary presentation, the lemma makes freeness of the dimension-four cyclic hull equivalent to perfection of the ideal generated by all coordinates of the primitive boundary relation. This is not the previously studied first-step threshold ideal, which consists of highest coefficients of later relations. The two ideals have different degrees even in the control below.

The degree-two hull is free

Proposition (prop:cube-four-degree-two-free-hull). For \(n=4,d=2\) in characteristic zero, the boundary-coordinate ideal \(I=(G_0,\ldots,G_{12})\subset B\) has minimal resolution \[0\longrightarrow B(-21)\oplus B(-22)\oplus B(-23)\longrightarrow B(-15)\oplus B(-16)\oplus B(-17)\oplus B(-18)\longrightarrow B\longrightarrow B/I\longrightarrow0.\] The actual cyclic hull is therefore graded free of rank twelve, with basis weights \[(0,1,2,3,4,4,5,5,6,6,7,8).\] This proves neither freeness in other degrees nor a new threshold value. The connection and distinguished vector in any chosen homogeneous hull basis still determine the exact polynomial annihilator.

Exact certificate and proof. The complete output retains the boundary vector, four minimal generators, and both matrices in the displayed resolution. The script extracts the unique vector supported in orders at most twelve from the already certified full bounded kernel. It verifies primitivity, constructs the ideal, checks its equality with the four-generator ideal, and verifies homogeneity, positive entry degrees, zero composition, and equality of the four maximal minors of the \(4\times3\) second matrix with \(I\). These are rational polynomial identities, not evaluations at parameter points.

Here is why the minor check independently proves exactness, rather than relying only on the resolution routine. Write the row of four generators as \(a\), the second matrix as \(S\), and \(Z=\ker(a:B^4\to B)\), with their displayed shifts understood. The minor ideal equals \(I\), which has gcd one because \(G\) is primitive. Thus \(S\) has generic rank three and, at every height-one prime, a unit maximal minor. Since \(aS=0\) and the row \(a\) is also unimodular there, \(\operatorname{im}S=Z\) at every such prime. The free image of the injective \(S\) is reflexive. The kernel \(Z\) is reflexive as well: a generic vector in all its height-one localizations belongs to \(B^4\) and satisfies \(az=0\). Taking intersections proves equality globally. This is the Hilbert–Burch argument in the present normal polynomial setting. Positive degrees of every nonzero differential entry establish minimality. The two lemmas then identify the actual full cyclic hull as free.

For the shifts, \(r=12,t=27\) and \(F_0^*=\bigoplus_{c=0}^{12}B(c)\). The dual sequence and the ideal resolution give the Laurent Hilbert numerator of \(L^*\): \[\sum_{c=0}^{12}z^{-c}-(z^{-12}+z^{-11}+z^{-10}+z^{-9})+(z^{-6}+z^{-5}+z^{-4}) =\sum_{c=0}^{8}z^{-c}+z^{-6}+z^{-5}+z^{-4}.\] Since the module is graded free, this determines its generator degrees. Dualizing gives the displayed hull weights. Their sum is 51, consistent with the original ambient weight sum 19 plus the known determinant-divisor weight \(4\cdot5+12=32\); this last agreement is a control, not a freeness argument. Flat field extension carries the exact certificate to every characteristic-zero field. \(\square\)

Control, scale and failures. The nontrivial encoding control is \(n=3,d=2\): its nine-coordinate primitive vector gives the previously proved ideal \((e_1^3-4e_1e_2+8e_3,(e_1^2-4e_2)^2)\), with generator degrees three and four, relation degree seven, and hull weights \((0,1,2,3,4,4,5,6)\). For the new case only one thirteen-coordinate vector, four scalar generators and a \(4\times3\) matrix are needed. Any nonzero higher minimal relation would reject the proposed free-hull mechanism at its first target; it was not found. Direct double dualization from the full nineteen-generator module timed out after 120 seconds; minimizing the stored 118-vector Gröbner presentation and dualizing the rebuilt \(19\times17\) relation matrix each also timed out after 120 seconds. All three passed their solved control and stopped without a dimension-four answer. The boundary reduction's generator minimization and resolution took about 0.0164 CPU seconds in the accepted run. The subsequent maximal-minor checks certify the answer. The failed runs are computation failures, not counterexamples.

General statement. lem:cube-boundary-cyclic-hull holds for every \(d\ge2\) in dimension four and characteristic zero; lem:primitive-column-hull-perfection holds for every nonzero homogeneous primitive column over a positively weighted polynomial ring. Together they replace the uniform free-hull question by perfection of one specific boundary-coordinate ideal. The exact control prop:cube-four-degree-two-free-hull passes that test at degree two. Neither the uniform perfection assertion nor the source kernel's first degree follows from that control.

The medium-reasoning pre-proof reviewer approved the boundary reduction with its characteristic and dimension restrictions, and the general criterion after removing the redundant torsion-free assumption. A fresh-context medium-reasoning correctness reviewer read the proofs, exact dependency excerpts, script and complete retained output without rerunning. It found no gap or unused substantive hypothesis; it confirmed the height-one comparison, the projective-dimension equivalence, independent maximal-minor exactness and every recorded shift.

Assessment and next step. The canonical cyclic hull is a viable free ambient model at the first unresolved degree, and an all-degree reduction now makes its freeness a concrete perfection question. The goal still needs uniform graded relations and their highest-order coefficient; freeness alone is not sufficient. Next use the boundary ideal's small resolution to construct an embedded homogeneous frame and its connection in the solved target, then identify which identities in that construction would extend with \(d\). 27 September 2026 — The free hull has a polynomial connection, but boundary derivatives do not generate its coefficient ideal

Working constructive hull lemma and all-degree subleading boundary identity. Exact dimension-four degree-two frame; the derivative-generated boundary-ideal shortcut is refuted. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and outcome. Open statement 3 requires the first degree of a relation with its marked top coefficient. The last cycle proved that boundary columns determine the cyclic hull in every dimension-four degree, and that the degree-two hull is free. Here the small resolution produces the actual embedded frame and polynomial connection, so the change of ambient module is concrete. The proposed simplification of the boundary-coordinate ideal to derivatives of its top equation fails at the second derivative. A general trace identity does recover the next-to-top coefficient, but it does not recover the remaining ideal. The original graded annihilator remains the endpoint.

Constructing the embedded hull from a small resolution

Constructive lemma (lem:hilbert-burch-ambient-frame). Work over a positively weighted polynomial ring \(B\). Suppose a homogeneous map \(\Phi:F_0\to M\), with \(F_0\) finite graded free and \(M\) finite reflexive, has kernel the nonzero column \(BG\). Choose some coordinates \(H\) of \(G\) that generate \(I=(G_i)\), and assume this proper ideal is perfect of height two. Let a graded unimodular change \(T\) subtract polynomial combinations of \(H\) from the other coordinates, so that \(TG=(0,H)^t\). Write \(F_0=F_{\rm free}\oplus F_H\) in these coordinates. If \[H:B(-t)\to F_H,\qquad S:U\to F_H^*,\qquad H^tS=0\] is its Hilbert–Burch resolution after the appropriate shift, then \[(\operatorname{im}\Phi)^{**}\cong F_{\rm free}\oplus U^*.\] Its polynomial embedding into \(M\) is \(L=(\Phi'_{\rm free},E)\), where \(\Phi'=\Phi T^{-1}\) and \(E\) is the unique generic solution of \[ES^t=\Phi'_H.\] In particular that solution has polynomial entries when \(M\) is free. When \(M\) is free with connection matrix \(C\) and the embedded hull is connection-stable, its connection in this basis satisfies \(L\widetilde C=\delta L+CL\), with polynomial \(\widetilde C\). The original source coefficients and distinguished vector must be retained.

Proof. The relation ideal hypothesis permits the elementary graded row operations defining \(T\). Since \(I\) has height two, \(H\) is primitive. This implies that the kernel of \(S^t:F_H\to U^*\) is precisely \(BH\): over the fraction field it has rank one and contains \(H\), and irreducible-denominator cancellation makes the multiplier polynomial. The maximal minors of \(S\) generate \(I\), whose height is two, so \(S^t\) is onto at every height-one prime. Thus the induced injection \(\operatorname{coker}H\to U^*\) becomes an isomorphism there. Taking reflexive hulls proves the displayed isomorphism, including the unchanged free summands.

The boundary embedding into \(M\) extends uniquely over that hull: a generic vector in the hull maps into every \(M_{\mathfrak p}\), and their intersection is \(M\). This proves existence of \(E\) over \(B\) and its uniqueness, since \(S^t\) is generically onto. It also proves injectivity of \(L\). When the hull is connection-stable, express its derivative in its free basis; the coordinates are polynomial and the Leibniz rule gives the covariance equation. Stability is an explicit hypothesis for this final assertion; in the cube application it follows from the identification with the full cyclic hull and the ambient lemma. \(\square\)

This is the constructive consequence of the perfection criterion, not an independent general freeness theorem. A selected coordinate set must actually generate the ideal; similar degrees alone do not prove that hypothesis.

What the boundary equation does determine in every degree

Lemma (lem:cube-four-subleading-boundary). In dimension four, characteristic zero and every \(d\ge2\), set \(r=8d-4\). Let \(G=(G_0,\ldots,G_r)\) be the primitive relation among the divided iterates \(x_c=\nabla^cv/c!\) in the symmetric companion frame, and put \(F=G_r\). Then \[\boxed{rG_{r-1}=-\delta F+(8d^2-10d+6)e_1F.}\] Consequently \((G_r,G_{r-1})=(F,\delta F)\). A constant rescaling of the primitive vector preserves the identity.

Proof. Put \(X=(x_0,\ldots,x_{r-1})\), \(q=\det X\), and write \(C\) for the original connection matrix. The boundary and collision theorems give, in this same frame, \[q=cgF,\qquad g=e_4^{d^2+(d-1)^2}\operatorname{Disc}(p)^{(d-1)^2},\qquad c\in\mathbf{k}^\times.\] Here \(\mathbf{k}\) is the ground field. The factorization follows by dividing the maximal-minor vector by its gcd, whose full divisor is the displayed collision factor. The noncollision-gcd clause is essential.

The identities \(\nabla x_c=(c+1)x_{c+1}\) show that all diagonal entries of \(X^{-1}(\delta X+CX)\) vanish except its last one. The relation gives that entry as \(-rG_{r-1}/F\). Taking the trace yields the usual Abel determinant identity \[-\frac{rG_{r-1}}F=\frac{\delta q}{q}+\operatorname{tr}C.\] The logarithmic derivatives are \(\delta e_4/e_4=-e_1\) and \(\delta\operatorname{Disc}/\operatorname{Disc}=-6e_1\). For the latter, use the squared root Vandermonde: each factor \(a_i-a_j\) has logarithmic derivative \(-(a_i+a_j)\), and each root occurs in three pairs. Hence \[\frac{\delta g}{g}=-(8d^2-14d+7)e_1.\]

The companion block on subset size \(s\) has trace \(\binom3{s-1}(s-7/2)e_1\): additive exterior powers multiply the original trace by \(\binom3{s-1}\), \(\operatorname{tr}B_0=-3e_1\), and \(\operatorname{tr}Z=e_1\). There are \(k_s=\max(0,\lfloor(d-s)/2\rfloor+1)\) jet copies and the nilpotent jet term has zero trace. For \(d=2u\), \((k_1,k_2,k_3,k_4)=(u,u,u-1,u-1)\); for \(d=2u+1\), it is \((u+1,u,u,u-1)\). Multiplying these by \((-5/2,-9/2,-3/2,1/2)\) gives \(-(4d-1)\) in both cases. Thus \[\operatorname{tr}C=-(4d-1)e_1.\] Substituting \(q=cgF\) into the trace identity gives the boxed formula. Characteristic zero makes \(r\) invertible, proving the ideal equality. \(\square\)

The Abel identity is standard; the new content here is its explicit composition with the recorded companion trace and collision factor, retaining the divided-iterate normalization. It determines only the first two boundary coefficients.

The actual degree-two embedded frame

Proposition (prop:cube-four-hull-connection). For \(n=4,d=2\) over every characteristic-zero field, there is an explicitly certified polynomial frame \(L\) for the actual cyclic hull in the original rank-twelve module, with ordered basis weights \[(0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,6,5,4),\qquad \det L=c\,e_4^5\operatorname{Disc}(p),\quad c\ne0.\] Its first nine columns are the original divided iterates of orders zero through eight; its distinguished vector is \((1,0,\ldots,0)^t\). Its polynomial connection \(\widetilde C\) satisfies the covariance equation above and has entry degrees \(1+w_j-w_i\). Thus it retains the exact annihilator and all original order/excess restrictions.

Construction and certificate. The script reads the full retained boundary vector and verifies \((G_9,G_{10},G_{11},G_{12})=(G_i)\). It records the coefficient lift for the other nine coordinates, the graded unimodular transform \(T\), and a \(4\times3\) syzygy matrix \(S\). It checks \(H^tS=0\) and equality of its maximal-minor ideal with \((G_i)\). The preceding constructive lemma therefore applies. With \(\Phi\) the independently rebuilt twelve-by-thirteen coefficient matrix, exact polynomial division solves \(ES^t=(\Phi T^{-1})_H\); multiplication back verifies it. The resulting frame is \((\Phi_0,\ldots,\Phi_8,E)\). Its determinant is the displayed collision factor times the retained nonzero rational constant.

The complete output gives \(T,S,L,\widetilde C\) and that constant. Every connection entry and frame entry has its required weight. The first eight columns of \(\widetilde C\) have just \(\widetilde C_{j+1,j}=j+1\), \(0\le j\le7\); the four remaining columns are retained in full. Exact covariance proves compatibility at every order. Independently rebuilding the exterior square-root columns verifies all 168 scalar divided-iterate identities through order thirteen. The check \(\delta L\ne0\) rules out dropping the covariance term. This control tests a twelve-by-twelve frame and a twelve-by-three polynomial extension, not another threshold row. The embedded-hull proof, not the finite iterate list alone, gives the all-order annihilator conclusion. \(\square\)

The next derivative leaves the ideal

Obstruction (obs:cube-boundary-derivative-ideal). For the same actual \(n=4,d=2\) boundary vector, set \(I=(G_i)\) and \(F=G_{12}\). Then \[F,\delta F\in I,\qquad \delta^2F\notin I.\] Thus \(I\) is not a differential ideal. In particular it is neither \((F,\delta F,\delta^2F,\delta^3F)\) nor the ideal generated by all derivatives of \(F\). This refutes the proposed derivative-only presentation, not the free-hull construction.

Exact proof. The all-degree identity specializes to \(12G_{11}=-\delta F+18e_1F\), which the script checks exactly. Polynomial ideal membership gives the list \((\text{true},\text{true},\text{false},\text{false})\) for derivatives zero through three. The complete nonzero remainder of \(\delta^2F\) modulo the Gröbner basis of \(I\) is retained; for example its coefficient of \(e_1^8e_2^3e_3\) is \(20242759680\ne0\). All its terms have weight seventeen, as required. Gröbner reduction is over \(\mathbb Q[e_1,e_2,e_3,e_4]\); faithful scalar extension preserves nonmembership in every characteristic-zero field. Since \(\delta F\in I\) but its derivative is outside \(I\), differential stability fails. Any derivative-generated ideal containing the second derivative therefore cannot equal \(I\). \(\square\)

This is the coordinate ideal of the boundary relation. The boundary-column image need not be stable under the connection, even though its hull equals the stable full cyclic hull. There is consequently no conflict with the ambient-hull lemma. In the three-dimensional control the residual ideal happened to be differential; that property cannot be imported into dimension four.

General statement. lem:hilbert-burch-ambient-frame constructs a faithful embedded hull whenever its explicit perfection and coordinate-generation hypotheses hold. lem:cube-four-subleading-boundary holds for every dimension-four degree \(d\ge2\) in characteristic zero. The exact frame is one control, and obs:cube-boundary-derivative-ideal falsifies a proposed uniform simplification at that control. The uniform perfection and filtered-annihilator laws remain open.

Verification gate. Re-read the boundary hull/perfection result, the original companion connection and covariance, the collision divisor and the boundary factorization. The medium-reasoning pre-proof reviewer checked the constructive extension and the Abel signs, trace and normalization. The complete frame/derivative audit passed. A fresh-context medium-reasoning correctness reviewer read the full proofs, dependencies, script and complete retained output without rerunning. It found no substantive gap; the statement now explicitly makes the source finite graded free and derives primitivity from the height-two hypothesis. It confirmed the all-degree trace calculation, embedded covariance and exact nonmembership scope.

Assessment and next step. The free ambient model is now explicit and exact in the first unresolved case, and its first two boundary coefficients are controlled in all degrees. The derivative-only ideal description fails, so extending that shortcut is not the next step. The next cycle is a route review centered on the missing uniform degree implication: compare the boundary-coordinate resolution with the first-step threshold resolution through the marked next-jet map, and test a mechanism that relates them while retaining the connection. Review the outstanding geometric and graded-cohomology leads against this concrete pair of ideals. No additional threshold sweep is justified by the current evidence.

Process. The small boundary resolution produced the full polynomial frame in one bounded run; testing the derivative hypothesis alongside it exposed a failed simplification before further refinement. No framework change was needed.

27 September 2026 — The first-step ideal is a marked Ext annihilator and a low-degree polar residual

Route review. Working intrinsic Ext description and all-degree polar-colon formula. Exact degree-two collision and polar decompositions; the uniform initial degree remains open. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

The line's general claim. Determine the odd-field cube's per-order function in every dimension by evaluating the remaining graded threshold ideals. The dimension-four characteristic-zero boundary is proved in every degree, but its first post-boundary initial degree is not. The last five cycles produced exact jet maps, collision divisors, reflexive hulls and one free hull connection. These models preserve the problem; they have not yet supplied the uniform threshold formula. This review asks which of their properties the goal actually needs and tests the next-jet map on the two different ideals now available.

Obstacle

For every \(d\ge2\), put \(r=8d-4\) and \(\lambda=10d^2-10d-5\). The immediate obligation is the least degree of a nonzero element of \(T_d=I^{(d+1)}_{r+1}\), with matching vanishing below it and a witness at it. A free ambient hull is a convenience, not this endpoint. In fact the marked quotient below does not require its freeness or perfection of the boundary-coordinate ideal. The new scalar formula reduces the question to the graded maps from \(B_\ell\) to the degree-\(\ell+\lambda+2\) part of the actual complete intersection, multiplying by one specified form. Their first nonzero kernel degree remains to be determined uniformly; \(F\) supplies the endpoint \(\lambda\) if none occurs earlier. Other orders, higher dimensions and small-prime stable orders remain separate open obligations.

The intrinsic defect and the marked next column

Lemma (lem:primitive-column-ext-defect). Let \(B\) be a positively graded polynomial ring over a field, \(F_0\) a finite graded free module, and \(B(-t)\xrightarrow{G}F_0\) a nonzero homogeneous primitive column. Suppose \(I=(G_i)\) is proper, and put \(L=\operatorname{coker}G\). There is a natural exact sequence \[0\longrightarrow L\longrightarrow L^{**}\longrightarrow \operatorname{Ext}^2_B(B/I,B)(-t)\longrightarrow0.\] No perfection assumption on \(I\) is needed.

In the dimension-four characteristic-zero cube, for every \(d\ge2\), take the boundary column image \(L_d\), \(t=r+\lambda\), and \(H_d=L_d^{**}=N_d^{**}\). The next divided iterate \(x_{r+1}\) belongs to \(H_d\). If \(w_d\) is its class in \[E_d=\operatorname{Ext}^2_B(B/I,B)(-t),\] then the exact first-step threshold ideal is \[\boxed{T_d=\operatorname{Ann}_B(w_d).}\] The marked class has degree \(r+1\) in \(E_d\), or degree \(1-\lambda\) in the unshifted Ext module. Annihilating the whole module is a different condition.

Proof. Primitivity implies that \(L\) is torsion-free and that \(I\) is contained in no height-one prime. Identifying a homomorphism \(I\to B\) with multiplication by an element of the fraction field, integrality at every height-one prime gives \(I^*=B\). Dualize the defining presentation to obtain \[0\longrightarrow L^*\longrightarrow F_0^*\longrightarrow I(t)\longrightarrow0.\] Dualizing this sequence gives \[0\longrightarrow B(-t)\xrightarrow{G}F_0\longrightarrow L^{**}\longrightarrow\operatorname{Ext}^1_B(I(t),B)\longrightarrow0.\] The first map is the original column under evaluation, and the middle map induces the natural injection \(L\to L^{**}\). The sequence \(0\to I\to B\to B/I\to0\) identifies its final term with \(\operatorname{Ext}^2_B(B/I,B)(-t)\), proving the claim.

For the cube, the all-degree boundary hull lemma puts the next iterate in \(H_d\). A polynomial \(b\) annihilates its quotient class exactly when \(bx_{r+1}\) is a polynomial combination of \(x_0,\ldots,x_r\). Moving that combination to the other side is precisely a relation with highest coefficient \(b\). No coefficient localization or change of order is involved. Since \(x_c\) has degree \(c\), subtracting the shift \(t=r+\lambda\) gives the asserted degree. \(\square\)

Scope and earlier implication. The older scalar lemma already expresses the full first-step ideal as an annihilator in an auxiliary complete intersection, in a broader parameter range. The new result is its intrinsic interpretation through the boundary-coordinate ideal and a particular Ext class, not a stronger general threshold theorem. Also \(I\subseteq T_d\) already follows from that older proof: its cross-product divisibility permits \(b=G_j,a=-B_j\) in the congruence criterion. Together with primitivity and the known proper height-two \(T_d\), this proves \(\operatorname{ht}I=2\) in every dimension-four degree. The Ext sequence independently gives the same inclusion. If \(B/I\) is Cohen–Macaulay, its canonical module is the unshifted Ext module further twisted by \(-10\), since the weights of \(B\) sum to ten. The description above is called the Ext defect so that no unproved Cohen–Macaulay or freeness condition is hidden in the terminology.

Only three boundary coefficients are needed

Lemma (lem:cube-first-step-polar-colon). For every \(d\ge2\) in dimension four over a characteristic-zero field, use the primitive divided-iterate boundary vector \(G\), set \(F=G_r\), and define \[Q=r(r-1)G_{r-2}-\delta^2F.\] Then \[\boxed{T_d=(F,\delta F):Q,\qquad\gcd(F,\delta F)=1.}\] Thus \((F,\delta F)\) is a complete intersection of weights \(\lambda,\lambda+1\), and the nonzero multiplier \(Q\) has weight \(\lambda+2\). This replaces the older guaranteed auxiliary weights \(\lambda+r,\lambda+r+1\), without assuming boundary-ideal perfection or higher derivative generation.

Proof of coprimality. The boundary theorem makes \(F\) squarefree and gives it no collision factor. The Wronskian-flow proof also shows that no noncollision irreducible factor \(\pi\) of the determinant is invariant under \(\delta\). To recall its argument, if \(\delta\pi=h\pi\), then along \(a_i(T)=a_i/(1+a_iT)\) the formal solution starting at a collision-free point of \(\pi=0\) remains there. The transport identity makes the corresponding nonzero Wronskian vanish to infinite order at the marked point, a contradiction in characteristic zero. Hence \(\pi\nmid\delta\pi\). Since each factor of \(F\) occurs once, no factor of \(F\) divides \(\delta F\). This argument may be made after extending the field and adjoining the roots; faithful descent gives coprimality over \(B\).

Proof of the colon formula. The Abel identity gives \[rG_{r-1}=-\delta F+a_de_1F,\qquad a_d=8d^2-10d+6.\] Thus \((F,G_{r-1})=(F,\delta F)\), and the two generators are coprime. Let the transported relation be \[Y_c=\frac{\delta G_c+cG_{c-1}}{r+1},\qquad Y_{r+1}=F.\] The old scalar proof works for any polynomial combination \(p\) of the coordinates of \(G\) coprime to \(F\); its higher common degree was an existence bound, not a restriction. Choose \(p=G_{r-1}\) and the corresponding \(q=Y_{r-1}\). For completeness, the known height-two property of \(T_d\) and the congruence criterion imply \[F\mid G_iY_j-G_jY_i\quad\text{for all }i,j.\] Indeed, at each irreducible divisor of \(F\) choose a member of \(T_d\) that is a unit there, and use its relation congruences. This retains the full valuation at that divisor. If \(bq\in(F,p)\), choose \(a\) with \(ap+bq\in(F)\); then \[p(aG_i+bY_i)=G_i(ap+bq)+b(pY_i-qG_i)\in(F).\] Coprimality of \(p,F\) gives all the required congruences, so \(b\in T_d\). The reverse implication is immediate from the same congruences. Therefore \(T_d=(F,p):q\).

Differentiating the Abel identity and reducing modulo \((F,\delta F)\) gives \[q=\frac{\delta G_{r-1}+(r-1)G_{r-2}}{r+1} \equiv\frac{r(r-1)G_{r-2}-\delta^2F}{r(r+1)}.\] The denominator is a nonzero field scalar. This proves the boxed formula. Homogeneity gives the three weights; \(Q\) cannot be zero, because that would make the colon the unit ideal, contrary to the proved properness of \(T_d\). \(\square\)

This is an explicit refinement of the old scalar presentation. The second derivative is corrected by the third boundary coefficient; the failed derivative-only ideal is not being reinstated. Put \(A=(F,\delta F)\). The exact graded maps are \(\nu_\ell:B_\ell\to(B/A)_{\ell+\lambda+2}\), \(b\mapsto bQ\); their kernels are \((T_d)_\ell\). If instead the source is \(B/A\), the kernel is \(T_d/A\), so \(\alpha(T_d)=\min\{\lambda,\alpha(T_d/A)\}\), with \(\alpha(0)=\infty\). Below \(\lambda\) the two source spaces coincide, and \(F\) supplies the endpoint if no earlier kernel appears. Replacing the specified multiplier by a generic form would change the problem.

Two different exact decompositions at degree two

Proposition (prop:cube-degree-two-polar-decomposition). For \(n=4,d=2\) in characteristic zero, let \(I=(G_0,\ldots,G_{12})\), let \(T=I^{(3)}_{13}\), and put \(q=e_4\operatorname{Disc}_4\). The exact polynomial identities are \[T=I:q^\infty,\qquad J=I:T,\qquad I=T\cap J,\qquad J:q^\infty=B.\] The residual collision ideal \(J\) has minimal generator weights \(8,9,10\), relation weights \(13,14\), and root-space curve degree 60. Independently, for the polar complete intersection \(A=(F,\delta F)\), \[T=A:Q,\qquad T^\vee=A:T,\qquad A=T\cap T^\vee,\qquad A:T^\vee=T.\] Here \(T^\vee\ne T\), \(Q\in T^\vee\setminus T\), and both linked ideals have generator weights \(12,13,14,15\) and relation weights \(17,18,19\), hence root-space degree 120. No radicality or all-degree decomposition is claimed.

Exact evidence. The Ext and collision certificate constructs the actual next column from the retained hull connection. In the quotient by the boundary columns, eliminating the nine free channels leaves \(\operatorname{coker}S^t\), and the actual last three coordinates give the marked class. Its annihilator is exactly the independently retained first-step ideal. The annihilator of the whole quotient is \(I\), which is strictly smaller. The same script computes and checks the saturation, quotient and intersection identities above; it retains the complete marked vector and ideal generators. The polar certificate checks the lower-degree formula over \(\mathbb Q\), computes the distinct residual link and retains all its generators and resolution matrices. The small independent audit checks each residual Hilbert–Burch matrix by zero composition, primitive generator gcd and equality of maximal-minor ideals. The height-one argument used in the earlier perfection proof then proves exactness; all entries have positive weight, giving minimality. Faithful scalar extension preserves every ideal equality in characteristic zero.

The collision scheme in full. Write \[D=e_1^2e_2^2-4e_2^3-4e_1^3e_3+18e_1e_2e_3-27e_3^2,\] \[A_4=8e_1^4-42e_1^2e_2+36e_2^2+54e_1e_3,\qquad A_5=2e_1^3e_2-8e_1e_2^2-6e_1^2e_3+36e_2e_3.\] A minimal generating set of \(J\) is \[e_2D+e_4A_4-80e_4^2,\quad e_3D+e_4A_5-8e_1e_4^2,\quad e_4D+(-5e_1^2+16e_2)e_4^2.\] Put \[J_0=(e_4^2,e_2D+e_4A_4,e_3D+e_4A_5,e_4D),\] \[P_1=(e_1^3-4e_1e_2+8e_3,(e_1^2-4e_2)^2-64e_4).\] The exact audit gives \(J=J_0\cap P_1\), \(J_0=J:(e_1^3-4e_1e_2+8e_3)^\infty\), and \(P_1=J:e_4^\infty\).

Primaryness and multiplicities. The ideal \(P_1\) is prime: solve linearly for \(e_3\) and \(e_4\), leaving a polynomial ring in \(e_1,e_2\). It parametrizes quartics that are squares of quadratics. For \(P_0=(e_4,D)\), irreducibility of the cubic discriminant gives a height-two prime, describing one zero root and a repeated nonzero root. The audit checks \(J_0\subseteq P_0\), \(e_4^2,D^4\in J_0\), so \(\sqrt{J_0}=P_0\). The Hilbert–Burch resolution makes \(B/J\) unmixed of height two. Saturation cannot introduce associated primes, so \(J_0\) is \(P_0\)-primary.

The identity \(e_2A_5-e_3A_4=2e_1D\) shows that, after inverting \(e_2\), \[J_0=(e_4^2,e_2D+e_4A_4).\] Since \(e_2\) is a unit at \(P_0\), this is a length-two quotient in the regular local parameters \(e_4,D\). The coefficient-ring local lengths are therefore two at \(P_0\) and one at \(P_1\). After flat extension to the ordinary root ring, the supporting complete intersections have degrees \(4\cdot6=24\) and \(3\cdot4=12\); thus the residual degree is \(2\cdot24+12=60\). These coefficient-ring lengths are not asserted to be the multiplicities of individual root-space components, where the map is ramified. The substitutions with roots \((0,u,u,v)\) and \((u,u,v,v)\) vanish identically, whereas the first residual generator at \((0,0,u,v)\) is \(u^3v^3(u-v)^2\ne0\). This excludes that generic triple-collision family as a component, not its special intersections. \(\square\)

The boundary-coordinate ideal therefore defines the actual first-step determinantal closure plus a precise collision residual in this degree. This is stronger than the previous assertion that the threshold scheme was the closure of its own collision-free part. It still does not identify that scheme with the reduced effectivity locus. The distinct polar residual \(T^\vee\) is a second degree-120 curve, not the degree-60 collision scheme \(J\).

Outside leads

  • Peskine–Szpiro linkage and residual duality. The complete-intersection/canonical-module viewpoint is described in Eisenbud–Ulrich, introduction and Section 1; its stronger duality statements impose depth and local-generation hypotheses. The new polar formula supplies an actual regular sequence and a specified residual multiplier. It does not permit assuming those extra hypotheses uniformly or replacing the multiplier by a general form. Test. Passed: at degree two the polar complete intersection links two distinct ideals with the same minimal shifts, and the corrected multiplier lies in precisely the residual one. Answers. A uniform graded description of that residual linkage would compute the annihilator's first degree; the Ext lemma retains the marked element even before a Cohen–Macaulay theorem is available.
  • Kapranov's configuration compactification. Kapranov's Chow-quotient model organizes collisions of marked points by boundary strata. Here the test concerns the actual extension scheme on the polynomial parameter chart, not just its support or a generic fibre. Test. Passed: the boundary-coordinate ideal splits into the first-step closure and a degree-60 collision residual, whose two pair-collision components have coefficient-ring lengths two and one. A generic triple-collision family is not a component. Answers. Computing these boundary contributions uniformly would separate the desired global ideal from collision terms before a section calculation. The source's compactification does not itself supply our graded multiplicities; those were calculated from the actual ideal.
  • Bernstein–Gelfand–Gelfand and the marked graded complex. The BGG note, Theorem 2 and its proof sketch retains coherent complexes, their grading and cohomological sector. Its ordinary polynomial grading applies after extension to the root ring, not directly by declaring the weighted ring standard graded. The graded Artin basis makes the kernel after extension a direct sum of shifted invariant kernels, with nonnegative shifts and a unique degree-zero basis element. Test. Passed: multiplication by the actual marked Ext class has rational matrices of sizes \(112\times27\) and \(118\times34\) in excesses eleven and twelve, with ranks 27 and 33. The whole Ext module has a different annihilator. Answers. Uniform injectivity below a candidate excess and noninjectivity at it would give exactly the missing threshold. An unmarked module, Hilbert numerator or Euler characteristic cannot replace this complex.

Absurd bridges

  • Feshbach elimination of virtual atomic states. The Feshbach–Schur map, Theorem 1.2, preserves kernels while reconstructing eliminated states when its complementary block is invertible. Translate the nine free hull channels into eliminable states and the three residual channels into the effective system. In our polynomial analogue the complementary block is the identity, so its inverse introduces no parameter denominator: the free equations solve uniquely for their nine coordinates, leaving \(S^tu+bw=0\). Test. Passed: the full twelve-channel quotient and the three-channel effective quotient give exactly the same ideal of allowed marked coefficients \(b\). Answers. A uniform polynomial elimination of this kind could reduce the global-degree calculation to a smaller effective system. A merely rational inverse would recreate the already refuted localization loss; no analytic spectral estimate is being imported.
  • Supersymmetric zero modes with the correct insertion and sector. This develops the repair of the earlier failed index shortcut. Following the positive-Hamiltonian construction in Witten, Sections 1–2, use the actual graded map \(A_\ell:b\mapsto bw\) as a two-term supercharge. Over \(\mathbb C\), the source-sector Hamiltonian is \(A_\ell^*A_\ell\), and \(\langle b,A_\ell^*A_\ell b\rangle=\|A_\ell b\|^2\); its zero states are exactly the desired coefficient relations. Test. Passed: exact rational Gram ranks equal 27 and 33, giving respectively zero and one source-sector zero mode at excesses eleven and twelve. The complete matrices are retained. Answers. A proved uniform positive lower bound below the first allowed degree would give the missing vanishing result. The translation is now faithful, but no such spectral bound has been found; the alternating index still cannot select the required sector.

Thus the renewal cutoff remains useful for the entire row but is unnecessary for this first-step annihilator. Follow-up. 27 September 2026 — Polynomial collision-logarithmic operators cannot recover the polar multiplier

Working logarithmic basis lemma in every odd characteristic. Exact refutation of the proposed weight-two operator formula, at every finite operator order; the uniform threshold remains open. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and stopping test. The goal still requires the first nonzero kernel degree of the specified map \(B_\ell\to(B/(F,\delta F))_{\ell+\lambda+2}\), multiplying by \(Q\). Could the collision geometry simplify that multiplier to a polynomial differential operator applied to \(F\)? The named mechanism predicts \(Q\equiv PF\pmod{(F,\delta F)}\), where \(P\) has weight two and is generated by collision-logarithmic vector fields and polynomial coefficients. A single exact failure on the retained \(n=4,d=2\) object refutes the uniform mechanism. No new dimension, degree or sample is needed. The first-order test fails, and allowing arbitrary finite operator order still fails.

A complete basis and the weight-two operator class

Lemma (lem:collision-logarithmic-operator-basis). Let \(k\) have characteristic different from two, let \(B=k[e_1,\ldots,e_n]\) with \(\deg e_j=j\), and let \(p(z)=\prod_i(z-a_i)\), \(q=e_n\operatorname{Disc}(p)\), with discriminant one when \(n=1\). The root derivations \[D_j=-\sum_{i=1}^n a_i^{j+1}\partial_{a_i},\qquad 0\le j

For \(n\ge3\), let \(\mathcal U\) be the associative algebra of operators on \(B\) generated by multiplication by \(B\) and these logarithmic derivations. For every homogeneous \(f\in B\), the image on \(f\) of its homogeneous weight-two part is exactly \[\mathcal U_2f=B_2f+B_1D_1f+kD_2f+kD_1^2f.\] This permits arbitrary finite differential order. The weight refers to the integer grading, not merely to the eigenvalue of the Euler operator modulo the characteristic.

Proof of the basis. The displayed root derivations commute with permutations, so preserve the symmetric polynomial ring in every characteristic. Each sends \(a_i\) into \((a_i)\), and sends \(a_i-a_l\) into \((a_i-a_l)\), since \(a_i^{j+1}-a_l^{j+1}\) is divisible by \(a_i-a_l\). Consequently \(D_jq/q\) is an invariant polynomial on the root ring and belongs to \(B\). The chain rule gives \[\det(D_j e_i)_{1\le i\le n,\ 0\le j

The polynomial \(q\) is reduced in \(B\). For \(n\ge2\), any factor of the discriminant, after substitution in the root ring, has equal multiplicity on every pair hyperplane by permutation invariance. The only possibilities are zero, one or two. Multiplicity one would give a scalar times the alternating Vandermonde, which is not symmetric in characteristic different from two. Thus the discriminant is irreducible and distinct from \(e_n\). The same argument after an algebraic closure shows geometric reducedness, so its gradient is not identically zero along its generic point. The case \(n=1\) is immediate.

Localize at a height-one prime of \(B\). Away from \(q\), the determinant is a unit and the displayed fields span all derivations. At a prime \((\pi)\) dividing \(q\), reducedness and generic smoothness make the logarithmic condition one independent linear condition modulo \(\pi\). Hence the logarithmic lattice has determinant valuation one inside the free derivation module. The displayed sublattice is contained in it and also has determinant valuation one, so they agree. Finally the logarithmic module is the intersection of these height-one lattices: the conditions are polynomial coefficients and regularity of \(\theta(q)/q\), both detected at height one in the normal ring \(B\). The free span of the \(D_j\) is likewise its height-one intersection. Equality follows globally.

Proof of the operator reduction. Write an operator as a finite sum of words in multiplication and the \(D_j\). Move polynomial coefficients to the left using \([D_j,b]=D_j(b)\). The new coefficient terms have the same total weight. A homogeneous weight-two word therefore has the form \(bD_{i_1}\cdots D_{i_s}\), with \(\deg b+\sum i_t=2\). Now \(D_0=-\sum j e_j\partial_{e_j}\) is minus weighted Euler. Acting on the homogeneous expression to its right, every occurrence of \(D_0\) is a scalar and can be deleted, even when that scalar is zero in the field. The remaining words are only \(1,D_1,D_2,D_1^2\), with coefficient degrees \(2,1,0,0\). Conversely all four indicated terms are allowed operators. This proves equality. The argument is the standard logarithmic determinant criterion made explicit for this collision divisor; no external novelty is claimed. \(\square\)

An exact obstruction for every finite operator order

Refutation (obs:cube-logarithmic-polar-operator). Over every characteristic-zero field, on the retained dimension-four degree-two object, let \(F=G_{12}\), \(\delta=D_1\), \(A=(F,\delta F)\), and \(Q=132G_{10}-\delta^2F\), using the primitive divided-iterate boundary vector and its fixed common normalization. Then \[Q\notin(F,\delta F,D_2F,\delta^2F).\] Consequently no weight-two operator \(P\in\mathcal U\), of any finite order, satisfies \(Q-PF\in A\). This excludes the stated uniform polynomial logarithmic mechanism. It does not exclude rational coefficients, operators outside \(\mathcal U\), or formulas retaining an additional independent boundary coefficient.

Proof and exact certificate. Here \(\deg F=15\), \(\deg\delta F=16\), and \(\deg Q=\deg D_2F=\deg\delta^2F=17\). The only possible homogeneous expression in the asserted ideal is a constant linear combination of \[e_1^2F,\quad e_2F,\quad e_1\delta F,\quad D_2F,\quad\delta^2F.\] The test is therefore one vector against a five-dimensional candidate span inside the 72-dimensional space \(B_{17}\), with a definite falsifying outcome. The derivative used is explicitly \[\begin{aligned} D_2={}&(-e_1^3+3e_1e_2-3e_3)\partial_{e_1} +(-e_1^2e_2+2e_2^2+e_1e_3-4e_4)\partial_{e_2}\\ &+(-e_1^2e_3+2e_2e_3+e_1e_4)\partial_{e_3} +(-e_1^2e_4+2e_2e_4)\partial_{e_4}. \end{aligned}\]

Append \(Q\) as the sixth column of that coefficient matrix. Its six rows indexed by \[e_1^{13}e_4,\ e_1^{11}e_2e_4,\ e_1^{11}e_3^2,\ e_1^{10}e_3e_4,\ e_1^9e_2^2e_4,\ e_1^9e_4^2\] have determinant \[628926517396994672454332957759289874475610696558310368215040\ne0.\] Thus the six forms are linearly independent over \(\mathbb Q\), and remain independent after every characteristic-zero field extension. The complete certificate retains the six-by-six matrix, derivative and both nonzero normal forms; the exact input \(F,\delta F,Q\) is the preceding polar certificate. The script constructs every logarithmic field from Newton sums, verifies its tangency and determinant, checks \(D_0F=-15F\) and \(D_1F=\delta F\), and independently verifies ideal nonmembership by exact Gröbner reduction. The lemma makes this exhaustive in the specified operator class, rather than a selection of candidate formulas. \(\square\)

A stronger ideal shortcut also fails. Let \(I=(G_i)\) be the boundary-coordinate ideal. The exact test finds \(I\ne(D_0F,\ldots,D_3F)\). There is also a structural contradiction using the retained saturation theorem: if they were equal, invert \(q\). The logarithmic fields then span every derivation, so \(\partial_{e_4}F\in I:q^\infty=T_2\). But the retained polynomial has nonzero \(\partial_{e_4}F\) of weight eleven, while the proved first-step initial degree is twelve. This is impossible. This observation and the earlier transport-derivative obstruction concern different proposed generators; neither makes the actual polar-colon formula false.

Scope of the repaired test. The first run ruled out the first-order class \((F,\delta F,D_2F)\). The next run tested the class with \(\delta^2F\) added, which the lemma now shows covers arbitrary finite order at weight two. The identity \(Q+\delta^2F=132G_{10}\) permits exchanging \(Q\) and \(G_{10}\) only while retaining \(\delta^2F\) in that ideal. It does not justify dropping that generator. Both the repaired membership and the separate stronger membership \(G_{10}\in(F,\delta F,D_2F)\) failed. No larger-parameter run follows these refutations.

General statement. lem:collision-logarithmic-operator-basis proves the basis in every dimension and every odd characteristic, and the weight-two operator reduction for every homogeneous polynomial when \(n\ge3\). obs:cube-logarithmic-polar-operator refutes the uniform multiplier mechanism by an exact characteristic-zero counterexample, including arbitrary finite operator order. It supplies no new value of the threshold function. The odd-field all-dimensional goal remains open.

The next cube-odd-characteristic cycle is a route review of the actual polar residual pair, starting from the already proved deformation pairing and Riemann–Roch to identify its two effectivity conditions and precisely which scheme or graded control is still missing. 27 September 2026 — The two polar conditions have different closures: the residual partner carries an extra collision scheme

Route review. Working all-dimensional polar-support interpretation and exact degree-two prefix linkage. An all-degree grading obstruction excludes fixed-size free compression; uniform thresholds remain open. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

The line's general claim. Determine the per-order polynomial multiplicity degree on the odd-field cube in every dimension. Open statement 3 requires the least generator degree of the actual first-step ideal \(T_d=(F,\delta F):Q\) in dimension four before later orders and dimensions. The previous cycle ruled out recovering \(Q\) from polynomial collision-logarithmic operators. This review returns to the actual polar geometry, rather than enlarging that refuted operator class. It identifies both effectivity conditions and tests whether the equal graded shifts of the two retained polar partners reflect equal collision-free geometry. They do not.

Obstacle

The sufficient endpoint is a matching vanishing bound and a nonzero witness for the specified maps \(B_\ell\to(B/(F,\delta F))_{\ell+\lambda+2}\), \(b\mapsto bQ\). A set-theoretic theta description alone cannot provide this. Nor can one infer a symmetry between parameter-space degrees because two divisors on each fibre both have degree \(g-2\). The exact control below shows why: one polar partner contains an additional collision scheme. A uniform graded resolution of the relevant residuals would be sufficient, but its existence, freeness of a hull, and global perfection are stronger conveniences, not prerequisites for the marked multiplication problem.

The two effectivity conditions in every dimension

Lemma (lem:cube-polar-effectivity-union). Let \(k\) be algebraically closed of characteristic different from two, \(n\ge3\), \(d>n-3\), and \[g=1+2^{n-2}(n-3),\qquad N=2^{n-1}d+1-g.\] Assume \(N\ne0\) in \(k\). At collision-free parameters, take the normalized root curve \(C\) with \(w_i^2=1+a_iT\), marked point \(p_0\) given by \(T=0,w_i=1\), and \(H=H_\infty\). Let \(A_m\) be its coefficient matrix through column \(m\), \(\Delta=\det A_{N-1}\), and \(\delta=-\sum a_i^2\partial_{a_i}\). Then the polar locus \(\Delta=\delta\Delta=0\) is, set-theoretically, the union \[\left\{h^0\bigl(dH-(N+1)p_0\bigr)\ge1\right\} \cup \left\{h^0\bigl((n-3-d)H+(N-1)p_0\bigr)\ge1\right\}.\] Both displayed divisor classes have degree \(g-2\). This includes points where the square matrix has corank at least two. For \(n=4\), characteristic zero and every \(d\ge2\), the same statement applies to \((F,\delta F)\), since \(\Delta\) differs from the primitive boundary polynomial by a collision unit.

Proof. The recorded root-curve result gives \(K_C\sim(n-3)H\) and \(V_d=H^0(C,\mathcal O(dH))\) of dimension \(N\). Set \(L=dH-Np_0\), of degree \(g-1\). The coefficient matrix is the Taylor truncation of this complete space, so its left nullity is \(h^0(L)\). Riemann–Roch gives \(h^0(K_C-L)=h^0(L)\). Thus either \(L-p_0\) or \(K_C-L-p_0\) effective implies \(\Delta=0\).

For completeness the earlier dimension-four deformation pairing extends directly to this range. For a basis element \(f=T^s w_S\), with \(D=-\delta\), \[Df=\frac12\left(\sum_{i\in S}a_i\right)f+sT^{s-1}w_S-\partial_Tf.\] The first two terms define a row operator \(R\) on \(V_d\); lowering \(s\) stays in the space. Writing \(b_c\) for the coefficient column, this gives \(Db_c=Rb_c-(c+1)b_{c+1}\) in every characteristic different from two. If \(A=A_{N-1}\) has corank one, choose nonzero left and right null vectors \(\lambda,\mu\), and write \(\operatorname{adj}A=\gamma\mu\lambda^{\mathsf T}\), \(\gamma\ne0\). Pairing the column identity gives \[\delta\Delta=\gamma N(\lambda^{\mathsf T}b_N)\mu_{N-1}.\] The product vanishes exactly when one of the two factors vanishes, since \(N\) is invertible.

The first factor vanishes precisely when the unique section of \(L\) vanishes one additional time, namely \(h^0(L-p_0)\ge1\). The second factor vanishes precisely when the first \(N-1\) columns are dependent. Their rank is then at most \(N-2\), equivalently \(h^0(L+p_0)\ge2\). Since \(\deg(L+p_0)=g\), Riemann–Roch reads \[h^0(L+p_0)=1+h^0(K_C-L-p_0),\] which gives the second effectivity condition. If instead the square matrix has corank at least two, its adjugate is zero and hence both \(\Delta\) and \(\delta\Delta\) vanish. Both \(L\) and \(K_C-L\) have at least two sections, so subtracting one point leaves each effective. This proves the union at every point. Each degree is \(g-2\) by the displayed formula for \(N\). Finally, off collisions \(\Delta=uF\) for a unit \(u\); \(\delta\Delta=u\delta F+F\delta u\) identifies the two polar ideals there. \(\square\)

This is an explicit Riemann–Roch composition of the existing two-factor deformation pairing and rank/effectivity formula, not a new transversality theorem. It neither identifies schemes nor controls the higher-contact locus's dimension. The condition \(N\ne0\) is essential to this argument: when it fails the transport pairing vanishes automatically. The normalized marked coordinates specify the transport field; an arbitrary marked point requires that normalization first. No factorial or bound \(p>N\) is used.

The exact prefix partner and its collision extension

Proposition (prop:cube-polar-prefix-collision-split). In the retained dimension-four degree-two characteristic-zero object, let \(I=(G_0,\ldots,G_{12})\) be the boundary-coordinate ideal, \(T=I^{(3)}_{13}\), \(A=(F,\delta F)\), \(T^\vee=A:T\), and \(q=e_4\operatorname{Disc}_4\). Let \(J=I:T\) be the already identified collision scheme. In the certified hull frame, take the columns \(0,\ldots,10\); eliminate their first nine identity columns, and let \(H_-\) be the remaining \(3\times2\) block. Put \(U=I_2(H_-)\). Then \[U=U:q^\infty=A:I=(T^\vee:q^\infty),\] \[A=I\cap U=T\cap J\cap U,\qquad T^\vee=U\cap J,\qquad T^\vee:U=J.\] The ideal \(U\) is distinct from both \(T\) and \(T^\vee\). Its minimal resolution is \[0\longrightarrow B(-13)\oplus B(-14) \longrightarrow B(-8)\oplus B(-9)\oplus B(-10) \longrightarrow B\longrightarrow B/U\longrightarrow0.\] Thus the root-space curve degree of \(U\) is 60 and its initial degree is eight. The corresponding values for \(T\) are 120 and twelve. The unsaturated polar partner \(T^\vee\) has degree 120 and initial degree twelve because it also includes the degree-60 collision scheme \(J\). No radicality or uniform-in-\(d\) decomposition is asserted.

Construction and proof. Use the retained polynomial hull connection and distinguished vector \(v\). Form the divided iterates \(x_c=(\delta+\widetilde C)^cv/c!\) through \(c=10\). Its first nine columns are the first nine standard coordinate vectors; this is checked exactly. Polynomial column operations therefore reduce the rank-drop ideal of that prefix to \(I_2(H_-)\). The hull frame embeds into the original companion frame with determinant a nonzero scalar times \(q\)'s powers, so it is invertible off collisions. Thus \(U\) describes the closure of the actual opposite prefix-rank scheme once its saturation equality is checked.

The three remaining row weights are \(6,5,4\), and the column weights are \(9,10\). Their complementary minors have weights \(8,9,10\). The complete exact certificate retains \(H_-\), all its minors, the saturated generators, the resolution matrices, and every displayed ideal equality. It independently identifies the ideal with the two-by-two minors of the first two rows of the retained four-by-three Hilbert–Burch matrix for \(I\). The stored resolution has zero composition, maximal-minor ideal exactly \(U\), and height two; Hilbert–Burch proves exactness, and positive entry weights prove minimality. Extending flatly to the ordinary root ring preserves these shifts and gives degree \[\frac{13^2+14^2-8^2-9^2-10^2}{2}=60.\] All operations are over \(\mathbb Q\), so the identities persist over every characteristic-zero field. The driver reconstructs the actual prefix rather than substituting a generic matrix. It checks the colon, saturation and intersection identities separately; a linkage theorem alone would not justify the intersections when components might be shared. \(\square\)

The control uses only the already retained \(n=4,d=2\) matrices: a \(12\times11\) prefix reduces to a \(3\times2\) block and three minors. Its substantive predictions were that the saturated polar partner equals this prefix ideal and that the discrepancy is exactly the previously found \(J\). Both pass. The stronger prediction that the polar partners remain equally graded after removing collisions fails: their initial degrees are twelve and eight, and their degrees are 120 and 60. The prior equal-shift statement about \(T\) and \(T^\vee\) remains true; this refinement identifies what their equality had concealed.

The small free compression cannot stay fixed as the degree grows

Lemma (lem:cube-perfect-boundary-generator-bound). In dimension four and characteristic zero, let \(d\ge2\), \(r=8d-4\), \(\lambda=10d^2-10d-5\), and let \(I=(G_i)\) be the primitive boundary-coordinate ideal. If \(I\) is perfect of height two, its number \(s\) of minimal homogeneous generators satisfies \[\boxed{\lambda\le(s-1)r-\frac{s(s-1)}2.}\] In particular \(s\ge5\) for every \(d\ge3\), and no fixed generator count under height-two perfection works for all \(d\). Thus the degree-two reduction to a height-two three-by-four boundary block after polynomial elimination of free channels cannot be a uniform global presentation of the same boundary ideal. This does not exclude rational or collision-localized compression, nor free hulls with a growing number of retained channels.

Proof. Set \(t=r+\lambda\). There is one coordinate \(G_i\) in each possible degree \(t-i\), for \(0\le i\le r\); some may vanish or be redundant. Hence each graded piece of \(I/B_+I\) has dimension at most one. The distinct degrees \(g_1<\cdots

Here \(L\) is the boundary column image. Dualizing its primitive one-relation presentation gives \(0\to L^*\to F_0^*\to I(t)\to0\). Remove redundant homogeneous coordinates of the last surjection by graded elementary operations. Its kernel is the direct sum of the shifted minimal syzygy module \(\bigoplus_iB(t-u_i)\) and a graded free module recording the redundant coordinates. Dualizing, \(H=L^{**}\) therefore contains direct free summands with generator weights \(t-u_i\). The boundary-hull theorem and the graded ambient embedding put \(H\) inside the original companion module, whose row weights are all nonnegative. Consequently every \(t-u_i\ge0\). It follows that \[s\lambda+\frac{s(s-1)}2\le\sum_jg_j=\sum_i u_i\le(s-1)(r+\lambda),\] which is the boxed inequality.

For \(s\le4\) and \(r\ge12\), the right side of that inequality is at most \(3r-6\). But \[\lambda-(3r-6)=10d^2-34d+13\] is one at \(d=3\) and strictly increasing for integer \(d\ge3\). This proves the stated obstruction. More generally, for fixed \(s\) the right side is linear in \(d\), while \(\lambda\) is quadratic. The claim about a three-channel polynomial model follows because a height-two three-by-four block presents its boundary-coordinate ideal by at most four maximal minors and makes it perfect. Both the grading and identification with the actual global boundary ideal must be preserved. \(\square\)

27 September 2026 — Dimension-four generic Hasse normality holds in every odd characteristic and every degree

Working proof of dimension-four normality for every degree at least two in every odd characteristic. Collision Smith exponents extend to the boundary range; small-prime threshold degrees remain open. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and endpoint. Open statement 2 asks whether the generic Hasse coefficient matrix has consecutive orders at small odd primes, in every dimension and degree. The proposed Frobenius-block induction did not yet control its coupled image. A stronger available test is the elliptic collision limit: its already recorded outer Tate coefficient has a numerator with constant term \(-2\). Nonvanishing of this coefficient survives every odd prime, even where simplicity and root counting fail. The proof below checks the arithmetic normalization and uses exactly the nonvanishing needed for normality. No additional parameter cases are run.

All odd characteristics in dimension four

Theorem (thm:cube-four-all-odd-normality). Over every field \(k\) of characteristic different from two and for every \(d\ge2\), the generic dimension-four root-curve space \(V_{4,d}\) has order set \[\operatorname{Ord}_4(d)=\{0,1,\ldots,8d-5\}.\] Equivalently its square Hasse coefficient determinant through column \(8d-5\) is nonzero over \(k(a_1,a_2,a_3,a_4)\). In the original integral normalization, the content of \(\Delta_{4,d}\) is a power of two. This proves the dimension-four case of conj:cube-refined-initial-segment-law in its full \(d\ge2\) range. Degree one retains the separately known Catalan order set; no assertion about degree-one exceptions is changed.

1. The all-odd collision reduction. By the collision-lattice lemma, in every characteristic different from two the full-series saturation as one parameter tends to zero has limit \[U_d=\bigoplus_{S\subseteq\{1,2,3\}} w_S k[T]_{\le d-|S|},\qquad w_i^2=1+a_iT,\] where a negative polynomial bound means zero. Its dimension is \(N=8d-4\). If its length-\(N\) jet map is invertible at one point over an extension of the field, its generic determinant is nonzero. Then truncating the collision-lattice basis gives an invertible reduction modulo the collision parameter, so the original generic dimension-four matrix is invertible too. We therefore prove normality of \(U_d\), using an elliptic Tate example.

2. Four intrinsic conditions without a formal logarithm. On the elliptic curve \(E=C_3\), choose the origin among the four points at infinity. Their divisor is \(D=E[2]\). The even-sign subgroup is the group of translations by \(E[2]\), and full sign change is inversion. The four-functionals proof identifies \(U_d\subset L(2dD)\) by three restrictions on the top pole coefficients and one on the next coefficients. This identification is valid in odd characteristic: use the even-sign translations as the four transport representatives. The function \(T\) is invariant under these translations, so \(T^d\) has the same top coefficient at each node. The three singleton characters are nontrivial on this subgroup, whereas the triple character is trivial on it. Consequently translation summation kills the singleton subleading terms and detects the omitted triple term with a nonzero factor four.

On a Tate curve with period \(q=\rho^2\), use representatives \(t_j=1,-1,\rho,-\rho\). At each node use the exact odd local parameter \[s_j=2\frac{z/t_j-1}{z/t_j+1}.\] It is carried to the other node parameters by translation, and inversion negates it. For \(v=z/t_j-1\), its expansion is \(s_j=v-v^2/2+O(v^3)\). Thus its second-order jet agrees with the logarithmic coordinate used in the characteristic-zero calculation; only this jet affects the top two pole coefficients. No formal logarithm or division by an odd integer is needed. Writing \[f=a_j s_j^{-2d}+b_j s_j^{-(2d-1)}+\text{lower pole terms},\] the intrinsic conditions are exactly \[U_d=\{f\in L(2dD):a_1=a_2=a_3=a_4,\quad \sum_j b_j=0\}.\tag{1}\]

3. Interpolation over an arbitrary odd characteristic. Put \(m=2d-1\), \(N=4m\), and take the complete field \(k(u)((\rho))\), with \(u\) transcendental over \(k\). Tate uniformization and its theta-function construction work over complete nonarchimedean fields in arbitrary characteristic; see Tate, A review of non-Archimedean elliptic functions, Theorem 1 and the theta-function section, pp. 14–15. Its meromorphic periodic functions are the rational functions of the elliptic curve. We use the theta product without its scalar factor depending only on the period: \[\Theta(x)=(1-x)\prod_{h\ge1}(1-q^h x)(1-q^h/x),\qquad L(x)=x\Theta'(x)/\Theta(x).\] It satisfies \(\Theta(qx)=-x^{-1}\Theta(x)\), \(\Theta(x^{-1})=-x^{-1}\Theta(x)\), has simple zeros at \(q^{\mathbb Z}\), and \(\Theta'(1)\) is a unit. These identities follow directly from the product over the integers.

Let \(P=[u]\) and \(Q=u^N\). Then \([N]P\ne O\): a power of the transcendental unit \(u\) cannot be a power of \(q\), including when the field characteristic divides \(N\). The four top evaluations on \(L((m+1)D-NP)\) are an isomorphism to \(k(u)((\rho))^4\). Indeed the space has dimension four by Riemann–Roch, while its kernel is \(L(mD-NP)\), a degree-zero space which is zero because \(mD\sim NO\) and \([N]P\ne O\). Here all jets are local quotient-ring, or Hasse, jets, not ordinary derivatives divided by factorials.

Set \[G(z)=z^{-m}\frac{\Theta(z/u)^N}{\Theta(z^2)^m},\qquad K_Q(x)=\frac{\Theta'(1)\Theta(Qx)}{\Theta(Q)\Theta(x)}.\] Their automorphy factors are \(G(qz)=QG(z)\) and \(K_Q(qx)=Q^{-1}K_Q(x)\). Define \(c_j\ne0\) and \(\ell_j\) by \[G(z)=c_j s_j^{-m}(1+\ell_j s_j+O(s_j^2))\quad\text{at }t_j.\] Then \[f_P(z)=G(z)\sum_j K_Q(z/t_j)/c_j\] is an elliptic function in \(L((m+1)D-NP)\) with all four top coefficients equal to one, hence is the unique such function. Its rationality on the Tate curve follows from periodicity and the theta construction. Its only poles are at the four nodes and its zero at \(P\) has order at least \(N\).

The inversion identity gives \(\Theta''(1)=0\). In the chosen odd coordinate, \[K_Q(z/t_j)=s_j^{-1}+L(Q)-\tfrac12+O(s_j).\] Thus the sum of the subleading coefficients of \(f_P\) is \[\Phi_d=\sum_j\ell_j+4L(Q)-2+\sum_{i\ne j}\frac{c_i}{c_j}K_Q(t_i/t_j).\tag{2}\] Any nonzero element of \(U_d\cap L((m+1)D-NP)\) would have a nonzero common top value, since the top-evaluation kernel is zero. After normalization it would be \(f_P\). Therefore that intersection is zero exactly when \(\Phi_d\ne0\). This is the precise length-\(N\) normality criterion; it uses no ordinary Wronskian simplicity theorem.

4. An integral leading term. All ensuing expansions take place over \[\mathcal R=\mathbb Z[1/2,u,u^{-1},(1-u^2)^{-1},(u^N-1)^{-1}],\] with formal parameter \(\rho\). In particular, reduction at any odd prime is legitimate. Write \[A_+=\Theta(u)^N,\quad A_-=\Theta(-u)^N,\quad B_+=\Theta(\rho/u)^N,\quad B_-=\Theta(-\rho/u)^N.\] Up to one common nonzero factor the coefficients \(c_j\) are \[A_+,\quad -A_-,\quad -Q\rho^{-m}B_+,\quad Q\rho^{-m}B_-.\] These follow by differentiating \(\Theta(z^2)\) at its four simple node zeros; only the unit \(2\Theta'(1)\) is inverted. Put \(K_\pm=K_Q(\pm\rho)\). The possibly leading cross contribution in (2) is \[-Q\rho^{-m}\left[K_+\left(\frac{B_+}{A_+}+\frac{B_-}{A_-}\right) -K_-\left(\frac{B_-}{A_+}+\frac{B_+}{A_-}\right)\right].\tag{3}\] The reverse cross terms are \(O(\rho^m)\), and the within-pair terms are \(O(1)\). The remaining term is also bounded, as the product identity yields \[\sum_j\ell_j+4L(Q)-2=4m-2-2N L(u^2)+4L(Q).\] This derivation uses only integer multiples and halves, not \(m^{-1}\) or \(N^{-1}\).

For \(A=(1-u)^N\), \(B=(1+u)^N\), \(C=N(u+u^{-1})\), and \(H=2-Q-Q^{-1}\), the theta product gives \[A_+=A+O(\rho^2),\quad A_-=B+O(\rho^2),\quad B_\pm=1\mp C\rho+O(\rho^2),\quad K_\pm=\frac{1\pm H\rho}{Q-1}+O(\rho^2).\] The constant term in the bracket of (3) cancels. Its coefficient of \(\rho\) is \[\frac{2}{Q-1}\left[H\left(\frac1A+\frac1B\right)+C\left(-\frac1A+\frac1B\right)\right].\] Since \(m\ge3\), all bounded terms disappear after multiplication by \(\rho^{m-1}\). Consequently the formal Laurent identity is \[\rho^{m-1}\Phi_d= \frac{-2W_N(u)}{(u^N-1)(1-u^2)^N}+O(\rho),\tag{4}\] where \[W_N(u)=Nu^{N-1}(1+u^2)\big((u-1)^N-(u+1)^N\big) -(u^N-1)^2\big((u-1)^N+(u+1)^N\big).\] The simplification uses \(QH=-(Q-1)^2\), \(QC=Nu^{N-1}(1+u^2)\), and \(AB=(1-u^2)^N\). This rederives the earlier outer-annulus identity in an explicitly integral coefficient ring; an analytic limit has not been reduced modulo a prime.

As an integer polynomial, \(W_N(0)=-2\), because \(N\) is even and greater than one. Thus its reduction is a nonzero polynomial in every odd characteristic. Evaluating its constant coefficient does not mean choosing the forbidden marked point \(u=0\): it proves nonvanishing of the rational function at transcendental \(u\). The leading coefficient in (4) is therefore nonzero in every odd characteristic, so \(\Phi_d\ne0\) and the required length-\(N\) jet map on \(U_d\) is invertible.

5. Back to the parameter matrix. The quotient of an elliptic curve by its two-torsion translations and inversion has degree eight. Choosing its coordinate to place the image of \(D\) at infinity and the image of \(P\) at zero gives the usual model \(w_i^2=1+a_iT\) after a field extension and nonzero character scalings. The marked point is outside \(E[4]\), and hence is unramified, since \(u\) is transcendental. The three parameters are distinct and nonzero. Affine changes of the quotient coordinate preserve each polynomial degree bound \(d-|S|\), by triangular invertible changes; character scalings are units. This gives an example where the actual generic parameter determinant of \(U_d\) is nonzero.

The all-odd collision lattice now has injective length-\(N\) reduction. Its truncated basis is invertible over the collision DVR, while the original basis differs from it by nonzero powers of the collision parameter and an invertible change over the fraction field. Thus the original dimension-four square Hasse determinant is nonzero. This proves the theorem over each prime field of odd characteristic and hence over every field of that characteristic by scalar extension; characteristic zero was already proved and also follows from the same calculation. The integral \(z\)-basis determinant differs from the square-root normalization by powers of two, so its nonzero content has no odd prime divisor. \(\square\)

The collision exponents reach the small-prime boundary

Corollary (cor:cube-four-odd-collision-smith). For \(n=4\), every \(d\ge2\), every field of characteristic different from two and every truncation order \(j\ge8d-5\), the nonzero Smith diagonal entries of \(A_j\) at a generic collision divisor have exponents zero for the basis elements of \(V_{3,d}\), and \(d-e(P)\) for the basis elements \(P\in V_{3,d-1}\), in the collision-lattice notation. Their sum is \[E_4(d)=d^2+(d-1)^2.\] Thus the all-odd Smith statement formerly known for \(j\ge8d\) now holds from the square boundary truncation onward.

Proof. The theorem’s proof gives injectivity of the limit space into length-\(N\) jets, hence also into length-\(j+1\) jets for every \(j\ge N-1\). A full-rank minor modulo the collision parameter is a unit, so the truncated saturated lattice is a direct summand. The existing basis of that lattice is obtained from the original basis by dividing each collision lift by its specified power \(\varepsilon^{d-e(P)}\). These are therefore exactly the elementary exponents. Their recorded sum is \(d^2+(d-1)^2\). The integral Möbius matrix equivalence transfers the conclusion to every collision form. No division by a factorial or by the characteristic is involved. \(\square\)

Falsifying controls and limits of the extension. If the characteristic \(p\) divides \(N\), write \(N=pM\). Then \[W_N(u)=-\left[(u^M-1)^2\big((u-1)^M+(u+1)^M\big)\right]^p.\] It is nonzero but has inseparable roots. This is an explicit control against extending the characteristic-zero simple-root proof: that stronger argument cannot be imported here. Likewise no torsion-exception exclusion, annular root count, small-prime squarefreeness or threshold \(10d^2-10d-5\) has been proved. The conclusion is generic Hasse normality and the stated collision Smith data. Higher-dimensional small-prime normality remains open.

The earlier symbolic audit already checks the rational simplification of the outer coefficient; it was inspected, not rerun. The new arithmetic proof supplies its integral ring and derives each leading term above. Tate's general-field setup, uniformization statement and theta-function construction were read; no complex root-counting result is used. The nonzero constant coefficient is an all-prime certificate, so a new finite prime sweep would not strengthen this proof.

General statement. thm:cube-four-all-odd-normality closes open statement 2 for dimension four in every degree at least two; cor:cube-four-odd-collision-smith extends the exact collision data to its boundary range in every odd characteristic. The first-step and other pre-stable degree formulas, higher-dimensional normality and the full odd-field goal remain open.
