27 September 2026 — Higher collision interpolation has bounded size, but ordinary confluence loses orders at odd primes

Working all-dimensional interpolation reduction and general odd-prime confluence obstruction. The remaining higher-dimensional normality determinant is not proved nonzero. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question. Open statement 2 is now proved through dimension four, in every degree at least two and every odd characteristic. Can its collision/interpolation mechanism address all remaining dimensions, without going through a list of larger finite cases? The complete series below reduces the collision test to a matrix whose size is bounded independently of the degree, including the low-degree range where the old Riemann–Roch dimension formula cannot be used. A second proof shows why simply repeating the characteristic-zero confluence formula is invalid at odd primes.

A bounded interpolation matrix in every degree

Lemma (lem:cube-bounded-collision-interpolation). Let \(k\) be algebraically closed of characteristic different from two, \(n\ge4\), \(d\ge2\), and take distinct nonzero root parameters on the smooth connected curve \(C=C_{n-1}\). Write \(H\) for its reduced infinity divisor, and set \[h=\deg H=2^{n-2},\quad g'=1+(n-4)2^{n-3},\quad g_n=1+(n-3)2^{n-2},\] \[N=N_{2,n}(d),\quad M=2d+n-3,\quad c=Mh+1-g'-N.\] There is a surjective coefficient map \(\Phi:L(MH)\to k^c\) whose kernel is precisely the collision series \[U_d=\bigoplus_{S\subseteq[n-1]}w_S k[T]_{\le d-|S|}.\] For each geometric marked point \(P\notin H\), \[\dim L(MH-NP)=c,\] and \(U_d\) has an invertible length-\(N\) Hasse jet map at \(P\) if and only if the square map \[\Phi_P:L(MH-NP)\longrightarrow k^c\tag{1}\] is invertible. Its size satisfies \[c\le(3n-8)2^{n-3},\] independently of \(d\). This is an exact criterion for the collision series. A nonzero instance at an unramified marked point, after normalization, is sufficient for generic normality of the original dimension-\(n\) series; generic nonvanishing of (1) is not asserted.

If \(d\ge n-2\), the smaller ambient space \(L(2dH)\) suffices and the matrix size is exactly \[c_0=(n-2)2^{n-3}.\tag{2}\] It is the direct higher-dimensional analogue of the four conditions used in the dimension-four proof. The larger choice \(M\) above retains a uniform bound without discarding the special low-degree cases.

Complete character spaces in every degree. First, on any smooth root curve \(C_s\) in odd characteristic and for every integer \(b\ge0\), \[H^0(C_s,\mathcal O(bH_s))= \bigoplus_{S\subseteq[s]}w_S k[T]_{\le\lfloor(b-|S|)/2\rfloor},\tag{3}\] with a negative bound meaning the zero block. To prove this, project onto the characters of the sign group using its invertible order \(2^s\). Every character component is \(w_S g(T)\), because the squarefree root monomials are a basis of the Kummer function-field extension. At a finite branch point a pole of \(g\) pulls back with even order at least two, while \(w_S\) can cancel at most one. At an unramified finite point \(w_S\) has no zero. Thus absence of finite poles forces \(g\) to be a polynomial. At infinity, \(T\) has pole order two and each \(w_i\) pole order one, giving the bound in (3). The reverse containment is immediate. This proof needs no nonspeciality assumption.

In particular, applying (3) to \(C_n\) gives \(N=h^0(dH_n)\) in every degree, rather than replacing \(N\) by its nonspecial formula prematurely. The elementary bound \(h^0(D)\le\deg D+1\) for an effective divisor and Riemann–Roch give \[2dh+1-g_n\le N\le2dh+1.\tag{4}\] The upper bound also follows directly by successively allowing one additional pole in an effective divisor. The lower bound is valid even when its right-hand side is negative.

The coefficient map. The ambient blocks in (3), with \(s=n-1,b=M\), are \[w_S k[T]_{\le\lfloor(M-|S|)/2\rfloor}. \] In each block retain the coefficients with \(0\le j\le d-|S|\), and let \(\Phi\) list the remaining coefficients. These independent coordinate projections are surjective and their kernel is \(U_d\). The ambient degree is greater than \(2g'-2=(n-4)h\), so its dimension is \(Mh+1-g'\). The collision-lattice count gives \(\dim U_d=N\), proving that the number of omitted coefficients is exactly \(c\). Only character projection and polynomial coefficient extraction are used; no high derivative, factorial or formal logarithm enters the definition.

Jets and the size bound. For every geometric \(P\notin H\), (4) gives \[\deg(MH-NP)\ge(n-3)h-1> (n-4)h=2g'-2.\] Hence its first cohomology vanishes and Riemann–Roch gives dimension \(c\). The full length-\(N\) jet map on \(L(MH)\) is onto, with kernel \(L(MH-NP)\). The kernel of (1) is exactly \(U_d\cap L(MH-NP)\), which is also the kernel of the length-\(N\) map on \(U_d\). Both relevant maps are square, proving the criterion. The lower bound in (4) yields \[c\le(n-3)h+g_n-g'=\frac{(3n-8)h}{2},\] which proves the bound independent of degree.

For the sharper range \(d\ge n-2\), the original divisor \(dH_n\) is nonspecial, so \(N=2dh+1-g_n\). Now \(2dH-NP\) has degree \(g_n-1\), exceeding \(2g'-2\) by \(h\), and dimension \(g_n-g'=c_0\). In the ambient character block of degree bound \(d-\lceil|S|/2\rceil\), the collision space omits exactly \(\lfloor|S|/2\rfloor\) top coefficients. Their total is \[\sum_{s=0}^{n-1}\binom{n-1}{s}\lfloor s/2\rfloor =(n-2)2^{n-3}.\] The endpoint \(d=n-2\) is included: its highest-character collision block has bound \(-1\), hence dimension zero, and the same count holds.

Transfer and its limits. At an unramified finite \(P\), translate \(T\) to make \(T(P)=0\) and scale the nonzero \(w_i(P)\) to one. The polynomial degree bounds defining \(U_d\) are preserved by invertible triangular changes. The all-odd collision lattice then transfers length-\(N\) injectivity to the original parameter matrix. This is a sufficient test, not a converse: a special collision determinant can vanish even when the undeformed determinant is nonzero. The exact criterion itself permits any geometric \(P\notin H\), but no ramified-point transport has been silently substituted for the normalized root parameter map. For a non-algebraically-closed field, apply the statement after geometric scalar extension; rank nonvanishing descends. \(\square\)

The older elliptic pushdown is a different exact representation of the original full series. It does not already provide these omitted-character functionals for its collision limit. Conversely, bounding the size of (1) does not prove its determinant nonzero or control the parameter degrees of a threshold witness.

A general odd-prime obstruction to copying the old confluence profile

Refutation (obs:cube-odd-unbalanced-confluence). Let \(k\) have odd characteristic \(p\), let \(A\ge2\), and let \(x=(1+\varepsilon T)^{1/2}\) over \(k((\varepsilon))\), normalized by \(x(0)=1\). The space \[V_A=k((\varepsilon))[T]_{\le A} +x\,k((\varepsilon))[T]_{\le A-2}\] has dimension \(2A\). Its order set and its full-series saturated \(\varepsilon\)-limit are respectively \[\begin{cases} \{0,\ldots,2A-1\},\quad k[T]_{\le2A-1},&p\nmid A,\\ \{0,\ldots,2A-2,2A\},\quad k[T]_{\le2A-2}\oplus kT^{2A},&p\mid A. \end{cases}\tag{5}\] Thus the characteristic-zero replacement of every degree pair \((\alpha,\beta)\) by the consecutive profile through \(\alpha+\beta+1\) does not extend without restriction to odd characteristic.

Proof. Since \(T=(x^2-1)/\varepsilon\), the space is exactly the polynomials in \(x\) of degree at most \(q=2A\) whose coefficient of \(x^{q-1}\) is zero: all even degrees through \(q\) and all odd degrees through \(q-3\) occur. Put \(y=x-1\). If a polynomial is \(\sum a_jy^j\), its missing coefficient condition is \[a_{q-1}-q a_q=0.\] An order-adapted basis is therefore \[1,y,\ldots,y^{q-2},\qquad y^q+q y^{q-1}.\] Here \(y=\varepsilon T/2+O(\varepsilon^2T^2)\). The final basis element has order \(q-1\) if \(p\nmid A\), and order \(q\) if \(p\mid A\). This proves both order sets. Divide each basis element by the corresponding power of \(\varepsilon\); its reduction is a nonzero scalar times the indicated monomial in \(T\). The reductions are independent and number \(q\), so these elements give the full saturated limit. For completeness, if an element in their fraction-field span had an integral series but a negative minimum coefficient valuation in this basis, multiplying by \(\varepsilon^{-m}\), where \(m<0\) is that minimum valuation, would give a nontrivial linear combination of the independent reductions equal to zero. Hence all coefficients are integral, proving saturation. \(\square\)

Where the obstruction enters. The first collision of the cube gives degree bounds \(d-|S|\). A second individual-variable confluence has the balanced pair \((j,j-1)\), \(j=d-|S|\); changing to \(x\) makes this the complete polynomial space through degree \(2j\), so that step is characteristic-safe. Its positive blocks have new degree bound \(2j\). A third confluence then encounters the pair \((2j,2j-2)\). When \(p\mid j\), (5) replaces the predicted last monomial \(T^{4j-1}\) by \(T^{4j}\). Boundary blocks with negative degree bounds must still be clipped separately. This is a precise obstruction to iterating the old profile rule, not a claim about an entire confluent determinant's rank.

The recorded confluence theorem expressly assumes characteristic zero; its proof uses the ordinary-derivative assertion that a rational function with derivative zero is constant. No correction to that theorem is needed. Nor does (5) refute the original balanced normality conjecture: already in dimension four, the newly proved all-odd theorem coexists with the changed third-confluence block when \(d\) is a positive multiple of \(p\). A degeneration losing its characteristic-zero profile is not evidence that the original generic space is nonnormal.

General statement. lem:cube-bounded-collision-interpolation gives an exact bounded-size collision criterion for every \(n\ge4,d\ge2\) in odd characteristic, with a sharper size in the nonspecial range. obs:cube-odd-unbalanced-confluence gives the complete order/profile change for every \(A\ge2\) at each odd prime. The remaining generic nonvanishing assertion for \(n\ge5\) is still open; neither result replaces that assertion by a proved surrogate.

Verification gate. A fresh-context medium-reasoning reviewer passed both complete proofs, all parameter ranges and the qualified third-confluence application, with no unused hypothesis requiring removal. Its clarification of the saturation valuation argument is incorporated. The medium pre-proof review checked all-degree completeness of the character basis, the special-degree bounds, residual nonspeciality, matrix sizes, the geometric-point and unramified-transfer qualifications, and the exact order-adapted basis in (5). Re-read the collision-lattice and four-functional proofs, elliptic pushdown and the characteristic-zero confluence argument. No finite parameter calculation was needed: the obstruction is an exact family and the interpolation construction follows from the displayed spaces.

Assessment and next step. The dimension-four arithmetic proof does have a general interpolation setting, but its scalar nonzero leading coefficient has not yet been replaced by a nonzero determinant in higher dimensions. Simple repeated confluence is not such a proof, because its order profiles change at odd primes. On cube-odd-characteristic, the next route review should test a nodal degeneration with distinct gluing points and the actual sign-character coefficient conditions, seeking a characteristic-safe leading determinant. Any graph or Cauchy representation must retain those conditions and prove its comparison with (1). The low-degree range stays in scope through the larger ambient space, and pre-stable parameter degrees remain a separate open obligation.

Process. The low-degree Riemann–Roch exception was handled by enlarging the complete ambient series by a fixed amount depending only on dimension. An explicit order-adapted basis exposed the failure of naive odd-characteristic confluence without adding a prime or dimension survey. No framework change was needed.

27 September 2026 — Nodal matching misses a full, explicitly filtered smoothing obstruction

Working all-dimensional calculation of extension torsion in odd characteristic. The higher-dimensional normality determinant remains open. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Obstacle

Open statement 2 still asks for generic Hasse normality for every \(n\ge5,d\ge2\) at the remaining odd primes. The bounded interpolation map retains the exact problem, but its determinant has not been proved nonzero. This review tests the proposed distinct-node approach against the actual section lattice. The answer is more precise than a warning about graph models: in the nonspecial range, the smoothing has an explicit torsion module whose longest elementary divisor is \(t^{n-3}\). Node values alone discard that entire module. The calculation below develops the previously recorded focused-collision obstruction rather than proposing another parameter survey.

General statement. lem:cube-collision-extension-torsion determines this module for every \(n\ge4,d\ge n-2\) in characteristic different from two. It refines lem:cube-focused-collision-series; the collision space and its total coefficient codimension were already supplied by lem:cube-bounded-collision-interpolation. The new information is the complete smoothing-torsion filtration and its precise finite lifting test. It does not establish conj:cube-refined-initial-segment-law, nor cover the special low-degree cases by the dimension formulas used here.

The actual extension module

Lemma (lem:cube-collision-extension-torsion). Let \(k\) be algebraically closed with \(\operatorname{char}k\ne2\), \(R=k[[t]]\), \(n\ge4\), and \(d\ge n-2\). Fix distinct nonzero \(a_1,\ldots,a_{n-1}\). In the projective diagonal family \(\mathcal C/R\), write \[w_i^2=z^2+a_iT\quad(i<n),\qquad w_n^2=z^2+tT,\] where \(z,w_i\) have degree one and \(T\) has degree two. Eliminating \(T\) gives a complete intersection of \(n-1\) quadrics in \(\mathbb P^n_R\). The central fibre is \(A\cup B\), with \(A=(w_n=z)\), \(B=(w_n=-z)\), both copies of \(C_{n-1}\). Their intersection is the reduced infinity divisor \(H\), of degree \(h=2^{n-2}\). Put \[g'=1+(n-4)h/2,\quad \mathcal L_j=\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}(d)(jB),\quad M_j=H^1(\mathcal C,\mathcal L_j)\qquad(0\le j\le d).\] For integers \(b\ge0\), let \(N_{2,s}(b)=\sum_{S\subseteq[s]}\max(0,\lfloor(b-|S|)/2\rfloor+1)\), and put \(N_{2,s}(b)=0\) for \(b<0\). Then \(M_0=0\), the natural maps identify \(M_{j-1}\) with a submodule of \(M_j\), and \[tM_j=M_{j-1},\qquad \dim_k(t^rM_d/t^{r+1}M_d)=N_{2,n-1}(n-4-r)\quad(r\ge0).\tag{ET}\] Consequently, noncanonically, \[M_d\simeq\bigoplus_{s=1}^{n-3}\bigl(R/(t^s)\bigr)^{\mu_s},\qquad \mu_s=N_{2,n-1}(n-3-s)-N_{2,n-1}(n-4-s).\tag{EF}\] In particular, there are \(g'\) summands and exactly one summand of maximal length \(n-3\). These are elementary divisors of coherent cohomology in the smoothing parameter, not the previously computed Smith exponents of the marked jet matrix.

The central sections of \(\mathcal L_d\), restricted to \(A\), form the subspace of \(L(2dH)\) whose node values agree in the normalization below. The actual extending subspace is \[U_d=\bigoplus_{S\subseteq[n-1]}w_S k[T]_{\le d-|S|},\] and its quotient inside the node-matching space is canonically \(M_d[t]\), of dimension \(g'\). For a central section with obstruction \(x\in M_d[t]\), lifting to \(\mathcal C\otimes_R R/(t^m)\) is equivalent to \[x\in t^{m-1}M_d\qquad(m\ge1).\tag{LT}\] Thus lifting modulo \(t^{n-2}\) is equivalent to being the reduction of an actual relative section. There are nonextendable central sections that lift modulo \(t^{n-3}\). This is the depth needed to detect every extension obstruction in this family; it is not a lower bound on the complexity of every possible normality proof.

Geometry and cohomology conventions. At a node, \(T\ne0\), and the last equation is \((w_n-z)(w_n+z)=tT\). Since two is invertible, the two components meet transversely and the total surface is regular there. Off the nodes the central component is smooth. The family is flat: its homogeneous equations form the expected complete intersection on both fibres, and the diagonal coordinate algebra is torsion-free over \(R\). The generic parameters \(a_1,\ldots,a_{n-1},t\) are distinct and nonzero in \(k((t))\). The components and the generic fibre are smooth connected root curves. All components are Cartier divisors on the regular surface, and \(A+B=\operatorname{div}(t)\). Hence \[\mathcal L_j|_A=\mathcal O_A((d+j)H),\qquad \mathcal L_j|_B=\mathcal O_B((d-j)H).\tag{R}\] Adjunction on \(B\), an intersection of \(n-2\) quadrics in \(\mathbb P^{n-1}\), gives \(K_B=(n-4)H\), and the degree and genus stated above. In general \(\omega_{\mathcal C/R}=\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}(n-3)\): the dimension-four notation \(\omega^d(dB)\) must not be copied unchanged.

We use coherent cohomology, not étale proper base change. The family is projective with one-dimensional fibres; its higher coherent cohomology above degree one vanishes over the affine base. Its line bundles are \(R\)-flat, and their cohomology is finite over \(R\). Equivalently, Stacks, Lemma 30.22.1 and Remark 30.22.2 give a finite projective complex computing these groups and their arbitrary base changes. The normalization sequence for \(\mathcal O_{\mathcal C_0}(d)\) has two copies of \(\mathcal O_B(dH)\) and the \(h\) node fibres. Both first cohomologies vanish, and evaluation onto the node fibres is onto because \(H^1(B,(d-1)H)=0\). Here \(d-1>n-4\). Thus \(H^1(\mathcal C_0,\mathcal O(d))=0\), and the multiplication-by-\(t\) sequence and Nakayama give \(M_0=0\).

The two maps in the filtration. Increasing the twist by \(B\) gives \[0\longrightarrow\mathcal L_{j-1}\longrightarrow\mathcal L_j \longrightarrow\mathcal O_B((d-j)H)\longrightarrow0.\tag{B}\] The map on global sections to the last term is onto, as follows. Set \(\sigma=(w_n-z)/t\), a global section of \(\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}(1)(B)\). Its divisor as that section is the horizontal divisor \(T=0,w_n=z\); this divisor misses \(B\). Thus \(\sigma|_B\) is nowhere zero. Every section of \(\mathcal O_B(bH)\), \(b=d-j\ge0\), has the character basis \[w_ST^qz^{b-|S|-2q},\qquad 0\le q\le\lfloor(b-|S|)/2\rfloor.\] These homogeneous polynomials lift to \(\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}(b)\), and multiplying by \(\sigma^j\) gives the required lifts in \(\mathcal L_j\), after using \(\sigma|_B\) to fix the frame. Completeness of this character basis was proved in every degree in the bounded-interpolation entry. Therefore (B) gives a short exact sequence \[0\longrightarrow M_{j-1}\longrightarrow M_j \longrightarrow H^1(B,(d-j)H)\longrightarrow0.\tag{B1}\] On the other component, multiplication by \(t\) identifies \(\mathcal L_j\) with \(\mathcal L_{j-1}(-A)\) inside \(\mathcal L_{j-1}\), so \[0\longrightarrow\mathcal L_j\xrightarrow{\ t\ }\mathcal L_{j-1} \longrightarrow\mathcal O_A((d+j-1)H)\longrightarrow0.\tag{A}\] The last line bundle has vanishing first cohomology. Thus the map \(M_j\to M_{j-1}\) in (A) is onto. Its composite with the inclusion in (B1) is multiplication by \(t\) on \(M_j\); consequently \(tM_j=M_{j-1}\), as claimed. Iterating gives \(t^rM_d=M_{d-r}\) for \(0\le r\le d\), and zero thereafter.

Elementary divisors. By (B1), the successive quotient at \(r\) is \(H^1(B,rH)\). Serre duality for line bundles on a proper smooth curve and \(K_B=(n-4)H\) give \[h^1(B,rH)=h^0(B,(n-4-r)H)=N_{2,n-1}(n-4-r).\] This proves (ET), including vanishing for \(r\ge n-3\). A summand \(R/(t^s)\) contributes one to this quotient precisely for \(r<s\); taking consecutive differences proves (EF). The first quotient has dimension \(h^1(B,\mathcal O_B)=g'\), and the last nonzero quotient has dimension \(h^0(B,\mathcal O_B)=1\). For orientation, the formula gives \(R/(t)\) at \(n=4\), and \((R/(t))^4\oplus R/(t^2)\) at \(n=5\). These are consequences of the exact formula, not a new finite-case certification.

The full extending lattice and the central discrepancy. The normalization sequence for \(\mathcal L_d|_{\mathcal C_0}\) uses \(\mathcal O_A(2dH)\oplus\mathcal O_B\). Its evaluation is onto, since \(H^1(A,(2d-1)H)=0\). It follows that \[h^0(\mathcal C_0,\mathcal L_d|_{\mathcal C_0})=(2d-1)h+2-g'.\] Restriction to \(A\) is injective: a constant on \(B\) vanishing at every node is zero. The section \(\sigma^d\) restricts nontrivially to \(B\); its restriction to \(A\), in the usual focused frame, is \(2^{-d}T^d\). This fixes the normalization in which the node values of \(F/T^d\) all agree.

The explicit relative sections \[S_{S,j}=t^{-j}w_Sz^{d-|S|-j}(w_n-z)^j, \qquad 0\le j\le d-|S|,\tag{S}\] have poles only along \(B\), of order at most \(d\). On the generic fibre, the squarefree \(w_S\), \(S\subseteq[n-1]\), are a free basis over \(k((t))[z,w_n]\); the equations express each \(w_i^2\) in that ring. Thus (S) is a basis in homogeneous degree \(d\), after the invertible triangular change from \(w_n\) to \(w_n-z\). Its number is \(N=N_{2,n}(d)=2dh+1-g_n\), with \(g_n=1+(n-3)h\). On \(A\), using \((w_n-z)(w_n+z)=tT\), its restrictions are \[2^{-j}T^jw_Sz^{2d-|S|-2j}.\] They are independent by the distinct sign characters and the distinct powers of \(T\). The module \(H^0(\mathcal C,\mathcal L_d)\) is finite free of rank \(N\), and reduction injects into central sections. Hence these \(N\) independent reductions fill that image; Nakayama makes (S) its full basis. In the chart \(z=1\), their span is precisely \(U_d\).

The multiplication-by-\(t\) sequence now identifies the quotient of all central sections by this extending image with \(M_d[t]\). Its dimension is \(g'\), also obtained by subtracting \(N\) from the displayed central dimension. The coefficient interpretation agrees: of the \((n-2)h/2\) omitted coefficients, exactly \(h-1\) are top coefficients of nonempty even characters and enforce node matching. The other \(g'\) coefficients are extension conditions; higher omitted coefficients in even characters must still be retained. No identification of the whole obstruction module with the single vector space \(H^1(B,\mathcal O_B)\) is asserted.

Finite lifting and its exact endpoint. For \(m\ge1\), put \(\mathcal C_m=\mathcal C\otimes_R R/(t^m)\). The sequence for multiplication by \(t^m\) gives a surjection from \(H^0(\mathcal C_m,\mathcal L_d|_{\mathcal C_m})\) onto \(M_d[t^m]\). Comparing it with the sequence for \(t\), the induced map on obstruction classes is multiplication by \(t^{m-1}\). Its image is \[t^{m-1}M_d[t^m]=M_d[t]\cap t^{m-1}M_d.\] Necessity in (LT) follows. Conversely, lift a preimage in \(M_d[t^m]\); its reduction has the prescribed central obstruction. The difference from the desired central section is the reduction of an actual relative section and can be corrected by that section. This proves sufficiency. Formula (EF) gives the endpoint and sharpness: a nonzero element \(t^{n-4}e\) in the longest summand lifts through \(m=n-3\), but not through \(m=n-2\). The terminology refers to lifting a central section, not to making a fixed chosen partial lift compatible. \(\square\)

Tests of the proposed comparison

The smallest already necessary control is the old dimension-four focused example; the proof above shows it is part of an all-dimensional family. For every allowed \(n,d\), the homogeneous section \[F_*=zT^{d-2}w_1w_2w_3\in L(2dH)\] has zero values at all nodes and therefore gives the central section \((F_*,0)\). It is not in \(U_d\): its character has size three and its exponent \(d-2\) exceeds the allowed \(d-3\). Thus any proposed comparison which uses only these node values kills a nonzero extension obstruction. This is a direct test of the proposed input data, not a claim that no graph with additional vertex or jet data could work.

A first-order repair is also insufficient uniformly. At \(n=5,d\ge3\), the length-two summand in (EF) supplies a nonextendable central section which nevertheless lifts modulo \(t^2\). More generally the unique longest summand has length \(n-3\). All of these controls hold for distinct nonzero parameters in every odd characteristic. They require no dimension or prime sweep and do not infer a failure of the smooth-fibre Hasse determinant.

27 September 2026 — The exact rational collision determinant has arithmetic resonances; smoothing repairs two minimal controls

Working all-degree arithmetic criterion for the rational four-block series. Quadratic smoothing repair is checked in two finite controls, not proved uniformly. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question. Open statement 2 needs a nonzero marked Hasse determinant at every odd prime. The nodal review showed why matching node values is insufficient. This cycle retains the entire actual limiting series and asks a stronger question: can its rational collision determinant itself serve as a characteristic-safe leading term? It cannot. The exact five-condition matrix has the factor \(N^2-1\); at every odd prime dividing it, the limiting jet map has generic corank one. This is an arithmetic refinement of the recorded characteristic-zero eight-term formula, not a new discovery of the codimension-five representation. Two minimal smoothing tests then distinguish failure of the limit from failure of the original series.

General statement. thm:cube-rational-collision-resonance gives the complete generic normality criterion for every integer \(A\ge3\) in odd characteristic. For the actual dimension-four second collision, \(A=2d\), its exceptional primes divide \((8d-5)(8d-3)\). This refutes that collision's universal constant-term nonvanishing, not conj:cube-refined-initial-segment-law. The separately registered check:cube-rational-resonance-smoothing tests whether higher deformation coefficients can repair the corank-one failure; no all-degree repair theorem is asserted.

The integral Hasse calculation

Theorem (thm:cube-rational-collision-resonance). Let \(k\) have characteristic different from two, take distinct nonzero \(a,b\), and let \(C_2\) be the smooth projective normalization of \[w_1^2=1+aT,\qquad w_2^2=1+bT.\] For \(A\ge3\), with a negative polynomial bound denoting zero, put \[V_A=k[T]_{\le A}+w_1k[T]_{\le A-2}+w_2k[T]_{\le A-2} +w_1w_2k[T]_{\le A-4},\qquad N=4A-4.\] Then \(\dim V_A=N\). Its length-\(N\) Hasse jet map at a generic finite geometric point is invertible if and only if \(N^2-1\ne0\) in \(k\). If \(N^2-1=0\), that generic jet map has kernel of dimension exactly one.

Conic coordinates and the five constraints. Work after algebraic scalar extension. There are nonzero constants \(c,c'\) and a rational parameter \(x\) with \[w_1=c(x+x^{-1}),\qquad w_2=c'(x-x^{-1}),\] and \(T\) an affine function with nonzero slope of \(x^2+x^{-2}\). Indeed choose \(c^2=(b-a)/(4b)\), \((c')^2=(b-a)/(4a)\); then \(w_1^2/a-w_2^2/b=1/a-1/b\). The resulting parametrization is birational, since \(x=(w_1/c+w_2/c')/2\). The two infinity points are \(x=0,\infty\).

The first block spans all symmetric even Laurent polynomials of degree at most \(2A\). The middle two blocks together span all odd Laurent monomials of degrees between \(-(2A-3)\) and \(2A-3\). The last block spans all antisymmetric even Laurent polynomials of degree at most \(2A-6\), and is empty at \(A=3\). These assertions follow by triangular expansion in \(x^2+x^{-2}\), with nonzero leading coefficients; only powers of two and \(c,c'\) are inverted. Multiplying the series by \(x^{2A}\) therefore identifies it with the polynomials \(f(x)=\sum_{i=0}^{N+4}a_ix^i\) satisfying exactly \[a_1=a_{N+3}=0,\qquad a_0=a_{N+4},\qquad a_2=a_{N+2},\qquad a_4=a_N.\tag{RC}\] These five independent conditions leave dimension \(N\). This also proves the endpoint \(A=3\), without counting a negative block as nonzero.

Let the generic marked point have coordinate \(u\), transcendental over the coefficient field. Multiplication by \(x^{2A}\) is a unit there. A polynomial of degree at most \(N+4\) vanishes to Hasse order at least \(N\) precisely when \[f(x)=(x-u)^N(g_0+g_1x+g_2x^2+g_3x^3+g_4x^4).\] Thus the jet kernel is the kernel of the five conditions (RC) on the five coefficients \(g_j\). This uses divisibility by \((x-u)^N\), with no ordinary-derivative or factorial criterion.

Elimination without odd denominators. Write \(Q=u^N\), \(b_i=\binom Ni\), and \[\alpha=b_2-N^2=-\frac{N(N+1)}2,\qquad \beta=b_4-Nb_3=-\frac{N(N^2-1)(N-2)}8.\] The identities are identities of integer-valued binomial expressions; their final denominators are powers of two. They remain valid at characteristic three. Since \(N\) is even, the constraints \(a_1=a_{N+3}=0\) and \(a_0=a_{N+4}\) eliminate \[g_1=Nu^{-1}g_0,\qquad g_4=Qg_0,\qquad g_3=NuQg_0.\] The remaining two equations on \((g_0,g_2)\) have matrix \[\begin{pmatrix} \alpha u^{N-2}(1-u^4)&Q-1\\ \beta u^{N-4}(1-u^8)+(1-N^2)(Q^2-1)&b_2u^2(u^{N-4}-1) \end{pmatrix}.\tag{RM}\] Every elimination pivot was a unit in \(k(u)\). In particular, \(N\) was never inverted.

Put \(m=A-1=N/4\) as an integer, and define the already recorded polynomial \[F_m(v)=1+v^{3m}-v^{m-1}\bigl(m(2m-1)-(4m^2-1)v+m(2m+1)v^2\bigr) -v^{2m-1}\bigl(m(2m+1)-(4m^2-1)v+m(2m-1)v^2\bigr).\] Direct expansion of (RM) gives \[\det(\mathrm{RM})=(N^2-1)F_m(u^4).\tag{RD}\] For clarity, taking the negative of this determinant first yields \[(Q-1)\{\beta u^{N-4}(1-u^8)+(1-N^2)(Q^2-1)\} -\alpha b_2u^N(1-u^4)(u^{N-4}-1)=-(N^2-1)F_m(u^4).\] Substituting the displayed \(\alpha,\beta,b_2\) proves (RD) over \(\mathbb Z[1/2]\). Since \(m\ge2\), \(F_m(0)=1\). Hence this polynomial is nonzero over every field, and (RD) is nonzero precisely when \(N^2-1\ne0\). In exceptional characteristic, (RM) still has the nonzero entry \(Q-1\), so its rank is exactly one. This proves the full criterion and generic corank assertion. The same conclusion descends from geometric scalar extension. \(\square\)

The old ordinary Wronskian formula has additional scalar factors coming from its dual series and its normalization. Those cannot be reduced modulo an odd prime and interpreted as the Hasse determinant. Equation (RD) computes the actual jet-kernel criterion integrally. The earlier all-degree simplicity theorem remains correct in its stated characteristic-zero scope; this arithmetic result neither changes it nor extends its squarefreeness assertion.

Which collision this actually tests

In the dimension-four collision space \(U_d\) on \(C_3\), send the third parameter to \(\varepsilon\). For a subset \(S\subseteq\{1,2\}\), put \(j=d-|S|\). Its two blocks are \[w_S\bigl(k((\varepsilon))[T]_{\le j}+\sqrt{1+\varepsilon T}\,k((\varepsilon))[T]_{\le j-1}\bigr).\] For \(j\ge0\), writing \(y=\sqrt{1+\varepsilon T}-1\) turns the parenthesized space into every polynomial in \(y\) of degree at most \(2j\). This follows from \(T=((y+1)^2-1)/\varepsilon\); the even and odd powers in \(y+1\) give all degrees through \(2j\). The normalized basis \((2y/\varepsilon)^r\), \(0\le r\le2j\), has reductions \(T^r\). Their reductions, multiplied by the independent remaining characters \(w_S\), are independent, so the usual minimum-valuation argument proves this is the full saturated limit. At \(j=0\) the second block is empty and the limit is just the constants. Thus for every \(d\ge2\), in every odd characteristic, the resulting rational series is exactly \(V_{2d}\), including the last block at \(d=2\).

Its dimension is \(N=8d-4\). The theorem therefore gives the exact exceptional set \[p\mid(8d-5)(8d-3).\] Both factors are odd and greater than one, so every such degree has some exceptional odd characteristic. The specialization uses the entire correct limiting space; its failure is not caused by omitting the node-extension conditions. It is also different from the unbalanced one-root obstruction: the confluence just used is characteristic-safe, and the resulting full rational series itself is nonclassical at these primes. Normalizing an unramified finite marked point by an affine change of \(T\) and nonzero rescalings of \(w_i\) preserves these degree bounds. Consequently generic marked-point failure also means failure of the normalized rational parameter determinant.

This does not refute the original all-odd dimension-four theorem. It shows why its proof cannot stop at this further collision's constant term. A determinant with zero reduction can have a nonzero higher smoothing coefficient.

The first smoothing test

Finite check (check:cube-rational-resonance-smoothing). The smallest cube instance is \(d=2,A=4,N=12\), with block dimensions \(5,3,3,1\). Use the exact saturated basis above: \[w_S\left(\frac{2(\sqrt{1+\varepsilon T}-1)}{\varepsilon}\right)^r, \qquad0\le r\le4-2|S|.\] Its coefficient of \(\varepsilon^kT^{r+k}\), before multiplication by \(w_S\), is \[c_{r,k}=\frac{(-1)^k}{4^k}\frac{r}{r+2k}\binom{r+2k}{k}\quad(k>0,r>0),\] with \(c_{r,0}=1\) and \(c_{0,k}=0\) for \(k>0\). The Catalan convolution in the last factor is an integer: it is the coefficient of \(z^k\) in \(C(z)^r\), where \(C=1+zC^2\), equivalently the formula follows by Lagrange inversion. The script forms that rational expression exactly before modular reduction, so no division by \(r+2k\) in the finite field occurs. Expanding through \(k=4\) and retaining columns \(T^0,\ldots,T^{11}\) computes the determinant modulo \(\varepsilon^5\) exactly.

Thus the two resonant controls are repaired at precisely quadratic order. Their corank-one marked jet matrices have one nonunit elementary divisor of order two, since an \(11\times11\) minor is already a unit. These are elementary divisors of this specific marked matrix over \(\mathbb F_p[[\varepsilon]]\); they are not the coherent-cohomology elementary divisors of the preceding entry. 27 September 2026 — Separate Hasse normality does not compose: the missing condition is joint transversality

Working all-prime family refuting automatic composition of normal blocks. The all-dimensional normality and pre-stable threshold goals remain open. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Obstacle

The preceding cycle found exact rational-limit resonances and two quadratic smoothing repairs. Before proving another theorem confined to the already solved dimension-four normality problem, this review tests the implication needed by open statement 2: would independently normal lower blocks imply normality of their combined marked system? Even in the actual rational root-cover series, the answer is no. The failure occurs for infinitely many degrees at every prime at least seven. A local repair can contribute only together with a theorem controlling the joint jet images. This review does not treat the two finite repairs as an all-dimensional induction.

General statement. cor:cube-local-normality-composition-failure is an explicit composition of obs:cube-odd-unbalanced-confluence and thm:cube-rational-collision-resonance. Its purpose is to falsify automatic composition, not to rename their formulas. The remaining positive assertion is still conj:cube-refined-initial-segment-law. The polynomial threshold compatibility class in lem:cube-dimensional-gluing is a related, already recorded obstruction; it is distinct from the left-series Hasse-rank test here.

A family of normal summands with a nonnormal sum

Corollary (cor:cube-local-normality-composition-failure). Let \(k\) have characteristic \(p\ge7\), let \(A\ge4\), and suppose \[p\mid(4A-5)(4A-3).\] On the smooth rational root curve \(w_1^2=1+aT,w_2^2=1+bT\), with \(a,b\) distinct and nonzero, set \[B_r=k[T]_{\le r}+w_1k[T]_{\le r-2},\qquad E=B_A,\qquad F=w_2B_{A-2}.\] At a generic finite geometric point, \(E\) has consecutive Hasse orders \(0,\ldots,2A-1\), and \(F\) has consecutive orders \(0,\ldots,2A-5\). Nevertheless their function-space direct sum \(E\oplus F=V_A\), of dimension \(4A-4\), has a length-\((4A-4)\) jet kernel of dimension one. For every fixed \(p\ge7\), there are infinitely many such \(A\), including infinitely many even \(A=2d\) relevant to the cube collision.

Proof. If \(p\mid A\), the resonance would force \(p\mid15\); the same is true if \(p\mid A-2\). Thus neither is possible for \(p\ge7\). For completeness, the fixed-curve version of the one-root calculation is as follows. Put \(x=w_1\). Since \(T=(x^2-1)/a\), \(B_r\) is exactly the polynomials in \(x\) of degree at most \(q=2r\) with missing coefficient \([x^{q-1}]\). At a generic point write \(x=v+y\), with \(v\ne0\). In the \(y\) coefficients the condition is \[c_{q-1}-qv c_q=0.\] When \(p\nmid r\), the basis \[1,y,\ldots,y^{q-2},\qquad y^q+qv y^{q-1}\] has orders \(0,\ldots,q-1\). On \(C_2\), \(x-v\) is a local parameter at a generic point; the additional quadratic cover is unramified there. Apply this with \(r=A\) and \(r=A-2\). Multiplication by the unit \(w_2\) preserves orders.

The sum is direct: \(w_2\notin k(w_1)\), since its square is a quadratic polynomial in \(w_1\) with two distinct simple roots, hence is not a square in \(k(w_1)\). Its direct sum is precisely the four-block space \(V_A\). The resonance theorem gives the one-dimensional generic jet kernel because \((4A-4)^2-1=(4A-5)(4A-3)\). Finally, \(4A\equiv3\) or \(5\pmod p\) each has a solution; adding multiples of \(2p\) gives arbitrarily large even solutions after choosing an even representative. This proves the infinite-family assertion. \(\square\)

This is a failure of joint jet independence despite independence as rational functions. It does not say that a full simultaneous smoothing is nonnormal. It also does not refute induction using additional structure of the original complete linear series. In particular, the summands \(B_r\) are the specified incomplete series on the rational curve; they must not be substituted for the original complete series without preserving their hypotheses.

The exact condition an induction would have to prove

The following standard Schur-complement calculation keeps the marked jets. Suppose \(r\) basis rows from a space \(E\) and \(s\) rows from a space \(F\) are evaluated through length \(r+s\). Write their matrix, split after the first \(r\) jet columns, as \[J=\begin{pmatrix}E_0&E_1\\F_0&F_1\end{pmatrix},\qquad E_0\in\operatorname{Mat}_{r\times r}.\] If \(E_0\) is invertible, subtract \(F_0E_0^{-1}\) times the upper block of rows from the lower block. This invertible row operation proves \[\det J=\det E_0\det\bigl(F_1-F_0E_0^{-1}E_1\bigr).\tag{JT}\] Separate normality of \(F\) controls its own initial columns; it does not make this residual matrix invertible. The corollary is an all-prime-family control in which both summands are normal and the residual is singular.

For the original dimension recursion, work over the rational parameter field \(k(a_1,\ldots,a_{n-1})\), put \(r=N_{2,n-1}(d)\), \(s=N_{2,n-1}(d-1)\), and use the recorded row split \[A_{n,d,r+s-1}=\begin{pmatrix}A_{n-1,d,r+s-1}\\ A_{n-1,d-1,r+s-1}C(a_n)\end{pmatrix}.\] Here \(C(a_n)\) is square-root convolution, with \(C_{j,c}=\binom{1/2}{c-j}a_n^{c-j}\) for \(j\le c\); its coefficients lie in \(\mathbb Z[1/2]\). If the degree-\(d\) lower series is normal, (JT) gives the exact remaining determinant in the new parameter \(a_n\). It does not require degree-\((d-1)\) normality; this matters at \(d=2\), where the degree-one Catalan exceptions persist. The lower block at \(a_n=0\) is a subset of the upper row space, so this residual vanishes at zero. Proving that it is not the zero polynomial, including its higher coefficients at resonant primes, is the missing induction statement. All entries are known, but the claim is not established merely by writing (JT).

No parameter-degree theorem is inferred from this fraction-field Schur complement. The original graded threshold problem must retain the polynomial compatibility class and its marked coordinate. Inverting \(\det E_0\) is appropriate for testing generic Hasse rank, but can discard precisely the degree obstruction in open statement 3.

27 September 2026 — A joint leading coefficient proves normality in unbounded degree progressions in every dimension

Working exact integral coefficient formula and all-dimensional normality theorem on specified degree progressions. Unrestricted small-prime normality remains open. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question. Open statement 2 requires nonvanishing of the combined Hasse determinant, not separate normality of its two summands. The composition review isolates that issue. This cycle computes a coefficient of the actual joint determinant, including its complete integer normalization. The coefficient has a classical shifted Catalan Hankel factor. Controlling that factor over a residue band gives a positive all-dimensional theorem: a fixed prime can support arbitrarily large degrees in a specified arithmetic progression. No larger-dimensional normality matrix is computed.

General statement. lem:cube-joint-leading-coefficient is an exact polynomial identity for every \(n\ge2,d\ge1\). Using the proved dimension-four theorem as the base, thm:cube-periodic-normality-band gives initial-segment orders for every \(n\ge5\), every integer \(b\ge n-2\), every prime \(p>2^{n-1}b\), and every degree \(d=b+tp\), \(t\ge0\). The bound depends on the fixed residue representative \(b\), not on the arbitrarily large degree \(d\). This proves an infinite subrange of conj:cube-refined-initial-segment-law; it does not prove the unrestricted conjecture or a pre-stable threshold formula.

The exact coefficient of the new root parameter

Lemma (lem:cube-joint-leading-coefficient). Use the full coefficient matrix of the basis \[T^qz_S,\qquad 2q+|S|\le d,\qquad z_i=\frac{1-\sqrt{1+4y_iT}}2\in\mathbb Z[y_i][[T]],\] through columns \(T^0,\ldots,T^{N_{2,n}(d)-1}\), and denote its determinant by \(\Delta_{n,d}\). Put \(\Delta_{n,0}=1\). This is the original integral determinant: the constant basis row and constant jet column can be removed without changing it. Order the rows recursively by whether the last root is absent or present, keeping the induced lower-dimensional order within each block. Set \[r=N_{2,n-1}(d),\quad s=N_{2,n-1}(d-1),\quad h=r-s\ge0.\] Then \(\deg_{y_n}\Delta_{n,d}\le rs\), and \[[y_n^{rs}]\Delta_{n,d} =(-1)^{sh+s(s-1)/2+s}\,H_s^{(h)}\, \Delta_{n-1,d}\Delta_{n-1,d-1},\tag{LC}\] where, writing \(C_j=\frac1{j+1}\binom{2j}j\), \[H_s^{(h)}=\det(C_{h+i+j})_{0\le i,j<s} =\prod_{1\le i\le j\le h-1}\frac{2s+i+j}{i+j}.\tag{CH}\] An empty product is one. In another fixed ordering only the overall sign changes. Identity (LC) is an identity of integer polynomials; after specialization, its displayed coefficient may be zero and the degree may drop.

Cauchy–Binet on the actual coupled matrix. First use \(w_i=\sqrt{1+a_iT}\) and denote the full determinant in the \(T^qw_S\) basis by \(D_{n,d}(a)\). Work over \(\mathbb Z[1/2]\). The row split is \[\begin{pmatrix}E\\FC(a_n)\end{pmatrix},\] where \(E\) has \(r\) rows, \(F\) has \(s\) rows, both have \(r+s\) columns, and \[C(a)_{j,k}=\begin{cases}\binom{1/2}{k-j}a^{k-j},&j\le k,\\0,&j>k.\end{cases}\] Expand the determinant by its last \(s\) rows, and expand each selected minor of \(FC\) by Cauchy–Binet. If its selected output columns are \(K\) and selected intermediate indices are \(J\), each a sorted set of size \(s\), its \(a\)-degree is \(\sum K-\sum J\) whenever the minor is nonzero. The maximal possible difference is \(rs\). It is attained uniquely by \[K=\{r,r+1,\ldots,r+s-1\},\qquad J=\{0,1,\ldots,s-1\}.\] The complementary upper columns are then \(0,\ldots,r-1\). Consequently \[[a_n^{rs}]D_{n,d}=D_{n-1,d}D_{n-1,d-1}\, \det\left(\binom{1/2}{r+j-i}\right)_{0\le i,j<s}.\tag{CB}\] No normality assumption was made in deriving this identity. In particular, zero lower minors or a zero scalar are not silently declared units.

The Catalan factor and its classical product. Reverse the rows of the last determinant. All its indices become \(h+1+i+j\ge1\), so \[\binom{1/2}{k}=\frac{(-1)^{k-1}C_{k-1}}{2^{2k-1}}\] allows row and column factors to be removed. The result is \[\det\left(\binom{1/2}{r+j-i}\right) =(-1)^{sh+s(s-1)/2}\,2^{-2rs+s}H_s^{(h)}.\tag{TC}\] Formula (CH) is classical; see Cigler, equation (1.1). Here is a complete independent verification so that its arithmetic use does not depend on a characteristic-zero determinant division.

Let \(P_s^{(h)}\) be the product in (CH), including \(P_0^{(h)}=1\). For \(s=1\), successively adding the pairs with last index \(h-1\) gives \[\frac{P_1^{(h)}}{P_1^{(h-1)}}=\frac{2(2h-1)}{h+1}\quad(h\ge1),\] with \(P_1^{(0)}=1\); these are exactly the Catalan ratios. Thus the determinant and product agree for \(s=0,1\). Desnanot–Jacobi condensation for the Hankel matrix gives, for \(s\ge2\), \[H_s^{(h)}H_{s-2}^{(h+2)} =H_{s-1}^{(h)}H_{s-1}^{(h+2)}-(H_{s-1}^{(h+1)})^2.\tag{DC}\] The product has the same recurrence. Indeed elementary cancellation gives \[\frac{P_s^{(h)}P_{s-2}^{(h+2)}}{P_{s-1}^{(h)}P_{s-1}^{(h+2)}} =\frac{(s-1)(2s-1)}{(s+h)(2s+2h-1)},\] \[\frac{(P_{s-1}^{(h+1)})^2}{P_{s-1}^{(h)}P_{s-1}^{(h+2)}} =\frac{(2h+1)(2s+h-1)}{(s+h)(2s+2h-1)}.\] The right-hand sides sum to one. For example, the cancellation in the first formula follows by taking the ratio of the products \[\frac{P_s^{(h)}}{P_{s-1}^{(h)}}= \prod_{j=1}^{h-1}\frac{(2s+2j)(2s+2j-1)}{(2s+j)(2s+j-1)}\] and the same expression with \((s,h)\) replaced by \((s-1,h+2)\). The second formula follows by adjoining the last index in each of the two successive \(h\)-products. All these calculations take place over \(\mathbb Q\), where \(P_{s-2}^{(h+2)}\) is positive and nonzero. Induction on \(s\) using (DC) proves (CH) for every \(h\ge0\). Since its left side is an integer determinant, it is an integral identity. Reduction modulo a prime is performed only afterward; denominators on the product side will be checked explicitly before use.

Return to the original integral normalization. Put \[L_{n,d}=\sum_{2q+|S|\le d}|S|.\] With \(a_i=4y_i\), the change \(w_S=\prod_{i\in S}(1-2z_i)\) is triangular on the downward-closed set of basis indices, with diagonal \((-2)^{|S|}\). Thus \[D_{n,d}(a)=(-2)^{L_{n,d}}\Delta_{n,d}(a/4),\] and the row split gives \[L_{n,d}=L_{n-1,d}+L_{n-1,d-1}+s.\] Converting the coefficient in (CB) therefore multiplies (TC) by \(4^{rs}(-2)^{-s}\). Its power of two cancels exactly, leaving the sign and the integer factor in (LC). This proves both the degree bound and the formula over \(\mathbb Z\). \(\square\)

An all-dimensional residue band

Theorem (thm:cube-periodic-normality-band). Let \(n\ge5\), let \(b\ge n-2\) be an integer, and let \(k\) be any field of positive characteristic \(p\) satisfying \[p>2^{n-1}b.\] Then the generic root-curve series has, for every integer \(t\ge0\) and \(d=b+tp\), \[\operatorname{Ord}_n(d)=\{0,1,\ldots,N_{2,n}(d)-1\}.\tag{PN}\] More generally, with the same \(n,b,p\), the conclusion holds for every nonnegative \(d\) whose residue modulo \(p\) lies in \(\{n-2,n-1,\ldots,b\}\). This includes arbitrarily large degrees for a fixed characteristic.

Proof by a residue-band induction. Fix the outer parameters \(n,b,p\). For each \(4\le m\le n\), prove normality for every degree \(e\ge m-2\) whose residue \(c\) modulo \(p\) lies in \(\{m-2,\ldots,b\}\). The assumption implies \(p>b\), so these are literal least nonnegative residues. At \(m=4\), all these degrees are at least two, and the all-odd dimension-four theorem is the base.

Suppose \(m\ge5\) and the band is proved at \(m-1\). The two lower series have degrees \(e\) and \(e-1\), and residues \(c\) and \(c-1\). Both degrees are at least \(m-3\), and both residues lie in \(\{m-3,\ldots,b\}\). Thus both lower determinants in (LC) are nonzero. There is no invocation of degree-one normality: at the bottom, \(e-1\ge2\).

For these degrees put \(h=2^{m-2}\). The complete root-curve dimension formula gives \[r=N_{2,m-1}(e),\qquad s=N_{2,m-1}(e-1) =h\left(e-\frac{m-2}{2}\right),\qquad r-s=h.\tag{NS}\] This formula is valid at the endpoint \(e=m-2\). One can check it directly without a nonspeciality shortcut: the generating series for the counts is \[\sum_{q\ge0}N_{2,l}(q)z^q=\frac{(1+z)^{l-1}}{(1-z)^2}.\] For \(l=m-1\), summing its coefficients gives the linear formula for \(q\ge l-2\); at the endpoint the last omitted summand is zero. Both \(q=e\) and \(q=e-1\) lie in this range, which proves (NS).

Every denominator in (CH) is \(i+j\le2h-2<p\). Modulo \(p\), each numerator \(2s+i+j\) equals the integer \[h(2c-m+2)+i+j.\] It is positive because \(c\ge m-2\). Its maximum is at most \[h(2b-m+4)-2\le2hb-2\le2^{n-1}b-2<p.\] Hence every numerator and denominator of (CH) is a unit modulo \(p\), and \(H_s^{(h)}\ne0\) in \(k\). Formula (LC) now exhibits a nonzero coefficient of the full dimension-\(m\) determinant, because its two lower determinants are nonzero polynomials and their coefficient ring is a domain. The combined determinant is therefore nonzero. This completes the induction and proves (PN), including the enlarged band. \(\square\)

What this advances, and what it does not

The earlier large-characteristic theorem required \(p>2^{n-1}d\), using a pole-degree bound to keep all relevant orders below \(p\). At \(d=b\), the present result is within that range. At every \(d=b+tp\) with \(t\ge1\), that old inequality fails, whereas (PN) still applies. Thus the new statement proves normality for an infinite family of degrees in the previously unresolved small-prime window, simultaneously in every dimension at least five.

This does not settle all residue classes, primes too small for a nonempty band, or the special range \(2\le d<n-2\). Those cases remain covered as questions by the exact larger-ambient interpolation criterion, not by this proof. The theorem gives generic stable orders at the specified degrees; it does not compute pre-stable parameter degrees, prove noncollision squarefreeness, or supply a full per-order formula.

Falsifying controls. The leading scalar is not always a power of two. The same exact formula gives \(H_2^{(2)}=3\) and \(H_4^{(4)}=1001=7\cdot11\cdot13\). Thus lower normality alone still does not make the joint leading coefficient a unit. At degree one, \(s=1,h=n-1\), so the scalar is the Catalan number \(C_{n-1}\), consistent with the recorded Catalan exceptions. These controls explain both why the explicit residue inequalities are necessary to this proof and why it does not contradict the normal-summand counterexample.

Exact verification. The GP script checks the condensation ratio identity symbolically, checks the Toeplitz-to-Hankel factors on four small normalization controls, and computes the original \((n,d)=(2,2)\) determinant of size five. The last test gives \[\Delta_{2,2}=-y_2^3y_1^6+3y_2^4y_1^5-3y_2^5y_1^4+y_2^6y_1^3,\] whose \(y_2^6\) coefficient is exactly \(y_1^3\), matching (LC) with \(r=3,s=2,h=1\), \(\Delta_{1,2}=y_1^2\), \(\Delta_{1,1}=-y_1\). The odd factor three is a negative control against an unjustified unit assertion. These checks validate identities and normalization, not a sample of (PN). The complete output is retained. The all-dimensional conclusion comes from the proof above.

Verification gate. The medium pre-proof reviewer checked that the new progression range is not covered by the old large-characteristic bound, and checked the residue-band induction and unique maximal Cauchy–Binet term. Its correction distinguishing the square-root determinant from the original integral determinant is incorporated in (LC). The dimension-four arithmetic, dimensional convolution and original determinant-criterion proofs were reread, along with the exact old large-characteristic statement and proof. Cigler's formula is identified as classical and independently proved here. A fresh-context medium-reasoning correctness reviewer passed the maximal-term argument, signs and normalization, condensation proof, endpoint counts, preserved residue bands, unit bounds and genuinely new range. No required mathematical correction or substantive unused hypothesis was found; its clarification that the theorem concerns generic parameters is incorporated.

Assessment and next step. A necessary nonvanishing implication now has a positive all-dimensional range beyond the degree-dependent large-prime theorem. The successful step is control of a coefficient of the joint determinant; separate block normality is used only after its arithmetic factor has been proved nonzero. On cube-odd-characteristic, next examine the remaining residue classes and small primes through other coefficients of that same determinant, preserving the exact integral normalization. Test whether a bounded collection of coefficient factors has no common odd divisor, rather than dividing away a bad leading factor. The full goal remains open.

Process. A classical constant-shift determinant evaluation replaced large-degree matrix calculations; the band induction keeps degree-one exceptions out of its base and avoids a dimension-by-dimension certificate list. No framework change was needed.

27 September 2026 — Frobenius leaves arbitrarily long zero windows at the nominal top of a normal determinant

Working modular degree bound and all-parameter obstruction to a fixed highest-coefficient window. Generic normality and the remaining per-order formula are still open in higher dimensions. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question. Open statement 2 still requires a nonzero coefficient of the actual combined Hasse determinant outside the proved residue bands. The previous cycle suggested using other coefficients when the leading Catalan factor vanishes. This cycle tests the specific sufficient mechanism of looking a fixed number of positions below the nominal highest degree. Frobenius refutes that mechanism even in the already-normal dimension-four family. This does not refute joint coefficient content or an adaptive coefficient choice.

General statement. lem:cube-frobenius-parameter-degree bounds the last-parameter degree of the reduced determinant in every dimension, using any characteristic power above its jet length. cor:cube-unbounded-top-coefficient-window gives unbounded consecutive zero strips in a family of nonzero determinants. Neither is a new finite normality check. The all-dimensional missing implication remains nonvanishing of the full determinant; the outcome changes the next test by excluding a fixed window at its nominal top.

A Frobenius bound on parameter degree

Lemma (lem:cube-frobenius-parameter-degree). Let \(n\ge2,d\ge1\), and set \[ r=N_{2,n-1}(d),\qquad s=N_{2,n-1}(d-1),\qquad N=r+s=N_{2,n}(d). \] Let \(k\) be a field of odd characteristic \(p\), and let \(q=p^e\ge N\), \(e\ge1\). For the original integral determinant \(\Delta_{n,d}(y)\) of the joint coefficient lemma, its reduction \(\overline\Delta_{n,d}\) satisfies \[ \deg_{y_n}\overline\Delta_{n,d}\le\min\left\{rs,\frac{s(q+1)}2\right\}.\tag{FD} \] The bound includes the zero polynomial, whose degree is taken to be \(-\infty\). It asserts no generic nonvanishing by itself.

Proof. Work first in \(k[a,T]/(T^N)\). Put \(\alpha=(q+1)/2\). The Frobenius identity gives \[ \big((1+aT)^\alpha\big)^2=(1+aT)^{q+1}=(1+aT)(1+a^qT^q)\equiv1+aT\pmod{T^N}. \] There is a unique square root with constant term one: if two such roots have the same square, their sum has constant term two and is a unit, so their difference is zero. Consequently \[ \sqrt{1+aT}\equiv(1+aT)^\alpha\pmod{T^N}.\tag{FT} \] Every coefficient through \(T^{N-1}\) has degree in \(a\) at most \(\alpha\). This uses a polynomial identity in characteristic \(p\), not a factorial division.

In square-root coordinates \(w_i^2=1+a_iT\), order the rows by whether the last root occurs. The actual \(N\)-jet matrix is \[ \begin{pmatrix}E\\FC(a_n)\end{pmatrix}, \] with \(r\) upper rows and \(s\) lower rows. Both \(E\) and \(F\) are independent of \(a_n\), and \(C\) multiplies truncated series by \(w_n\). By (FT), each entry of the lower block has \(a_n\)-degree at most \(\alpha\), whereas the upper block has degree zero. Each determinant term takes one entry from each row, so \(\deg_{a_n}\overline D_{n,d}\le s\alpha\). The earlier Cauchy–Binet argument also gives the characteristic-independent bound \(rs\).

The exact normalization is \[ D_{n,d}(a)=(-2)^{L_{n,d}}\Delta_{n,d}(a/4),\qquad L_{n,d}=\sum_{2j+|S|\le d}|S|. \] Both two and four are units in \(k\), so this scalar and invertible parameter scaling preserve degree. This proves (FD). It is a bound on the reduction modulo \(p\), not on the integral polynomial over \(\mathbb Z\). \(\square\)

A zero strip whose width is unbounded

Corollary (cor:cube-unbounded-top-coefficient-window). For each prime \(p\equiv5\pmod8\), \(p\ge13\), put \(d=(p+3)/8\). In dimension four, \[ r=4d,\quad s=4d-4,\quad N=8d-4=p-1. \] The polynomial \(\overline\Delta_{4,d}\) is nonzero, but all its coefficients at the \(s\) exponents \[ rs-s+1,\ rs-s+2,\ldots,rs \] in \(y_4\) vanish identically as polynomials in the other parameters. These widths \(s=(p-5)/2\) are unbounded. Thus no fixed-width consecutive window anchored at the nominal top exponent \(rs\) can certify generic normality for all odd primes and degrees, even just in dimension four.

Proof. Since \(d\ge2\), the dimension-three count gives the displayed \(r,s\). Take \(q=p\) in (FD); its hypotheses hold because \(N=p-1\). Then \[ \alpha=(p+1)/2=4d-1=r-1, \qquad \deg_{y_4}\overline\Delta_{4,d}\le s(r-1)=rs-s. \] This proves the stated coefficient vanishing. The all-odd dimension-four theorem proves that the full reduced determinant remains nonzero. The conclusion therefore distinguishes a failed coefficient certificate from a failure of generic normality.

For completeness, arbitrarily large primes congruent to five modulo eight require no distribution theorem here. If there were only finitely many, let \(x\) be their product, including five. Then \(x\) is odd and \(x^2+4\equiv5\pmod8\). Any prime divisor \(v\) of \(x^2+4\) is odd and does not divide \(x\). Modulo \(v\), \((x/2)^2=-1\), so an element has order four in \(\mathbb F_v^\times\). Hence \(v\equiv1\pmod4\), and thus \(v\equiv1\) or \(5\pmod8\). Their product, with multiplicities, is five modulo eight, so at least one prime divisor is five modulo eight. It is absent from the assumed list, since every listed prime divides \(x\) and therefore cannot divide \(x^2+4\). This contradiction proves infinitude and hence unbounded \(s\). Given any fixed width \(W\), choose such a prime with \(s\ge W\). Its \(W\) highest nominal coefficient positions all vanish while the determinant is nonzero. \(\square\)

Scope, controls and next action

Controls. The implication is uniform and comes from the exact truncated-square identity. No prime sweep or larger matrix computation is needed. The argument permits all coefficients in the displayed strip to vanish simultaneously; dividing its integral coefficients by the chosen prime before reduction can produce nonzero coefficients, but these are no longer coefficients of the original reduced determinant and cannot certify its nonvanishing. It does not claim that the actual degree is exactly \(rs-s\), or exclude a fixed number of suitably chosen interior coefficients. A window measured from the actual reduced degree has a different meaning, and finding that degree already requires information not provided by the nominal leading term. Degree-one Catalan exceptions and normal-summand composition obstructions are unaffected.

Verification gate. Re-read the complete joint coefficient proof, its integral normalization, and the dimension-four all-odd normality proof; inspected their recorded dependency and refinement links. The medium pre-proof reviewer found no duplicate in the two dependency entries and bounded searches, confirmed the prime-power version and corrected the wording to refer explicitly to the reduced determinant. A fresh-context medium-reasoning correctness reviewer passed both proofs, the prime-power normalization, endpoint counts, infinitude argument and fixed-width quantifiers. Its required clarification is incorporated: division by the prime before reduction changes the coefficients and is not a certificate for the original reduced determinant. No substantive unused hypothesis was found.

Assessment and next step. This closes a proposed shortcut, not the stable-order conjecture. On cube-odd-characteristic, next examine the characteristic-dependent support of the convolution matrix, allowing coefficient positions to move with Frobenius blocks. The necessary endpoint is a nonzero minor of the coupled matrix, with a coefficient proved nonzero after reduction; sparse support alone does not preclude cancellation between terms. Use the new zero strip as a required control and the normal-summand counterexample as the transversality control. Keep the pre-stable polynomial-degree question separate.

Process. A direct Frobenius identity answered the fixed-window test without deriving a succession of subleading formulas or running case sweeps; no framework change was needed.

27 September 2026 — The moving Frobenius coefficient is nonzero on an unbounded prime-power family

Working moving-coefficient identity and sharp modular parameter degree in dimension four. Normality in this dimension was already known; higher-dimensional normality remains open. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question. The zero-strip obstruction defeats a fixed nominal top window. The next possible certificate is the coefficient at the characteristic-dependent degree bound itself. This cycle derives its actual coupled matrix, then proves nonvanishing on the whole family that produced the zero strips, including characteristic powers rather than only primes. A rational interpolation calculation supplies a unit scalar. It is a test of the coefficient mechanism for open statement 2, not an additional normality theorem for a previously unknown dimension.

General statement. lem:cube-frobenius-moving-coefficient identifies the coefficient for every dimension and every odd characteristic power above the jet length. thm:cube-four-frobenius-sharp-degree proves that the bound is sharp for every \(q=p^e\ge13\) with \(q\equiv5\pmod8\), at \(n=4,d=(q+3)/8\). This is an infinite family at each prime \(p\equiv5\pmod8\), taking odd exponents large enough. The full odd-field per-order goal remains open.

Sharp degree on the zero-strip family

Theorem (thm:cube-four-frobenius-sharp-degree). Let \(k\) have odd characteristic \(p\). For every \(q=p^e\ge13\), \(e\ge1\), with \(q\equiv5\pmod8\), put \[ d=(q+3)/8,\qquad r=4d,\quad s=4d-4,\quad N=8d-4=q-1,\quad \alpha=4d-1=(q+1)/2. \] Then the original determinant satisfies \[ \deg_{y_4}\overline\Delta_{4,d}=s\alpha=(4d-4)(4d-1). \tag{SD} \] In particular, the coefficient in (MI) is nonzero. This proves that the earlier zero strip ends exactly at its Frobenius bound on this family. Generic normality in dimension four was already established independently.

1. A collision of the actual two blocks. In (MC), \(E\) is the length-\(N\) matrix of \(V_{3,d}\) and \(F\) that of \(V_{3,d-1}\). Set \(a_3=\varepsilon\) and let \(v=\sqrt{1+\varepsilon T}-1\). For each \(S\subseteq\{1,2\}\), the block in \(V_{3,j}\) has the form \[ w_S\left(k[T]_{\le\lfloor(j-|S|)/2\rfloor} +\sqrt{1+\varepsilon T}\,k[T]_{\le\lfloor(j-|S|-1)/2\rfloor}\right). \] Over \(k(\varepsilon)\), these are exactly the polynomials in \(v\) of degrees \(0,\ldots,j-|S|\), multiplied by \(w_S\): use \(\varepsilon T=v^2+2v\) and \(\sqrt{1+\varepsilon T}=1+v\). The even and odd leading degrees give an invertible triangular change of basis. A negative bound means an empty block.

Consequently one may use the rows \(w_S(2v/\varepsilon)^b\), \(0\le b\le j-|S|\), as a basis over the fraction field. Since \[ 2v/\varepsilon=2T/(\sqrt{1+\varepsilon T}+1)\longrightarrow T, \] their reductions give precisely \[ U_j=\bigoplus_{S\subseteq\{1,2\}}w_S k[T]_{\le j-|S|}. \] No odd integer is divided out. The character blocks are independent over \(k(T)\), so this gives their full dimension. Make this row change separately in \(E\) and \(F\); multiplying the second set of rows by \(T^\alpha\) commutes with the change. Both row-change determinants are nonzero over \(k(\varepsilon)\). It therefore suffices to prove that the limiting length-\(N\) matrix of \[ U_d\ +\ T^\alpha U_{d-1}\tag{RL} \] is invertible. This is the first balanced collision of the original weighted blocks; it is not the further unbalanced confluence that produced the earlier arithmetic resonances.

2. Rational coordinates and the exact coefficient constraint. Over \(k(u)\), with \(u\) transcendental, take \[ T=\frac{(x^2-u^2)(x^2-u^{-2})}{x^2},\quad w_1=\frac{x+x^{-1}}{u+u^{-1}},\quad w_2=\frac{x-x^{-1}}{u-u^{-1}}. \tag{RP} \] Then \(w_i^2=1+a_iT\), where \(a_1=(u+u^{-1})^{-2}\) and \(a_2=(u-u^{-1})^{-2}\) are distinct and nonzero. At \(P:x=u\), \(T=0\), \(w_1=w_2=1\), and \(dT/dx=2(u^4-1)/u^3\ne0\). Thus \(x-u\) and \(T\) define the same jet-length filtration. For every \(j\ge1\), \[ U_j=x^{-2j}\{P(x):\deg P\le4j,\ P(0)=[x^{4j}]P\}.\tag{UP} \] Indeed each basis row lies in the Laurent range \([-2j,2j]\); only \(T^j\) reaches its two extreme exponents, with equal coefficients. This proves inclusion in the displayed space. Both spaces have dimension \((j+1)+2j+(j-1)=4j\), by the independent character blocks, so inclusion is equality.

3. The one upper row and the lower matching condition. A relation in the kernel of (RL) is \(f+T^\alpha g=0\) modulo \(T^N\), with \(f\in U_d\) and \(g\in U_{d-1}\). Necessarily \(f\) vanishes to order at least \(\alpha=r-1\) at \(x=u\). By (UP), its numerator is \((x-u)^\alpha(A+Bx)\). As \(\alpha\) is odd, the equality of its constant and leading coefficients forces \(B=-u^\alpha A\). Thus the possible \(f\)'s form exactly the line generated by \[ f=x^{-r/2}(x-u)^\alpha(1-u^\alpha x).\tag{FL} \] If \(f=0\), the remaining condition forces \(g\) to vanish to order \(N-\alpha=s+1\), impossible for a nonzero numerator of degree at most \(s\). Hence a kernel exists exactly when this displayed nonzero \(f\) can be matched by some \(-T^\alpha g\).

Cancel the factor \((x-u)^\alpha\) in \(f/T^\alpha\), and multiply by \(x^{s/2}\). The resulting regular function near \(u\) is \[ H(x)=\frac{x^{2\alpha-2}(1-u^\alpha x)}{(x+u)^\alpha(x^2-u^{-2})^\alpha}. \tag{HF} \] The exponent follows from \(s/2-r/2=-2\). Matching the remaining \(s+1\) jets is equivalent to asking whether the unique Taylor polynomial of \(H\) about \(u\), through degree \(s\), belongs to the polynomial space in (UP) for \(j=d-1\). These are Hasse/Taylor coefficients in the quotient ring, with no factorial inversion. The sign of \(g\) is immaterial to the linear constraint. Define \[ \Lambda(H)=\operatorname{Taylor}_{u,s}(H)(0) -[x^s]\operatorname{Taylor}_{u,s}(H). \] Then (RL) is invertible exactly when \(\Lambda(H)\ne0\).

4. The scalar has a unit leading term. Set \(x=uz\). Since \(2\alpha-2=q-1\), \[ H(uz)=(-1)^\alpha u^{3\alpha-2}G_u(z),\qquad G_u(z)=\frac{z^{q-1}(1-u^{\alpha+1}z)}{(z+1)^\alpha(1-u^4z^2)^\alpha}. \] Taylor coefficients of \(G_u\) at \(z=1\) belong to \(k[[u]]\), since its denominators have nonzero constant terms there. Let \(A_u(z)=\operatorname{Taylor}_{1,s}(G_u)(z)\), a polynomial of degree at most \(s\). Changing coordinates gives \[ \Lambda(H)=(-1)^\alpha u^{3\alpha-2} \left(A_u(0)-u^{-s}[z^s]A_u\right).\tag{LF} \] Its second term has strictly smaller possible \(u\)-valuation because \(s=\alpha-3\ge4\). We show that its leading coefficient is a unit.

Modulo \((z-1)^q\), Frobenius gives \(z^q=1\), \((z+1)^q=2\). Since \(s

Thus \([z^s]A_u=\alpha-1+O(u)\), while \(A_u(0)\in k[[u]]\). Formula (LF), with \(\alpha\) odd, yields \[ \Lambda(H)=(\alpha-1)u^{3\alpha-2-s}+O(u^{3\alpha-1-s}) =(\alpha-1)u^{q+2}+O(u^{q+3})\ne0. \] This proves invertibility of the rational limiting matrix. The independent row changes before the collision therefore prove that the original moving coefficient in (MC) is a nonzero polynomial. A nonzero value on this parameter family suffices; no assertion of nonvanishing at every specialization is made. Formula (MI) transfers nonvanishing to the original integral normalization. The preceding Frobenius bound supplies \(\deg\overline\Delta\le s\alpha\), so equality follows. \(\square\)

Working graph-divisor obstruction and route review. The doubled-cycle graph is a proposed degeneration control, not an identified root-curve skeleton. Higher-dimensional normality and pre-stable degrees remain open. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Obstacle

The periodic band theorem advanced the all-dimensional stable-order implication. The next two cycles refuted fixed nominal top windows and proved that a moving coefficient survives on their full dimension-four prime-power family. The latter is a valid joint calculation, but it remains in a dimension whose normality was already known. Another refinement confined to that family would not discharge the remaining obligation in conj:cube-refined-initial-segment-law. Open statement 3 also still needs polynomial parameter degrees, not just generic matrix rank.

General statement. lem:cube-doubled-cycle-tropical-obstruction tests a different proposed sufficient mechanism: use divisor-rank specialization to exclude exceptional sections on a graph. On every equal-pair doubled cycle with at least four vertices, every point is tropical Weierstrass for every canonical power of exponent at least two. This gives an all-parameter obstruction to ordinary rank certificates on that graph family. It does not identify those graphs with the root-curve skeletons, refute other graphs, or rule out refined tropical information retaining the actual linear series.

The needed implication. For a smooth root curve and its complete degree-\(d\) space of dimension \(N\), normality at an unramified marked point means \(H^0(dH-NP)=0\). Baker's specialization inequality, Lemma 2.8 and Corollary 2.10, supplies a sufficient test: over a complete discretely valued field with algebraically closed residue field, on an actual strongly semistable regular model, if the specialized divisor has rank \(-1\), the algebraic space is zero. The direction is crucial; an effective graph divisor need not lift to an algebraic section. No assumption that a curve is already classical is needed for this rank inequality.

An entire family where the ordinary graph test cannot work

Lemma (lem:cube-doubled-cycle-tropical-obstruction). Let \(\Gamma\) be the compact metric graph obtained from a cycle with \(m\ge4\) vertices by replacing each edge with two parallel edges of equal positive length. Lengths belonging to different pairs may differ. Its genus is \(g=m+1\), and its canonical divisor is \(K=2\sum_{i=1}^m v_i\). For every integer \(d\ge2\), put \[ N=2md-m=r_\Gamma(dK)+1. \] For every point \(P\in\Gamma\), the divisor \(dK-NP\) is linearly equivalent to an effective divisor. Thus the ordinary tropical Weierstrass locus of \(dK\) is the whole graph.

Proof. We use metric-graph Riemann–Roch in its divisor-rank sense, Mikhalkin–Zharkov, Theorem 7.3. In particular, a divisor of degree at least the genus is equivalent to an effective one; a divisor of degree greater than \(2g-2\) has rank equal to degree minus genus. Since \(d\ge2\), these statements give \[ r_\Gamma(dK)=2md-(m+1)=N-1. \] The degree count \(g=2m-m+1\) and the valence-four formula for \(K\) give the other stated quantities.

Choose an edge pair containing \(P\); if \(P\) is a vertex, choose either incident pair. Construct a metric graph \(\Gamma'\) with the same \(m\) vertices as follows. Retain the two chosen edges separately, doubling their lengths. Merge each of the other equal-length pairs into a single edge of that original length. The graph has \(m+1\) edges and genus two: topologically it is a theta graph with possible valence-two vertices.

Define \(\varphi:\Gamma\to\Gamma'\) to be the identity on the vertices, to expand each retained edge by two, and to map each edge of every merged pair isometrically onto its target edge. At the endpoints of the chosen pair, each retained target direction receives slope two and the other direction receives slopes \(1+1\). At each other original vertex, both target directions receive \(1+1\). The map is therefore harmonic of degree two. On interiors the same local-degree statement is immediate. If \(P'=\varphi(P)\), then \[ \varphi^*(P')=2P,\qquad \varphi^*\left(\sum_{i=1}^m v_i'\right)=K. \tag{HP} \] For an interior \(P\), its chosen target edge has only that one preimage, with expansion two. The vertex case also has one preimage of local degree two.

Here pullback preserves principal and effective divisors. Explicitly, for an integer-slope piecewise-linear function \(f\) on \(\Gamma'\), the function \(f\circ\varphi\) still has integer slopes. Summing its outgoing slopes over each target direction multiplies the target sum by the common local degree, so \(\operatorname{div}(f\circ\varphi)=\varphi^*\operatorname{div}(f)\). Pullback coefficients of an effective divisor are nonnegative. These observations justify the use of (HP) without an unproved lifting assertion.

Put \(t=\lceil N/2\rceil\). The divisor \[ A=d\sum_{i=1}^m v_i'-tP' \] on \(\Gamma'\) has degree \[ md-\left\lceil\frac{2md-m}{2}\right\rceil =\lfloor m/2\rfloor\ge2=g(\Gamma'). \] Riemann–Roch therefore gives \(A\sim E\ge0\). Pulling back yields \(dK-2tP\sim\varphi^*E\ge0\). Adding the effective divisor \((2t-N)P\), of degree zero or one, proves \(dK-NP\sim\varphi^*E+(2t-N)P\ge0\). This holds for every point and every allowed length choice. Since \(N=r(dK)+1\), it proves the Weierstrass assertion. \(\square\)

Scope of the obstruction. For \(m=4\), the genus is five and \(N=8d-4\), matching the numerical dimension-four canonical-power setup. This motivated the graph control; matching genus and dimension does not identify a degeneration. Even if such a model with the correct divisor is constructed, the lemma shows that ordinary rank specialization on it cannot prove normality at any graph point. An actual curve with a given graph carries more information than all effective graph divisors. The proof makes no assertion that every graph function lifts.

Exact graph control. Before the uniform proof, the GP control subdivided every edge of the equal-length doubled four-cycle once. There are twelve vertices, sixteen edges and genus five. At \(d=2\), with \(P\) the first midpoint, it tested effectivity of \(2K-12P\), of degree four. There are at most \(\binom{15}{4}=1365\) vertex-supported effective candidates. One grounded Laplacian inverse was reused; the search stopped at candidate thirteen, finding \(E=2v_1+2v_2\). In the saved vertex order, \[ 2K-12P-E=L(-2,-2,2,2,-8,-2,0,0,2,2,0,0)^{\mathsf T}, \] where \(L\) is the positive graph Laplacian. The full matrix, determinant 1024, divisor and integral potential are retained in the output. Direct multiplication checks the certificate. This decides the proposed midpoint test negatively; the lemma then eliminates all point and length sweeps on this entire graph family.
