Question. The route review required the actual cover graph and the marked divisor before using tropical specialization. This cycle constructs both from the branch inertia. One exact dimension-five test gave an effective divisor, rather than an excluding point. A point-fixing symmetry then upgrades that outcome to all dimensions, all points and all nonspecial degrees on this entire chain family. No further graph-point, degree or dimension sweep is needed.

General statement. lem:cube-tame-chain-model constructs a totally degenerate family of root covers for every \(n\ge3\) in every characteristic different from two, with its divisor \(H\) identified. thm:cube-chain-tropical-rank-obstruction proves that \(dH-NP\) is graph-effective up to equivalence for every point whenever \(n\ge4,d\ge n-2\). Thus ordinary graph rank cannot discharge open statement 2 on this family. This closes that proposed sufficient mechanism; it neither disproves conj:cube-refined-initial-segment-law nor computes the graded thresholds of statement 3.

The cover, its graph and its infinity divisor

Lemma (lem:cube-tame-chain-model). Let \(k\) be algebraically closed of characteristic different from two. Fix \(n\ge3\), and positive rational numbers \(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_{n-2}\). After a common rescaling of lengths, there is a family over a complete discrete valuation ring with residue field \(k\) and fraction field \(K\), whose smooth generic curve is a root cover \[ K(T)(\sqrt{1+a_1T},\ldots,\sqrt{1+a_nT}) \] with distinct nonzero parameters after a finite field extension and choice of an unramified origin. Its semistable special fibre has rational components, with the following metric dual graph \(\Gamma_n\). This is existence of a degenerating family, not a claim about the reduction of every fixed root curve.

Let \(G=\mathbb F_2^n\), let \(b_1,\ldots,b_n\) be its standard basis, and put \(b_{n+1}=\sum_{i=1}^n b_i\). Define \[ c_j=\sum_{i=1}^{j+1}b_i\quad(1\le j\le n-2), \] \[ B_1=\langle b_1,b_2\rangle,\quad B_j=\langle c_{j-1},b_{j+1}\rangle\ (2\le j\le n-2),\quad B_{n-1}=\langle b_n,b_{n+1}\rangle. \] The vertices in layer \(j\) are \(G/B_j\); the edges from layer \(j\) to layer \(j+1\) are \(G/\langle c_j\rangle\), each joining the two cosets containing its representative. Every edge of this layer has length \(\ell_j\). There are \[ V=(n-1)2^{n-2},\qquad E=(n-2)2^{n-1},\qquad g=1+(n-3)2^{n-2}. \] The generic reduced infinity divisor, representing \(\mathcal O_C(1)\), specializes to \[ H_\Gamma=2\sum_{v\text{ in layer }n-1}v,\qquad \deg H_\Gamma=2^{n-1}. \tag{IH} \] Moreover \(K_\Gamma\sim(n-3)H_\Gamma\). In dimension four, suppressing the valence-two endpoint vertices gives the doubled four-cycle of the preceding obstruction, with paired lengths \(2\ell_1\) and \(2\ell_2\).

Construction of the admissible special cover. Take a chain of \(n-1\) projective lines. The first has the two marked leaves with inertias \(b_1,b_2\), the last those with inertias \(b_n,b_{n+1}\), and the intermediate component \(j\) has leaf \(b_{j+1}\). Adjacent components meet at the node labelled \(c_j\). At every component, the three incident leaf or node inertias are the three distinct nonzero elements of its rank-two group \(B_j\), and sum to zero. The connected local cover is the degree-four Klein-group cover of a projective line branched at three points. Explicitly it is the rational conic \(u^2=t, v^2=t-1\), with the three branch points \(0,1,\infty\); the two independent sign changes give the prescribed group after relabelling. Thus no component genus is hidden.

Induce this local cover from \(B_j\) to \(G\), obtaining components indexed by \(G/B_j\). Above a node with inertia \(c_j\), its points are indexed by \(G/\langle c_j\rangle\); glue equal labels on adjacent components. The node has the local tame form \(u=x^2,v=y^2\), with the inertia acting by \((x,y)\mapsto(-x,-y)\). This gives the claimed incidence and balanced admissibility. The resulting cover is connected: following paths through component cosets permits translations by the vertex groups, and those groups together contain all the branch generators. The number of components and nodes therefore gives the asserted genus.

Smoothing and regular refinement. Choose positive integers \(a_j\) proportional to the desired lengths. A base marked chain with node parameters of valuations \(2a_j\) can be obtained from branch points \[ 0,\ t^{s_1},\ t^{s_2},\ldots,t^{s_{n-2}},\ 1,\ \infty, \qquad s_j=2\sum_{h=j}^{n-2}a_h. \] Successive scales \(T/t^{s_j}\) give the three special points \(0,1,\infty\) on each component; unstable intermediate components may be contracted to nodes of the specified thickness. Apply Wewers, Theorem 3.1.1 and Section 3.2, to this projective marked nodal base and the constructed tame admissible cover. Choose node data \(xy=t^{a_j}\), with \(uv=t^{2a_j}\), equivariantly on each \(G\)-orbit. The balanced inertia preserves \(xy\); translating the coordinates transports the data to every node in its orbit. The uniqueness in the deformation theorem lifts the \(G\)-action and its group law. The theorem algebraizes the formal cover.

The generic cover is connected, smooth and \(G\)-Galois, with the labelled branch inertias. Each standard quadratic character is branched at its finite leaf and infinity; its function field is a quadratic root of the corresponding linear polynomial in the base coordinate, up to a scalar. After a finite extension removing the scalar twists, these characters identify the generic curve with the root cover. Translate the base coordinate to an unramified marked point and normalize each root there to obtain \(w_i^2=1+a_iT\). Resolve the surface nodes \(xy=t^{a_j}\): their chains of valence-two rational components subdivide the corresponding metric edges into unit lengths. This yields a strongly semistable regular model when that is needed for the specialization inequality. A common denominator and rescaling handle rational lengths. At \(n=3\), the model is semistable with valence-two rational components, not an unmarked stable curve.

The divisor and canonical relation. In the homogeneous model \(w_i^2=z^2+a_iT\), the coordinate \(T\) has weight two. Eliminating it gives the usual \(n-1\) quadrics in \(\mathbb P^n\), with homogeneous coordinates \(z,w_1,\ldots,w_n\). The divisor \(z=0\) is reduced and is exactly the infinity fibre with each ramification point counted once; it represents \(\mathcal O_C(1)\). Each degree-four last-layer component has two points above its infinity leaf, both smooth. Their specializations give (IH); no node supports this horizontal divisor. All endpoint vertices have valence two and all intermediate vertices valence four. Define a piecewise-linear function constant on each layer, with left-to-right slope \(-(j-1)\) on layer-\(j\) edges. Common edge length within a layer makes the function well-defined. Its outgoing slope sum is \(-2\) at each intermediate vertex, zero at the first layer and \(2(n-3)\) at the last. Thus \[ \operatorname{div}(f)=(n-3)H_\Gamma-K_\Gamma. \] For \(n=4\), each end-to-middle incidence is a union of two \(K_{2,2}\)'s. Suppressing its endpoint vertices gives two doubled matchings on the four middle vertices; connectivity makes their union a doubled four-cycle. Each suppressed path has length \(2\ell_j\), and the canonical relation is \(H_\Gamma\sim K_\Gamma\). \(\square\)

The whole actual chain graph is Weierstrass in the nonspecial range

Theorem (thm:cube-chain-tropical-rank-obstruction). For \(n\ge4\), every integer \(d\ge n-2\), and every point \(P\) on \(\Gamma_n\), put \[ N=2^{n-2}(2d-n+3)=\deg(dH_\Gamma)+1-g. \] Then \(dH_\Gamma-NP\) is equivalent to an effective divisor. Also \(r_\Gamma(dH_\Gamma)=N-1\), so its ordinary tropical Weierstrass locus is the entire graph. The statement holds for all positive layer lengths, hence in particular for all the rational-length models just constructed.

1. An exact butterfly description. Put \(k=n-2\) and \(M=2^k\). Label each of \(k+1\) levels by the binary strings \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_k)\). Between levels \(j-1\) and \(j\), join two strings exactly when they agree outside coordinate \(j\); their two values at coordinate \(j\) are independent. Each stage is a disjoint union of \(K_{2,2}\)'s, with common length \(\ell_j\). This describes the coset graph, not just its genus. Indeed for a representative \(g=(g_1,\ldots,g_n)\) of a layer-\(j\) coset, set \[ x_l=\begin{cases}g_1+g_{l+1},&l

2. A point-fixing involution with enough fixed vertices. Suppose \(P\) is on an edge of stage \(j\), and let \(L_0\) and \(R_0\) be that edge's common bits in positions respectively below and above \(j\). A vertex point can use any incident edge. Define a level-preserving involution \(\sigma\) as follows. For a vertex at level \(aj\), toggle bit \(j+1\); otherwise fix it. The latter instruction is absent at \(j=k\).

The controls \(R\) on the left and \(L\) on the right do not change under their respective toggles, so this is an involution. It preserves each internal edge: the toggled coordinate is constant through the earlier stages, except at the last left or first right stage where that coordinate is freely replaced. Across stage \(j\), an edge has fixed exterior bits \((L,R)\) and arbitrary incoming and outgoing bits at \(j\). Toggling either of those two bits independently preserves its \(K_{2,2}\). Thus \(\sigma\) is a graph automorphism. It is an isometry because it preserves stages, and it fixes the marked edge pointwise.

The fixed vertices lie only at levels \(j-1\) and \(j\). At the first there are \(2^j\), with \(R=R_0\); at the second there are \(2^{k-j+1}\), with \(L=L_0\). Exactly four edges are fixed: the crossing \(K_{2,2}\) with exterior bits \((L_0,R_0)\). No edge is inverted, because levels are preserved. Therefore \[ \chi(\Gamma^\sigma)=2^j+2^{k-j+1}-4\ge2\qquad(k\ge2). \tag{FX} \]

3. Quotient genus, marked divisor and effectivity. Give the orbit graph \(\Gamma'\) the original length on each exchanged edge pair and twice the original length on each fixed edge. The quotient \(\varphi:\Gamma\to\Gamma'\) has expansion one on exchanged edges and two on fixed edges. At a fixed vertex each fixed direction contributes two and each exchanged pair contributes \(1+1\); thus its local degree is two. Nonfixed vertex pairs have local degree one at each preimage. This is a harmonic morphism of degree two. Counting vertex and edge orbits gives \[ g'=\frac{g+1-\chi(\Gamma^\sigma)}2\le\frac{g-1}2. \] The marked point has one preimage with local degree two, so \(\varphi^*P'=2P\). Since \(\sigma\) preserves the last level, \(H_\Gamma\) is invariant; its coefficients at fixed vertices are even. It therefore descends to an integral divisor \(H'\) with \(\varphi^*H'=H_\Gamma\) and degree \(M\): use coefficient one at a fixed last-level vertex and coefficient two at the image of a exchanged last-level pair.

The integer \(N=M(2d-k+1)\) is even. Hence \[ A=dH'-\frac N2P',\qquad \deg A=Md-\frac{M(2d-k+1)}2=\frac{(k-1)M}{2}=\frac{g-1}2\ge g'. \] Metric Riemann–Roch, in the same imported form used in the preceding lemma, gives \(A\sim E\ge0\). Harmonic pullback preserves principal and effective divisors, by the outgoing-slope calculation there. Thus \[ dH_\Gamma-NP=\varphi^*A\sim\varphi^*E\ge0. \] Finally \(d\ge k\) implies \(\deg(dH_\Gamma)>2g-2\). Riemann–Roch gives \(r(dH_\Gamma)=\deg(dH_\Gamma)-g=N-1\), as required. \(\square\)

The stopped test and its implications

Exact marked test. The chain-graph script first checks the small coset counts, connected Laplacian ranks and canonical relation at \(n=3,4\). Its sole normality-mechanism test is \(n=5,d=3\), with every original edge subdivided into three unit edges and \(P\) one third along the stage-two edge with coset representative zero. The regular graph has 128 vertices, 144 edges and genus 17; \(\deg(3H)=48\), \(N=32\) and \(\deg(3H-32P)=16\). A negative coefficient in the \(P\)-reduced divisor would have supplied the desired excluding certificate. Instead, exact burning gives an effective representative with coefficient seven at \(P\), plus coefficients two, three, two and two at the four other listed support vertices. The 84 firing steps preserve \(D_{\mathrm{final}}=D_{\mathrm{initial}}-Lf\). The complete output records all edges and labels, \(H\), the reduced divisor, integral potential and burn order. Direct multiplication certifies effectivity, so the conclusion does not depend on a rank heuristic.

Encoding checks. The independent involution checker exhausts all cosets at \(n=3,4,5\) and verifies the butterfly identification, then every cut and exterior bit pattern at \(k=2,3\). It checks involution, adjacency, preservation of \(H\), exact fixed vertex/edge counts and quotient genus; the output retains each permutation. The wrong expansion-one choice on fixed edges is rejected because its fibre degree differs from that on exchanged pairs. These are finite encoding controls for the proved uniform construction, not additional prime or degree normality cases. The two initial GP runs encountered a vector-minimum API mistake and a reserved function name; neither produced mathematical results despite exit code zero. Full output inspection caught both, and their failed logs remain in the archive.

What has changed. The proposed graph is now an actual tame root-cover degeneration, with \(H\) and allowable edge lengths identified. But the needed negative-rank point does not exist in any higher dimension in the stated nonspecial range. No choice of degree, graph point or layer lengths can repair ordinary divisor-rank specialization on this chain family. The all-dimensional theorem, not the single dimension-five test, justifies stopping that series. Other degeneration types and refined data of the actual extending linear series are not refuted.

The involutions used in the proof are graph automorphisms, not asserted to lift to automorphisms of the root-cover family. Likewise their effective pulled-back divisors are not asserted to lift to algebraic sections. This distinction is essential: it is precisely the information ordinary graph rank may discard. The earlier normality theorems remain intact.

Verification gate. The medium pre-proof reviewer checked the local inertias, coset incidence, counts, infinity divisor, canonical slopes, regular-model qualifications and dimension-four contraction. It then checked the butterfly involution, crossing-edge compatibility, fixed-set count, quotient degree and rank obstruction. Read Wewers' exact deformation-data setup and full Section 3.2 proof, including algebraization; the old topological elliptic-gluing surface was reread and is a different construction. The Riemann–Roch and specialization source scopes are those verified in the preceding review. A fresh-context medium-reasoning correctness reviewer passed the smoothing and lifted action, regular refinement, infinity multiplicities, canonical slopes, butterfly coordinates, every cut endpoint, fixed counts, quotient metric and rank argument. Its two notation corrections are incorporated: the generic field is \(K\), distinct from the residue field, and the weight-two coordinate is eliminated to identify the ordinary hyperplane bundle. The saved programs and outputs agree with the stated evidence. No substantive unused hypothesis remains.

Assessment and next step. This discharges a methodological test for open statement 2 by ruling out the ordinary graph certificate on the actual all-dimensional chain degeneration. It leaves the original nonvanishing implication open. Next on cube-odd-characteristic, return to the actual balanced Hasse spaces and inspect their Frobenius decomposition, retaining the coupled images and characteristic-dependent coefficients. The graph proof explains why a larger ambient space of functions cannot replace them. Seek a statement controlling the full jet filtration, or a precise obstruction to the proposed recursion; do not collect another already-normal low-dimensional example. Pre-stable thresholds continue to require the polynomial parameter ring.

Process. One failed excluding-point test was replaced by a uniform fixed-set argument. Its general proof stopped further graph computations; small exhaustive checks validate only the new encoding. No framework change was needed.

27 September 2026 — Maximal jet ranks at every Frobenius power still miss a genuine order-sequence defect

Working exact power-field rank dictionary and uniform counterexample to a power-length rank criterion. The counterexample is an actual rational collision series, not the original complete cube series. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question. After the ordinary tropical-rank route failed on the actual chain family, return to Frobenius on the balanced Hasse spaces. A tempting induction would track only the ranks at jet lengths \(1,p,p^2,\ldots\), equivalently independence over successive power fields. The precise dictionary is valid. Its proposed sufficiency for normality is not: in the recorded rational collision family, every one of those ranks can be maximal while the length equal to the dimension has a one-dimensional kernel. This is a test of the information required by an induction, not a new generic-rank case sweep.

General statement. lem:cube-frobenius-power-rank-dictionary gives the classical rank interpretation with a complete proof and its exact application to the original balanced cube rows. cor:cube-frobenius-power-profile-failure constructs an infinite family at every prime \(p\ge7\) for which the entire power-length rank profile is maximal but the order sequence is not consecutive. This refines the rational-resonance obstruction without claiming a counterexample to conj:cube-refined-initial-segment-law. The remaining implication in open statement 2 must control positions inside Frobenius blocks.

What a power-field rank measures

Lemma (lem:cube-frobenius-power-rank-dictionary). Let \(k\) be perfect of characteristic \(p>0\), and let \(F/k\) be a one-variable function field with separating element \(T\). For \(q=p^e\), \(e\ge1\), and a finite-dimensional \(k\)-space \(V=\langle f_1,\ldots,f_m\rangle\subset F\), the generic rank of its length-\(q\) Hasse jet map is \[ \operatorname{rank}_F(D_T^{(j)}f_i)_{1\le i\le m,\ 0\le j

Proof. Put \(h=[F:k(T)]\). Frobenius identifies the extension \(F^q/k(T^q)\) with \(F/k(T)\), since \(k\) is perfect, so it has degree \(h\). On the other hand \([F:k(T^q)]=hq\). Hence \([F:F^q]=q\). Separability implies \(T\notin F^p\): a \(p\)-th root of \(T\) in \(F\) would be a nontrivial purely inseparable element over \(k(T)\). If \(T^{p^s}\in F^q\) for \(s

Write \(f_i=\sum_{l=0}^{q-1}c_{il}T^l\), with \(c_{il}\in F^q\). The Taylor identity \(h(T+U)^q\) shows that every positive Hasse derivative of \(h^q\) of order less than \(q\) is zero. Therefore the matrix in (PR) is the product of \((c_{il})\) with \[ B_{l,j}=\begin{cases}\binom lj T^{l-j},&l\ge j,\\0,&l

For the cube put \(w_S=\prod_{i\in S}w_i\), where \(w_i^2=1+a_iT\). The exact identity \[ w_S^q(T^u w_S)=T^u\prod_{i\in S}(1+a_iT)^{(q+1)/2} \] multiplies each original row by a nonzero element of \(F^q\), so it preserves the right side of (PR). Reduction in the displayed basis gives (BP), with the same balanced degree vector. No odd scalar is removed. The rank criterion is classical; the proof is included so that no unavailable source theorem or characteristic-zero Wronskian normalization is imported. \(\square\)

Why later blocks remain coupled. The multiplier \(w_S^q\) depends on the row and is not a scalar in \(k\). For \(0\le b0\) start at the next block. Thus the individual row rescalings in (BP) do not preserve the full original \(k\)-linear series or its arbitrary-length jet matrix. The next result shows that even knowing the correct original ranks at every power length is insufficient.

A maximal profile with a missing order

Corollary (cor:cube-frobenius-power-profile-failure). Let \(k\) have characteristic \(p\ge7\). Let \(c\) be the unique odd integer in \(\{1,\ldots,p-1\}\) satisfying \[ 4c\equiv3\ \text{or}\ 5\pmod p. \] For every \(e\ge1\), put \(q=p^e\), \(A=q+c\) and \(N=4A-4\). On the rational root curve \[ w_1^2=1+aT,\qquad w_2^2=1+bT,\qquad ab(a-b)\ne0, \] let \[ V_A=k[T]_{\le A}+w_1k[T]_{\le A-2}+w_2k[T]_{\le A-2} +w_1w_2k[T]_{\le A-4}. \] Then, at a generic finite geometric point, for every integer \(j\ge0\), \[ \operatorname{rank}J_{p^j}(V_A)=\min(p^j,N),\tag{MP} \] but \[ \operatorname{rank}J_N(V_A)=N-1.\tag{DF} \] Moreover \(A\) is even, so this is the actual second rational collision series of the dimension-four degree-\(A/2\) space. It is not that original complete space, whose all-odd normality is already proved.

1. The parameters exist uniformly. The representatives of \(4c=3\) and \(4c=5\) modulo \(p\) have sum \(p+2\). Indeed, if \(p=4h+1\), they are \(h+1\) and \(3h+2\); if \(p=4h+3\), they are \(3h+3\) and \(h+2\). For \(p\ge7\), both lie between one and \(p-1\). Their sum is odd, so exactly one is odd. Since \(q\) is odd, \(A=q+c\) is even and at least four. Also \[ p\mid(4A-5)(4A-3)=N^2-1. \] The rational collision theorem, with its exact integral Hasse normalization, now gives \(\dim V_A=N\) and (DF).

2. There is room between adjacent power lengths. We have \(q0. \] For \(p=7\), the odd representative is \(c=3\), so \(pq-4A=3q-12>0\). Thus in every case \[ q

3. Small powers are surjective. For \(p^j\le q\), the polynomial block contains \(1,T,\ldots,T^{p^j-1}\). At a generic point the map to the \(T\)-line is unramified, so \(T-T(P)\) is a local parameter. Those polynomials span all length-\(p^j\) jets after scalar extension to the marked-point field. Hence the rank is \(p^j\), the maximal possible value by (ROOM).

4. Larger powers are injective. In the rational coordinate used in the resonance theorem, the two infinity points are \(P_0,P_\infty\); \(T\) has pole order two at each, and \(w_1,w_2\) have pole order one at each. Every element of \(V_A\) has the same common pole bound \[ V_A\subseteq L\bigl(2A(P_0+P_\infty)\bigr),\qquad \deg\bigl(2A(P_0+P_\infty)\bigr)=4A. \] The polynomial block attains this bound, and the other blocks have smaller pole orders. This common divisor persists after extension to the generic marked-point field, so it also bounds a linear combination whose coefficients depend on that point. A nonzero such function cannot vanish to order greater than \(4A\) at a point outside the poles. By (ROOM), every power \(p^j\ge pq\) gives an injective jet map, of rank \(N\). There is no prime power strictly between \(q\) and \(pq\), completing (MP). The even-\(A\) identification with the actual second collision is the characteristic-safe saturation proved in the resonance entry. \(\square\)

Scope. The example refutes a criterion based solely on the sequence of ranks at all Frobenius-power lengths, even though those are the correct original jet ranks. Over a perfect geometric constant field, (PR) translates it equally into a counterexample to sufficiency of all successive power-field span dimensions. It does not refute an induction retaining the actual residual matrices, flags or positions within each block, and it does not supply a counterexample to the complete cube normality conjecture. The known smoothing can repair the limit's defect.

Source audit, verification and next action

Source scope. The primary Hidalgo–Kontogeorgis–Leyton-Álvarez–Paramantzoglou paper, Theorem 17, uses characteristic zero or \(p>2^{n-1}\) for the type-\((2,n)\) natural embedding. The hyperosculating-weight paper is formulated for closed Riemann surfaces. Neither supplies the needed small-prime, all-degree normality theorem. The power-field viewpoint led to Garcia–Voloch, Wronskians and linear independence in fields of prime characteristic, Manuscripta Mathematica 59 (1987), 457–469. Its bounded original scan was located through the archive manifest and retained only in temporary storage. The scan has no extracted article text; no theorem from its unread image pages is used. The dictionary above is proved directly. The earlier optional request for the original Stöhr–Voloch paper remains separate.

Verification gate. Re-read the complete rational resonance proof, including its conic coordinate, five conditions, exact corank and safe even-degree collision. Its retained relations show no correction changing this scope. The medium pre-proof reviewer confirmed that the power-profile statement is a new diagnostic corollary of that theorem, checked the opposite-parity representatives and both size inequalities, and required the common pole divisor to be stated over the generic marked-point field. It also checked the standard dictionary's perfect-constant-field scope. No numerical run is needed: the rank claims follow from an explicit polynomial subspace, the common pole divisor and the already-proved exact resonance. A fresh-context medium-reasoning correctness reviewer passed both full proofs, the power-field degree and triangular matrix, balanced row factors and later-block product rule, both parity cases, the special prime seven, the common pole bound after scalar extension and the exact resonance dependency. No mathematical correction or unused hypothesis was found.

Assessment. Frobenius-power rank tests are necessary information, but even their complete profile does not locate all generic orders. This closes a proposed shortcut before investing in a sequence of initial-block calculations. The missing all-dimensional normality implication is unchanged. To advance it, the recursion must retain the between-power residual and prove its nonvanishing for the complete balanced root series, with the original degree vector intact.

Next step. On cube-odd-characteristic, make the next cycle a route review: both the graph test and this power-profile test have left the full normality implication open. Compare any exact Frobenius residue map with the original Schur residual before adopting it; a new description alone is insufficient. Reassess the pre-stable polynomial-degree route as well, and choose a test that can change one of those general obligations.

27 September 2026 — Rank-only tests fail; degree two has an explicit marked free hull in every dimension

Working all-dimensional degree-two hull and exact exterior-square annihilator model in characteristic zero. Route review; the uniform filtered degree problem remains open. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Obstacle

Open statement 3 asks for the least polynomial parameter degree of a relation at each order. The all-dimensional symmetric connection already represents that question, but its generic rank and collision divisor do not determine its filtered cyclic-image defect. Open statement 2 also survives the latest tests: the actual tame chain has no excluding graph point, and even the complete Frobenius-power rank profile misses a possible intervening order. Repeating those tests at larger dimensions or degrees cannot establish the needed implication. This review tests a different structural question: can the degree-two cyclic hull be described in every dimension with an explicit graded basis, connection and distinguished vector, so that its remaining defect is an exact exterior-square relation problem?

General statement. thm:cube-degree-two-schur-hull proves a free cyclic hull for every dimension in degree two; lem:cube-degree-two-exterior-annihilator identifies its full polynomial annihilator with a marked exterior-square annihilator, with an exact order shift and no loss of excess. The first is new structural information beyond a change of matrix; the second keeps the information needed to use it. Neither computes the still-missing uniform threshold values, nor extends the hull claim to arbitrary degree or positive characteristic.

An explicit degree-two hull in every dimension

Theorem (thm:cube-degree-two-schur-hull). Let \(k\) have characteristic zero, \(n\ge2\), \(R=k[a_1,\ldots,a_n]\), \(B=k[e_1,\ldots,e_n]\), and \(a_0=0\). In degree two use the actual root-series rows \[ 1,\quad T,\quad g_{ij}(T)=\sqrt{(1+a_iT)(1+a_jT)}\quad(0\le i<j\le n). \] These are exactly \(1,T,w_i,w_iw_j\). Let \(v_c\) be their coefficient column at \(T^c\), and \(N_R=\sum_{c\ge0}Rv_c\). For \(0\le u<v\le n\), put \[ s_{uv}(X,Y)=\frac{X^uY^v-X^vY^u}{Y-X},\qquad (F_{uv})_{ij}=(a_i-a_j)^2s_{uv}(a_i,a_j), \] with the first two coordinates of \(F_{uv}\) zero. Then \[ N_R^{**}=Rv_0\oplus Rv_1\oplus\bigoplus_{u<v}RF_{uv}. \] Under the existing symmetric companion embedding, this frame descends to a homogeneous \(B\)-basis of the companion cyclic hull. Its weights are \(0,1,u+v+1\); its Hilbert numerator is \(1+t+\sum_{u<v}t^{u+v+1}\). This is the explicit all-dimensional refinement of the earlier degree-two hulls, not a claim that the cyclic image itself is free.

Proof of containment. Write \(x=a_i,y=a_j\). Direct differentiation gives \[ g_{ij}''(T)=-\frac{(x-y)^2}{4((1+xT)(1+yT))^{3/2}}. \] Thus, for \(c\ge2\), its coefficient is \((x-y)^2h_{c-2}(x,y)\), with \(h_{c-2}\in k[X,Y]\) symmetric homogeneous of degree \(c-2\). Every symmetric polynomial \(h\), evaluated on all pairs of the \(n+1\) roots, is an \(R\)-linear combination of the \(s_{uv}\). Indeed, reduce \((Y-X)h(X,Y)\) separately in \(X,Y\) modulo \[p_0(X)=X\prod_{i=1}^n(X-a_i).\] The two monic reductions commute with swapping variables. Their remainder is alternating, of degree at most \(n\) in each variable, hence uniquely \(\sum_{u<v}c_{uv}(X^uY^v-X^vY^u)\). Evaluation and division by the nonzero polynomial \(a_j-a_i\) in the fraction field give the required equality of polynomial evaluations. This proves \(N_R\subseteq L_R\), where \(L_R\) is the displayed span; \(v_0,v_1\) are already its first two generators.

Embedded determinant and hull equality. Set \(V=\prod_{0\le i<j\le n}(a_j-a_i)\). The pair evaluation matrix of \(X^uY^v-X^vY^u\) is the second compound of the \((n+1)\)-by-\((n+1)\) Vandermonde matrix. Its determinant is \(V^n\). For completeness, \(\det(\bigwedge^2A)=(\det A)^n\) follows on diagonalizable invertible matrices by multiplying eigenvalues in pairs; that set is dense over an algebraic closure in characteristic zero, and both sides are polynomials in the entries, so the identity holds identically. Dividing each pair row by \(a_j-a_i\) gives determinant \(V^{n-1}\). The factors \((a_i-a_j)^2\) then give \[ \det(v_0,v_1,(F_{uv})_{u<v})=V^{n+1} \] in the common lexicographic pair order. The first two rows form an identity block. In particular \(L_R\) is free of the required rank.

The all-truncation collision theorem, in the raw frame as justified in the cyclic-defect proposition, gives colength \(E_n(2)=2+(n-1)=n+1\) for the full cyclic image at every collision hyperplane. Equivalently, its nonzero Smith exponents are two once and one \(n-1\) times. The determinant of \(L_R\) has exactly that valuation. The inclusion \(N_R\subseteq L_R\) and equal DVR colengths therefore give equality there. At every other height-one prime, the same proposition's pole-degree argument says the columns through \(2^n\) span the raw ambient module. The determinant of \(L_R\) is a unit there as well. Hence \(N_R\) and \(L_R\) agree at all height-one primes. Intersecting those localizations in their common fraction space proves \(N_R^{**}=L_R\).

Descent and grading. Let \(\Theta:R\otimes_BM_B\hookrightarrow M_R^{\rm raw}\) be the polynomial companion frame from symmetric descent. It sends the companion cyclic image to \(N_R\). Flat base change commutes with duals of finite presented modules: present a module by finite free modules, apply \(\operatorname{Hom}(-,B)\), and use flatness to preserve the resulting kernel. Applying this twice, and using the injective generic identification through \(\Theta\), gives \[ \Theta(R\otimes_BN_B^{**})=N_R^{**}=L_R. \] In particular each \(F_{uv}\) has polynomial companion coordinates; this also follows because the free image of \(\Theta\) is reflexive and contains \(N_R\). Each \(F_{uv}\), and \(v_0,v_1\), is invariant under permutation of the finite roots together with their raw rows. Equivariance and injectivity of \(\Theta\) imply that every companion coordinate is symmetric, hence in \(B\). These columns lie in \(N_B^{**}\): membership descends by faithful flatness, or by the Artin basis containing \(1\). Their \(B\)-span becomes all of \(R\otimes_BN_B^{**}\); faithful flatness gives a basis over \(B\). The polynomial \(s_{uv}\) has degree \(u+v-1\), so \(F_{uv}\) has weight \(u+v+1\). The original row shift for \(T\) is one, giving weights zero and one for \(v_0,v_1\). No full \(S_{n+1}\)-action on vectors is assumed. \(\square\)

The marked exterior-square connection

Lemma (lem:cube-degree-two-exterior-annihilator). Keep this setting and \(\delta=-\sum_i a_i^2\partial_{a_i}\). On \(E=B[X]/p_0(X)\), let \[ \mathcal D=\delta_{\rm coeff}-X^2\partial_X-\tfrac12X. \] The pair block of the preceding hull is \(\bigwedge^2E\), with the basis \(X^u\wedge X^v\mapsto F_{uv}\) shifted in weight by one, and induced connection \(\mathcal D^{[2]}\). The two additional basis vectors satisfy \[ \nabla v_0=v_1,\qquad \nabla v_1=-\tfrac14F_{01}. \] For \(\mathscr A_B=B[\partial;\delta]\), with polynomial coefficients on the left, \[ \operatorname{Ann}_{\mathscr A_B}(v_0) =\{Q\partial^2:Q\in\operatorname{Ann}_{\mathscr A_B,\wedge^2E}(1\wedge X)\}. \] This is right multiplication by \(\partial^2\). It shifts both order and total degree by two, preserving the excess, and remains exact after extension from \(B\) to \(R\). Thus the original degree-two threshold at order \(m\) equals the exterior-model threshold at order \(m-2\), with the same excess; orders below two have no nonzero annihilator.

Proof. First \(\mathcal D\) is well-defined modulo \(p_0\). Put \(L=\delta_{\rm coeff}-X^2\partial_X\). For each moving root, \(L(X-a_i)=-X^2+a_i^2=-(X+a_i)(X-a_i)\), and \(L(X)=-X^2\). Therefore \(Lp_0=-((n+1)X+e_1)p_0\). The derivation \(L\) preserves \((p_0)\), and so does the multiplication term \(-X/2\). In the monomial basis, \[ \mathcal D X^u=-(u+\tfrac12)X^{u+1}\pmod{p_0}. \] This gives an explicit polynomial matrix over \(B\), with monic reduction only at exponent \(n+1\).

In the raw character connection the pair row has diagonal entry \((x+y)/2\). The first two rows are the nilpotent block sending the constant row's basis vector to the \(T\)-row's basis vector. On a pair entry \((x-y)^2h(x,y)\), direct differentiation gives \[ \nabla((x-y)^2h)=(x-y)^2\left[-(x^2\partial_x+y^2\partial_y)h-\tfrac32(x+y)h\right]. \] For the alternant \(A=(y-x)h\), multiplication of the bracket by \(y-x\) equals \[ -(x^2\partial_x+y^2\partial_y)A-\tfrac12(x+y)A. \] This is exactly the sum of \(\mathcal D\) acting on the two factors of the alternant. Evaluating at the roots respects monic reduction, proving the exterior connection formula. Scalar coefficients obey the same \(\delta\)-Leibniz rule. Finally the first two columns satisfy \(\nabla v_0=v_1\) and \(\nabla v_1=2v_2=-F_{01}/4\), either directly or from the coefficient recurrence.

Write an arbitrary operator uniquely as \(\sum_{j\ge0}b_j\partial^j\). Since every iterate from order two on lies in the pair block, its action on \(v_0\) has first two basis components \(b_0,b_1\). An annihilator must therefore have \(b_0=b_1=0\), and is uniquely \(Q\partial^2\). Its remaining action is \(-QF_{01}/4\), proving both implications. No rational coefficients or collision factors are inverted. The hull-preservation lemma identifies this annihilator with the original one. Homogeneity of the frame and of the degree-one connection identifies the original grading; right multiplication by \(\partial^2\) changes order and degree by exactly two. The operator dictionary uses \(P_W=\sum W_c\partial^c/c!\); factorials are nonzero constants in characteristic zero. Therefore the equality respects the highest-order coefficient and its degree, up to units, and faithful flat descent preserves initial degree. \(\square\)

27 September 2026 — The degree-two cyclic defect is supported exactly on two disjoint root collisions

Working all-dimensional fibre-rank and support theorem in characteristic zero. The residual scheme and filtered relation degrees are not determined. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and outcome. Open statement 3 still needs polynomial relation degrees. The new free hull does not supply them, so this cycle tests its actual marked cyclic quotient. The concrete question is whether that defect can occur away from configurations containing two disjoint equal pairs. The answer is no, and the proof gives its fibre dimension at every root multiplicity pattern in every dimension. This locates the higher-codimension object that a graded relation theorem must describe; it does not replace that object by its support or claim a threshold from a rank.

Every collision partition has an exact defect dimension

Theorem (thm:cube-degree-two-cluster-defect). Let \(k\) have characteristic zero, \(n\ge2\), and \(B=k[e_1,\ldots,e_n]\). In degree two let \(N_B\) be the symmetric companion cyclic image and \(C=N_B^{**}/N_B\). Pull back to \(R=k[a_1,\ldots,a_n]\), with \(a_0=0\). At any geometric point, let the \(n+1\) labeled values \(a_0,\ldots,a_n\) have distinct values \(b_1,\ldots,b_s\), of multiplicities \(m_1,\ldots,m_s\). Put \[ \eta(1)=0,\qquad \eta(m)=\frac{(m-2)(m-3)}2\quad(m\ge2). \] Then \[ \dim_{\bar k}(C\otimes_B\bar k) =\sum_{i=1}^s\eta(m_i)+\sum_{i<j}(m_i-1)(m_j-1). \tag{CD} \] The fibre uses the coefficient values of the chosen root point. Consequently the support of \(R\otimes_BC\), as a closed set, is exactly \[ \bigcup_{\substack{\{i,j\}\cap\{u,v\}=\varnothing\\i<j,\ u<v}} V(a_i-a_j,\ a_u-a_v). \] Equivalently, the defect is nonzero precisely when at least two clusters have size at least two, or a single cluster has size at least four. A triple cluster alone causes no defect. The statement is about fibres of the cokernel and its set-theoretic support, not about an injective specialized cyclic image, its scheme multiplicities or its graded presentation.

The generating series in the exact hull. Use the marked exterior model \(E=B[X]/p_0\), \(p_0=X\prod_i(X-a_i)\), with \(\mathcal D=\delta_{\rm coeff}-X^2\partial_X-X/2\) and marked vector \(g=1\wedge X\). The first two original directions \(v_0,v_1\) are already in the cyclic image, and \(\nabla^2v_0=-g/4\). Thus \(C\), up to the harmless overall grading shift, is exactly the cokernel of the columns \(\mathcal D^{[2]\,j}g\) in \(\bigwedge^2E\). Here \(\mathcal D^{[2]}\) is the induced sum connection, not the exterior power of a linear map.

On polynomial representatives, for every \(j\ge0\), \[ \mathcal D^j1=(-1)^j(1/2)_jX^j,\qquad \mathcal D^jX=(-1)^j(3/2)_jX^{j+1}\pmod{p_0}. \] These follow by induction from \(\mathcal DX^u=-(u+1/2)X^{u+1}\). Reduction does not change them because \(\mathcal D\) preserves the ideal \((p_0)\). The connection obeys the exterior Leibniz rule, so induction gives the binomial Leibniz formula for every iterate on \(1\wedge X\). Hence the entire divided-iterate series is \[ \sum_{j\ge0}\frac{T^j}{j!}\mathcal D^{[2]\,j}g =f(X,T)\wedge h(X,T),\qquad f=(1+XT)^{-1/2},\quad h=X(1+XT)^{-3/2}. \tag{GS} \] All coefficients lie in the original polynomial quotient. This identity is proved before specialization: it does not assume that the parameter derivation descends to an arbitrary point's residue field.

Fibre rank is a row-series dimension. Specialize the polynomial coefficient columns in (GS) to a geometric point. Chinese remainders give \[ E_{\bar k}\cong\bigoplus_i\bar k[z_i]/z_i^{m_i},\qquad X=b_i+z_i. \] The corresponding decomposition of \(\bigwedge^2E_{\bar k}\) consists of its internal exterior blocks and cross tensor blocks. The rank of the infinite column matrix equals the dimension over \(\bar k\) of the span of its coordinate series in \(\bar k[[T]]\). Indeed, a linear functional annihilates every column exactly when its corresponding linear combination of row series is zero; the finite-dimensional target identifies the two ranks. The right exact sequence defining \(C\) then gives its fibre dimension as the target dimension minus this rank. No equality between the specialized image and \(N_B\otimes_B\bar k\) is assumed.

An internal cluster. At a cluster of size \(m\) and value \(b\), the coefficient of \(z^u\) in \(f(b+z,T)\) is \[ f_u(T)=c_uT^u(1+bT)^{-u-1/2},\qquad c_u=\binom{-1/2}{u}\ne0. \] Since \(h=-2\partial_Tf\), the row indexed by \(z^u\wedge z^v\), \(0\le u<v<m\), in (GS) is \[ f_uh_v-h_uf_v =-2c_uc_v(v-u)\frac{T^{u+v-1}}{(1+bT)^{u+v+2}}. \tag{IC} \] The constant is nonzero in characteristic zero. When \(m\ge2\), the integers \(u+v\) cover every value \(1,\ldots,2m-3\): use \((0,t)\) for \(t\le m-1\), and \((t-m+1,m-1)\) thereafter. If \(b=0\), the resulting functions are the distinct monomials \(T^{t-1}\). If \(b\ne0\), their successive pole orders \(t+2\) at \(T=-1/b\) prove independence. The rank of this block is therefore \(2m-3\); at \(m=1\) the block is zero.

Two distinct clusters. At values \(b\ne c\) and sizes \(m,\ell\), set \(x=b+z,y=c+w\). The cross-block generating expression is \[ f(x,T)h(y,T)-h(x,T)f(y,T) =(y-x)((1+xT)(1+yT))^{-3/2}. \] Multiplication by \(y-x=(c-b)+(w-z)\) is an invertible, \(T\)-independent linear map on the truncated local algebra \(\bar k[z,w]/(z^m,w^\ell)\). It therefore preserves the span dimension of the coefficient row series. After removing it, those rows are nonzero constant multiples of \[ ((1+bT)(1+cT))^{-3/2}U^uV^v,\qquad U=\frac{T}{1+bT},\quad V=\frac{T}{1+cT}, \quad 0\le u<m,\quad0\le v<\ell . \] All binomial constants \(\binom{-3/2}{u}\binom{-3/2}{v}\) are nonzero. The identity \[ U-V=(c-b)UV \] reduces each mixed monomial, by induction on \(u+v\), to the span of \[ 1,U,\ldots,U^{m-1},V,\ldots,V^{\ell-1}. \] These functions are independent. If both \(b,c\) are nonzero, successive highest pole orders at their two distinct poles force all positive-power coefficients to vanish, then the constant vanishes. If one is zero, its positive powers are polynomials, while the other family has a distinct finite pole; the same argument followed by polynomial independence applies. Both cannot be zero. Thus every cross block has rank \(m+\ell-1\).

Independence between blocks. Exactly one cluster value is zero, because \(a_0=0\). For each nonzero \(b_i\), the linear polynomial \(1+b_iT\) has a simple zero at a different point. Its square class is independent of those of the other linear polynomials, as witnessed by these valuations. In the multiquadratic function field obtained by adjoining their square roots, products over different subsets are linearly independent over \(\bar k(T)\), by the sign-change character decomposition. Each cross block above has the square character of the unordered pair of its nonzero cluster values: a singleton when one value is zero, and a two-element subset otherwise. These characters are distinct for distinct cross blocks, and none is trivial. They therefore cannot cancel each other or the internal rational blocks.

The internal blocks at nonzero values have disjoint finite poles and are proper rational functions, tending to zero at infinity. Their spaces have zero intersection with the polynomial space from the zero cluster, and are independent of each other: in a putative sum, the principal part at each distinct finite pole must vanish; the corresponding proper rational function is then zero. Thus all the block ranks add.

Rank subtraction and support. The exterior target decomposes with dimensions \(\binom{m_i}{2}\) and \(m_im_j\). Subtract the proved ranks. For an internal block the deficit is zero at \(m=1\), and \[ \binom m2-(2m-3)=\frac{(m-2)(m-3)}2 \] for \(m\ge2\). A cross-block deficit is \(m\ell-(m+\ell-1)=(m-1)(\ell-1)\). This proves (CD). Every term is nonnegative; an internal term is positive exactly for \(m\ge4\), and a cross term exactly when both multiplicities are at least two. Those conditions are exactly the existence of two disjoint equal pairs among the labeled roots. Since \(C\) is finite, Nakayama identifies nonzero fibres with support at closed points. Over the algebraic closure the parameter ring is Jacobson, so equality at all geometric closed points gives the asserted closed support; faithful scalar extension gives the original-field statement. \(\square\)

The smallest nonvacuous control is \(n=3\), with six exterior rows: it contains the different mechanisms of two double clusters and a quadruple cluster, as well as a triple-cluster negative control. The script research/tools/bmd_cube_exterior_clusters.gp checks all 42 polynomial entries of (GS) through order six against independently iterated symbolic connection columns. It then tests every one of the 15 set partitions of the four labeled roots, using distinct integer cluster values. Exactly four partitions have defect one: the three double-pair partitions and the all-equal partition. All others have full rank six. The existing complete monic order-nine result for the original eight-dimensional model proves that these seven exterior columns generate its whole cyclic image, so this is not merely a short-prefix rank observation. The full output retains the symbolic matrix and all partition results. No larger-dimension run was needed.

The known \(n=3\) defect is \((B/(f,h^2))(-4)\), \(h=e_1^2-4e_2\), \(f=e_1h+8e_3\). Its support is precisely the image of \((2,2)\), including the all-equal limit, and its nonzero fibres have dimension one. Its generic transverse length is two. This is an explicit warning: the present support and rank formula do not imply reducedness, identify an annihilator ideal, or determine graded relation degrees. Likewise this theorem concerns the quotient inside the Schur hull, not the earlier quotient of the raw ambient module, whose divisorial collision factors have already been removed.

27 September 2026 — Two squared root differences give the generic double-pair defect

Working local scheme theorem in characteristic zero, every dimension admitting the stratum. Root transverse length four; symmetric lengths depend on which pairs contain the distinguished zero root. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and outcome. The all-dimensional cluster formula identifies support and fibre ranks but leaves the actual defect scheme unknown. This cycle tests whether the solved four-root local module survives after other distinct roots are added. It does, in the root parameter ring: the quotient is cyclic and is cut out by the squares of the two root differences. The proof separates the first-order missing directions from all spectator rows, rather than assuming that the deformed cyclic image splits by square characters. Open statement 3 still needs the global graded module and its order filtration.

The scheme along the open double-pair stratum

Theorem (thm:cube-double-pair-local-module). Let \(k\) have characteristic zero, \(n\ge3\), \(B=k[e_1,\ldots,e_n]\), \(R=k[a_1,\ldots,a_n]\), and \(a_0=0\). In degree two let \(C=N_B^{**}/N_B\) be the actual symmetric companion cyclic defect. At a geometric root point whose multiplicity pattern is exactly \((2,2,1,\ldots,1)\), write \(x=a_i-a_j\) and \(y=a_u-a_v\) for its two disjoint root differences. If \(\mathcal O\) is the completed local root ring at that point, then, as an unfiltered module, \[ \mathcal O\otimes_BC\cong\mathcal O/(x^2,y^2). \tag{LP} \] Consequently the generic transverse root-ring length is four. In the symmetric ring the generic transverse length is two on the stratum where one pair contains \(a_0\), and one on the stratum where both pairs are among \(a_1,\ldots,a_n\). The second type requires \(n\ge4\). These are statements on the open stratum; they do not describe intersections of collision strata or assert a global graded splitting.

A universal column cokernel. To keep the distinguished zero root from obscuring the deformation, temporarily allow all \(n+1\) roots to vary. For a monic polynomial \(p(X)\) of degree \(n+1\), define a column map into \(\bigwedge^2(S[X]/p)\) by the coefficients of \[ f(X,T)\wedge h(X,T),\qquad f=(1+XT)^{-1/2},\quad h=X(1+XT)^{-3/2}. \tag{UC} \] Call its cokernel \(C^\circ\). This definition uses only polynomial coefficient columns and monic reduction, so it commutes with arbitrary base change by right exactness. When \(p=p_0=X\prod_{i=1}^n(X-a_i)\), the exact exterior model and its generating-series identity identify this cokernel, up to an irrelevant grading shift, with \(C\). No double dual is taken after restricting \(a_0=0\), and no nonflat base-change assertion for double duals is used.

In formal coordinates near the chosen root pattern, factor \[ p(X)=((X-b)^2-A)((X-c)^2-D)\prod_\nu(X-d_\nu), \] where the central values \(b,c,d_\nu\) are distinct, and \(A=D=0\) at the chosen point. Let \(S\) be the complete local coefficient ring with these parameters, allowing the centers and the simple roots to vary as well. Their mutual differences are units. Chinese remainders give two quadratic blocks \(S[z]/(z^2-A)\), \(S[w]/(w^2-D)\), and the simple blocks. The target exterior module splits accordingly; this is a decomposition of the ambient module, not an asserted splitting of its cyclic image.

The unique central row relation. In the cross block of the two quadratic factors, (UC) is \[ (c-b+w-z)((1+(b+z)T)(1+(c+w)T))^{-3/2}. \] Multiplication by \(c-b+w-z\) is an invertible, \(T\)-independent \(S\)-linear transformation near the central point. Remove it. Let \(F_{uv}(T)\), \(u,v\in\{0,1\}\), be the coefficient row series of the remaining expression in the basis \(1,z,w,zw\). Put \[ U=\frac{T}{1+bT},\quad V=\frac{T}{1+cT},\quad H=((1+bT)(1+cT))^{-3/2},\qquad c_j=\binom{-3/2}{j}. \] Modulo \(I=(A,D)\), these rows are \(H,\,c_1HU,\,c_1HV,\,c_1^2HUV\). Since \(U-V=(c-b)UV\), their unique relation is \[ \Lambda=F_{10}-F_{01}+\tfrac23(c-b)F_{11}=0\pmod I. \tag{R} \] Their rank is three. The internal quadratic blocks have rank one, and every block involving a simple root has full rank. Their central row series are independent of the cross block by the square-character and pole argument in the cluster theorem. That argument also works when none of the centers is zero: all cross characters are distinct two-element subsets, and the internal rational pole spaces are independent. If one center is zero, the previously proved singleton-character and polynomial-space cases apply. Thus the entire central column matrix has corank one, with (R) its sole row relation.

The two deformation directions remain independent. Reducing powers using \(z^2=A,w^2=D\) and differentiating (R) at \(A=D=0\), with centers fixed, gives \[ \begin{aligned} H^{-1}\partial_A\Lambda &=c_3U^3-c_2c_1U^2V+\tfrac23(c-b)c_3c_1U^3V =\tfrac58U^2V,\\ H^{-1}\partial_D\Lambda &=c_1c_2UV^2-c_3V^3+\tfrac23(c-b)c_1c_3UV^3 =-\tfrac58UV^2. \tag{J} \end{aligned} \] Here \(c_1=-3/2,c_2=15/8,c_3=-35/16\), and the simplifications use the same identity \(U-V=(c-b)UV\). The classes of \(U^2V\) and \(UV^2\) modulo \(\langle1,U,V\rangle\) are independent: the first has, modulo that span, a nonzero \(U^2\) term and the second a nonzero \(V^2\) term, because \(c-b\) is a unit. At nonzero distinct centers the two new highest pole orders distinguish them; if one center is zero, its polynomial degree two distinguishes it from the other finite pole.

Multiplication by \(H\) puts both residuals in the character of the selected cross block. No central spectator row has that character, so independence holds modulo the whole central row span. This conclusion is only about the central fibre and its first variations; it does not split the deformed cyclic image into independent blocks. As a symbolic check on (J), the coefficients at \(T^3,T^4\) of the two residuals have determinant \[ \det\begin{pmatrix} 5/8&-5/8\\ -5(7b+5c)/16&5(5b+7c)/16 \end{pmatrix} =\frac{25}{64}(c-b)\ne0. \] This two-coefficient identity is an audit of the residual formulas. Independence modulo all old rows is supplied by the preceding character and pole proof, not by this determinant alone.

From first variations to the exact local ideal. Write \(r=\binom{n+1}{2}\). Choose \(r-1\) coefficient columns and rows giving a unit minor at the central point. Gaussian elimination over \(S\) turns their block into an identity and eliminates it from the remaining columns. The cokernel is cyclic, \(C^\circ\cong S/J\), where \(J\) is generated by the remaining scalar entries. All \(r\)-minors vanish modulo \(I\): over the formal center stratum the same sole relation (R) holds, and the chosen minor stays a unit. Hence \(J\subseteq I\).

The linear parts of these residual scalar entries are the two derivatives in (J), taken modulo the whole old row span. Changing pivots or lifting the central row relation only adds old row combinations to those derivatives. Their proved independence therefore says that their coefficient linear forms span both normal directions \(A,D\). In other words \(J+\mathfrak m I=I\), where \(\mathfrak m\) is the maximal ideal of \(S\). Nakayama applied to the finite module \(I/J\) yields \(J=I\). We have proved \(C^\circ\cong S/(A,D)\), not merely containment of its support. Although the column list is infinite, its image and residual ideal are finite modules over the Noetherian ring \(S\), and the pivot and normal-direction witnesses use finitely many columns.

Root restriction and symmetric lengths. In labeled root coordinates, a quadratic pair has center equal to its mean and \(A=x^2/4\); the other has \(D=y^2/4\). Pull back the actual column cokernel to those coordinates and then impose \(a_0=0\). Right-exact base change of the established quotient gives (LP). This covers a pair containing \(a_0\) as well: its mean varies with its other root, but the equation \(A=x^2/4\) still holds. The basis \(1,x,y,xy\) of the transverse quotient gives length four.

For clarity about descent, pass to an unramified extension of the symmetric local ring that labels the distinct clusters; this does not change transverse lengths. If both pairs are finite, their stabilizer swaps the two roots in each pair independently. Its normal invariant parameters are \(s=x^2,t=y^2\), and the root ring is free of rank four over this transverse invariant ring. If one pair contains the fixed root zero, only the finite pair is swapped: the normal invariant parameters are \(s=x,t=y^2\), with root-ring rank two. The symmetric defect is locally cyclic, since its geometric fibre has dimension one by the cluster theorem. Write it as \(B_{\rm loc}/J_B\). Faithful flatness and (LP) identify \(J_B\) by contraction: it is \((s,t)\) in the first case and \((s^2,t)\) in the second, after the stated unramified extension and completion. Thus the symmetric transverse lengths are respectively one and two. \(\square\)

Checks and compatibility. The symbolic program research/tools/bmd_cube_double_pair_first_order.gp verifies both rational identities (J), the coefficient Jacobian and its determinant, with formal distinct centers rather than a dimension sweep. It also pulls back the exact four-root ideal \((f,h^2)\) under \(a_1=x,a_2=b+y,a_3=b-y\): \[ f=(x-2b)(x^2-4y^2),\qquad h^2\bmod(x^2-4y^2)=64y^2(y^2-bx+b^2). \] At \(x=y=0,b\ne0\), both displayed extra factors are units, giving exactly \((x^2,y^2)\). The complete output retains these identities. This checks the old case and the new deformation mechanism. No higher-dimensional numerical example is needed; spectator independence is proved. The no-double-double-surface lemma concerns a global hypersurface with special restrictions, and neither implies nor contradicts this codimension-two local quotient.

General statement. thm:cube-double-pair-local-module determines the unfiltered local defect scheme on every open double-pair stratum in every dimension in characteristic zero at degree two. It advances open statement 3 from set-theoretic support to local thickness. Gaussian pivots are local and can mix operator orders: no global graded relation degree or filtration-preserving splitting has been proved.

A fresh-context medium-reasoning correctness reviewer passed the universal construction, all central row independence, residual derivatives, Nakayama step, root restriction, ramification lengths and old-module comparison. No substantive gap or unused hypothesis was found; its local and unfiltered scope is retained.

Assessment and next step. The local four-root mechanism persists with arbitrary simple spectator roots, with no extra transverse thickness. Its two symmetric lengths explain why the parameter ring matters. The next cycle on cube-odd-characteristic must test a global implication for the marked graded module: determine whether these local pieces assemble without additional modules supported on intersections of the double-pair strata, and whether a proposed presentation retains the order filtration. 27 September 2026 — The defect's generators are explicit, but independent components and a transverse Dunkl action fail

Working graded-generator corollary and local commutator obstruction in characteristic zero. Neither gives the filtered relation degrees; the Cherednik exclusion has an explicitly local scope. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and outcome. Open statement 3 requires a global graded relation theorem, not another local description. This cycle extracts the first graded Betti data already implied by the exact model, tests whether the double-pair components can assemble independently, and examines a concrete representation-theoretic route to a resolution. The generator formula is an explicit corollary of the previous proof. Independent assembly fails at the all-equal point, and the proposed rank-one transverse Dunkl action fails a trace identity. No new threshold value is claimed.

The minimal homogeneous generators in every dimension

Corollary (cor:cube-degree-two-defect-generators). Let \(k\) have characteristic zero, \(n\ge2\), \(B=k[e_1,\ldots,e_n]\), \(\deg e_j=j\), and \(C=N_B^{**}/N_B\) for the actual degree-two cyclic image. Its minimal homogeneous generator polynomial is \[ \beta_0(C;t)=\sum_{0\le u<v\le n}t^{u+v+1}-\sum_{w=2}^{2n}t^w. \tag{BG} \] Thus its minimal number of generators is \((n-1)(n-2)/2\). For \(n\ge3\) its first generator degree is four; for \(n=2\), \(C=0\). In particular \(C\) is not cyclic for \(n\ge4\). After extension to the root ring \(R\), it is not a direct sum, with arbitrary grading shifts, of the component quotients \[ R/((a_i-a_j)^2,(a_u-a_v)^2) \] over all unordered disjoint pairs of unordered pairs among \(a_0=0,a_1,\ldots,a_n\), for any \(n\ge3\).

Proof. Modulo \(B_+=(e_1,\ldots,e_n)\), the exterior module is \(\bigwedge^2(k[X]/X^{n+1})\), with the original shift one. The basis vector \(X^u\wedge X^v\) has weight \(u+v+1\). The two other hull directions \(v_0,v_1\) already lie in \(N_B\). The generating-series calculation at the zero cluster says that the coefficient row indexed by \(u<v\) is \[ -2(v-u)\binom{-1/2}{u}\binom{-1/2}{v}T^{u+v-1}. \] Its constant factor is nonzero. Therefore the specialized cyclic image has exactly one nonzero vector in each weight \(2,\ldots,2n\), and zero in other weights. Each possible sum \(u+v=1,\ldots,2n-1\) occurs, by the explicit pairs in the cluster proof. Right-exact quotient specialization subtracts these one-dimensional spaces from the Schur frame's weight multiplicities. This proves the dimension of every graded piece of \(C/B_+C\); graded Nakayama gives (BG). No specialization of an injection is assumed.

At \(t=1\), the difference is \(\binom{n+1}{2}-(2n-1)=(n-1)(n-2)/2\). For \(n=2\) every coefficient is zero, so graded Nakayama gives \(C=0\). For \(n\ge3\), weights two and three each have one pair, and weight four has the two pairs \((0,3),(1,2)\), proving the first generator degree. The total exceeds one for \(n\ge4\), proving noncyclicity. This refines, rather than independently rediscovers, the all-equal fibre count.

Put \(N=n+1\). There are \(3\binom N4\) double-pair components, because choosing four labels leaves three pairings. Each displayed component quotient has a one-dimensional fibre at the origin, irrespective of its grading shift. Their direct sum would therefore have origin fibre dimension \(3\binom N4\), whereas the actual root-ring fibre dimension is \((N-2)(N-3)/2\). For \(N\ge4\), their ratio is \(N(N-1)/4>1\). Hence this direct sum cannot be the actual module. This does not refute a presentation with gluing maps and nontrivial relations at component intersections. \(\square\)

The first two known cases agree: (BG) is \(t^4\) at \(n=3\) and \(t^4+t^5+t^6\) at \(n=4\). These are consequences of the proved formula, not new computation. The generator degrees of the defect are not the leading-coefficient degrees of annihilators; its presentation and the marked order filtration remain necessary.

A precise obstruction to the transverse Dunkl shortcut

Lemma (lem:cube-double-pair-dunkl-obstruction). Let \(K\) have characteristic zero and \(M=K[x,y]/(x^2,y^2)\). Let \(X\) be multiplication by \(x\), and let \(s\) act by \(x\mapsto-x,y\mapsto y\) on the invariant generator \(1\). For no \(c\in K\) is there a \(K\)-linear endomorphism \(Y\) of \(M\) satisfying \[ [Y,X]=1-2cs. \tag{DC} \] The same holds with the two normal variables exchanged. Thus the actual transverse defect on every open double-pair stratum cannot carry this rank-one rational-Cherednik normal action with its polynomial multiplication and natural finite-pair reflection unchanged.

Proof. In the basis \(1,x,y,xy\), the reflection has diagonal \(1,-1,1,-1\), so its trace is zero. The trace of the right side of (DC) is four for every \(c\). The trace of a commutator of finite-dimensional endomorphisms is zero, since \(\operatorname{tr}(YX)=\operatorname{tr}(XY)\). This contradicts characteristic zero.

To apply this exact representation to the actual defect, use the local scheme theorem. There is always a finite pair: if one pair contains the distinguished zero root, use the other. Label the distinct clusters by an unramified extension and take the invariant coefficient field along the stratum. The root module is \(K[x,y]/(x^2,y^2)\). Its cyclic generator can be taken from the symmetric-ring cyclic quotient in the proof of that theorem, so the finite-pair transposition fixes it and changes only the sign of its corresponding root-difference coordinate. All tangential coefficient-field elements are fixed. This is precisely the reflection used above. The hypothesis that \(Y\) is \(K\)-linear is essential to the finite trace argument and is part of the stated normal-action test. \(\square\)

Source and scope audit. The motivation was the graded-resolution programme for equal-coordinate arrangements in Bowman–Norton–Simental, On BGG resolutions of unitary modules for quiver Hecke and Cherednik algebras. Its Section 9.1.3 concerns the coordinate ring of a reduced arrangement with \(N=ke\), and its introductory resolution theorem assumes an actual Cherednik module of the specified type. Matching support does not identify our thickened marked module with it. We read those scope passages, not the entire proof, and import no resolution or regularity theorem. The normalization (DC) follows from Definition 2.1 in Etingof–Stoica, Unitary representations of rational Cherednik algebras, by taking one reflection with root–coroot pairing two. We read that definition; the obstruction itself is the elementary trace proof above.

This excludes only the specified unchanged transverse action. It does not exclude all BGG methods, indirect functors, different modules, non-\(K\)-linear tangential operators, or algebras with a different commutator. No completion or parabolic-restriction theorem is invoked to promote it to an unrestricted global nonexistence statement. The local thickness and natural reflection, not an unproved analogy between supports, are what falsify the shortcut.

General statement. cor:cube-degree-two-defect-generators gives the complete zeroth graded Betti row in every dimension in characteristic zero and rules out independent component assembly. lem:cube-double-pair-dunkl-obstruction tests the concrete transverse algebraic structure required by one proposed resolution route, for every parameter. The missing global filtered relation theorem is still open.

The medium pre-proof reviewer identified (BG) as a graded corollary and the trace argument as a new local obstruction. A fresh-context medium-reasoning correctness reviewer passed the weight shift, quotient specialization, component count, equivariant local generator and precisely scoped trace exclusion. No mathematical gap or unused hypothesis was found. No new numerical run was needed: the earlier generating-series encoding audit and the displayed four-dimensional basis suffice.

Assessment and next step. The explicit generators are useful constraints on a global presentation, but this cycle computes no threshold. The direct-sum and unchanged transverse-Dunkl routes fail before a larger computation is warranted. Next on cube-odd-characteristic, return to the exact filtered polynomial kernel: inspect the retained complete degree-two rational row for structural relations that can be expressed in the all-dimensional exterior model. Formulate and test a uniform relation-degree statement, preserving the highest-order coefficient. Any proposed symmetry or resolution must imply that degree statement; a new unfiltered presentation alone is insufficient.

27 September 2026 — The full degree-two cyclic defect is not Cohen–Macaulay in dimension four

Working graded obstruction from the retained complete rational row. The full cyclic defect is not Cohen–Macaulay at the homogeneous origin; its bounded annihilator kernel is not free. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and outcome. Open statement 3 needs the first degree of each filtered polynomial relation. The uniform free hull and local defect schemes do not provide those relations. This cycle returns to the retained exact row and tests a concrete possible simplification: could the full cyclic defect have a codimension-two Cohen–Macaulay resolution, turning the bounded annihilator kernel into a free module? The grading contradicts that hypothesis already in the exact unresolved-dimension control. This concerns the full cyclic image, and neither contradicts the proved perfection of the boundary-coordinate ideal nor the Cohen–Macaulay first-step ideal.

A degree obstruction to a free second syzygy

Lemma (lem:graded-codimension-two-kernel-bound). Let \(B=k[z_1,\ldots,z_n]\) have positive variable weights, and let \[ \Phi:F=\bigoplus_{i=1}^{U}B(-c_i)\longrightarrow L=\bigoplus_{j=1}^{r}B(-w_j) \] be homogeneous and of generic rank \(r\). Put \(K=\ker\Phi\) and \(C=\operatorname{coker}\Phi\). Suppose \(C\ne0\) has codimension two, and every nonzero homogeneous vector of \(K\) has total degree at least \(\mu\). If \(K\) is graded free, then \[ \mu(U-r)\le\sum_i c_i-\sum_j w_j. \tag{KB} \] In particular (KB) holds if \(C\) is Cohen–Macaulay at the homogeneous maximal ideal. No minimality assumption on the displayed presentation is required.

Proof. If \(K=\bigoplus_{\nu=1}^{U-r}B(-b_\nu)\), its rank is \(U-r\) by the generic rank hypothesis. Each basis vector is a nonzero homogeneous kernel element, so \(b_\nu\ge\mu\). Additivity of Hilbert series in \[ 0\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow F\longrightarrow L\longrightarrow C\longrightarrow0 \] gives \[ H_C(t)=\frac{Q(t)}{\prod_{j=1}^n(1-t^{\deg z_j})},\qquad Q(t)=\sum_jt^{w_j}-\sum_it^{c_i}+\sum_\nu t^{b_\nu}. \] The denominator has a zero of order \(n\) at one and \(\dim C=n-2\), so \(Q(1)=Q'(1)=0\). The second equality yields \(\sum_\nu b_\nu=\sum_i c_i-\sum_j w_j\). Summing \(b_\nu\ge\mu\) proves (KB).

If \(C\) is Cohen–Macaulay at the graded maximal ideal, Auslander–Buchsbaum there gives projective dimension two. A minimal graded free resolution over the positively weighted polynomial ring has the same length: after localization its matrices are still minimal, because their entries lie in the graded maximal ideal. Comparing its length-two resolution with the displayed free presentation shows that \(K\) is graded projective, with any nonminimal free summands retained. A finite graded projective module over \(B\) is graded free: lift a homogeneous basis modulo the graded maximal ideal, use graded Nakayama for surjectivity, split the surjection, and apply graded Nakayama again to its zero-fibre kernel. Thus the first assertion applies. This is the standard Hilbert-numerator moment argument, used here with a lower bound on actual kernel degrees. \(\square\)

The exact row makes the free-kernel inequality impossible

Corollary (cor:cube-full-cyclic-defect-noncm). For \(n=4,d=2\) over every characteristic-zero field, the actual full symmetric cyclic defect \(C=N_B^{**}/N_B\) is not Cohen–Macaulay at \(B_+=(e_1,e_2,e_3,e_4)\). The complete bounded annihilator kernel on coefficient orders \(0,\ldots,18\) is not a free graded \(B\)-module.

Proof. By the Schur hull theorem, the full hull is free of rank twelve with weights \[ (0,1,2,3,4,4,5,5,6,6,7,8),\qquad \sum_jw_j=51. \] The monic cutoff lemma and the retained complete rational row give a monic order-nineteen annihilator. Hence the columns of orders zero through eighteen generate the full cyclic image, and we have the exact presentation \[ \Phi:\bigoplus_{c=0}^{18}B(-c)\longrightarrow N_B^{**},\qquad \operatorname{coker}\Phi=C. \] The source-weight sum is \(0+\cdots+18=171\), and the generic kernel rank is \(19-12=7\). The polynomial embedded change to the Schur hull preserves the original kernel, so it does not alter any relation degrees.

The certified threshold row is infinite below order twelve and is \[ 15,\ 12,\ 11,\ 6,\ 5,\ 2,\ 2,\ 0 \quad\hbox{at orders }12,13,\ldots,19. \] For bounded orders twelve through eighteen, adding the order gives the least possible total degrees \[ 27,\ 25,\ 25,\ 21,\ 21,\ 19,\ 20. \] Thus every nonzero homogeneous vector in \(\ker\Phi\) has degree at least nineteen; degree nineteen is attained at order seventeen. These are the original coefficient coordinates. Passing to the Ore operator coefficients \(W_c/c!\) rescales them by nonzero characteristic-zero constants and changes no total degree. No new numerical computation or unproved lower-bound lift is used here.

The cluster support theorem says the root-ring pullback of \(C\) has exactly the double-pair union as support. In four root parameters its components have codimension two. Since \(R\) is finite faithfully flat over \(B\), \(C\) also has codimension two and is nonzero. If its bounded kernel were free, the lemma would require \[ 19(19-12)=133\ \le\ 171-51=120, \] which is false. The kernel is therefore not graded free. If \(C\) were Cohen–Macaulay at the homogeneous origin, the last part of the lemma would make that kernel graded free, the same contradiction. Scalar extension preserves the exact row and all the displayed gradings, so the conclusion holds over every characteristic-zero field. \(\square\)
