27 September 2026 — A genuine finite-jet model retains the hidden extension, with an explicit endpoint cost

Working five-root global power inclusion and all-dimensional conditional endpoint bound. The Artin test retains the extension class; a general jet-power bound and intermediate-order thresholds remain open. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and outcome. Open statement 3 needs a polynomial degree mechanism retaining the actual lower layers and marked order. The route review proposed testing whether a power of the pair ideal lies in the EPD image. Individual arcs discard the known hidden class, but the full transverse first-order algebra retains it. A complete finite-distribution calculation there proves a square inclusion; the known global dimension filtration then proves \(J^4\subseteq\mathcal L(J)\) for the five-root family. This is a global polynomial inclusion, not just agreement of reduced fibres. In every dimension a power inclusion gives a finite free jet presentation and an explicit monic endpoint bound. The general power inclusion and the intermediate-order lift still need proof.

General statement. lem:cube-epd-finite-jet-endpoint proves, for every \(N\ge5\), that \(J^q\subseteq\mathcal L(J)\) yields a finite graded presentation and original degree-two monic order at most \((q+3)N-1\). prop:cube-five-root-epd-jet-power proves the hypothesis globally with \(q=4\) for the existing five-root control. The latter is an exact consequence of a complete Artin certificate and the global curve/vertex filtration, with no new dimension or threshold row sampled.

A finite-jet power gives an explicit polynomial monic endpoint

Lemma (lem:cube-epd-finite-jet-endpoint). In characteristic zero, let \(N=n+1\ge5\), \(S=k[c_2,\ldots,c_N]\), \(P=S[s,v]\), with weights \(\deg c_i=i,\deg s=1,\deg v=2\), and put \(c_0=1,c_1=0\). Write \(a_j=[t^j](\sum_{i=0}^N(-1)^ic_it^i)/(1-st+vt^2)\), \(J=(a_{N-1},a_N)\), and \[ \mathcal L=\partial_s^2+s\partial_s\partial_v+v\partial_v^2+\tfrac52\partial_v. \] Suppose, for an integer \(q\ge1\), that \(J^q\subseteq\mathcal L(J)\) as \(S\)-submodules. Then the full centered defect has a finite graded \(S\)-free presentation \[ (J/J^{q+2})(-2)\xrightarrow{\mathcal L}(P/J^q)(-4)\longrightarrow C^c\longrightarrow0. \tag{FJ} \] The source and target ranks are respectively \[ \binom N2\left(\frac{(q+2)(q+3)}2-1\right),\qquad \binom N2\frac{q(q+1)}2. \] Its first-relation weights are at most \((q+3)N-2\). Consequently the least original degree-two monic operator order is at most \((q+3)N-1\). This implication is all-dimensional; the power inclusion is an explicit hypothesis, and no intermediate-order threshold formula is asserted.

Proof of the presentation. The recorded EPD theorem gives \(C^c=(P/\mathcal L(J))(-4)\), the regular sequence \(a_{N-1},a_N\) of weights \(N-1,N\), and an \(S\)-free pair algebra \(P/J\) of rank \(\binom N2\). Its Schur basis has weights \(u+v-1\), \(0\le u<v<N\), hence largest weight \(2N-4\). The regular-sequence conormal layers are \[ J^i/J^{i+1}\cong \bigoplus_{a+b=i}(P/J)(-a(N-1)-bN). \] These can also be seen by eliminating the two highest parameter coefficients: replacing \(c_{N-1},c_N\) by \(a_{N-1},a_N\) is a triangular polynomial coordinate change. Lifting homogeneous bases of the conormal layers gives graded \(S\)-free bases of all the finite quotients in (FJ), since the layers are free. Counting the layers gives the displayed ranks.

The operator \(\mathcal L\) has differential order two, so the product rule gives \(\mathcal L(J^{q+2})\subseteq J^q\). Its induced map in (FJ) is well-defined and homogeneous of degree zero with the displayed shifts. The cokernel is \(P/(\mathcal L(J)+J^q)\), shifted by four, hence is exactly \(C^c\) under the hypothesis. The largest source weight before shifting is \((2N-4)+(q+1)N\); its shift by two gives \((q+3)N-2\). Homogeneous unit cancellations passing to the minimal free cover remove equal-weight source and target summands and introduce no larger first-relation weights.

From relation weights to a monic order. The deflated free target \(F\) is a minimal \(S\)-free cover of \(C^c\), since its marked image \(M=\mathscr A_0v\) lies in \(S_+F\). The marker weight is \(w_1=2N-1\). Let \(U\) be the least core monic order, whose existence follows from Noetherian finite generation. Then \(v,Dv,\ldots,D^{U-1}v\) are a minimal \(S\)-generating set of \(M\): a homogeneous dependence with a constant coefficient on any one of them would, by positive parameter weights, give a smaller monic relation. The monic order-\(U\) relation and differentiation generate every later iterate from this prefix. Thus the minimal first-relation weights of \(C^c\) are precisely \(w_1,w_1+1,\ldots,w_1+U-1\). Their maximum is bounded by the source maximum in (FJ). Exact marked deflation shifts original order by \(w_1\), so the least original monic order is \(w_1+U\le(q+3)N-1\). The original polynomial degree is the same for this homogeneous monic operator. \(\square\)

Four powers suffice globally in the five-root model

Proposition (prop:cube-five-root-epd-jet-power). For \(N=5\) over every characteristic-zero field, \[ J^4\subseteq\mathcal L(J),\qquad J=(a_4,a_5)\subset P=S[s,v]. \tag{JP} \] The image of \(J^2\) in \(C^c=(P/\mathcal L(J))(-4)\) lies in its vertex torsion. In the transverse first-order algebra \[ T=k[\epsilon_3,\epsilon_4,\epsilon_5]/(\epsilon_3,\epsilon_4,\epsilon_5)^2, \quad(c_2,c_3,c_4,c_5)=(-15,10+\epsilon_3,60+\epsilon_4,-72+\epsilon_5), \] one has \(J_T^2\subseteq\mathcal L(J_T)\), while \(J_T\not\subseteq\mathcal L(J_T)\). The global exponent four is sufficient, not asserted least.

The full transverse test. Use the retained complete minimal three-by-ten presentation of \(C^c\) and the known weight-eight class \(\eta=[a_4]\). Over \(T\) the actual defect has dimension five over \(k\), and \(\eta_T\ne0\). This is certified over \(\mathbb Q\) by expansion in the basis \(1,\epsilon_3,\epsilon_4,\epsilon_5\): a complete dual basis annihilates the presentation, and a retained normalized functional takes value one on \(\eta_T\). The complete calculation below expresses every one of these five dual functionals on \(P_T/\mathcal L(J_T)\) as distributions at the mixed pair point \((s,v)=(1,-6)\). On the constant parameter component their ordinary jet order is at most three; on each of the three first-order parameter components it is at most one. There is no contribution at the two same-cluster pair points.

At the reduced parameter values, both \(a_4,a_5\) vanish to ordinary order at least two at \((1,-6)\), as direct value and gradient evaluation verifies. Thus any element of \(J_T^2\), including arbitrary polynomial multiples, has constant parameter component vanishing to order at least four there, and each first-order parameter component vanishing to order at least two. All five functionals annihilate it, proving \(J_T^2\subseteq\mathcal L(J_T)\). Nonvanishing of \(\eta_T=[a_4]\) proves failure for the first power. This is a test of the whole Artin algebra, not only individual tangent arcs.

Why this implies the global assertion. Let \(T_0\) denote vertex torsion, to distinguish it from the Artin algebra. The proved dimension filtration gives \(K/T_0\cong k[z](-8)\), with parameters \((-15z^2,10z^3,60z^4,-72z^5)\), and \(T_0\) is supported in weights ten through eighteen. Since \(\eta\) is nonzero in weight eight, its image generates the degree-eight piece of the curve layer; normalize that isomorphism so it maps to one. The pair ideal \(J\) lies in the normalization ideal, so every \(h\in J^2\) maps into \(K\).

Take homogeneous \(h\in J^2\), of input weight \(d\ge8\). Its class modulo \(T_0\) is \(\lambda z^{d-4}\eta\). Every integer \(d-4\ge4\) lies in the semigroup generated by two and three, so choose a polynomial \(r(c_2,c_3)\) whose restriction to the curve is \(z^{d-4}\). Hence \([h]=\lambda r\eta+\tau\) with \(\tau\in T_0\). In the displayed Artin specialization, vertex torsion maps to zero because \(c_2\) is invertible, whereas it acts nilpotently on \(T_0\). The element \(r_T\) has constant term one at \(z=1\), so is a unit. The transverse square inclusion makes \([h]_T=0\); since \(\eta_T\ne0\), this forces \(\lambda=0\). Therefore the image of \(J^2\) lies in \(T_0\) globally.

Finally \(J^4\subseteq J^2\), and each homogeneous element of \(J^4\) has input weight at least sixteen, hence defect weight at least twenty. Its image lies in \(T_0\), which has no such weights, so that image is zero. This proves (JP). The argument uses inclusion and grading, never multiplication of cokernel classes: \(\mathcal L(J)\) is still only an \(S\)-submodule. Rational exactness and flat field extension give every characteristic-zero field. \(\square\)

For this control, (FJ) has source rank 200 and target rank 100, with the sufficient original monic bound 34. The exact minimum was already known to be nineteen. The purpose of this larger finite presentation is the jet structure and its possible uniform generalization, not a faster computation or an improved five-root threshold. Its order filtration still needs a controlled polynomial lift.

Bounded adjoint distributions test all jet orders

The exact driver works with the complete existing defect presentation. Base change to the nonflat Artin algebra is legitimate for this cokernel: \(J\otimes_S T\to J_T\) is onto, \(\mathcal L\) is \(S\)-linear, and right exactness gives \((P/\mathcal L(J))\otimes_S T=P_T/\mathcal L(J_T)\). No injection of the tensor product of the image is assumed. Expanding the target in the four-element parameter basis gives a twelve-dimensional vector space; the full relation image has codimension five. The program retains its complete dual basis and a normalized detector of \(\eta_T\).

For a defect functional \(\ell\), define \(\psi(h)=\ell(q(h))\), where \(q(h)=(Y-X)h(X+Y,XY)\) in the pair algebra. This factors through \(P_T/J_T\). It also kills every harmonic polynomial: the program checks the complete retained cyclic image, and the proved monic cutoff makes those columns generate all the harmonic images. Since \(\mathcal L\) is onto with that harmonic kernel, there is a unique functional \(\lambda\) on \(P_T\) with \(\psi=\lambda\mathcal L\); under the EPD cokernel isomorphism it is precisely \(\ell\). The issue is whether this functional is a finite jet distribution, not whether an abstract functional exists.

The reduced root polynomial is \(p_0(Z)=(Z+2)^3(Z-3)^2\). In the deformed root algebra \(p_0\) lies in the square-zero parameter ideal, so \(p_0^2=0\). The two root clusters therefore have nilpotence bounds six and four. On their alternating pairs the support points are \((-4,4),(1,-6),(6,9)\) in \((s,v)\), with ordinary total jet bounds ten, eight and six respectively. For example the mixed tensor has nilpotent local root coordinates of orders six and four, so every polynomial of local total order nine vanishes; \(s-s_0,v-v_0\) lie in that root-coordinate maximal ideal. The same argument gives bounds eleven and seven for the vanishing ideals at the same-cluster points. The driver independently checks all boundary monomials in the actual pair multiplication matrices. Their generalized eigenspace dimensions over \(\mathbb Q\) are 12, 24 and 4, totaling the full dimension 40.

Here is the finite completeness argument. At a support point \((s_0,v_0)\), transposing \(\mathcal L\) multiplies the highest finite-distribution symbol by \[ \xi^2+s_0\xi\zeta+v_0\zeta^2. \] This polynomial is nonzero, even at a coincident pair, so the order of every nonzero finite distribution rises by exactly two. Distinct support points cannot cancel, and the argument applies separately to the four parameter components because \(\mathcal L\) has no parameter-dependent coefficients. Thus bounds ten, eight and six for \(\psi\) give exhaustive candidate bounds eight, six and four for \(\lambda\). If any bounded adjoint system failed, no larger finite jet order could repair it. This is a standard principal-symbol argument, not a conjectured truncation.

In local coordinates \(x=s-s_0,y=v-v_0\), the adjoint equations use \[ \mathcal L(x^ay^b)=a(a-1)x^{a-2}y^b+s_0abx^{a-1}y^{b-1} +v_0b(b-1)x^ay^{b-2}+b(a+b+\tfrac32)x^ay^{b-1}. \] Every matrix entry is independently checked by symbolic differentiation. The three rational matrices have sizes \(66\times45\), \(45\times28\), \(28\times15\). All twenty right-hand sides—five functionals times four parameter components—lie in their images. The resulting jets vanish at the first and third support points. At the mixed point their maximum component orders are exactly \(3,1,1,1\), giving the square-ideal conclusion proved above. The full matrices of moments and solutions, all dual functionals, the detector and successful checks are retained in the certificate. The accepted final computation took about 3.14 CPU seconds.

The five-root bound 34 is weaker than the known exact endpoint nineteen; its value is the verified mechanism, not sharper constants in a solved case. General statement. lem:epd-finite-jet-galois-separation proves the finite-distribution exactness over every characteristic-zero field. thm:cube-epd-global-finite-jets proves \(J^q\subseteq\mathcal L(J)\) for some finite \(q\) for every \(N\ge5\), with explicit Artin and primary-thickness costs. Galois characters separate every finite harmonic jet

Lemma (lem:epd-finite-jet-galois-separation). Over a characteristic-zero field, put \[ \mathcal L=\partial_s^2+s\partial_s\partial_v+v\partial_v^2+\tfrac52\partial_v, \qquad H(t)=(1+st+vt^2)^{-3/2}=\sum_{j\ge0}H_j(s,v)t^j. \] A finite-support distribution on \(k[s,v]\) means a linear functional factoring through a quotient by powers of finitely many maximal ideals. A finite-support distribution \(\psi\) annihilates all \(H_j\) if and only if \[ \psi=\mathcal L^t\phi,\qquad (\mathcal L^t\phi)(f)=\phi(\mathcal Lf), \] for a unique finite-support distribution \(\phi\). Its support is contained in that of \(\psi\). At each geometric support point where \(\psi\) has ordinary total jet order at most \(m\), \(\phi\) has order at most \(m-2\); for \(m=0,1\) both local components must vanish. Equivalently, polynomial EPD harmonics detect all finite jets modulo the transposed operator. This statement concerns ordinary local jet order, not weighted parameter degree.

One support point. First work over an algebraically closed field and fix \(a=(s_0,v_0)\). The space of distributions of order at most \(m\) at \(a\) has dimension \(\binom{m+2}{2}\). Put \(Q=1+s_0t+v_0t^2\). Evaluating such a distribution on \(H(t)\) gives \[ \frac{R(t)}{Q^{m+3/2}},\qquad \deg R\le2m. \] Indeed, a derivative \(\partial_s^a\partial_v^b\) contributes a nonzero constant times \(t^{a+2b}Q^{m-a-b}\), where \(a+b\le m\). The \(2m+1\) derivatives \[ \partial_v^j\ (0\le j\le m),\qquad \partial_s\partial_v^j\ (0\le j<m) \] give numerators with distinct lowest powers \(0,1,\ldots,2m\), since \(Q(0)=1\). Their scalar rising-factorial coefficients are nonzero in characteristic zero. They form a basis of the polynomials of degree at most \(2m\). Thus the kernel of evaluation on all \(H_j\) has dimension \(\binom m2\).

The direct identity \(\mathcal LH(t)=0\) puts the image of \(\mathcal L^t\) from distributions of order at most \(m-2\) in that kernel. Its top symbol multiplies a nonzero distribution symbol by \(\xi^2+s_0\xi\zeta+v_0\zeta^2\), a nonzero polynomial. Hence it is injective and raises order by exactly two. Its source dimension is \(\binom m2\), proving equality with the kernel. For \(m=0,1\), the evaluation map is already injective. This proves the local assertion, including coincident-root points.

Separating different points. Factor each \(Q\) as \((1+bt)(1+ct)\). Distinct support points are distinct unordered pairs \(\{b,c\}\). For all distinct nonzero values occurring, the square classes of \(1+bt\) are independent in \(k(t)^*/k(t)^{*2}\): the valuation at \(t=-1/b\) detects its individual exponent. In the corresponding multiquadratic Galois extension, an off-diagonal pair has the sign-change character of its two nonzero values, or the singleton character when one is zero. These nontrivial characters are distinct for distinct off-diagonal pairs. Applying the character projections to \(\psi(H)=0\) therefore forces each such local rational numerator to vanish separately.

Diagonal pairs have trivial character. At \(b=c\ne0\), their contribution has denominator \((1+bt)^{2m+3}\) and numerator degree at most \(2m\), so it is a proper rational function with a pole only at \(-1/b\). Different diagonal values have disjoint poles. The diagonal value zero contributes a polynomial. Partial-fraction uniqueness separates these contributions too. The equality of formal series at \(t=0\) is an equality in the multiquadratic function field, since the chosen square roots with constant term one embed it in an algebraic extension of \(k((t))\). Thus every local component satisfies the one-point condition, and their unique preimages sum to \(\phi\). The principal-symbol argument also excludes extra support or a nonzero finite-support kernel.

For a general characteristic-zero field, extend to a finite Galois field splitting the finite support points and their quadratics. The bounded spaces of distributions and the displayed maps are finite-dimensional and commute with that extension. Uniqueness makes the constructed preimage Galois invariant, so it descends. Finally \(\ker\mathcal L\) is spanned by the \(H_j\): in weighted degree \(d\), the coefficient recurrence for \(g=\sum_b\alpha_b s^{d-2b}v^b\) has successive nonzero coefficient \((b+1)(d-b+\tfrac12)\) on \(\alpha_{b+1}\). It proves that \(\mathcal L:P_d\to P_{d-2}\) is onto with one-dimensional kernel, generated by \(H_d\). This also proves surjectivity of \(\mathcal L\) on polynomials. \(\square\)

The jet-power inclusion exists in every dimension

Theorem (thm:cube-epd-global-finite-jets). Let \(k\) have characteristic zero, \(N=n+1\ge5\), \(S=k[c_2,\ldots,c_N]\) with \(\deg c_i=i\), and \(P=S[s,v]\). Put \(c_0=1,c_1=0\) and \(a_j=[u^j](\sum_{i=0}^N(-1)^ic_i u^i)/(1-su+vu^2)\). For the EPD operator above, there is an integer \(q\ge1\) such that \[ J^q\subseteq\mathcal L(J),\qquad J=(a_{N-1},a_N)\subset P=S[s,v]. \tag{GJ} \] More precisely, the following two quantitative statements hold.

  1. If the parameter ring is specialized to a finite-dimensional local Artin algebra \(T\) over a characteristic-zero coefficient field \(K\), with residue field \(K\) and maximal ideal \(\mathfrak n^e=0\), then \[ J_T^{(2N+1)e-4}\subseteq\mathcal L(J_T). \]
  2. Write a finite primary decomposition of zero in \(C_0=P/\mathcal L(J)\) as \(0=\bigcap_i Q_i\), with \(M_i=C_0/Q_i\) primary for \(\mathfrak p_i\). Choose \(e_i\ge1\) with \(\mathfrak p_i^{e_i}M_i=0\), and put \(E=\max_i e_i\). Then (GJ) holds with \(q=(2N+1)E-4\). The finite-jet presentation therefore gives original degree-two monic order at most \[ N\bigl((2N+1)E-1\bigr)-1. \]

The parameter \(E\) measures nilpotence in a chosen primary decomposition and is not bounded here by an explicit function of \(N\). Thus this proves all-dimensional finite-jet existence and a cost in terms of primary thickness, not an explicit dimension-only threshold formula.

Artin proof: the functional and its actual support. Base change gives \(C_0\otimes_S T=P_T/\mathcal L(J_T)\) by right exactness; no flatness of \(T\) is assumed. This is finite-dimensional over \(K\), because the EPD quotient is the cokernel of the finite free pair target. Take any \(K\)-linear functional \(\ell\) on it. Precomposing with \(\mathcal L\) gives \(\psi=\ell\mathcal L\), which factors through the finite pair algebra \(P_T/J_T\) and annihilates every harmonic polynomial. Choose a \(K\)-basis \(t_i\) of \(T\); the component functionals \(\psi_i(f)=\psi(t_if)\) annihilate every \(H_j\).

Let \(p_0\) be the residue polynomial \(p\bmod\mathfrak n\), retaining all root multiplicities. In \(T[Z]/p\), \(p_0\) lies in \(\mathfrak n\), so \(p_0^e=0\). After a splitting field extension, a reduced root cluster of multiplicity \(m_i\) has local nilpotence bound \(em_i\). A pair of clusters therefore gives ordinary pair-coordinate jet bound \(e(m_i+m_j)-2\), allowing \(i=j\), and hence at most \(2eN-2\). The pair algebra is identified as a \(P_T\)-module with the alternating part of the two root factors, so nilpotence and this jet bound transfer through that module identification; no algebra structure on the alternating part is used. The coarser root-power algebra may contain extra diagonal simple-root points; they are not used as actual support. Indeed the reduced pair ideal \(J_0\) maps into \(\mathfrak n(P_T/J_T)\), so \(J_0^e\) annihilates this quotient. Every component \(\psi_i\) is therefore supported at zeros of \(J_0\), where both reduced pair generators vanish.

The Galois-separation lemma now gives a finite-support preimage \(\lambda_i\) of \(\psi_i\), of jet order at most \(2eN-4\), at the same points. This is exactly \(f\mapsto\ell(t_if)\): both precompose with the surjective operator \(\mathcal L\) to \(\psi_i\). Thus every parameter component of every defect functional has that finite jet bound.

The power estimate. Expand an element of \(J_T^q\) as a sum of polynomial multiples of products of \(q\) pair generators. Each generator is its reduction plus a polynomial with coefficients in \(\mathfrak n\). Terms using at least \(e\) perturbation factors vanish. Each remaining term has at least \(q-e+1\) reduced generators, all vanishing at the actual support point. Consequently every coefficient-field component vanishes there to ordinary order at least \(q-e+1\). Taking \(q=(2N+1)e-4\) gives \(q-e+1=2eN-3\), greater than the jet bound \(2eN-4\). Every \(\ell\) therefore kills the image of \(J_T^q\), proving that image zero. Faithful field extension descends the conclusion from a splitting field. Products of Artin local algebras are handled componentwise.

Global proof: finitely many Artin detections suffice. The \(S\)-module \(C_0\) is finite. Noetherian primary decomposition gives the quotients \(M_i\) in the statement, with \(\sqrt{\operatorname{Ann}M_i}=\mathfrak p_i\); finite generation of the prime supplies a finite power \(\mathfrak p_i^{e_i}\) annihilating \(M_i\). Every element outside \(\mathfrak p_i\) acts injectively on the primary module, so \(M_i\to(M_i)_{\mathfrak p_i}\) is injective. Set \(A_i=S_{\mathfrak p_i}/\mathfrak p_i^{e_i}S_{\mathfrak p_i}\). The map \(C_0\to(M_i)_{\mathfrak p_i}\) factors through \(C_0\otimes_S A_i\).

Each \(A_i\) is a local Artin algebra over a coefficient field isomorphic to \(\kappa(\mathfrak p_i)\) and containing the original \(k\). For completeness, choose a transcendence basis of this finitely generated residue field over \(k\), and lift it to \(A_i\). Every denominator with nonzero residue is a unit, embedding the corresponding rational function field. The remaining residue extension is finite separable in characteristic zero. A primitive element lifts to an actual root of its minimal polynomial by finite Hensel correction across the nilpotent maximal ideal, since the derivative is a unit. This embeds the residue field compatibly with \(k\); the finite maximal-ideal filtration makes \(A_i\) finite-dimensional over it.

The Artin assertion kills the image of \(J^{(2N+1)e_i-4}\) in every \(C_0\otimes_S A_i\). For \(q=(2N+1)E-4\), its image is consequently zero in each localized \(M_i\), then in each \(M_i\) by injectivity. The intersection \(\bigcap_iQ_i=0\) forces its image in \(C_0\) to be zero. This is (GJ). Substitution into the proved finite-jet endpoint bound \((q+3)N-1\) gives the displayed monic estimate. No assertion about multiplication of defect classes, reduced-fibre detection or a global splitting is used. \(\square\)

The triple-double extension is unchanged by simple spectators

Theorem (thm:cube-triple-double-formal-stability). Work in characteristic zero with \(S_N=k[c_2,\ldots,c_N]\), \(N\ge5\), and centered monic polynomial \(p_N(Z)=\sum_{j=0}^N(-1)^jc_jZ^{N-j}\), \(c_0=1,c_1=0\). At a geometric coefficient point of exact root pattern \((3,2,1,\ldots,1)\), label the separated root clusters and complete the coefficient local ring. After formal coefficient coordinates and translation and scaling of the selected five-root factor, there is an isomorphism of complete local rings \[ \widehat S_N\cong\widehat S_5[[t_1,\ldots,t_{N-5}]], \] where \(\widehat S_5\) is completed at \((c_2,c_3,c_4,c_5)=(-15,10,60,-72)\). Under this isomorphism, \[ C_N\otimes\widehat S_N\cong (C_5\otimes\widehat S_5)\widehat\otimes_{\widehat S_5}\widehat S_5[[t_1,\ldots,t_{N-5}]]. \tag{FS} \] The comparison also identifies the normalization quotient and its kernel. These are unfiltered coefficient-module isomorphisms; they are not isomorphisms of the marked Ore connections and carry no global polynomial degree bound.

In the completed coefficient base, the local pair ideal satisfies \(J_N^2\subseteq\mathcal L(J_N)\), whereas the first-power image is nonzero. At the generic triple-double prime, after an unramified residue-field extension if necessary, let \(R\) be the completed transverse local coefficient ring with maximal ideal \(\mathfrak m\), and write \(C\to D\) for the normalized top quotient. Then \(K=\ker(C\to D)\) is one-dimensional over \(R/\mathfrak m\), lies in \(\mathfrak mC\), and survives modulo \(\mathfrak m^2C\). In particular \[ 0=K\cap\mathfrak m^2C \] is a primary decomposition with quotients \(D\) and \(C/\mathfrak m^2C\), whose primary nilpotence exponents are respectively one and two. Exponent one cannot detect the embedded class. This controls the first embedded collision stratum uniformly, not the higher strata or full-collision vertex.

Finite jets permit an actual local decomposition. The all-dimensional jet-power theorem supplies some \(q_N\) with \(J_N^{q_N}\subseteq\mathcal L(J_N)\). Choose \(q\ge\max(q_N,4)\), so the degree-\(N\) and five-root defects both have the exact finite presentations \[ J/J^{q+2}\xrightarrow{\mathcal L}P/J^q\longrightarrow C_0\longrightarrow0, \] with grading shifts suppressed. The finite algebras \(P/J^{q+2}\) over a complete local coefficient ring have compatible idempotents for the distinct pair-support points. For a polynomial representative \(e\) of one such idempotent, \(e^2-e\in J^{q+2}\). Differentiating in \(s,v\) gives \((2e-1)e_s,(2e-1)e_v\in J^{q+1}\). The product rule therefore gives \(\mathcal L(ef)=e\mathcal L(f)\pmod{J^q}\). Multiplication by the lifted idempotent on \(J/J^{q+2}\) is consequently compatible with its reduction on \(P/J^q\). This finite-level argument makes no assumption that an image in an infinite formal-function space is closed.

The local pair and coefficient rings. Hensel factorization near the given point writes the universal monic polynomial as \[ p(X)=f_3(X)f_2(X)\prod_\nu(X-d_\nu), \] with pairwise coprime residual factors. For the selected cross pair, use formal coordinates \(x\) near the triple root and \(y\) near the double root. The change \((x,y)\mapsto(s,v)=(x+y,xy)\) has unit Jacobian because \(x-y\) is a unit. 27 September 2026 — A proposed all-dimensional support theorem isolates the lower collision defect

Provisional characteristic-zero argument for every N ≥ 5; the mandatory fresh-context correctness review is pending because reviewer creation is unavailable. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and outcome. Open statement 3 needs quantitative control of the primary thickness in the finite-jet model. The preceding result computes the first embedded stratum. This cycle asks whether extra kernel can occur away from its closure. The complete argument below identifies that closure as the proposed exact support, including configurations with many double clusters and an isolated quadruple cluster. Its pre-proof scope review passed, but the mandatory fresh-context correctness gate could not run; this entry does not promote the result to a working proof. Even if verified, it locates the remaining thickness problem without bounding it.

General statement. thm:cube-normalization-kernel-support is the all-parameter claim tested here: the normalization kernel has exactly the triple-double closure as support, in every characteristic-zero dimension \(N\ge5\). The proof retains the actual normalization map and finite-jet module, rather than inferring kernel vanishing from reduced fibres. The global degree bound and original intermediate-order thresholds remain open.

The lower defect lives exactly on the triple-double closure

Provisional theorem (thm:cube-normalization-kernel-support). Let \(k\) have characteristic zero, \(N\ge5\), \(S=k[c_2,\ldots,c_N]\), and \(p(Z)=\sum_{j=0}^N(-1)^jc_jZ^{N-j}\), with \(c_0=1,c_1=0\). Let \(C_N\) be the full centered degree-two defect and \(K_N\) the kernel of its actual normalization quotient \(C_N\twoheadrightarrow D_{22}(-4)\). Let \(\Delta_{32}\subset\operatorname{Spec}S\) be the reduced closed locus of polynomials divisible by \( (Z-b)^3(Z-c)^2\), allowing \(b=c\). Then \[ \operatorname{Supp}_S K_N=\Delta_{32},\qquad \dim K_N=N-4. \] At the generic point of this irreducible locus, \(K_N\) has length one. Equivalently, \(\sqrt{\operatorname{Ann}_S K_N}\) is the prime ideal of \(\Delta_{32}\). This is a support theorem, not an equality of annihilator ideals or a description of the deeper primary components. The original order filtration and its degree thresholds are not identified.

The locus and the necessary root patterns. Over an algebraic closure, parameterize the locus by \[ p(Z)=(Z-b)^3(Z-c)^2R(Z),\qquad \deg R=N-5, \] with \(R\) monic and the total trace zero. For \(N=5\), the trace is \(3b+2c=0\), giving an affine line. For \(N\ge6\), the next coefficient of \(R\) is \(3b+2c\), and its remaining coefficients are free. Thus the parameter space is affine of dimension \(N-4\) and is integral. The map to coefficient space is finite: \(b,c\) are integral roots of \(p\), and monic division expresses all coefficients of \(R\) polynomially in \(b,c,c_2,\ldots,c_N\). Its image is therefore closed and irreducible. Its dense open subset has exact pattern \((3,2,1,\ldots,1)\), and there the distinct triple and double roots determine \(b,c,R\) uniquely.

A polynomial lies in this image precisely when it has a root of multiplicity at least five, or distinct roots of multiplicities at least three and at least two. Consequently, outside \(\Delta_{32}\), either every cluster has size at most two, or there is exactly one cluster of size three or four and every other root is simple. This includes arbitrarily many distinct double clusters; treating only the open two-double-root stratum would not suffice.

The quartic comparison, including the actual map. We first establish \(C_4\cong D_{22,4}(-4)\). Put \(S_4=k[c_2,c_3,c_4]\). The centering lemma gives the faithfully flat finite free extension \(B=S_4[\mu]/p_c(-\mu)\cong k[e_1,e_2,e_3]\). The complete anchored defect is \[ B\otimes_{S_4}C_4\cong B/(f,h^2)(-4),\quad h=e_1^2-4e_2,\quad f=e_1h+8e_3. \] Compute the base-changed normalization directly. The anchored polynomial is \(X^4-e_1X^3+e_2X^2-e_3X\). Writing it as \((X^2-uX+v)^2\) imposes \[ e_1=2u,\quad e_2=u^2+2v,\quad e_3=2uv,\quad v^2=0. \] Eliminating \(u=e_1/2\) and \(v=-h/8\) gives exactly \(f=h^2=0\). This incidence ring is the base change of the centered normalization: translate the centered squared quadratic by \(\mu=e_1/4\), and impose the anchored root equation. Hence \(B\otimes D_{22,4}\cong B/(f,h^2)\), not its reduction.

The normalization theorem supplies the actual surjection between these two modules. A surjective endomorphism of the cyclic module \(B/(f,h^2)\) is multiplication by a unit in that quotient and is injective. Thus this base-changed normalization map is an isomorphism; faithful flatness gives the assertion over \(S_4\). In particular there is no extra kernel at the total quartic collision. The doubled anchored ring is compatible with a reduced centered normalization; replacing the anchored ring by its reduction would invalidate this argument.

For use with finite jets, the EPD presentation also holds at \(N=4\). Indeed let \(P=S_4[s,v]\), let \(J\) be the kernel of the alternating pair map, and let \[ \mathcal L=\partial_s^2+s\partial_s\partial_v+v\partial_v^2+\tfrac52\partial_v. \] The polynomial integration and harmonic-kernel argument in the EPD proof is independent of \(N\): \(\mathcal L\) is onto and its kernel is the \(S_4\)-span of the harmonic coefficients. Taking the quotient of \(P/J\) by their images therefore identifies \(C_4=(P/\mathcal L(J))(-4)\). The normalization map in this presentation is ordinary evaluation on the chosen squared quadratic. Every member of \(J\) evaluates to zero there: on the dense locus of distinct quadratic roots this follows from the alternating representative and their nonzero difference, and it extends as a polynomial identity on the integral centered normalization. Since the normalization map is now an isomorphism, \(J\subseteq\mathcal L(J)\). Thus the quartic has a finite-jet presentation with \(q=1\); we do not invoke the \(N\ge5\) jet theorem outside its stated scope.

Formal pair decomposition for arbitrary root patterns. Work at a geometric coefficient point and complete its local coefficient ring. Hensel factorization writes \(p=\prod_i f_i\), with \(f_i\) monic of degree \(m_i\) and separated residual roots \(b_i\). Their coefficients, subject to the one trace equation, are formal coordinates: the multiplication Jacobian is invertible by Chinese remainders. The global jet theorem supplies \(q\) such that the completed \(C_N\), with shifts suppressed, is the cokernel of \[ J/J^{q+2}\xrightarrow{\mathcal L}P/J^q. \] We may increase \(q\) to accommodate the quartic presentation as well.

The finite idempotent argument applies to every root pattern, not only to \((3,2)\). For completeness, choose a representative \(e\) of an idempotent of \(P/J^{q+2}\). Differentiating \(e^2-e\in J^{q+2}\) puts its first pair derivatives in \(J^{q+1}\) and its second derivatives in \(J^q\), since \(2e-1\) is a unit modulo these powers. The product rule gives \(\mathcal L(ef)=e\mathcal L(f)\pmod{J^q}\). Compatible source and target idempotents therefore split the actual cokernel. Their support points are the unordered pairs \((b_i,b_j)\), encoded by both sum and product, with an internal point \(i=j\) present only if \(m_i\ge2\).

These pieces depend only on the selected factors. For \(i\ne j\), use \(x\) near \(b_i\) and \(y\) near \(b_j\). Their difference is a unit, the exact local pair ideal is \((f_i(x),f_j(y))\), and \[ \mathcal L=\partial_x\partial_y-\frac32\frac{\partial_x-\partial_y}{x-y}. \] Every unselected factor of \(p(x),p(y)\) is a unit. For an internal piece, use symmetric pair coordinates; its quotient is the alternating pair module of the selected factor \(f_i\), and its kernel is exactly the kernel for that factor. This follows by Chinese remainders on the two root algebras and taking the alternating summand, which commutes with the coefficient base change in characteristic zero. Equivalently, in the completed two-root ring the condition is \((y-x)h\in(f_i(x),f_i(y))\); the other factors are units. This argument identifies the full pair ideal and hence all of its powers, not just its support. No division by \(x-y\) is made on an internal diagonal.

The normalization algebra likewise decomposes after completion, with one point for each possible selected quadratic \(Q\) such that \(Q^2\mid p\). A cross choice requires \(m_i,m_j\ge2\), and an internal choice requires \(m_i\ge4\). Evaluation of an idempotent is the corresponding branch idempotent because \(J\) vanishes in the normalization. Thus the actual normalization map respects these decompositions. In the cross piece its incidence equations are \(f_i(x)=f_i'(x)=f_j(y)=f_j'(y)=0\); in an internal piece it is the squared-quadratic incidence for the selected factor. These are exactly the same maps as for the smaller selected polynomial.

To detect pieces with zero central fibre, use the support-preserving adjoint lemma. It identifies the dual of each EPD cokernel piece with the harmonic-annihilating distributions of the corresponding pair block. This justifies using the individual cluster deficits: internal size \(m\) contributes \((m-2)(m-3)/2\) for \(m\ge2\), and a cross block contributes \((m_i-1)(m_j-1)\). In particular internal sizes two and three and every cross pair with a singleton have zero central fibre. The finite cokernels then vanish by Nakayama. This does not assume that the EPD isomorphism is linear for multiplication by arbitrary pair polynomials.

Vanishing of the kernel outside the claimed support. If all clusters have size at most two, only cross pairs of double clusters remain. For each selected pair, its four-root formal model is the two-double-root quartic. The quartic normalization comparison proves that this entire local piece maps isomorphically to its normalization branch. Other double clusters provide smooth independent factor coefficients; they need not be simple. The trace equation can be eliminated using a center of the selected quartic, and the EPD operator is invariant under that coefficient-dependent translation. Thus the selected centered quartic coordinates and the remaining \(N-4\) coefficient coordinates give a smooth formal extension. Every normalization branch is accounted for separately, even when there are three or more double clusters.

If there is one cluster of size three and only simple spectators, every piece is zero, as is the normalization. If there is one cluster of size four and only simple spectators, the only nonzero piece is its internal pair piece. Translate its center and remove the unit spectator factors as above; this is the centered quartic module with smooth parameters, compatibly with the squared-quadratic incidence. The quartic comparison again makes the normalization map an isomorphism. These exhaust the possible patterns outside \(\Delta_{32}\). Completion is faithfully flat, so \(K_N\) vanishes at every such geometric point.

Reverse inclusion and generic length. The triple-double formal theorem identifies the normalization kernel at every exact \((3,2,1,\ldots,1)\) point with the nonzero quintic kernel with smooth spectators. At the generic triple-double prime its length is one. Thus the support of the finite \(S\)-module \(K_N\), which is closed, contains the dense open stratum and its closure \(\Delta_{32}\). The preceding vanishing gives equality. Field extension is faithfully flat, so the geometric conclusion descends to the stated characteristic-zero field. The parameter count gives dimension \(N-4\). The radical-annihilator formulation follows from the support identity. \(\square\)

Checks and scope. The quartic comparison retains the square-zero anchored parameter \(v\), reproducing exactly the old ideal \((f,h^2)\); reducing that ring would give the wrong answer. The argument separately handles every number of double clusters, whose normalization has one completed branch for each selected pair, and an isolated quadruple cluster, where division by the root difference is forbidden. These are structural tests of the universal statement, not a new finite dimension series. The triple-double theorem supplies the nonzero control and generic length; the full-collision vertex lies in the resulting closure and is not removed. All computation certificates are reused as prior evidence; no new numerical run is needed.

The medium pre-proof reviewer required the actual quartic normalization map, separate normalization branches for multiple double clusters, and a justified quartic jet presentation outside the stated \(N\ge5\) jet theorem. 27 September 2026 — Coefficient derivatives give a polynomial detector of the lower kernel

Provisional all-dimensional characteristic-zero extraction formula, with an exact universal symbolic certificate; mandatory fresh-context correctness review remains pending. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and outcome. The already-reviewed generic triple-double kernel line needs a global polynomial extraction map before it can contribute degree information. A conormal-linear map fails: taking the pair-polynomial ideal closure of the EPD image erases the kernel. Combining coefficient derivatives with pair derivatives produces the explicit map below. Its action on the first class is \(20(c-b)^7R(c)^2\), nonzero generically, and its homogeneous degree is known. The universal symbolic identities and independent coordinate controls pass. The mandatory fresh-context correctness review is still unavailable, so the formula and its global interpretation remain provisional. The preceding provisional support theorem is not used as a proved dependency.

General statement. thm:cube-kernel-polynomial-extraction proposes a homogeneous polynomial \(S\)-linear map from the actual normalization kernel to the triple-double parameter ring for every \(N\ge5\), with an explicit nonzero marked value. cor:cube-epd-conormal-extraction-obstruction records the precise failure of the simpler \(P\)-linear construction. These address open statement 3's graded extraction problem; neither the full image nor the remaining primary nilpotence is determined.

Why conormal-linear extraction erases the kernel

Provisional corollary (cor:cube-epd-conormal-extraction-obstruction). Use the EPD setup: \(S=k[c_2,\ldots,c_N]\), \(P=S[s,v]\), \(J=(a_{N-1},a_N)\), \(I=(E_{N-3},\ldots,E_N)\), \(N\ge5\), in characteristic zero. The \(P\)-ideal generated by the \(S\)-submodule \(\mathcal L(J)\) is \(I\). Every \(P\)-linear map from \(I\) to a \(P\)-module that annihilates \(\mathcal L(J)\) is therefore zero. In particular a \(P/I\)-linear map \(I/I^2\to M\) cannot detect \(K\) while annihilating those relations. If \(IM=0\), the same holds for the restriction to \(I\) of any \(k\)-linear differential operator \(P\to M\) of order at most one.

Proof. The recorded identities and the product rule give \[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal La_{N-1}&=-\tfrac12E_{N-3},& \mathcal La_N&=-\tfrac12E_{N-2},\\ \mathcal L(sa_N)&=2E_{N-1}-\tfrac32sE_{N-2},& \mathcal L(va_N)&=\tfrac52E_N-\tfrac32sE_{N-1}. \end{aligned} \] These four images generate \(I\) as a \(P\)-ideal; the opposite inclusion follows from the proved \(\mathcal L(J)\subset I\). This proves the first assertions. An operator \(T\) of order at most one is a derivation plus multiplication by \(T(1)\), as in Stacks, Example 10.133.5. For \(h\in I\), the multiplication part vanishes in \(M\), and the derivation rule gives \(T(ph)=pT(h)\), since \(hM=0\). Its restriction is therefore \(P\)-linear and the preceding conclusion applies. This is an explicit consequence of the earlier EPD identities, not a new general differential-operator theorem. It does not exclude the higher-order \(S\)-linear construction below. \(\square\)

A global polynomial formula with an explicit marked value

Provisional theorem (thm:cube-kernel-polynomial-extraction). Let \(k\) have characteristic zero and \(N\ge5\). In the preceding EPD setup, \(K=(I/\mathcal L(J))(-4)\). Let \(D_{32}\) be the parameter ring of \[ p(Z)=(Z-b)^3(Z-c)^2R(Z),\qquad R\text{ monic of degree }N-5,\qquad \operatorname{trace}(p)=0. \] For \(N=5\), this is \(k[b,c]/(3b+2c)\). For \(N\ge6\), it is the polynomial ring in \(b,c\) and the remaining coefficients of \(R\), whose next coefficient is \(3b+2c\). Give root coordinates weight one and coefficients their usual weights. The coefficient expansion defines the \(S\)-module structure. Put \[ d=c-b,\qquad q=\frac{p''(c)}2,\qquad r=\frac{p'''(c)}6. \] Regard \(h\in P\) as a symmetric polynomial in \(x,y\), with \(s=x+y,v=xy\). Define coefficient directional derivatives \(\Delta_j\), for \(j=1,2\), by varying \(p(Z)\) by \((Z-b)^j\), holding \(b,c,x,y\) fixed. Explicitly, \[ \Delta_1=(-1)^{N-1}\partial_{c_{N-1}}-b(-1)^N\partial_{c_N}, \quad \Delta_2=(-1)^{N-2}\partial_{c_{N-2}} -2b(-1)^{N-1}\partial_{c_{N-1}}+b^2(-1)^N\partial_{c_N}. \] Apply these derivatives before substituting the coefficients of the factored polynomial. All displayed operator coefficients stand on the left and are not differentiated.

For \(h\in I\), define \[ \begin{aligned} \Theta(h)=\big[& (-42dq+21d^2r)h_y-7d^2q\,h_{yy} +d^2(18q-6dr)h_{xy}+2d^3q\,h_{xyy}\\ &+24dq^2\Delta_1h+18q^2\Delta_2h -12dq^2\partial_x\Delta_2h\big]_{x=b,y=c}. \end{aligned}\tag{KE} \] Then the proposed formula is polynomial, \(S\)-linear on \(I\), and annihilates \(\mathcal L(J)\). It induces a homogeneous map \[ \Theta:K\longrightarrow D_{32}(N-6),\qquad \Theta([a_{N-1}])=20dq^2=20d^7R(c)^2. \tag{KV} \] Thus it is nonzero on the already-proved generic triple-double kernel line. Surjectivity, the complete image, and a global description of its kernel are not asserted. In particular its image is an \(S\)-submodule; it has not been shown to be an ideal of \(D_{32}\).

The parameter ring and \(S\)-linearity. The displayed parameter ring is integral. The root parameters \(b,c\) are integral over the coefficient image, and monic division recovers \(R\); hence the coefficient map is finite. Its generic polynomial has a uniquely determined triple root and double root. The parameter ring is normal and is the normalization of that locus. This argument is independent of the pending support equality for \(K\).

For every \(h\in I\), on this parameter ring, \[ h(b,c)=h_x(b,c)=0.\tag{IZ} \] To prove this, first take distinct roots with \(R(b)R(c)\ne0\). In the selected local pair component the normalization incidence is generated by \(p(x),p'(x),p(y),p'(y)\). At the fixed polynomial these generate \(((x-b)^2,y-c)\), up to units. Thus both value and the \(x\)-derivative of \(h\) vanish. The identities extend over all of \(D_{32}\), because they are polynomial identities on an integral ring and hold on its dense open subset. For \(a\in S\), the extra terms in \(\Theta(ah)-a\Theta(h)\) are multiples of \((\Delta_ja)h(b,c)\) or \((\Delta_2a)h_x(b,c)\). They vanish by (IZ). Pair derivatives themselves are \(S\)-linear. This proves \(S\)-linearity on \(I\); the same formula on all of \(P\) is not asserted to be \(S\)-linear.

Complete local-symbol calculation. Normalize the ordered pair to \(b=0,c=1\), write \(z=y-1\), and set \[ p(x)=P_3x^3+P_4x^4+P_5x^5+\cdots,\quad p(1+z)=Q_2z^2+Q_3z^3+Q_4z^4+Q_5z^5+\cdots. \] Treat these coefficients as independent symbols. A polynomial identity for these independent jets implies it for jets of the same actual polynomial; no converse inference from a failed independent-jet test is used. Here \[ \mathcal L=\partial_x\partial_z+ \frac{3}{2(1-x+z)}(\partial_x-\partial_z). \] The normalized polynomial functional in ordinary derivative notation is \[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal T(h)=\big[& (-42Q_2+21Q_3)h_z-7Q_2h_{zz} +(18Q_2-6Q_3)h_{xz}+2Q_2h_{xzz}\\ &+24Q_2^2\delta_1h+18Q_2^2\delta_2h -12Q_2^2\partial_x\delta_2h\big]_{0,0}, \end{aligned}\tag{NT} \] where \(\delta_jp(Z)=Z^j\). It has no division by any polynomial jet.

Here is the exhaustive finite algebraic verification of \(\mathcal T\mathcal L(J)=0\). The local ideal is \((p(x),p(y))\), since the pair difference is a unit. Use all ten monomials \(u=x^az^b\) with \(a+b\le3\), for each of these two generators. For a candidate functional, order its eight base Taylor coefficients by \[ z,z^2,xz,x^2,z^3,xz^2,x^2z,x^3, \] then append value and \(x\)-coefficient for each of \(\delta_0,\delta_1,\delta_2\). Evaluation and \(x\)-coefficient in the base component are omitted because they already vanish on \(I\). For a generator \(g=p(x)\) or \(p(y)\), the row is the eight coefficients of \(\mathcal L(gu)\), followed by those two coefficients of each \(\mathcal L((\delta_jg)u)\). This explicitly defines the twenty-by-fourteen matrix \(M\), without a rank or generic-module assumption.

The complete matrix is retained in the exact symbolic certificate. Over the rational function field of the independent jets it has rank eleven and nullity three. The decisive identity, stronger than that rank information, is \[ M\,\begin{pmatrix} -42Q_2+21Q_3\\-14Q_2\\18Q_2-6Q_3\\0\\0\\4Q_2\\0\\0\\ 0\\0\\24Q_2^2\\0\\18Q_2^2\\-12Q_2^2 \end{pmatrix}=0. \tag{JS} \] The factors two at the second and sixth entries convert ordinary derivatives in (NT) to Taylor coefficients. Every entry of this product is checked as an exact rational-function identity, with the displayed vector polynomial. The row construction by differentiation is a reproducible universal polynomial certificate, not a sampled rank test.

No omitted source monomial can affect the result. In the base component \(g\) vanishes to order at least two, \(\mathcal L\) lowers ordinary local order by at most two, and the functional uses jets through three. A source of order at least four therefore contributes zero. In a coefficient-variation component the source has order at least four even if \(\delta_jg\) is a unit; after applying \(\mathcal L\), its order is at least two, beyond the retained first jets. This proves completeness for arbitrary formal pair multipliers. The script also verifies every degree-four row is zero as a direct control. Only \(P_3,P_4,Q_2,Q_3,Q_4\) occur: the fifth jets are independently checked absent.

For coefficient-dependent multipliers, the extra Leibniz terms involve the value or \(x\)-derivative of \(\mathcal L(g\,\delta_ju)\). Both vanish: for \(g=p(y)\), \(p(c)=p'(c)=0\); for \(g=p(x)\), also \(p''(b)=0\). Thus the same certificate annihilates arbitrary local members of \(J\), including the parameter dependence of their chosen representations. This addresses the difference between a vector-space jet test and an \(S\)-module map.

Restoring coordinates without leaving denominators. Put \(x=b+dX,y=b+dY\), and use \(\widetilde p(T)=p(b+dT)\), without dividing by its leading coefficient. Then the normalized quadratic and cubic jets at \(Y=1\) are \(Q_2=d^2q,Q_3=d^3r\), pair derivatives transform by \(\partial_X=d\partial_x,\partial_Y=d\partial_y\), and the coefficient variations giving \(T^j\) are \(d^{-j}\Delta_j\). Substitution in (NT) has the common factor \(d^2\); dividing by that factor gives exactly (KE). All its resulting coefficients are polynomial. The EPD operator transforms by a scalar \(d^2\), which does not affect annihilation. Hence \(\Theta\mathcal L(J)=0\) on the dense open set \(dqR(b)\ne0\). Every resulting value is a polynomial in the integral parameter ring, so the identity extends over \(d=0\), \(q=0\), and all spectator collisions. Detection on those closed loci is not claimed.

The marked value and grading. The identity \[ a_{N-1}(x+y,xy)=\frac{p(y)-p(x)}{y-x} \] gives, in the normalized coordinates, the Taylor coefficient row \[ (0,Q_2,0,0,-Q_2+Q_3,Q_2,0,-P_3;\ 0,0,1,0,1,1). \] Its product with (JS)'s vector is \(20Q_2^2\), not zero. Under the coordinate change the actual \(a_{N-1}\) has the additional factor \(d^{-1}\), and \(\Theta\) was obtained by dividing the operator by \(d^2\). Its value is therefore \(20d^{-3}Q_2^2=20dq^2\). Since \(q=d^3R(c)\), this proves (KV). Thus the test detects the specified class, not merely a nonzero abstract functional.

The weights are \(\deg d=1,\deg q=N-2,\deg r=N-3\). The operators \(\Delta_j\) have weight \(j-N\), while each pair derivative lowers weight by one. Every term of (KE) raises raw polynomial weight by \(N-2\). Since the source \(K\) assigns \(h\) weight \(\deg h+4\), the map to \(D_{32}(N-6)\) is homogeneous of degree zero. The output for the first class has raw degree \(2N-3\), and target degree \(2N-3-(N-6)=N+3\), matching the known source degree. The image contains \(S\cdot20d^7R(c)^2\); replacing that inclusion by surjectivity or cancelling that factor on the whole image is unjustified. \(\square\)

The exact quintic control follows without another computation. In \(N=5\), use the reviewed filtration \(0\to T\to K\to k[z](-8)\to0\), with \(b=-2z,c=3z\). The finite-length \(T\) is killed by a power of \(c_2\), whereas \(c_2=-15z^2\) acts injectively on \(D_{32}=k[z]\); hence \(\Theta(T)=0\). The class \(\eta=[a_4]\) has degree eight, and \(T\) starts in degree ten, so its nonzero image is a scalar generator of \(k[z](-8)\). An \(S\)-linear map \(k[z]\to k[z]\) is \(k[z]\)-linear: \(z^2\theta(zf)=\theta(z^3f)=z^3\theta(f)\), using \(z^2,z^3\) from the coefficient image, and cancellation of \(z^2\) gives \(\theta(zf)=z\theta(f)\). The marked value \(20(5z)^7\) therefore identifies \[ \ker\Theta=T,\qquad \operatorname{im}\Theta=z^7k[z]\subset D_{32}(-1), \] up to a nonzero scalar. This is a composition of the existing exact filtration with the proposed extraction formula, and retains the latter's provisional status. No new quintic resolution is required.

Every lower-kernel class has a pair-ideal representative

Lemma (lem:cube-epd-pair-ideal-reduction; verification pending). Work in characteristic zero with \(N\ge5\), \(S=k[c_2,\ldots,c_N]\), \(P=S[s,v]\), and the recorded EPD objects \[ a_j=[T^j]\frac{p^{\rm rev}(T)}{1-sT+vT^2},\quad E_j=[T^j]\frac{p^{\rm rev}(T)}{(1-sT+vT^2)^2},\quad J=(a_{N-1},a_N),\quad I=(E_{N-3},\ldots,E_N). \] Then \[ I=J+\mathcal L(J) \tag{JR} \] as \(S\)-submodules of \(P\). For a homogeneous \(h\in I\) of raw weight \(e\), there is a homogeneous \(f\in J\) of weight \(e+2\) with \(h-\mathcal Lf\in J\). Consequently the actual normalization kernel has the exact representative description \[ K=(I/\mathcal L(J))(-4) \cong\bigl(J/(J\cap\mathcal L(J))\bigr)(-4). \] Neither \(\mathcal L(J)\) nor its intersection with \(J\) is asserted to be an ideal.

Proof. Write \(m=N-3\), \(a=a_{N-1}\), \(b_*=a_N\), and define the pair-variable operators \[ \mathscr E=s\partial_s+2v\partial_v,\qquad \mathscr D=2\partial_s+s\partial_v. \] The already-proved coefficient identities give \[ a=E_{m+2}-sE_{m+1}+vE_m,\qquad b_*=E_{m+3}-sE_{m+2}+vE_{m+1}. \] In particular \(J\subset I\), and \(I/J\) is generated as a \(P\)-module by the classes of \(E_m,E_{m+1}\). The recorded derivatives \(\mathcal La_j=-E_{j-2}/2\), \(\partial_sa_j=E_{j-1}\), \(\partial_va_j=-E_{j-2}\) and the product rule give, for \(u,w\in P\), \[ \mathcal L(au+b_*w)\equiv E_m\alpha+E_{m+1}\beta\pmod J, \] where \[ \begin{pmatrix}\alpha\\\beta\end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -\tfrac12-\mathscr E&-v\mathscr D\\ \mathscr D&-\tfrac12-\mathscr E+s\mathscr D \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix}u\\w\end{pmatrix}. \tag{EM} \] For example the term \(a\,\mathcal Lu+b_*\,\mathcal Lw\) lies in \(J\), and replacing \(E_{m+2}\) by \(sE_{m+1}-vE_m\) gives the displayed second column. This proves the identity in the actual polynomial quotient; no independence of the two classes in \(I/J\) is assumed.

Introduce independent ordered variables \(x,y\), with \(s=x+y,v=xy\). There is a free decomposition \[ S[x,y]=P\oplus yP, \] since \(y^2-sy+v=0\) and \(x=s-y\). Under \((u,w)\mapsto u+yw\), matrix (EM) is exactly \[ \mathscr Bf=-\tfrac12f+(y-x)\partial_xf. \] Indeed \(\mathscr B(u)=(-1/2-\mathscr E)u+y\mathscr Du\), and applying it to \(yw\), with \(\partial_xy=0\), gives the second column after reducing \(y^2=sy-v\). In coordinates \(y,t=y-x\), one has \(\partial_x=-\partial_t\), so \[ \mathscr B(y^at^r)=-(r+\tfrac12)y^at^r. \] These scalars are nonzero in characteristic zero. Dividing each monomial by its scalar defines a polynomial \(S\)-linear inverse, preserving weight. Thus (EM) is a bijection on the free coefficient pairs.

Given \(h\in I\), choose any representation \(h\equiv E_m\alpha+E_{m+1}\beta\pmod J\). Solve (EM) for \(u,w\). The preceding product identity gives \(h-\mathcal L(au+b_*w)\in J\), proving \(I\subset J+\mathcal L(J)\). The reverse inclusion follows from \(J\subset I\) and \(\mathcal L(J)\subset I\). If \(h\) has weight \(e\), take \(\alpha\) of weight \(e-m\) and \(\beta\) of weight \(e-m-1\). The inverse preserves the weight of \(\alpha+y\beta\), so \(au+b_*w\) has weight \(e+2\). The quotient isomorphism is now the elementary second isomorphism theorem for \(S\)-modules. \(\square\)

The full detector image and the next normalization quotient

Theorem (thm:cube-triple-double-normalization-quotient; conditional on the extraction verification gate). In the same setting let \(D_{32}\) parameterize \(p(Z)=(Z-b)^3(Z-c)^2R(Z)\) with total trace zero, as in the polynomial extraction formula. Put \(d=c-b\), \(q=p''(c)/2=d^3R(c)\), and \[ F=20dq^2=20d^7R(c)^2. \] For that polynomial \(S\)-linear functional \(\Theta:I\to D_{32}\), the complete image, not merely its ideal closure, is \[ \Theta(I)=F D_{32}. \tag{IM} \] Hence division by \(F\) gives a unique global polynomial homogeneous surjection \[ \chi:K\twoheadrightarrow D_{32}(-N-3),\qquad \chi([a_{N-1}])=1. \tag{N32} \] Combining this with the reviewed kernel-support theorem and generic length one, its kernel \(K_2\) is the largest submodule of \(K\) of dimension at most \(N-5\). Thus there are exact sequences \[ 0\longrightarrow K_2\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow D_{32}(-N-3)\longrightarrow0, \qquad 0\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow C_N\longrightarrow D_{22}(-4)\longrightarrow0. \] No splitting, bound on \(K_2\)'s primary nilpotence, or original per-order threshold is asserted.

Product values of the polynomial detector. Keep the ordered triple root \(b\) and double root \(c\) distinct initially, and take \(u\in P\). The formula for \(\Theta\) is \(S\)-linear on \(I\), so it suffices to take \(u\in k[s,v]\). Let \(a=a_{N-1}\) and \(b_*=a_N\). The divided differences are \[ a(x+y,xy)=\frac{p(y)-p(x)}{y-x},\qquad b_*(x+y,xy)=\frac{yp(y)-xp(x)}{y-x}. \] The exact product calculation gives \[ \begin{aligned} \Theta(au)&=F\,[\,u-\tfrac25d\,u_x\,]_{b,c},\\ \Theta(b_*u)&=Fc\,[\,u-\tfrac25d\,u_x\,]_{b,c}. \end{aligned}\tag{PV} \] Here coefficient derivatives in \(\Theta\) hold \(b,c\) fixed, and the pair derivative \(u_x\) holds \(y\) fixed.

To verify these identities in full, at \((b,c)\) the values and first derivatives of \(a\) vanish, as does \(a_{xy}\), while \[ a_{yy}=\frac{2q}{d},\quad a_{xyy}=\frac{2q}{d^2},\quad \Delta_1a=1,\quad \Delta_2a=d,\quad \partial_x\Delta_2a=1. \] Substitute \(h=au\) in (KE). Its four contributions not already zero are \[ -14dq^2u,\quad 4dq^2u+4d^2q^2u_x,\quad 24dq^2u+18dq^2u,\quad -12dq^2u-12d^2q^2u_x. \] Their sum is \(20dq^2u-8d^2q^2u_x\), the first formula. For \(b_*\), the corresponding six displayed jets are respectively \(c\) times those for \(a\): this follows directly from its divided difference, with \(b_{*,xyy}=2cq/d^2\), and \[ \Delta_1b_*=x+y-b,\quad \Delta_2b_*=x^2+xy+y^2-2b(x+y)+b^2. \] At \((b,c)\) these have values \(c,cd\), and the \(x\)-derivative of the second is \(c\). The same product calculation yields the second formula. Since both sides of (PV) are polynomial on the integral parameter ring, the identities extend over \(d=0\) and all spectator collisions. Thus (PV) proves common-factor divisibility on every member of \(J\), not only on the first class.

Surjectivity uses both pair-ideal generators. Treat \(x,y\) first as independent ordered variables over \(S\). The operator \[ \mathscr A f=f-\tfrac25(y-x)\partial_xf \] is an \(S\)-linear polynomial automorphism of \(S[x,y]\): in coordinates \(y,t=y-x\) it sends \(y^at^r\) to \((1+2r/5)y^at^r\). Its inverse divides by those nonzero scalars and preserves weight. It need not preserve the symmetric subring by itself. Every polynomial uniquely has the form \(u+yw\), with \(u,w\in P\). Applying both formulas (PV) therefore gives \[ F^{-1}\Theta(au+b_*w)= [\mathscr A(u+yw)]_{x=b,y=c}. \tag{PS} \] The evaluation map \(S[x,y]\to D_{32}\) is onto: the target is generated by \(S,b,c\), since monic division of \(p\) by \((Z-b)^3(Z-c)^2\) recovers every coefficient of \(R\) polynomially. Automorphy of \(\mathscr A\) and (PS) prove \(\Theta(J)=F D_{32}\) as an actual \(S\)-module image. A span of symmetric \(u\) alone would not prove this conclusion.

By (JR), every \(h\in I\) is \(j+\mathcal Lf\), with \(j,f\in J\). The proposed extraction theorem gives \(\Theta(\mathcal Lf)=0\). Consequently \(\Theta(I)=\Theta(J)=F D_{32}\). The polynomial \(F\) is nonzero in the integral parameter ring; every value is divisible by it there, including over its zero set. This defines a unique polynomial \(S\)-linear map \(\Theta/F\), with no localization left in its target. It annihilates \(\mathcal L(J)\) and is onto, proving (N32). The raw weight of \(F\) is \(2N-3\). Cancelling it changes the prior target shift \(N-6\) to \(N-6-(2N-3)=-N-3\), as stated. The source class \([a_{N-1}]\) has weight \(N+3\) and maps to the target generator \(1\) in that same weight.

The next dimension layer, with extensions retained. The now-reviewed support theorem gives \(\operatorname{Supp}K=\Delta_{32}\), an irreducible locus of dimension \(N-4\), and generic length one. The finite birational normalization module \(D_{32}\) has the same generic length. A surjection between those generic modules is an isomorphism. Thus \(K_2=\ker\chi\) is supported on a proper closed subset and has dimension at most \(N-5\). Every lower-dimensional submodule of \(K\) maps to zero in \(D_{32}\): any nonzero \(S\)-submodule of that domain has the same annihilator as \(D_{32}\), hence dimension \(N-4\). This proves maximality of \(K_2\). In the quintic control, the previous exact filtration already identifies it as the length-sixteen vertex torsion and the normalized quotient as \(k[z](-8)\); this is a consistency check, not another computation. The kernel is not identified with the image of \(J^2\): in that control vertex torsion begins in weight ten, while the image of \(J^2\) begins no earlier than weight twelve. \(\square\)

Checks and falsifiers. Both inverse operators act on the full ordered-pair polynomial ring, identified with two symmetric coefficient slots. Restricting the second inverse to the symmetric slot alone would lose surjectivity and is explicitly avoided. The reduction uses arbitrary presentations in \(I/J\), so it does not assume its two generators are free. Weight checks give a reduction preimage exactly two degrees higher and the normalized quotient shift \(N+3\). The quintic result recovers the already-known \(k[z](-8)\) quotient and vertex kernel without recomputing its resolution. Its weight-ten vertex class refutes the tempting identification of the remaining kernel with the image of \(J^2\), whose first possible weight is twelve. No finite collection of cases substitutes for either inverse-operator argument.

27 September 2026 — The residual kernel carries every actual finite-generator Tor degree

The line's general claim. Determine the cube's per-order degree over every odd field and in every dimension. This degree-two characteristic-zero line must bound the least polynomial degree of a relation with a prescribed highest order. Since the last review, finite EPD jets were proved to exist globally, the first embedded formal module and its exponent were identified, and the normalization-kernel support theorem passed fresh review. The polynomial extraction and next normalized quotient have complete arguments and exact certificates but still await their mandatory fresh reviews. None of these advances has changed a per-order threshold beyond the retained rational row.

Obstacle

The global finite-jet exponent depends on primary thickness that is still uncontrolled in dimension. The two normalized layers, even if the recent quotient passes review, leave a residual kernel \(K_2\). The original order filtration imposes an additional cost beyond total generator degrees. The question here is whether deleting that smaller-dimensional kernel is harmless for the Tor mechanism. The exact quintic filtration disproves it sharply: every actual second-Tor degree is lost after deleting vertex torsion. Thus another support description or a decomposition only away from the coefficient vertex cannot discharge the required degree implication. The small-prime stable-order problem remains separate.

General statement. The all-dimensional lem:cube-ore-generators-from-tor and thm:cube-epd-global-finite-jets make the missing implications precise: control the actual second Tor action and polynomial order lifts, or obtain a quantitative primary bound and retain those lifts. The proposed thm:cube-triple-double-normalization-quotient retains a kernel rather than declaring a splitting. cor:cube-vertex-controls-core-tor tests the general shortcut of discarding that kernel on an already-complete control, without extending the dimension table.

Deleting the vertex kills the image of the entire actual second Tor space

Corollary (cor:cube-vertex-controls-core-tor; fresh correctness review pending). In the characteristic-zero quintic coefficient ring \(S=k[c_2,c_3,c_4,c_5]\), with weights \(2,3,4,5\), let \(C\) be the complete centered degree-two defect and \(T=H^0_{S_+}(C)\) its known length-sixteen vertex submodule. Put \(C'=C/T\). Then \[ \operatorname{Tor}_2^S(C',k)_j=0\quad(j>18), \] whereas the actual \(\operatorname{Tor}_2^S(C,k)\) is supported precisely in degrees \(19,20,21,22,23\), with dimensions \(1,2,5,5,4\). Consequently \[ \operatorname{Tor}_2^S(T,k)\twoheadrightarrow\operatorname{Tor}_2^S(C,k), \qquad \operatorname{Tor}_2^S(C,k)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Tor}_2^S(C',k) \text{ is zero}. \tag{VT} \] The associated sheaves of \(C,C'\) on the weighted \(\operatorname{Proj}S\) are identical. Thus deleting vertex torsion, or retaining only that associated sheaf, loses the image of every actual second-Tor class used by the finite Ore-generator mechanism. This does not say that \(T\) alone determines those classes or their connection, does not affect the separate monic-generator term, and does not rule out reconstruction retaining local cohomology and the extension maps.

The exact two upper layers. The reviewed dimension filtration gives \[ 0\longrightarrow k[z](-8)\longrightarrow C'\longrightarrow k[u,v](-4)\longrightarrow0, \] with coefficient maps \[ \begin{aligned} (c_2,c_3,c_4,c_5)&=(2v-3u^2,-2u(u^2+v),v^2-4u^2v,-2uv^2),\\ (c_2,c_3,c_4,c_5)&=(-15z^2,10z^3,60z^4,-72z^5). \end{aligned} \] We compute free resolutions of these two modules directly from their parameterizations, rather than assuming that a Hilbert numerator specifies their Betti degrees.

For \(D=k[u,v]\), eliminate \(v=(c_2+3u^2)/2\). Define \[ \begin{aligned} g_3&=5u^3+c_2u+c_3,\\ g_4&=4c_4-c_2^2+2c_2u^2+15u^4,\\ g_5&=2c_5+c_2^2u+6c_2u^3+9u^5. \end{aligned} \] The ring \(A=S[u]/(g_3)\) is free over \(S\) with basis \(1,u,u^2\), of weights \(0,1,2\). It is a polynomial ring after eliminating \(c_3\). The elements \(g_4,g_5\), of weights four and five, form a regular sequence in \(A\): successively eliminate \(c_4\) and \(c_5\) using their unit leading constants four and two. The quotient is \(k[c_2,u]\cong k[u,v]\), with exactly the displayed coefficient map. The Koszul resolution on \(g_4,g_5\) is therefore an \(S\)-free resolution \[ 0\to A(-9)\to A(-4)\oplus A(-5)\to A\to D\to0. \] All entries of the first map to \(A\) have coefficient weight at least two, and the next differential likewise has positive coefficient weights after using the basis \(1,u,u^2\). Hence the resolution is minimal over \(S\). After shifting by four, its second Tor degrees are exactly \(13,14,15\).

For \(B=k[z]\), rescale \(a=-c_2/15\), \(b=c_3/10\), so \(a=z^2,b=z^3\). Over \(k[a,b]\), the normalization has generators \(1,z\) and presentation \[ 0\to k[a,b](-3)\oplus k[a,b](-4) \xrightarrow{\left(\begin{smallmatrix}b&a^2\\-a&-b\end{smallmatrix}\right)} k[a,b]\oplus k[a,b](-1)\to k[z]\to0. \] The determinant \(a^3-b^2\) is nonzero, giving injectivity. The two relations reduce every module element to the stated parametrized normal form: equivalently, if \(f(a,b)+zg(a,b)=0\) after \(a=z^2,b=z^3\), divide \(f,g\) by the monic relation \(b^2-a^3\) and compare the even and odd powers of \(z\); the resulting relations are generated by the two displayed columns. Alternatively, regard the target as a free rank-two \(k[a]\)-module with multiplication by \(b\) represented by \(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&a^2\\a&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)\); the matrix \(bI-M_b\) gives precisely this presentation up to a column sign.

Now change the remaining coefficient variables to \[ e_4=c_4-\tfrac4{15}c_2^2,\qquad e_5=c_5-\tfrac{12}{25}c_2c_3. \] These are independent variables of weights four and five over \(k[a,b]\), and both act by zero on \(B\). Extend the preceding resolution polynomially and tensor with their Koszul complex. This is exact, since they form a regular sequence on the polynomial extension of \(B\); all differentials have positive coefficient weights and the resolution is minimal. Before the shift by eight, the second free module has degrees \[ 7,\quad8^{[2]},\quad9^{[2]},\quad10. \] Thus \(\operatorname{Tor}_2^S(B(-8),k)\) has degrees \(15,16^{[2]},17^{[2]},18\).

The two exact-sequence tests. Apply the graded Tor long exact sequence to the displayed extension defining \(C'\). In any degree greater than eighteen, both its adjacent second Tor groups from \(B(-8)\) and \(D(-4)\) vanish, so the middle one vanishes. The actual complete resolution of \(C\), retained in the filtration record and used in the Tor-connection calculation, gives \[ \operatorname{Tor}_2^S(C,k): \quad 19,\quad20^{[2]},\quad21^{[5]},\quad22^{[5]},\quad23^{[4]}. \] The sequence for \(0\to T\to C\to C'\to0\) now gives (VT) degree by degree. Outside this displayed support its target is zero, so the first map is surjective as a whole graded vector-space map. We have neither computed nor asserted its kernel. This proves the claim without recomputing the full resolution.

The finite generator contribution in the core is \(\operatorname{Tor}_2^S(C,k)(9)\), with degrees lowered by nine, not raised. Its entire image is killed by passage to \(C'\). We do not apply the cyclic-marker theorem to \(C'\) as though it were another marked defect \(F/\mathscr Av\). If connection compatibility is desired, \(T\) is stable: \(\delta_0(S_+)\subset S_+\) implies \(\delta_0(S_+^r)\subset S_+^r\), and applying the connection to \(at=0\), \(a\in S_+^r\), shows that the same power kills \(\nabla t\). Thus \(C'\) inherits the connection and naturality gives the corresponding Tor maps. This still does not determine the quotient connection from \(T\) alone.

Finally \(T\) has finite length and sheafifies to zero on \(\operatorname{Proj}S\), so \(\widetilde C=\widetilde {C'}\). Their different second-Tor behavior is an explicit counterexample to reconstructing the required graded generator information solely from that associated sheaf. The argument is about this actual graded module; it is not a blanket objection to the separate first-step sheaf or to methods preserving additional graded data. \(\square\)
