Uniform minimal resolutions of both normalization modules

Lemma (lem:cube-normalization-koszul-resolutions; working proof). Let \(k\) have characteristic zero, \(N\ge5\), \(S=k[c_2,\ldots,c_N]\), with \(\deg c_j=j\), and let \(D_{22}\) and \(D_{32}\) be the coefficient algebras parameterizing the centered factorizations \(p=Q^2R\), \(Q=Z^2-sZ+v\), and \(p=(Z-x)^3(Z-y)^2R\), respectively. Put \[ b_{22}(t)=\frac{(1-t^{N-3})(1-t^{N-2})}{(1-t)(1-t^2)},\qquad b_{32}(t)=\frac{(1-t^{N-4})(1-t^{N-3})}{(1-t)^2}. \] For a finite graded \(S\)-module \(M\), write \(\beta_i(M;t)=\sum_j\dim_k\operatorname{Tor}_i^S(M,k)_j\,t^j\). Then \[ \begin{aligned} \beta_i(D_{22};t)&=b_{22}(t)\,e_i(t^{N-1},t^N),\\ \beta_i(D_{32};t)&=b_{32}(t)\,e_i(t^{N-2},t^{N-1},t^N), \end{aligned}\tag{KR} \] where \(e_i\) is the elementary symmetric polynomial, zero beyond the number of its arguments. These are minimal-resolution formulas, not only alternating Hilbert-series identities. All constructions are over the coefficient ring \(S\).

Two finite free intermediate algebras. Write \(p^{\rm rev}(T)=\sum_{j=0}^N(-1)^jc_jT^j\), with \(c_0=1,c_1=0\). In \(P=S[s,v]\), let \[ E_j=[T^j]\frac{p^{\rm rev}(T)}{(1-sT+vT^2)^2}, \qquad A_{22}=P/(E_{N-3},E_{N-2}). \] The exact normalization equations give \(D_{22}=P/(E_{N-3},\ldots,E_N)\). In the ordered-pair ring \(Q=S[x,y]\), define \[ F_j=[T^j]\frac{p^{\rm rev}(T)}{(1-xT)^3(1-yT)^2}, \qquad A_{32}=Q/(F_{N-4},F_{N-3}). \] The equations \(F_{N-4},\ldots,F_N\) give exactly \(p(Z)=(Z-x)^3(Z-y)^2R(Z)\), with \(R\) monic of degree \(N-5\): truncated division in reversed polynomials gives its coefficients, and the next five zero coefficients are precisely the remainder equations. This is a scheme-theoretic factorization identity, valid also at \(x=y\). Thus their quotient is \(D_{32}\).

The first two \(E\)-equations eliminate \(c_{N-3},c_{N-2}\), each with coefficient \(1\) or \(-1\), so they form a regular sequence and \(A_{22}\) is a polynomial ring as a \(k\)-algebra. For \(N\ge6\), the analogous \(F\)-equations eliminate \(c_{N-4},c_{N-3}\). At \(N=5\), the first equation is instead \(F_1=3x+2y\), eliminating \(y\), and \(F_2\) then eliminates \(c_2\). This also gives a regular sequence and a polynomial intermediate algebra. This exceptional trace equation must not be treated as a nonexistent coefficient \(c_1\).

Finiteness and freeness, not just a fibre count. For \(A_{22}\), the zero-coefficient fibre is the complete intersection with generating series \((1-sT+vT^2)^{-2}\), whose first two tail equations and regularity were proved in the first-lifting theorem. Its Hilbert polynomial is \(b_{22}(t)\). For \(A_{32}\), write \[ H_j(x,y)=[T^j](1-xT)^{-3}(1-yT)^{-2}. \] Logarithmic differentiation gives \[ (j+1)H_{j+1}=\big((j+3)x+(j+2)y\big)H_j-(j+4)xyH_{j-1}. \tag{HR} \] The common zero locus of \(H_{N-4},H_{N-3}\) is only the origin. If \(xy\ne0\), the recurrence propagates consecutive vanishing backwards to \(H_0=0\), impossible. If \(x=0\), then \(H_j=(j+1)y^j\); if \(y=0\), then \(H_j=\binom{j+2}{2}x^j\). The first relevant index is at least one, and these nonzero characteristic-zero constants force both coordinates to vanish. The two equations are therefore a regular sequence in \(k[x,y]\), and the fibre Hilbert polynomial is \(b_{32}(t)\).

For either intermediate algebra \(A\), lift a homogeneous \(k\)-basis of its finite zero fibre. These lifts generate \(A\) over \(S\): subtract their residue-field expression from a homogeneous element; the remainder is a sum \(\sum c_i a_i\) with each \(a_i\) of strictly smaller degree, and induction completes the reduction. Hence the corresponding finite graded free module \(G\) maps onto \(A\). The regular-sequence Hilbert identity for the first two equations gives \[ H_A(t)=H_S(t)b_{22}(t)\quad\hbox{or}\quad H_S(t)b_{32}(t), \] exactly the Hilbert series of \(G\). The homogeneous kernel has zero dimension in every weight and is zero. Thus \(A_{22},A_{32}\) are free over \(S\), with precisely the stated basis-weight polynomials. This supplies the missing step from the fibre calculation to freeness.

Exactness and minimality of the Koszul resolutions. In \(A_{22}\), the remaining equations \(E_{N-1},E_N\) successively eliminate the two remaining highest coefficients. They form a regular sequence, of weights \(N-1,N\). In \(A_{32}\), the remaining \(F_{N-2},F_{N-1},F_N\) similarly eliminate the three highest coefficients and form a regular sequence of weights \(N-2,N-1,N\). Their Koszul complexes are therefore resolutions of \(D_{22},D_{32}\), respectively, by modules free over \(S\).

Regularity alone does not prove these \(S\)-resolutions minimal. In the first intermediate zero fibre, the recurrence \[ (j+1)H_{j+1}=(j+2)sH_j-(j+3)vH_{j-1} \] for \((1-sT+vT^2)^{-2}\) puts the remaining equations in the ideal of the first two. Recurrence (HR) does the same for the three ordered-pair equations. Thus each multiplication map used in either Koszul differential is zero modulo \(S_+\). In any of the lifted homogeneous free bases, all its matrix entries lie in \(S_+\); every differential of the Koszul complex is minimal. Tensoring with \(k\) now gives exactly (KR). \(\square\)

A bounded polynomial source, and the precise relation bound still needed

Theorem (thm:cube-residual-generator-bound; working proof). Use the actual defect \(C\), its normalization kernel \(K\), and the reviewed exact sequence \[ 0\to K_2\to K\to D_{32}(-N-3)\to0. \] Then \(K_2\) admits a polynomial graded \(S\)-free cover whose weight polynomial is \[ \begin{aligned} R_N(t)={}&t^{2N-1}(1+t)(1+t+\cdots+t^{N-4})\\ &+t^{N+3}b_{32}(t)(t^{N-2}+t^{N-1}+t^N). \end{aligned}\tag{RS} \] Consequently it has a homogeneous generating family of at most \[ (N-3)(3N-10) \] elements, all in weights \(2N-1\) through \(4N-6\). Equivalently \(\beta_0(K_2;t)\le R_N(t)\) coefficientwise. The family need not be minimal. This bound is independent of the unknown monic cutoff and the unknown global primary exponent.

Let \(B=\max\{j:\operatorname{Tor}_1^S(K_2,k)_j\ne0\}\), with \(B=-\infty\) if this space is zero. The least original degree-two monic order satisfies \[ U_{\rm original}\le\max(4N-5,\ B+1). \tag{ME} \] Moreover \[ U_{\rm original}\ge\binom N2+2,\qquad B\ge\binom N2+1\quad(N\ge8). \tag{QB} \] Thus those first-syzygy weights cannot have a uniform linear-in-\(N\) bound, despite the linear generating-weight bound. The remaining sufficient implication for this endpoint is a quantitative upper bound on the first-syzygy weights of \(K_2\), not merely its generator weights. Intermediate specified-order thresholds and their cancellation costs remain outside this conclusion.

The common cover is essential. The reviewed first-lifting theorem proves that \(C\to D_{22}(-4)\) induces an isomorphism on minimal homogeneous generator spaces, both with polynomial \(t^4b_{22}(t)\). This is stronger than a surjection and was proved using actual unit pivots and the normalization fibre. The Tor sequence therefore gives a surjection \[ \operatorname{Tor}_1^S(D_{22}(-4),k)\twoheadrightarrow K/S_+K. \] More concretely choose a common minimal free cover \(G_0\to C\to D_{22}(-4)\). The first free module \(G_1\) of the normalization resolution maps onto the kernel of \(G_0\to D_{22}(-4)\), and its image in \(C\) is all of \(K\). Thus \(G_1\to K\) is a polynomial free cover with weight polynomial \(\beta_1(D_{22}(-4);t)\).

Compose this cover with the surjection to \(D_{32}(-N-3)\). Its residue-field map is onto. Choose homogeneous constant changes of basis, separately in each weight, to isolate a minimal free cover \(B_0\) of that target inside \(G_1\); write \(G_1=B_0\oplus G\). Since the chosen \(B_0\) maps onto the target, lift the images of the generators of \(G\) to \(B_0\) and subtract those lifts. This triangular polynomial source change makes \(G\) map to zero in \(D_{32}(-N-3)\), without changing its weights. A change between this minimal cover and the one from (KR) is polynomially invertible: ordering weights makes the degree-zero diagonal blocks constant and invertible, with strictly triangular positive-degree off-diagonal blocks. No parameter is inverted.

Let \(B_1\to B_0\) be the first differential of the shifted \(D_{32}\) resolution, transported by that change of cover. Its image maps to \(K_2\), as does \(G\). These two images generate \(K_2\): lift any element to \(G_1\), and its \(B_0\)-component lies in the kernel of the cover of \(D_{32}(-N-3)\), hence is an image of \(B_1\). We have constructed a polynomial surjection \[ G\oplus B_1\twoheadrightarrow K_2. \] It uses only the two normalization resolutions, the actual maps to \(K\) and \(D_{32}\), and homogeneous polynomial lifts. This is a finite generating source, not just the infinite ordered-pair incidence reformulation.

Its weights and size. The polynomial for \(G\) is \[ \begin{aligned} \beta_1(D_{22}(-4);t)-\beta_0(D_{32}(-N-3);t) &=t^{N+3}\big((1+t)b_{22}(t)-b_{32}(t)\big)\\ &=t^{2N-1}(1+t)(1+t+\cdots+t^{N-4}). \end{aligned} \] This subtraction concerns the split free-cover summands just constructed, not an informal subtraction of Hilbert series of modules. Adding \(\beta_1(D_{32}(-N-3);t)\) gives (RS). The second summand has largest weight \((N+3)+(2N-9)+N=4N-6\), and the first has largest weight \(3N-4\). The least possible weight is \(2N-1\). Evaluation at \(t=1\) gives \(2(N-3)+3(N-4)(N-3)=(N-3)(3N-10)\). The equivalent coefficientwise inequality also follows directly from the two Tor exact sequences, since \(K/S_+K\to D_{32}(-N-3)/S_+D_{32}(-N-3)\) is onto in each degree.

Why the missing first syzygies control the monic endpoint. The two exact sequences for \(K_2\subset K\subset C\) give, degreewise, \[ \operatorname{supp}\operatorname{Tor}_1(C,k) \subseteq \operatorname{supp}\operatorname{Tor}_1(K_2,k) \cup\operatorname{supp}\operatorname{Tor}_1(D_{32}(-N-3),k) \cup\operatorname{supp}\operatorname{Tor}_1(D_{22}(-4),k). \] By (KR), the last two maxima are \(4N-6\) and \(3N-4\). Thus \(\max\operatorname{supp}\beta_1(C)\le\max(B,4N-6)\).

The exact marked core is \(C=F/\mathscr A_0v\), with \(F\) a minimal \(S\)-free cover, since \(M=\mathscr A_0v\subset S_+F\), and marker weight \(w=2N-1\). Its least monic order \(U\) exists by Noetherian stabilization of the \(S\)-spans of successive iterates. As proved in the endpoint lemma, the minimal \(S\)-generators of \(M\) are exactly \(v,Dv,\ldots,D^{U-1}v\). For clarity, \(M/S_+M\) is cyclic over \(k[D]\). A homogeneous relation at its first degree \(w+j\) means \(D^jv\) is an \(S_+\)-linear combination of iterates of smaller weight, hence gives a monic annihilator of order \(j\); conversely a monic relation gives this dependence. Therefore its degrees are precisely \(w,\ldots,w+U-1\). The minimal-cover exact sequence identifies this space with \(\operatorname{Tor}_1(C,k)\).

Marked deflation shifts original order by exactly \(w\), preserving the leading coefficient. Hence \[ U_{\rm original}=w+U=1+\max\operatorname{supp}\beta_1(C), \] and (ME) follows. This uses the actual marked module, not a reconstructed unmarked quotient. The generated source for \(K_2\) has bounded weights, but its relation weights have not been bounded. Even the modules \((S/S_+^r)(-(2N-1))\) have one generator in the allowed lowest weight and support only at the coefficient vertex, while their minimal relation from \(c_N^r\) has weight \(2N-1+Nr\). The ideal \(S_+^r\) is preserved by \(\delta_0\), so they also carry the coefficient connection. As \(r\) varies, these relation weights are unbounded. Thus the source bound, support and existence of a connection alone cannot close (ME); additional cube-specific relations are necessary. \(\square\)

The rank budget forces quadratic relation weights. The full defect \(C\) has torsion support over \(S\), so after passing to \(L=\operatorname{Frac}(S)\), its marked image spans the entire free core \(F_L\), of rank \(\binom{N-2}{2}\). The derivation extends to \(L\). Let the first dependence among successive iterates have highest iterate \(D^dv\). Dividing by its nonzero leading coefficient gives a rational monic relation of order \(d\). Differentiation makes the span of \(v,\ldots,D^{d-1}v\) stable, while minimality makes those vectors independent. They therefore span the whole cyclic core and \(d=\operatorname{rank}F\). A polynomial monic relation cannot have smaller order than the rational one. Exact marked deflation now gives \[ U_{\rm original}\ge2N-1+\binom{N-2}{2}=\binom N2+2. \] For \(N\ge8\), this lower bound exceeds \(4N-5\) by \((N-7)(N-2)/2>0\). Formula (ME) then forces \(B+1\ge U_{\rm original}\ge\binom N2+2\), proving (QB). This feasibility test rules out a linear relation bound before attempting such a construction; it introduces no new dimension sample.

27 September 2026 — A controlled monomial argument gives a dimension-only cutoff

Working proof: an explicit recursive monic bound and residual first-syzygy bound; no sharp threshold formula or complexity claim. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and outcome. Open statement 3 requires polynomial relations with controlled original order. The preceding residual source left its first-syzygy weights unbounded. The fixed free ambient connection supplies more information than the source and its abstract connection alone: homogeneous remainders of successive marked iterates have linearly controlled monomial degrees. An explicit finite recursion bounds the length of that sequence. This gives a dimension-only upper bound for the degree-two monic endpoint, and hence for the actual residual first syzygies. It is deliberately coarse and is not evaluated at cube parameters; it does not determine any new specified-order threshold.

General statement. thm:graded-connection-effective-monic-cutoff quantitatively refines the earlier Noetherian monic-existence argument for every positively graded polynomial connection of fixed free rank, marker weight and minimum basis weight. cor:cube-effective-residual-relations applies it for every characteristic-zero \(N\ge5\) and bounds the first-syzygy weights of the actual \(K_2\). The earlier thm:cube-residual-generator-bound remains valid; its assessment that cube-specific relations are necessary is narrowed below.

An explicit termination bound for marked graded connections

Theorem (thm:graded-connection-effective-monic-cutoff; working proof). Let \(S=k[z_1,\ldots,z_s]\), with positive integer variable weights, and let \(\delta\) be a degree-one derivation. Let \(F=\bigoplus_{i=1}^r S e_i\) be a graded free module with a degree-one connection \(\nabla\), so \(\nabla(fu)=\delta(f)u+f\nabla u\). Let \(v\) be homogeneous of weight \(w\), put \(e=\min_i\deg e_i\), and \(b=\max(0,w-e)\). The zero module and zero marker have cutoff zero and may be removed first. For \(r\ge1\), define the following nonnegative integer function on vectors of counts \(a=(a_s,\ldots,a_0)\) and times \(t\ge0\). Write \(\epsilon_j\) for one count in dimension \(j\): \[ L_b(0;t)=0,\qquad L_b(a;t)=1+\max_{j:a_j>0} L_b(T_j(a,t);t+1), \tag{DL} \] where \[ T_0(a,t)=a-\epsilon_0,\qquad T_j(a,t)=a-\epsilon_j+(b+t)\epsilon_{j-1}\quad(j>0). \] Every recursive call strictly decreases \((a_s,\ldots,a_0)\) in lexicographic order, with dimension \(s\) first. Thus (DL) is a finite, explicitly computable integer recursion, with no algebraic input or unknown stopping parameter. The least monic annihilator order \(U\) of \(v\) over \(S[D;\delta]\) satisfies \[ U\le L_b(r\epsilon_s;0). \tag{GC} \] The annihilator can be chosen homogeneous of total degree \(U\). No characteristic-zero assumption is needed for this general statement.

Why the recursion terminates. Lexicographic order on a finite tuple of nonnegative integers is well founded when the first coordinate is compared first: in a descending sequence that coordinate can decrease only finitely often, after which induction applies to the remaining tuple. Changing the auxiliary integer \(t\) does not change this order. Each maximum has at most \(s+1\) branches. Equivalently, every branch decreases the ordinal \(\omega^s a_s+\cdots+\omega a_1+a_0\), and the finitely branching recursion tree has no infinite branch. Well-founded recursion therefore defines a finite natural number at each input. An implementation can evaluate the displayed calls using integer arithmetic and maximum; no claim of feasible running time is made.

The controlled monomial argument. A colored monomial is a pair \((i,\alpha)\), with \(1\le i\le r\) and \(\alpha\in\mathbb N^s\); divisibility requires equal colors and componentwise comparison. Consider a sequence \(m_t=(i_t,\alpha_t)\) such that \(|\alpha_t|\le b+t\), and no earlier \(m_u\) divides a later \(m_t\). Initially each color is one copy of \(\mathbb N^s\). After choosing a point, delete its upward cone. Partition the remaining points into translated coordinate orthants, each with some coordinates fixed and the other coordinates ranging independently above nonnegative lower bounds. Coordinates local to any such orthant are obtained by subtracting those lower bounds, so their sum is at most the sum of the original exponents.

Suppose the next point lies in an orthant with \(j>0\) free coordinates and has local coordinates \(\alpha=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_j)\). The complement of its upward cone inside that orthant is the disjoint union of the slabs specified by the first index \(h\) for which \(x_h<\alpha_h\): fix \(x_h\) at one of \(0,\ldots,\alpha_h-1\), require \(x_i\ge\alpha_i\) for \(i<h\), and leave the later coordinates free. Each slab is a translated copy of \(\mathbb N^{j-1}\), and there are \(\sum_h\alpha_h\le b+t\) of them. A zero-dimensional orthant is simply deleted. Orthants of other colors or from earlier splits may contain further forbidden points; retaining them only enlarges the available set and is harmless for an upper bound. Thus one selected \(j\)-dimensional component can be replaced by at most \(b+t\) components of dimension \(j-1\). Pad with empty, never-selected components to obtain exactly the transition \(T_j\). The local coordinate bound persists in every real child.

Induction in the same well-founded order proves that a sequence beginning with counts \(a\) at time \(t\) has length at most \(L_b(a;t)\): remove its first point, use the indicated transition including empty padding, and apply the induction hypothesis to the remaining sequence. This proves the controlled-sequence bound without importing a numerical length-function theorem. It is the elementary quantitative version of the monomial divisibility argument already used in the polynomial Ore model; no independent novelty claim is made.

Successive iterates produce the required sequence. Set \(v_t=\nabla^t v\) and \(M_t=\sum_{j<t}S v_j\). If \(v_t\in M_t\), then \(M_t\) is connection-stable: differentiating its first \(t\) generators stays in it, and the Leibniz rule treats coefficients. All later iterates then lie in it. Homogeneous decomposition of the dependence gives coefficients \(f_j\in S_{t-j}\) with \(v_t=\sum_{j<t}f_jv_j\), hence the homogeneous monic annihilator \(D^t-\sum_{j<t}f_jD^j\). Conversely any monic order-\(t\) annihilator gives such a dependence after taking its homogeneous component of total degree \(t\). Thus the first dependence index is exactly \(U\).

Fix a module monomial order. At every strict step, reduce the homogeneous \(v_t\) against a homogeneous Gröbner basis of \(M_t\). Its nonzero remainder \(h_t\) is homogeneous of weight \(w+t\), and its leading monomial is outside \(\operatorname{in}(M_t)\). If that monomial is \(z^\alpha e_i\), positivity of the integer variable weights gives \[ |\alpha|\le\sum_\nu (\deg z_\nu)\alpha_\nu=w+t-\deg e_i\le b+t. \] For \(u<t\), \(h_u\in M_{u+1}\subseteq M_t\). Therefore its leading monomial belongs to \(\operatorname{in}(M_t)\) and cannot divide the new leading monomial. The strict steps give precisely a controlled colored bad sequence. The bound just proved prevents more than \(L_b(r\epsilon_s;0)\) strict steps, so a dependence occurs by that index and proves (GC). Individual Gröbner bases exist for finitely generated submodules of a polynomial free module; their degrees do not enter this argument, because homogeneous reduction preserves the weight of the single remainder. \(\square\)

Dimension-only bounds for the actual cube endpoint and residual relations

Corollary (cor:cube-effective-residual-relations; working proof). For the actual characteristic-zero degree-two cube with \(N=n+1\ge5\), define \[ \Lambda_N=L_{2N-5}\left(\binom{N-2}{2}\epsilon_{N-1};0\right), \qquad Q_N=2N-1+\Lambda_N. \] Let \(U_{\rm original}\) be the least original monic order and \(B=\max\operatorname{supp}\operatorname{Tor}_1^S(K_2,k)\), with maximum \(-\infty\) for a zero space. Then \[ \binom N2+2\le U_{\rm original}\le Q_N, \qquad B\le\max(Q_N-1,5N-7). \tag{CB} \] These bounds depend only on \(N\), not on the unknown primary exponent, a computed cutoff, a parameter point, or a choice of characteristic-zero field. The previously proved lower bound \(B\ge\binom N2+1\) for \(N\ge8\) still holds.

Proof. The exact marked core is free over \(S=k[c_2,\ldots,c_N]\), with rank \(\binom{N-2}{2}\), a degree-one polynomial connection, marker of weight \(2N-1\), and homogeneous basis \(D^jb_r\) for \(r\ge2\), whose minimum weight is four. Thus the general theorem applies with \(s=N-1\), \(b=2N-5\). Marked deflation preserves the highest coefficient and shifts order by exactly \(2N-1\); this proves the upper bound for \(U_{\rm original}\). Its lower bound was proved from generic cyclic rank in the residual-source theorem.

Use the actual reviewed exact sequences \[ 0\to K\to C\to D_{22}(-4)\to0, \qquad 0\to K_2\to K\to D_{32}(-N-3)\to0. \] Their long exact Tor sequences give \[ \max\beta_1(K_2)\le \max\left(\max\beta_1(C),\max\beta_2(D_{22}(-4)), \max\beta_2(D_{32}(-N-3))\right). \] The notation \(\max\beta_i\) denotes the largest weight with nonzero Tor. The minimal normalization resolutions have second-Tor maxima \(4N-5\) and \(5N-7\), respectively: their basis-weight maxima are \(2N-8\) and \(2N-9\), and the largest pairs of Koszul weights are \(2N-1\) in both cases, followed by shifts four and \(N+3\). The actual marked minimal cover gives \(\max\beta_1(C)=U_{\rm original}-1\). Consequently \[ B\le\max(U_{\rm original}-1,5N-7)\le\max(Q_N-1,5N-7), \] as asserted. No normalization splitting or replacement of the marked connection is involved. \(\square\)

Controls and limits. For a rank-one connection over \(k[z]\), with \(\delta=0\), \(\nabla=0\), and marker \(z^b\), the true cutoff is one. The recursion gives \(L_b(\epsilon_1;0)=b+1\): after the first step only \(b\) zero-dimensional components remain. This checks the time convention and demonstrates deliberate slack. With no variables, \(L_b(r\epsilon_0;0)=r\), the usual linear-dependence bound. A zero marker has cutoff zero. These are direct symbolic checks, not numerical experiments.

In the quintic control the recorded actual core cutoff is ten, original cutoff nineteen, and residual first-Tor maximum eighteen. Our recursion at \(b=5\), \(s=4\), \(r=3\) is consistent and much weaker: one permitted path selects dimensions four, three, two, one successively, creating eight zero-dimensional components at time four; removing these alone already gives a path of length twelve, with other components still present. Thus \(\Lambda_5\ge12\), without evaluating its full recursion. More generally the recursion permits at least one step for each original component, so \(\Lambda_N\ge\binom{N-2}{2}\); the bound is consistent with the generic quadratic lower bound. Neither control is new cube data, and no larger parameter run is needed.

Its counterexample \((S/S_+^a)(-(2N-1))\) still correctly shows that bounded generators, small support and an abstract connection do not suffice. The present argument additionally fixes the free ambient rank and grading and the homogeneous marked vector. Those data uniformly control the degrees of remainders and rule out arbitrarily long bad sequences. We do not assert that the counterexample admits such a realization with these data fixed. The previous mathematical source bound and quadratic lower bound are unchanged.

The search found qualitative Dickson/Noetherian antecedents, so this is a quantitative refinement with no novelty claim. The review record retains both verdicts. No Lean claim is made.

27 September 2026 — The full graded defect already retains the order flag

Working proof: intrinsic recovery of leading-coefficient ideals from the first syzygy's degree-generated flag; no new threshold values. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and outcome. Open statement 3 needs the original specified-order thresholds. The preceding recursive bound controls an endpoint but not these ideals. This cycle tests whether the full graded defect actually needs additional marked differential data to retain its order flag. It does not in the minimal marked setting: the first syzygy has exactly one minimal generator in each consecutive weight, and its intrinsic degree-generated submodules are precisely the iterate prefixes. This removes an unnecessary data requirement. It does not compute the full defect from its normalization layers or give a new threshold formula.

General statement. thm:graded-defect-intrinsic-order-flag recovers every leading-coefficient ideal from the graded isomorphism class of the full defect over the fixed coefficient ring, provided the marked free cover is minimal. cor:cube-thresholds-from-graded-defect applies this to the degree-two cube in every characteristic-zero dimension \(N\ge5\). The consecutive first-Betti weights are already in the residual-source proof; the new refinement is the intrinsic flag and its cyclic quotient ideals.

The first syzygy has an intrinsic order filtration

Theorem (thm:graded-defect-intrinsic-order-flag; working proof). Let \(S=k[z_1,\ldots,z_s]\) be positively integer graded, with \(S_0=k\) and \(\mathfrak m=S_+\). Let \(F\) be finite graded free with a degree-one \(\delta\)-connection, and let \(v\ne0\) be homogeneous of weight \(w\). Put \(A=S[D;\delta]\), \(M=Av\), \(C=F/M\), and assume \(M\subset\mathfrak mF\). Let \(U\) be the least monic order in \(J=\operatorname{Ann}_A(v)\), which exists. Let \(\Omega C\) be the kernel of any minimal graded free cover of \(C\). Define \[ G_{-1}=0,\qquad G_j=S\cdot\bigoplus_{d\le w+j}(\Omega C)_d\quad(j\ge0), \qquad I_j=\operatorname{Ann}_S(G_j/G_{j-1}). \tag{IF} \] Then \(w=\min\operatorname{supp}\operatorname{Tor}_1^S(C,k)\), this Tor space has one basis vector in every weight \(w,\ldots,w+U-1\), and no others. For \(0\le j<U\), \[ G_j/G_{j-1}\cong(S/I_j)(-w-j). \tag{CQ} \] Moreover \(I_j\) is exactly the order-\(j\) leading-coefficient ideal of \(J\): \[ I_j=\left\{f\in S:\exists f_0,\ldots,f_{j-1}\in S, \ fD^j+\sum_{i<j} f_iD^i\in J\right\}. \tag{LC} \] For \(j\ge U\), the flag is constant and \(I_j=S\), agreeing with (LC). Thus all these ideals, including their placement at each order, depend only on the full graded \(S\)-module isomorphism class of \(C\), with the coefficient ring and absolute grading fixed. This does not assert determination by its Betti table or associated sheaf.

The minimal iterate cover. Write \(v_i=D^iv\). The monic-existence argument proves that the first dependence \(v_U\in\sum_{i<U}Sv_i\) has index \(U\); the prefix then remains stable under the connection. Thus these first \(U\) iterates generate \(M\). They are a minimal homogeneous generating set. Indeed, if the class of \(v_j\) vanished in \(M/\mathfrak mM\), homogeneity expresses it using only generators of smaller weight: an \(\mathfrak m\)-coefficient has strictly positive weight, so an iterate of weight at least \(w+j\) cannot occur. This would give a monic relation of order \(j<U\). Since all the generator weights are distinct, a homogeneous linear dependence of their residue classes is exactly such a vanishing. Hence \[ M/\mathfrak mM\cong\bigoplus_{i=0}^{U-1}k(-w-i). \] The assumption \(M\subset\mathfrak mF\) makes \(F\to C\) a minimal free cover. Tensoring its kernel sequence with \(k\) therefore identifies \(M/\mathfrak mM\) with \(\operatorname{Tor}_1(C,k)\), proving the asserted weights and recovering \(w,U\) from \(C\). These facts reprove the already recorded consecutive-weight argument, not a new independent Betti formula.

Identifying the intrinsic flag. Use this minimal cover first, so \(\Omega C=M\). Its first \(j+1\) iterates have weights at most \(w+j\) and therefore lie in \(G_j\). Conversely any homogeneous element of \(M\) of weight at most \(w+j\) is a combination of the minimal iterates with homogeneous coefficients. Positive grading forbids any contribution from an iterate of weight greater than \(w+j\). Thus \[ G_j=Sv_0+\cdots+Sv_j\quad(0\le j<U), \qquad G_j=M\quad(j\ge U-1). \] The map \(S(-w-j)\to G_j/G_{j-1}\) sending one to \([v_j]\) is onto. Its kernel consists exactly of coefficients \(f\) for which \(fv_j\) is in the preceding prefix. This is both the annihilator of the cyclic quotient and the set (LC), proving (CQ) and (LC). At and above \(U\), multiplying a monic relation by powers of \(D\) supplies monic relations at every order, so the zero quotient and unit leading ideal agree.

Why the construction is independent of the cover. A graded isomorphism \(C\to C'\) lifts to a degree-zero map between their minimal graded free covers by choosing homogeneous preimages of a homogeneous basis. Modulo \(\mathfrak m\), the map is an isomorphism. The cover basis-weight multisets agree; the determinant of the lift is therefore homogeneous of weight zero and has nonzero constant reduction. It is a unit, so the lift is a graded isomorphism, restricting to an isomorphism \(\Omega C\to\Omega C'\). Every graded isomorphism preserves the submodule generated by elements of weight at most a specified bound. Hence it preserves (IF) and the annihilator ideals over the fixed \(S\).

Equivalently, choose any minimal relation cover \(F_1\to\Omega C\). Its basis weights are the distinct consecutive weights \(w+i\). A homogeneous change of this basis sends the weight-\(w+j\) basis vector to a nonzero constant multiple of itself plus polynomial multiples of vectors of smaller weight. It is triangular and preserves every initial prefix. On a vector supported through position \(j\), its highest coordinate is multiplied only by that nonzero constant. Its kernel's leading-coordinate ideals therefore agree with (LC). The full polynomial differential of a minimal presentation suffices; no compatibility of the chosen basis with \(D\) is needed. \(\square\)

Application to every characteristic-zero degree-two cube

Corollary (cor:cube-thresholds-from-graded-defect; working proof). Let \(N=n+1\ge5\), \(S=k[c_2,\ldots,c_N]\) in characteristic zero, and let \(C\) be the actual centered degree-two defect, with its full polynomial grading. Apply (IF) to \(\Omega C\), with \(w=2N-1\). For the original degree-two threshold, namely savings three, and \(j\ge0\), \[ \ell_0(3,2N-1+j)=\operatorname{indeg} I_j, \qquad \operatorname{indeg}(0)=+\infty,\quad \operatorname{indeg}(S)=0. \tag{CT} \] There is no original relation below \(2N-1\). After \(j\ge U\), all thresholds are zero. Consequently the full graded \(S\)-module \(C\) determines the complete characteristic-zero degree-two row. Its normalization quotients or their direct sum are not asserted to determine \(C\).

Proof and grading. The exact marked deflation supplies a free core \(F\) and vector \(v\) of weight \(w=2N-1\), with \(C=F/Av\) and all iterates in \(S_+F\). It preserves the leading coefficient, shifts original order and total degree by \(w\), and excludes original relations below that shift. Thus the theorem applies. A homogeneous \(f\in I_j\) of weight \(\ell\) gives a relation with coefficient of \(D^i\) of weight \(\ell+j-i\), by taking the weight-\(w+j+\ell\) part of \(fv_j\in G_{j-1}\). The core operator has order \(j\), total degree \(j+\ell\), and excess \(\ell\). Its original lift has order \(w+j\) and the same excess. Conversely every homogeneous original operator descends this way. The established centered prefix descent preserves initial degrees over the original parameter ring. This proves (CT), including the zero and unit ideals. \(\square\)

The quintic falsification control survives. For \(N=5\), the recorded minimal presentation has \(F_0\) basis weights four, five, six, and \(F_1\) basis weights nine through eighteen. The first four columns are therefore the intrinsic prefix through weight twelve, regardless of homogeneous changes of minimal bases. In the marked presentation these are \(v,Dv,D^2v,D^3v\). The retained primitive minor relation has core order three, total degree eighteen, and leading coefficient weight fifteen. Viewed in \(F_1\), it has weight \(9+18=27\); its last coordinate has weight \(27-12=15\). Triangular changes of the minimal relation basis preserve that coefficient ideal and the absence of smaller excess at that order. This recovers the same boundary data without rerunning a matrix calculation.

The saved eight-order cancellation is still real: its minimum intermediate order eleven concerns expressions in six fixed Ore generators of the annihilator. These are different from the ten consecutive-weight \(S\)-generators of \(\Omega C\). The theorem makes no assertion that those six homogenized operators form an order-compatible basis. It reconstructs the order flag from the complete commutative presentation, whose exact polynomial kernel already retains the cancellation.

Those statements are too broad for the present minimal marked setting. The full graded module over the fixed coefficient ring determines the intrinsic flag above. A Betti table, Tor barcode, associated sheaf, separate normalization layers, or unspecified ungraded isomorphism still does not supply that module and its graded presentation. The vertex-loss obstruction, the six-generator Rees calculation, and the need to retain extension data are unchanged. No earlier numerical or mathematical theorem is retracted.

It found no mathematical correction or gap. The medium pre-proof reviewer required explicit minimality, positive grading, the fixed coefficient ring, \(G_{-1}=0\), and zero/unit ideal conventions; all are incorporated. 27 September 2026 — The normalization layers leave a four-parameter extension ambiguity

Working proof and refutation of graded extension rigidity: exact characteristic-zero extension family, with fixed layers and minimal generator weights. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and outcome. Open statement 3 now asks for the full graded defect or its intrinsic first-syzygy flag. This cycle tests a concrete shortcut: do the two normalized layers, together with the known minimal generator weights, determine their extension? The smallest retained instance already refutes that hypothesis. Its degree-zero extension space has dimension five, and a nonempty open part of its projectivization gives nonisomorphic middle modules with exactly the same generator weights. No larger dimension test is needed to reject this rigidity mechanism.

General statement. prop:cube-normalization-extension-nonrigidity constructs and classifies an algebraic family of graded extensions over every characteristic-zero field. The fixed quintic normalization data are used to refute the proposed all-dimensional rigidity rule, not to add another fitted parameter case. The actual cube quotient is one member; no other member is asserted to be a cube defect.

An exact extension space and its middle modules

Proposition (prop:cube-normalization-extension-nonrigidity; working proof). Let \(k\) have characteristic zero and \(S=k[c_2,c_3,c_4,c_5]\), with coefficient weights \(2,3,4,5\). Let \(D=k[u,v]\), of weights one and two, and \(B=k[z]\), of weight one, have the normalization coefficient maps \[ (c_2,c_3,c_4,c_5)|_D=(2v-3u^2,-2u(u^2+v),v^2-4u^2v,-2uv^2), \] \[ (c_2,c_3,c_4,c_5)|_B=(-15z^2,10z^3,60z^4,-72z^5). \] Then \[ \dim_k\operatorname{Ext}^1_S(D(-4),B(-8))_0=5. \tag{EX} \] Its classes are the six scalar coordinates \((a_0,a_1,a_2,b_0,b_1,b_2)\) subject to the single equation \[ 18(a_0-2a_1+a_2)+15(b_0-2b_1+b_2)=0. \tag{EC} \] Nonzero classes modulo common scalar, a \(\mathbf P^4(k)\), classify the non-split middle modules up to graded \(S\)-isomorphism. In the nonempty open subset \[ a_0\ne0,\qquad (a_1,b_0)\ne(0,0), \tag{OP} \] every middle module \(E\) in \(0\to B(-8)\to E\to D(-4)\to0\) has exactly three minimal generators of weights four, five and six. All have the same Hilbert series and the same two dimension-filtration layers. The actual quotient \(C/T\) belongs to this open subset. Thus fixing these graded data does not determine even that quotient. A common free source of weights four, five and six is meant here, not an identified presentation map or kernel.

The known exact resolution. The reviewed upper-layer calculation gives \[ A=S[u]/(g_3),\quad g_3=5u^3+c_2u+c_3, \] \[ g_4=4c_4-c_2^2+2c_2u^2+15u^4,\qquad g_5=2c_5+c_2^2u+6c_2u^3+9u^5. \] Here \(A\) is \(S\)-free on \(1,u,u^2\), and \(g_4,g_5\) form a regular sequence with quotient \(D\). Its minimal \(S\)-free resolution, shifted by four, is \[ 0\to A(-13)\xrightarrow{(-g_5,g_4)}A(-8)\oplus A(-9) \xrightarrow{(g_4,g_5)}A(-4)\to D(-4)\to0. \tag{KR5} \] This resolution is used with its actual multiplication maps, not inferred from its Hilbert numerator.

The complete degree-zero cocycle calculation. Apply graded \(\operatorname{Hom}_S(-,B(-8))\). The degree-zero Hom from \(A(-4)\) is zero, since its generators have weights four, five and six while the target begins in weight eight. Thus there are no degree-zero coboundaries. A degree-zero map out of the middle free module is exactly the pair \[ \phi_4(1,u,u^2)=(a_0,a_1z,a_2z^2),\qquad \phi_5(1,u,u^2)=(b_0z,b_1z^2,b_2z^3). \] This gives all six possible coefficients, with no omitted polynomial parameter.

Specialize the multiplication matrices to \(B\). In \(A\otimes_S B\), put \(q=(u-z)^2\). Direct substitution and reduction by the cubic give \[ g_3=5(u-z)^2(u+2z),\qquad g_4=15z^2q,\qquad g_5=-18z^3q. \tag{SP} \] For the last two equalities, reduction uses \(u^3=3z^2u-2z^3\). In particular \(uq=-2zq\) and \(u^2q=4z^2q\). Evaluating the first differential of (KR5) under the Hom pair on \(1\) therefore gives \[ \phi_4(-g_5)+\phi_5(g_4) =\bigl(18(a_0-2a_1+a_2)+15(b_0-2b_1+b_2)\bigr)z^5. \] Its values on \(u,u^2\) are this same expression multiplied by \(-2z,4z^2\), respectively. Thus the map from the six-dimensional Hom space to the three-dimensional next Hom space has rank exactly one, and its kernel is (EC). Since the preceding Hom space is zero, this proves (EX). The maps \(\phi_i\) are \(S\)-linear, not asserted \(A\)-linear: evaluation of the specialized matrices uses their unique \(B\)-linear extensions to \(A\otimes_S B\). This distinction is essential to the computation.

Actual extensions, without an existence shortcut. For any solution \(\phi=(\phi_4,\phi_5)\) of (EC), form the graded \(S\)-module \[ E_\phi=\bigl(B(-8)\oplus A(-4)\bigr) \Big/\left\langle\bigl(-\phi_4(x)-\phi_5(y),g_4x+g_5y\bigr): (x,y)\in A(-8)\oplus A(-9)\right\rangle_S. \tag{PO} \] The map onto \(D(-4)\) is evident. The copy of \(B(-8)\) injects: a relation with zero second component comes from the image of the first differential in (KR5), and the cocycle condition says its first component is also zero. This constructs the exact extension. Changes of lifts of the cover would be degree-zero Hom maps from \(A(-4)\), all zero, so these coordinates also give the usual equivalence classes of graded extensions with the endpoints identified.

Classification of unmarked middle modules. Each endpoint is a domain finite and birational over its coefficient image. For \(B\), the image contains \(z^2,z^3\), hence has fraction field \(k(z)\). For \(D\), at a generic quintic with two distinct double roots and one distinct simple root, the monic gcd of the polynomial and its derivative is its unique double-root quadratic; this recovers \(u,v\) over the coefficient fraction field. Finiteness is already supplied by (KR5) and the reviewed normalization maps.

An \(S\)-linear endomorphism of either endpoint extends generically to multiplication on its rank-one coefficient fraction field. Its value at one belongs to the endpoint ring, and multiplication by that value agrees everywhere by torsion freeness. Thus its endomorphism ring is the normalization ring itself. The degree-zero automorphisms are exactly \(k^*\). Also \(B(-8)\) is the canonical largest submodule of \(E\) of dimension at most one: any such submodule maps to zero in \(D(-4)\), because every nonzero submodule of that domain has dimension two. Conversely \(B\) is pure of dimension one. Every middle-module isomorphism therefore preserves this submodule and induces scalar automorphisms on both endpoints. The standard pushout/pullback action on an extension class multiplies it by a nonzero scalar; this is also immediate by rescaling the two summands in (PO). Hence the projective classes are precisely the isomorphism classes of the non-split middle modules. The endpoints and all isomorphisms keep the coefficient ring fixed.

The open generator condition. Tensoring the extension with \(k=S/S_+\) gives the connecting map \[ \operatorname{Tor}_1(D(-4),k)\longrightarrow B(-8)/S_+B(-8) \longrightarrow E/S_+E\longrightarrow D(-4)/S_+D(-4)\to0. \] The target of the connecting map has basis \(1,z\) in weights eight and nine. In the resolution (KR5), the weight-eight generator is the first basis element of \(A(-8)\), and the weight-nine generators are its \(u\) basis element and the first basis element of \(A(-9)\). Their images are \(a_0\), \(a_1z\), and \(b_0z\), up to a common harmless sign. Thus surjectivity is exactly (OP). It is equivalent to the middle module having only the three minimal generators inherited from \(D(-4)\). The point \((a_0,a_1,a_2)=(1,1,1)\), \((b_0,b_1,b_2)=(0,0,0)\) satisfies (EC) and (OP), proving nonemptiness. On the chart \(a_0=1\), the independent parameters may be \(a_1,a_2,b_0,b_1\), with \[ b_2=-\tfrac65(1-2a_1+a_2)-b_0+2b_1, \] excluding only \(a_1=b_0=0\). This is the stated four-parameter family. Hilbert series agree by additivity in the extension, and the purity argument fixes the two dimension layers.

The actual \(C/T\) has the required minimal generator weights. The retained complete presentation gives minimal weights four, five and six for \(C\), and its vertex submodule \(T\) begins in weight ten. Therefore \(T\subset S_+C\), and quotienting by it leaves the minimal generator space unchanged. The reviewed normalization quotient is an isomorphism on those generator spaces. Its connecting map is consequently onto, so its extension class lies in (OP). \(\square\)

Checks and limits. The calculation exhausts all six homogeneous coefficients and all three cocycle equations; the next differential has rank one because its nonzero scalar equation occurs in every row with the stated powers of \(z\). Degree-zero boundaries vanish for an independent grading reason. The displayed parameter point is a non-split extension satisfying the generator condition, whereas the zero class is split and has the two extra minimal generators in weights eight and nine. These are exact symbolic controls; no numerical sample or resolution rerun is needed. The result does not claim that these alternative modules are cube defects, have a compatible connection, or share the actual defect's threshold ideals. It identifies ambiguity in reconstructing a module from the stated graded layer data alone.

Verification gate. A fresh-context medium correctness reviewer passed the full calculation, the explicit pushout, scalar endpoint automorphisms, canonical dimension layer, projective classification, open generator condition and actual quotient membership. It found no gap or unused substantive hypothesis; the stronger characteristic-zero scope correctly matches the actual-module dependencies. The medium pre-proof reviewer required \(\mathbf P^4(k)\) over the stated field and the distinction between a common free source and an identified presentation; both are incorporated. The exact upper-layer Koszul resolution and the actual quintic filtration were reread. The review record retains the verdicts. No novelty claim is made.

Assessment and next step. The shortcut from normalized layers and generator weights to the full graded object is refuted by a positive-dimensional family, so further support classification alone cannot recover the intrinsic flag. The next test on cube-odd-characteristic is whether compatibility with the actual polynomial connections cuts this explicit degree-zero extension space down to the cube's class. Work on the extension space itself, not another threshold row. If compatible classes still vary, identify the extra polynomial condition before claiming reconstruction. Even a unique upper extension would leave the residual vertex module and its extension, higher savings, and the independent small-prime branch unresolved.

Process. The existing exact Koszul maps reduced the rigidity test to one scalar equation, replacing a new computer-algebra run; the resulting family identifies precisely which reconstruction shortcut fails.

27 September 2026 — The polynomial connection selects the quintic upper extension

Working proof: the prescribed endpoint connections select one projective extension class in the complete quintic family; vertex reconstruction remains open. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and outcome. Open statement 3 requires the full graded defect to recover its intrinsic order flag. The preceding family refutes reconstruction from normalized layers and generator weights alone. This cycle tests whether their actual degree-one polynomial connections select the extension. They do in the quintic case: the compatible extension space is one-dimensional, so its nonzero projective class is unique. This reconstructs the upper quotient with the vertex removed, not the complete defect or its threshold row.

General statement. prop:cube-quintic-connection-extension-rigidity classifies compatibility on the entire previously constructed extension space over every characteristic-zero field. It is a symbolic test of the general connection-based reconstruction mechanism, not a new numerical parameter sample. The proof identifies the degree gap that limits its immediate extension to higher dimensions.

Unique nonzero compatible class

Proposition (prop:cube-quintic-connection-extension-rigidity; working proof). Use \(S,D,B,A,g_i\) and the six extension coordinates of the preceding proposition. Write \(c=c_2,d=c_3,e=c_4,f=c_5\). Give \(S\) the centered derivation \[ \delta c=3d,\quad \delta d=4e-\tfrac65c^2,\quad \delta e=5f-\tfrac45cd,\quad \delta f=-\tfrac25ce. \] The actual endpoint connections are \[ \nabla_D=\delta_D-\tfrac72u,\qquad \delta_Du=2u^2+\tfrac15c, \qquad \nabla_B=-z^2\partial_z-\tfrac{25}{2}z. \tag{CN} \] Among graded extensions \(0\to B(-8)\to E\to D(-4)\to0\), the classes admitting a degree-one \(\delta\)-connection making both maps compatible are exactly the line spanned by \[ (a_0,a_1,a_2,b_0,b_1,b_2) =\left(1,-\tfrac35,-\tfrac{17}{5},-\tfrac{41}{25},-\tfrac3{25},\tfrac{71}{25}\right). \tag{CC} \] Thus all nonzero compatible middle modules are isomorphic to the actual \(C/T\). For a fixed extension with its endpoint maps, its compatible degree-one connection is unique. No analogous assertion about the vertex extension \(0\to T\to C\to C/T\to0\) is made.

Identifying the actual endpoint connections. The reviewed EPD compatibility gives the connection on the first normalization quotient as root drift minus \(7s/2\). Its two roots have derivatives \(-b^2-\kappa,-c^2-\kappa\), with \(\kappa=2c_2/5\), so their sum \(u\) satisfies \(\delta_Du=-u^2+2v-2\kappa\). Substituting \(v=(c_2+3u^2)/2\) gives the first formula in (CN).

The vertex torsion \(T\) is connection-stable. Indeed \(\delta(S_+^r)\subseteq S_+^r\), and if \(S_+^rt=0\), then \(a\nabla t=-\delta(a)t=0\) for every \(a\in S_+^r\). Thus the actual \(C/T\) has a compatible quotient connection. Its lower dimension layer is stable as well: if an ideal \(I\) annihilates a vector, then \(I^2\) annihilates its derivative, by applying the Leibniz rule twice. The cyclic support, and hence its dimension, cannot increase. The canonical dimension-one submodule is therefore preserved.

On that layer the coefficient derivation extends to \(\delta_Bz=-z^2\), as is seen already from \(c_2=-15z^2\) and \(\delta c_2=30z^3\), or directly from the root drift. To identify the scalar part of the connection, use \(a=a_4\), \(a_5\), and \(s=x+y\) in the EPD representative. If \(V\) is the coefficient-plus-root derivation, then \(Vp(t)=-5t p(t)\) at a marked root variable and \(V(y-x)=-(x+y)(y-x)\). Differentiating the divided difference gives \[ Va=-5a_5+sa,\qquad \nabla a=-5a_5-\tfrac52sa. \] The reviewed product formulas, at triple root \(-2z\) and double root \(3z\), give \[ \chi(a)=1,\qquad \chi(a_5)=3z,\qquad \chi(sa)=\tfrac75(-2z)+\tfrac35(3z)=-z. \] Hence the induced connection sends one to \(-25z/2\). Subtracting \(\delta_B\) leaves an \(S\)-linear endomorphism of \(B\), which is multiplication by its value at one, by the preceding endpoint endomorphism calculation. This proves the second formula in (CN) on the actual layer.

The unique lift on the free cover. Let \(F_0=A(-4)\) with \(S\)-basis \(1,u,u^2\) in weights four, five and six. Its relation module begins in weight eight. Thus \(\nabla_D\) has a unique homogeneous degree-one lift on these three generators. Reduction by \(5u^3+cu+d=0\) gives its connection matrix, with columns recording images of the basis: \[ H=\begin{pmatrix} 0&c/5&-d/10\\ -7/2&0&3c/10\\ 0&-3/2&0 \end{pmatrix},\qquad \nabla_0=\delta+H. \tag{FC} \] For an extension \(E\), lifts of these generators from \(D(-4)\) are unique because their weights are below eight. Their connection images have weights five, six and seven, again below the minimum weight of \(B(-8)\). Consequently any compatible connection on \(E\) is forced to be induced by \(\nabla_B\oplus\nabla_0\) on the pushout presentation. In particular there is no adjustable degree-one cross map \(F_0\to B(-8)\). Such a connection exists exactly when this direct-sum connection preserves the relation submodule in that presentation.

Four necessary relation identities. Let \(r_{4i},r_{5i}\) be the free generators of \(A(-8)\oplus A(-9)\) corresponding to \(u^i\), for \(0\le i\le2\), and let \(d_1\) be its map \((g_4,g_5)\) into \(F_0\). There is a unique lift of the connection on each such relation generator: its image has weight at most twelve, whereas the Koszul kernel begins in weight thirteen. We need only four of the resulting identities: \[ \begin{aligned} \nabla_1r_{40}&=-\tfrac{13}{2}r_{41}+10r_{50},\\ \nabla_1r_{41}&=-\tfrac92r_{42}+10r_{51}+\tfrac25c\,r_{40},\\ \nabla_1r_{50}&=-\tfrac95r_{42}-\tfrac72r_{51}-\tfrac{26}{25}c\,r_{40},\\ \nabla_1r_{42}&=10r_{52}+\tfrac{11}{10}c\,r_{41}+\tfrac{11}{10}d\,r_{40}. \end{aligned} \tag{RL} \] They are identities over the full polynomial coefficient ring. To verify them without an implicit lift computation, the six columns of \(d_1\), in order \(r_{40},r_{41},r_{42},r_{50},r_{51},r_{52}\), are \[ \begin{pmatrix} 4e-c^2&cd/5&3d^2/5&2f-21cd/25&9d^2/25&-4c^2d/125\\ -3d&4e-4c^2/5&4cd/5&4c^2/25&2f-12cd/25&9d^2/25-4c^3/125\\ -c&-3d&4e-4c^2/5&-9d/5&4c^2/25&2f-12cd/25 \end{pmatrix}. \tag{MX} \] These follow by multiplying the reduced \(g_4,g_5\) by \(1,u,u^2\) and using the cubic. Apply \(\delta+H\) to the first, second, fourth and third columns, respectively; substitution of the displayed coefficient derivation and (FC) gives exactly \(d_1\) applied to the four right sides of (RL). This is a direct polynomial-identity check, not a numerical specialization.

Linear compatibility constraints. In the pushout, the relation \(d_1r\) equals \(\phi(r)\) in the lower layer. Therefore connection compatibility requires \(\nabla_B\phi(r)=\phi(\nabla_1r)\). Since \[ \nabla_B(z^i)=-(i+25/2)z^{i+1},\qquad c|_B=-15z^2,\quad d|_B=10z^3, \] the four relations (RL) give \[ \begin{aligned} -25a_0+13a_1-20b_0&=0,\\ 12a_0-27a_1+9a_2-20b_1&=0,\\ -156a_0+18a_2-135b_0+35b_1&=0,\\ 22a_0-33a_1+29a_2+20b_2&=0. \end{aligned} \tag{LC5} \] Together with the earlier cocycle equation (EC), these leave exactly the line (CC). For completeness, the first three equations give \[ a_1=\frac{25a_0+20b_0}{13},\qquad a_2=\frac{87a_0+80b_0}{13},\qquad b_1=\frac{66a_0+45b_0}{65}. \] Eliminating \(b_2\) between the fourth equation and (EC) gives \(1312a_0+800b_0=0\), hence \(b_0=-41a_0/25\), and the remaining coordinates are (CC). All denominators are nonzero constants in characteristic zero. This also shows that a necessary compatible class with \(a_0=0\) is zero.

Why four necessary equations suffice. We have proved only an upper bound of one on the compatible subspace using (RL); we do not silently assume that the two unused relation equations vanish. Existence comes from the actual \(C/T\): its stable dimension filtration gives a compatible extension with precisely the endpoint connections (CN). The preceding proposition places its class in the open generator locus, so its class is nonzero. It must span the necessary line (CC). Compatibility is a homogeneous linear condition on the cocycle coordinates, because it is invariance of the linear pushout relations under the fixed direct-sum connection. Scalar multiples of a compatible class are therefore compatible, including zero. The necessary line is consequently the entire compatible space, and all unused conditions vanish on it. Uniqueness of the connection follows from the absence of the cross map established above. \(\square\)

Controls and limits. In (CC), \(a_0=1\) and \(a_1=-3/5\), so the class meets the open generator condition. Its cocycle values are \(a_0-2a_1+a_2=-6/5\) and \(b_0-2b_1+b_2=36/25\), which cancel in (EC). The split zero class is compatible but has the two extra generators already recorded. Conversely the preceding open-family point \((1,1,1,0,0,0)\) violates the first equation of (LC5), with value \(-12\). Thus the test rejects a genuine non-split extension with the correct graded generators, not only an irrelevant split example. No new threshold or matrix-rank run is used.

The argument is restricted to the quintic family with the specified endpoint connections. Its free-cover uniqueness uses a strict weight gap: the upper cover generators have weights at most six, their derivatives at most seven, while the lower module begins at eight. One cannot assume that gap in higher dimensions. Moreover the vertex Tor obstruction shows that reconstructing \(C/T\) alone discards every actual second-Tor image needed in the earlier generator mechanism. The unique upper extension is a reconstruction step, not the answer for the full defect.

27 September 2026 — Connection reconstruction needs an Ext obstruction, not a blanket rigidity rule

Route review: general extension obstruction, all-dimensional normalization connection data, a nonrigidity family, and the next cube-specific rigidity test. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

The line and what the goal needs. Open statement 3 requires the full odd-field per-order thresholds. On the current characteristic-zero degree-two line, the full graded defect determines the intrinsic order flag, and a recursive endpoint bound exists. Neither gives the actual flag ideals. The quintic upper layers have a four-parameter graded ambiguity, removed by their prescribed connections. The general missing implication is reconstruction of the actual graded extensions, including the residual module; reconstructing only the upper quotient would still omit the vertex contribution already known to matter.

General statement. lem:graded-connection-extension-obstruction gives the correct all-module compatibility criterion, including cross maps. lem:cube-normalization-connection-data supplies the actual lower density and identifies the first nonvanishing cross-map space for every characteristic-zero \(N\ge5\). obs:connection-compatible-extension-nonrigidity refutes a blanket uniqueness rule with an explicit family over any field. The narrower conj:cube-normalized-extension-rigidity remains open beyond the quintic case; its next test is selected by a structural change, not a fitted sequence.

The compatibility obstruction retains the allowed cross map

Lemma (lem:graded-connection-extension-obstruction; working proof). Let \(S\) be a positively graded polynomial ring over \(k\), let \(\delta\) be a degree-one \(k\)-derivation, and let \(M,L\) be finite graded modules with degree-one \(\delta\)-connections. There is a canonical degree-one \(k\)-linear operator \[ \mathscr E:\operatorname{Ext}^1_S(M,L)_0\longrightarrow \operatorname{Ext}^1_S(M,L)_1. \tag{EO} \] A degree-zero extension class admits a compatible degree-one connection if and only if it belongs to \(\ker\mathscr E\). For a fixed extension with its two endpoint maps, the set of compatible connections, when nonempty, is an affine space under \(\operatorname{Hom}_S(M,L)_1\). This last statement concerns connections on the fixed extension, not their isomorphism classes.

Construction and independence. Choose a graded free resolution \(F_\bullet\to M\). Lift the connection successively to degree-one connections \(\nabla_i\) on \(F_i\) commuting with the differentials: lift generator images first, then lift their syzygy images, which are cycles by the preceding commuting square. On the Hom complex set \[ \mathscr E_i(\phi)=\nabla_L\phi-\phi\nabla_i. \] The Leibniz terms cancel, so this is an \(S\)-linear map \(F_i\to L\) of degree one more than \(\phi\). As an operator on the Hom space it is \(k\)-linear and satisfies the \(\delta\)-Leibniz rule, not generally \(S\)-linearity. The commuting squares give \(\mathscr E(\phi d)=\mathscr E(\phi)d\), hence an operator on cohomology. Two connection lifts differ by a degree-one \(S\)-linear chain map lifting zero on \(M\). Inductively lifting through the exact resolution constructs a chain homotopy between them. Precomposition gives a cochain homotopy on Hom, so the Ext operator is independent of that choice. A comparison of two free resolutions is treated in the same way: its failure to commute with the lifted connections is a chain map lifting zero and is null-homotopic. This proves canonicity. It generalizes the already proved connection-lifting argument on Tor.

The exact descent condition. Write a degree-zero extension using a cocycle \(\phi:F_1\to L\) as \[ E=(L\oplus F_0)/\{(-\phi(r),d_1r):r\in F_1\}. \] For a degree-one \(S\)-linear map \(u:F_0\to L\), consider \[ (l,f)\longmapsto(\nabla_Ll+u(f),\nabla_0f). \] On the displayed relation, subtract the relation indexed by \(\nabla_1r\). The remainder is \((-\mathscr E_1(\phi)(r)+u(d_1r),0)\). Since \(L\) injects into the extension, descent is equivalent to \[ \mathscr E_1(\phi)=u d_1. \tag{XM} \] Thus the obstruction is the class (EO). Conversely, any compatible connection on \(E\), compared with a homogeneous lift \(F_0\to E\), gives just such a map \(u\), by the Leibniz rule. This proves necessity as well as sufficiency. Finally the difference of two compatible connections is an \(S\)-linear map vanishing on \(L\) and with image in \(L\), so it factors uniquely through a degree-one map \(M\to L\). Every such map can be added. \(\square\)

The actual lower connection and the onset of cross maps

Lemma (lem:cube-normalization-connection-data; working proof). For the characteristic-zero cube with \(N\ge5\), the normalized quotient \(K\twoheadrightarrow L=D_{32}(-N-3)\) carries the polynomial connection \[ \nabla_{32}=\delta_{32}-\tfrac72b-\left(N+\tfrac32\right)c, \qquad p(Z)=(Z-b)^3(Z-c)^2R(Z), \tag{ND} \] where \(\delta_{32}\) is the factorization root drift \(r'=-r^2-2c_2/N\). Let \(M=D_{22}(-4)\) have its already proved connection \(\delta_{22}-7s/2\), and let \(F_0\to M\) be its minimal free cover. Then \[ \operatorname{Hom}_S(F_0,L)_1=0\iff N=5, \qquad \dim_k\operatorname{Hom}_S(F_0,L)_1=1\quad(N=6). \tag{ON} \] For every \(N\ge6\) this cross-map space is nonzero. The actual extension \(0\to L\to C/K_2\to M\to0\) gives a nonzero element of \(\ker\mathscr E\) in (EO). Nonzero free-cover cross maps do not themselves prove ambiguity of extension classes or of descended connections.

Proof. The first normalization connection is already in the EPD block proof. The kernel \(K\) is stable. Its maximal submodule \(K_2\) of dimension at most \(N-5\) is stable as well: if \(Ih=0\), then \(I^2\nabla h=0\), so taking a derivative cannot increase cyclic support dimension. Thus the normalized quotient has an induced connection. The factorization root drift defines a polynomial derivation on \(D_{32}\), because it is symmetric in residual roots and preserves trace zero, and it induces the displayed coefficient derivation on \(S\). Subtract it from the quotient connection. The difference is \(S\)-linear. Since \(D_{32}\) is finite birational over its coefficient image, such an endomorphism is generically multiplication on a rank-one fraction field, hence everywhere multiplication by its value at one, which belongs to the domain \(D_{32}\).

For \(a=a_{N-1}\), the divided-difference calculation gives \(\nabla a=-Na_N-5sa/2\). The quotient product formulas, whose gate was subsequently closed, give \[ \chi(a)=1,\quad \chi(a_N)=c,\quad \chi(sa)=(7b+3c)/5. \] Their substitution yields (ND). No discriminant or resultant is inverted in the resulting map. For \(N=5\), \(b=-2z,c=3z\) gives \(-25z/2\), matching the proved control.

The minimal normalization resolution gives \(F_0\) weight polynomial \(t^4b_{22}(t)\), with unique top weight \(2N-4\). The target \(L\) starts in weight \(N+3\) and has nonzero components in every subsequent weight: its polynomial normalization ring contains a nonzero variable of weight one. A free generator of weight \(q\) contributes \(L_{q+1}\) to the degree-one Hom space. Thus all contributions vanish precisely when \(2N-3<N+3\), namely \(N=5\) in this range. At \(N=6\), only the unique top generator of weight eight contributes \(L_9=k\), proving (ON).

Finally \(K_2\) begins in weight at least \(2N-1\), above every minimal generator weight of \(C\), whose maximum is \(2N-4\). Hence \(K_2\subset S_+C\), so \(C/K_2\) has the same minimal generator space as \(C\), and thus as \(M\). A split extension \(M\oplus L\) would have additional generators from the nonzero \(L\). The actual extension is therefore non-split. Its connection is compatible by stability, proving the nonzero-kernel assertion. \(\square\)

Compatible connections do not imply general rigidity

Obstruction (obs:connection-compatible-extension-nonrigidity; working proof). Over any field \(k\), for any \(r\ge0\), let \[ S=k[x,y,z,t_1,\ldots,t_r],\qquad \delta=x^2\partial_x+y^2\partial_y+z^2\partial_z+ \sum_i t_i^2\partial_{t_i}, \] with all variables of weight one. For each \(\lambda\in k\), put \[ E_\lambda=S/(y-\lambda x,x^2,xz). \tag{NR} \] These are pairwise nonisomorphic graded \(S\)-modules in compatible extensions of the fixed normal polynomial modules \[ 0\to k[t_1,\ldots,t_r](-1)\xrightarrow{1\mapsto x}E_\lambda \to k[z,t_1,\ldots,t_r]\to0. \] They have the same Hilbert series, dimension-filtration layers and single minimal generator of weight zero, and fixed endpoint connections. Thus those data, including compatible connections, do not imply uniqueness in general. This is not a family of cube defects.

Proof and falsifying checks. Modulo \(y-\lambda x\), every class has a unique expression \(f(z,t)+xg(t)\), because \(x^2=xz=0\). This proves the exact sequence, the Hilbert series and the generator assertion. Both endpoints are polynomial domains, of dimensions \(r\) and \(r+1\); the lower endpoint is the canonical maximal submodule of dimension at most \(r\). The derivation preserves the ideal since \[ \delta(y-\lambda x)=(y-\lambda x)(y+\lambda x)+(\lambda^2-\lambda)x^2, \] \[ \delta(x^2)=2x^3,\qquad \delta(xz)=x^2z+xz^2. \] It induces the fixed lower connection \(\sum t_i^2\partial_{t_i}\), because \(\delta x=x^2=0\), and the fixed upper connection \(z^2\partial_z+\sum t_i^2\partial_{t_i}\). Distinct parameters give distinct degree-one parts \(k(y-\lambda x)\) of the annihilator ideal, and a cyclic quotient's annihilator is invariant under any \(S\)-module isomorphism. This proves nonisomorphism without relying only on extension equivalence. For \(r=1\), the layer dimensions are two and one, matching the simplest normalization pattern. For \(r=0\), the kernel is finite length and vanishes on \(\operatorname{Proj}S\); all these modules then have the same associated sheaf. On the only relevant standard open, inverting \(z\) forces \(x=y=0\), so the localized connections also agree. \(\square\)

The cube-specific conjecture and its first new test

Conjecture (conj:cube-normalized-extension-rigidity; open beyond \(N=5\)). For every characteristic-zero \(N\ge5\), the actual normalization modules \(M=D_{22}(-4)\), \(L=D_{32}(-N-3)\), with their specified connections, satisfy \[ \dim_k\ker\bigl(\mathscr E:\operatorname{Ext}^1_S(M,L)_0 \to\operatorname{Ext}^1_S(M,L)_1\bigr)=1. \tag{CRG} \] The lower bound one is proved above, so the open claim is the upper bound. The quintic theorem proves that case. The generic family (NR) does not have these cube modules and hence does not refute (CRG). The conjecture is about extension classes, not uniqueness of connections on a fixed extension, and even its proof would leave the residual extension to reconstruct.

Why six roots, and exactly what the test must compute. Six roots are the first case with an adjustable free-cover cross map, so the quintic proof cannot simply be repeated with that map set to zero. Here \(b_{22}=1+t+2t^2+t^3+t^4\), \(L=k[b,c](-9)\), and the degree-zero Hom complex for the minimal upper-layer Koszul resolution has dimensions \[ 0\longrightarrow k^{42}\longrightarrow k^{54}, \] while \(\operatorname{Hom}_S(F_0,L)_1\) has dimension one. If \(m_i=[t^i]b_{22}\), the counts are \(\sum m_i((i+1)+(i+2))=42\) and \(\sum m_i(i+7)=54\). These are exact space sizes for the next test, not results of a rank run. It must compute cocycles and equation (XM), including that one-dimensional cross-map space. Kernel dimension one passes this first new test; a larger dimension refutes (CRG); zero contradicts the actual nonzero extension and signals an encoding error. No further dimension should be run until this prediction is decided and its consequence understood.

Obstacle

The unresolved cube-specific assertion is the upper bound one on the kernel in (CRG), with the cross-map term in (XM) included. Its lower bound is already known. Even uniqueness of this upper extension leaves the actual residual module and its extension, which can affect the intrinsic flag ideals. Full-module reconstruction is sufficient but stronger than directly evaluating those ideals; rigidity is a convenient reconstruction shortcut, not a necessary condition for the goal. A failed rigidity test should return us to the actual EPD extension representative or the flag quotient itself, rather than impose a new uniqueness requirement.

Treat the six extension coordinates as the displacements of three planar joints and the five equations as bar constraints; a rigidity theorem would turn extension uniqueness into a graph sparsity test. Such a rigidity matrix has the two translations and rotation in its kernel, so with three noncoincident planar joints its rank is at most three, not the proved five. For completeness the edge row pairs with a motion through \((p_i-p_j)\cdot(v_i-v_j)\); common translations vanish and a skew rotation gives zero dot product. Coincident degeneracy cannot increase the rank to five. The proposed unpinned translation therefore fails before any generic-graph theorem can be imported. Pinning or adding non-bar constraints would require a new justified model. Answers. A valid rigidity-matrix realization could replace the Ext rank question by a graph criterion, but this candidate realization is impossible. Test. Falsified for this direct mechanical translation.

27 September 2026 — Six-root compatibility is one-dimensional only when the cross map is retained

Exact finite-dimensional rational certificate over the complete six-root polynomial normalization family; the all-dimensional conjecture remains open. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and outcome. Open statement 3 needs the graded defect's intrinsic flag ideals. The connection-rigidity conjecture proposes one sufficient upper-extension reconstruction step. Six roots are its first new structural test because the free-cover cross-map space first becomes nonzero there. The complete rational calculation gives a one-dimensional compatible extension-class space. For the chosen free-cover lift, forcing the cross map to zero leaves only the zero class, falsely excluding the actual nonzero extension. The size series stops here: no seven-root run is proposed.

General statement. The registered all-parameter target is conj:cube-normalized-extension-rigidity; it remains open for \(N\ge7\). The new check:cube-six-root-compatible-extension verifies its first cross-map case over the entire characteristic-zero polynomial coefficient family. It is a finite dimension control, not a proof for all dimensions or a new per-order threshold.

Complete rational compatibility test

Exact check (check:cube-six-root-compatible-extension). Let \(S=\mathbb Q[c_2,\ldots,c_6]\), \(M=D_{22}(-4)\), and \(L=D_{32}(-9)=\mathbb Q[b,c](-9)\), with the actual prescribed connections. The complete degree-zero extension space has dimension twenty, and \[ \dim_{\mathbb Q}\ker\bigl(\mathscr E:\operatorname{Ext}^1_S(M,L)_0 \to\operatorname{Ext}^1_S(M,L)_1\bigr)=1. \tag{N6} \] Also \(\operatorname{Hom}_S(M,L)_1=0\), so a fixed compatible extension has a unique compatible connection. For the particular polynomial free-cover lift specified below, requiring its cross map \(u\) to vanish reduces the compatible-class space to zero. That last assertion depends on the lift and is not an invariant of arbitrary choices. All these rank conclusions extend to every characteristic-zero field by scalar extension from \(\mathbb Q\).

Exact source and target, before any ranks. Use \(P=S[s,v]\), weights one and two for the pair variables, and \[ E_j=[T^j]\frac{p^{\rm rev}(T)}{(1-sT+vT^2)^2},\qquad A=P/(E_3,E_4). \] The reviewed minimal normalization resolution is \[ 0\to A(-15)\xrightarrow{(-E_6,E_5)} A(-9)\oplus A(-10) \xrightarrow{(E_5,E_6)} A(-4)\to M\to0. \] Its \(S\)-basis for \(A\) is \(1,s,s^2,v,s^3,s^4\), with weights \(0,1,2,2,3,4\). To check the basis selection, the zero-coefficient equations give \(sv=2s^3/3\), \(v^2=s^4\), and \(s^5=0\). These six monomials match the already-proved free rank and Hilbert polynomial. The full parameter calculation uses a pair-weight-first monomial order, with \(v\) before \(s\), and verifies every coordinate reconstruction after normal form. The first free-cover weights are therefore \(4,5,6,6,7,8\); first relations have weights \(9,10,11,11,12,13,10,11,12,12,13,14\), and second relations \(15,16,17,17,18,19\).

The lower coefficient map is obtained from \[ p(Z)=(Z-b)^3(Z-c)^2(Z+3b+2c). \] In particular \(c_2=-6b^2-6bc-3c^2\), and the actual drift and density are \[ \delta_{32}b=(b+c)^2,\quad \delta_{32}c=2b(b+c),\qquad \nabla_L=\delta_{32}-\tfrac72b-\tfrac{15}{2}c. \] The certificate retains all five coefficient images and verifies that their derivatives agree with the centered coefficient derivation. No parameter is assigned a numerical value and no root difference is inverted.

Connection lifts and complete homogeneous spaces. On the pair polynomial representatives use \[ \delta_Ps=-s^2+2v-2\kappa,\quad \delta_Pv=-s(v+\kappa),\quad \kappa=c_2/3, \qquad \nabla_P=\delta_P-7s/2. \] Reduce the images of the six chosen basis monomials modulo \((E_3,E_4)\) to define the selected \(S\)-free cover connection \(H_0\). This is a lift from the full normalization, not an assertion that \(\delta_P\) preserves the intermediate ideal. If \(d_1\) is its relation matrix, solve the exact homogeneous equations \[ d_1H_1=\delta(d_1)+H_0d_1 \] one weight at a time over \(\mathbb Q\). Each coefficient space is exhausted by its complete weighted monomial basis. The program verifies the resulting polynomial identity and every matrix-entry weight. Thus \(H_1\) is an actual connection lift on the relation cover; no rational-parameter solve is substituted for the polynomial one.

A degree-zero cocycle \(\phi:F_1\to L\) has forty-two scalar coordinates. There are no degree-zero coboundaries, since the maximum weight eight of \(F_0\) is below the minimum weight nine of \(L\). The conditions \(\phi d_2=0\) give a \(54\)-by-\(42\) rational matrix \(C_0\). The degree-one compatibility expression \[ \mathscr E_1(\phi)=\delta_{32}(\phi) -\left(\tfrac72b+\tfrac{15}{2}c\right)\phi-\phi H_1 \] has fifty-four scalar coordinates. The unique free-cover cross coordinate is the constant value of \(u\) on the weight-eight basis element \(s^4\); all other values vanish by degree. The exact descent condition is \(\mathscr E_1(\phi)-ud_1=0\).

Accordingly, form the full joint rational system on forty-three unknowns, forty-two for \(\phi\) and one for \(u\), with the cocycle and compatibility blocks. The accepted output gives \(\operatorname{rank}C_0=22\), hence \(42-22=20\) extension coordinates. The joint kernel has dimension one and its projection to the forty-two \(\phi\)-coordinates also has dimension one. Its zero-\(\phi\) subspace is zero, which proves the separate connection-freedom assertion. With \(u=0\), the restricted system has rank forty-two and hence only the zero cocycle. These are distinct calculations: the class dimension is the rank of the projected joint kernel, not an assumed equality with the dimension of the joint kernel.

The retained joint kernel is normalized to \(u(s^4)=1\); its first cocycle coordinate, the value on the weight-nine generator \(E_5\), is \(-28/43\). Thus both components are nonzero. The full forty-three-coordinate vector, both relation matrices, both connection matrices, cochain and cross-map coordinate lists, and the complete rational systems are in the certificate; the row-coordinate definitions are in the driver. Reassembling every basis vector of the computed joint kernel gives zero residual in both original polynomial equations, not only in their coefficient encoding.

Controls and completeness. The same Macaulay2 driver first reconstructs the quintic normalization with basis \(1,s,s^2\) and the previously proved \(g_4,g_5\) relations. It recovers the five-dimensional degree-zero Ext space and the line \((1,-3/5,-17/5,-41/25,-3/25,71/25)\), with no cross variable. It rejects the old open-family point \((1,1,1,0,0,0)\) as incompatible and rejects the known class after an intentional density change. This control is needed to validate the new coefficient/connection encoding; no old threshold row or resolution suite is rerun.

The six-root space counts were fixed before launch, and every polynomial coefficient in those spaces is included. The actual nonzero class supplied by the general theorem is the mandatory nonvacuous control: a zero projected kernel would have signalled an error. The observed one-dimensional kernel passes the stated prediction, while the forced-zero-cross control fails in the expected meaningful way. The first run stopped on a Macaulay2 API mistake treating a ring-generator list as a matrix; after correcting that handling, the complete run passed. The failed run is archived as an implementation failure, not failed mathematics.

What this changes. The cube-specific rigidity conjecture is now verified at \(N=5,6\), with the second case showing that the general cross-map term is indispensable for the selected lift. It remains open for \(N\ge7\). No complete residual kernel, vertex extension, sharp monic order or specified-order threshold follows. The successful calculation is over polynomial normalization coordinates throughout, but it still treats one new root count; it cannot be promoted to an all-dimensional theorem.
