27 September 2026 — A global first jet determines all maps between the normalization layers

Working all-dimensional characteristic-zero proof: the normalization Hom module and its connection are explicit; uniqueness of compatible extension classes remains open. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and outcome. Open statement 3 still needs the actual intrinsic flag ideals. After the six-root test, the selected route asks for a uniform upper bound on compatible extension classes. This cycle identifies one of its terms completely in every dimension: all module maps between the normalized layers are evaluation plus one specified first derivative. Consequently a compatible connection on a fixed extension is unique for every \(N\ge5\), even when its free presentation has adjustable cross maps. This does not prove uniqueness of compatible extension classes; it separates that remaining problem from connection-lift freedom and correctly accounts for coboundaries in future calculations.

General statement. thm:cube-normalization-first-jet-hom describes the full polynomial Hom module and its induced connection for all characteristic-zero \(N\ge5\). cor:cube-normalization-connection-uniqueness removes the degree-zero and degree-one Hom terms uniformly and gives the exact quotient of raw cocycle/lift pairs by presentation changes. The target extension-class rigidity conjecture remains open beyond the two verified root counts.

The torsion-free pullback is a global dual-number algebra

Theorem (thm:cube-normalization-first-jet-hom; working proof). Let \(S=k[c_2,\ldots,c_N]\) in characteristic zero, \(N\ge5\), and let \(D=D_{22}\), \(B=D_{32}\) be the actual centered normalization algebras. Write their factorizations as \[ p(Z)=Q(Z)^2R_{22}(Z),\quad Q=Z^2-sZ+v, \qquad p(Z)=(Z-b)^3(Z-c)^2H(Z). \] Give \(\epsilon\) weight one. There is a global graded \(S\)-algebra map \[ j:D\longrightarrow B[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2), \quad Q\longmapsto(Z-b-\epsilon)(Z-c), \quad R_{22}\longmapsto(Z-b+2\epsilon)H. \tag{J1} \] Its \(B\)-linear extension \(B\otimes_S D\to B[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)\) is onto, and its kernel is exactly the \(B\)-torsion submodule. Write \(j(f)=\operatorname{ev}(f)+\epsilon\tau(f)\). Then \[ \operatorname{Hom}_S(D,B)=B\operatorname{ev}\oplus B\tau \cong B\oplus B(1),\qquad \deg\operatorname{ev}=0,\quad\deg\tau=-1. \tag{HM} \] Every homomorphism is recovered polynomially by \[ \phi=\phi(1)\operatorname{ev} +\bigl(\phi(s)-(b+c)\phi(1)\bigr)\tau. \tag{HV} \] Neither the jet quotient nor this formula requires a root difference or resultant to be inverted.

With the actual endpoint connections \(\nabla_D=\delta_D-7s/2\) and \(\nabla_B=\delta_B-7b/2-(N+3/2)c\), the induced Hom connection is \[ \begin{aligned} \mathscr E(\operatorname{ev})&=-(N-2)c\operatorname{ev},\\ \mathscr E(\tau)&=\tfrac72\operatorname{ev}+ \bigl(2b-(N-2)c\bigr)\tau. \end{aligned} \tag{HC} \] It acts on coefficients by the \(\delta_B\)-Leibniz rule.

The map is defined over the full coefficient ring. Modulo \(\epsilon^2\), \[ (Z-b-\epsilon)^2(Z-b+2\epsilon)=(Z-b)^3. \] Thus the substituted factors in (J1) multiply to exactly the given \(p\). Their trace is preserved, as also follows from its unchanged coefficient of \(Z^{N-1}\). The defining factorization equations of \(D\) therefore hold in the target, and the induced map on \(S\) is its fixed map to \(B\), with no \(\epsilon\)-term. In particular both coefficient functionals are \(S\)-linear, despite \(\tau\)'s derivative interpretation. We have \(j(s)=b+c+\epsilon\), so \(\epsilon\) is in the image of the \(B\)-linear extension; it is onto. Also \(\operatorname{ev}(1)=1,\tau(1)=0\) and \(\tau(s)=1\).

The generic fibre is exactly one first jet. Let \(K=\operatorname{Frac}B\). At its generic polynomial, \(b\ne c\), \(H\) is squarefree and coprime to \((Z-b)(Z-c)\). These conditions define a nonempty open set in the polynomial normalization parameter space; the quintic trace relation does not force \(b=c\). Pass faithfully to a splitting field if necessary. The algebra \(K\otimes_S D\) represents the monic quadratic factors \(Q\) with \(Q^2\mid p\), with the remaining monic factor determined by division. A diagonal \(Q=(Z-a)^2\) would require multiplicity at least four and is impossible here. The only unordered repeated-root pair is \(b,c\).

Off the diagonal, label its two roots \(x,y\). Chinese remainder for the comaximal ideals \((Z-x)^2,(Z-y)^2\) identifies \(Q^2\mid p\), scheme-theoretically, with \[ p(x)=p'(x)=p(y)=p'(y)=0. \] At the ordered branch \((b,c)\), the first two equations generate \((x-b)^2\): the remaining factor of \(p'(x)\) is a unit, with value \(3(b-c)^2H(b)\). The second pair generate \(y-c\), since the corresponding derivative factor has value \(2(c-b)^3H(c)\). The local algebra is therefore \(K[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)\), with \(x=b+\epsilon,y=c\). The swapped branch is exchanged freely by the two-element permutation action, and its unordered quotient leaves exactly one such algebra. There are no other support points. The generic surjection furnished by (J1) is consequently an isomorphism; faithful descent gives the assertion over \(K\) itself.

Global Hom, without a flatness shortcut. The pullback algebra is finite over \(B\). Its jet-map kernel becomes zero over \(K\), so every kernel element is \(B\)-torsion. Conversely all \(B\)-torsion maps to zero in the free target. Thus the kernel is exactly that torsion; the pullback algebra itself is not asserted flat or torsion-free. Every \(B\)-linear map from it to the domain \(B\) kills the kernel, and hence factors uniquely through the global jet quotient. Adjunction identifies those maps with \(\operatorname{Hom}_S(D,B)\). The two coefficient maps on the dual numbers give (HM). Evaluating at \(1,s\) gives (HV), whose two coefficients belong to \(B\) even on collisions. Grading in (J1) gives the stated degrees.

The actual connection on these two maps. Extend the root-drift derivation on \(B\) to the jet algebra by \(\delta\epsilon=-2b\epsilon\). It preserves \((\epsilon^2)\). The displaced roots \(b+\epsilon\) and \(b-2\epsilon\) in (J1) then both have derivative \(-r^2-\kappa\) modulo \(\epsilon^2\), with the fixed \(\kappa=2c_2/N\). The root \(c\) and the residual roots have their prescribed drift. Therefore the factorization map is derivation-compatible. Equivalently, \[ \operatorname{ev}(\delta_D f)=\delta_B\operatorname{ev}(f),\qquad \tau(\delta_D f)=\delta_B\tau(f)-2b\tau(f). \] These are polynomial identities, so the root description introduces no residual localization. Also \(\tau(sf)=(b+c)\tau(f)+\operatorname{ev}(f)\). Substitute these identities in \(\mathscr E(\phi)=\nabla_B\phi-\phi\nabla_D\). Subtracting the source density adds \(7(b+c)/2\) to the target density, leaving \(-(N-2)c\); the derivative identity contributes \(+2b\tau\), and the derivative of the source density contributes \(7\operatorname{ev}/2\). This proves (HC). \(\square\)

Connection freedom vanishes uniformly, while class coboundaries must be removed

Corollary (cor:cube-normalization-connection-uniqueness; working proof). Put \(M=D_{22}(-4)\) and \(L=D_{32}(-N-3)\). Then \[ \operatorname{Hom}_S(M,L)\cong B(1-N)\oplus B(2-N). \tag{SH} \] In particular its degree-zero and degree-one parts are zero for every \(N\ge5\). An extension with the two endpoint maps and their connections fixed therefore has at most one compatible degree-one connection, whenever one exists. This does not imply that there is only one compatible extension class.

For any selected free resolution and connection lifts in the obstruction lemma, define the finite-dimensional raw solution space \[ Z=\{(\phi,u):\phi\in\operatorname{Hom}_S(F_1,L)_0, \ u\in\operatorname{Hom}_S(F_0,L)_1, \ \phi d_2=0,\ \mathscr E_1\phi=ud_1\}. \] There is an exact sequence \[ 0\to\operatorname{Hom}_S(F_0,L)_0 \xrightarrow{\ \psi\mapsto(\psi d_1,\mathscr E_0\psi)\ } Z \longrightarrow\ker(\mathscr E:\operatorname{Ext}^1_0\to\operatorname{Ext}^1_1) \to0. \tag{BQ} \] Moreover the projection from \(Z\) to its \(\phi\)-coordinate is injective. For the minimal normalization cover, the left space in (BQ) vanishes for \(N=5,6\), first becomes nonzero at \(N=7\), and has dimension one at that first occurrence. These are weight consequences, not another rank computation.

Proof. Applying the two endpoint shifts to (HM) adds \(1-N\) to Hom's grading shift, giving (SH). Its lowest generator weight is \(N-2\ge3\), so both indicated pieces vanish. The fixed-extension connection torsor then gives uniqueness. If \((0,u)\in Z\), the map \(u\) kills \(\operatorname{im}d_1\), hence descends to \(\operatorname{Hom}(M,L)_1=0\); this proves injectivity of the projection.

The map in (BQ) lands in \(Z\) because the Hom differential commutes with \(\mathscr E\). Its kernel consists of maps \(\psi\) descending to \(\operatorname{Hom}(M,L)_0=0\), so it is injective. The obstruction criterion gives surjectivity on the right. If a raw pair has zero extension class, write \(\phi=\psi d_1\). Its equation implies \((u-\mathscr E_0\psi)d_1=0\); the degree-one Hom vanishing gives \(u=\mathscr E_0\psi\). This proves exactness in the middle.

Finally the minimal free cover has unique largest generator weight \(2N-4\), and the target begins at \(N+3\). A degree-zero free-cover Hom map can occur precisely when \(2N-4\ge N+3\), namely \(N\ge7\). The target has every nonnegative relative degree, and at \(N=7\) only the unique top generator of weight ten maps to the one-dimensional first target piece. Thus a future raw system must subtract the dimension of these presentation-change pairs before inferring the compatible class dimension. The quintic and six-root calculations needed no such subtraction because this space was zero there. \(\square\)

A nonflat control for the global argument. In the retained quintic normalization put \(B=k[z]\) and \(q=(u-z)^2\). The previous exact equations give \[ B\otimes_S D\cong B[u]/(q(u+2z),z^2q). \] As a graded \(B\)-module this is \[ B\oplus B(-1)\oplus(B/(z^2))(-2), \] using \(1,u,q\) as generators. The cubic first makes \(1,u,u^2\) a basis over \(B\); the remaining ideal is exactly the \(B\)-span of \(z^2q\), since \(uq=-2zq\). The jet quotient kills the nonzero torsion summand and sends \(u\) to \(z+\epsilon\). This refutes the stronger assertion that the entire pullback algebra is already the dual numbers globally. It does not affect (HM), because every map into the domain kills that torsion. No new computation was run, and no torsion summand of the higher Ext groups is discarded by this Hom argument.

Checks and remaining gap. The first jet exists polynomially on all collision loci; generic factorization is used only to identify its relative torsion kernel. The Hom formula then descends globally by the target-domain argument and by evaluations at \(1,s\), not by assuming flatness. The explicit quintic torsion is a falsifying control against that assumption. Both known cases' zero connection freedom now follow from (SH) uniformly. The nonzero free-cover cross map at six roots remains necessary for its chosen presentation; it is not a free parameter in the descended connection. The first nonzero degree-zero presentation-change space at seven roots is handled by (BQ), without running a new case.

Attempted direction and scope. Finite complete-intersection duality was considered as a way to replace Ext by a Koszul homology calculation. A naive connection transfer through the two-equation intermediate algebra is invalid: its defining ideal is not preserved by the actual drift, since the derivative of its second tail equation contains the next tail equation. A correct duality approach must retain the full invariant tail ideal and the dual density. No unverified connection-duality statement is used here. The direct jet quotient supplies the all-dimensional Hom result without that extra interface.

Verification gate. A fresh-context medium correctness reviewer passed the global factorization and trace, ordered and unordered generic scheme calculation, exact torsion kernel, Hom factorization, connection signs, shifts, raw-pair exactness, first presentation-change dimension and quintic nonflat control. It found no gap, needed mathematical fix or unused substantive hypothesis. The medium pre-proof reviewer required explicit exclusion of diagonal quadratics, the free permutation quotient and the target-domain argument rather than a flatness assumption; all are supplied. Both reviews distinguish uniqueness of connection on a fixed extension from uniqueness of extension classes. The review record retains their verdicts.

Assessment and next step. The connection-freedom term is now completely controlled in every dimension, and future raw kernels have an exact, known presentation-change quotient. The desired upper bound on compatible extension classes is still untouched by this alone: it concerns \(\operatorname{Ext}^1\), not Hom. On route cube-odd-characteristic, analyze that first Ext group through the full normalization tail complex with its correct induced connection, and determine whether a horizontal class vanishing on the distinguished lowest relation must be zero. Use the explicit jet Hom maps to handle boundaries rather than add root counts. The residual extension, higher savings and small-prime branch remain open parts of the original goal.

27 September 2026 — The actual upper extension cannot be a square-zero algebra thickening

Working all-dimensional characteristic-zero obstruction: compatible square-zero algebra extensions split. The module-extension rigidity conjecture remains open. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and outcome. Open statement 3 still needs the actual graded threshold ideals. The current sufficient reconstruction route asks for an upper bound on compatible first-Ext classes. A possible shortcut would replace those module extensions by algebra thickenings of the double-pair normalization and then use algebra-deformation methods. The theorem below rules this out uniformly: every square-zero algebra extension with the prescribed grading and endpoint connections has zero underlying module-extension class. The actual upper extension is nonzero, so it lies outside that category. This removes a tempting shortcut; it does not prove the desired Ext upper bound.

General statement. thm:cube-square-zero-extension-obstruction holds for every characteristic-zero field and every \(N\ge5\). The polynomial first-jet quotient controls the entire bilinear Leibniz defect, while the four exact normalization equations propagate under the actual root drift. No root count is added.

Compatible algebra thickenings have zero module-extension class

Theorem (thm:cube-square-zero-extension-obstruction; working proof). Let \(S=k[c_2,\ldots,c_N]\), \(\deg c_j=j\), in characteristic zero, \(N\ge5\). Write \(D=D_{22}\) and \(B=D_{32}\) for the centered polynomial normalization algebras \[ p(Z)=(Z^2-sZ+v)^2R_{22}(Z)=(Z-b)^3(Z-c)^2H(Z). \] Put \(M=D(-4)\), \(L=B(-N-3)\), with the actual endpoint connections \[ \nabla_M=\delta_D-\tfrac72s,\qquad \nabla_L=\delta_B-\tfrac72b-(N+\tfrac32)c, \] where every root has drift \(r'=-r^2-\kappa\), \(\kappa=2c_2/N\). Suppose a graded \(S\)-module extension \(0\to L\to E\to M\to0\) has a compatible degree-one connection. Suppose further that \(A=E(4)\) can be made a unital commutative graded \(S\)-algebra, with the given quotient map an algebra map \(A\to D\), and the given kernel \(I=B(1-N)\) a square-zero ideal. Then \(A\to D\) has a graded \(S\)-algebra section, so the original module extension splits. Consequently the actual non-split upper extension \(C/K_2\) admits no such algebra structure after this shift. No Leibniz rule for the initial connection on \(A\) is assumed. The exact density coefficients specify the actual cube application and its split control; the splitting argument below uses only that the endpoint operators differ from their drifts by scalar multiplication.

1. The bilinear Hom space has a uniform weight gap. The global first-jet theorem gives a surjection \[ B\otimes_S D\longrightarrow J=B[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2),\qquad s\longmapsto b+c+\epsilon, \] with \(\deg\epsilon=1\), which is an isomorphism over \(\operatorname{Frac}B\). Tensor two copies over \(B\). Right exactness gives a surjection \[ B\otimes_S D\otimes_S D\longrightarrow J\otimes_B J=B[\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2]/(\epsilon_1^2,\epsilon_2^2). \tag{BJ} \] It too is a generic isomorphism. Its kernel is exactly \(B\)-torsion: localization kills the kernel, and every torsion element maps to zero in the free target. Thus every map to \(B\) factors uniquely through (BJ). Adjunction and the four coefficient functionals give \[ \operatorname{Hom}_S(D\otimes_S D,B) \cong B\oplus B(1)^{\oplus2}\oplus B(2). \tag{BH} \] After shifting the target to \(I=B(1-N)\), its lowest generator weight is \(N-3\ge2\). Therefore \[ \operatorname{Hom}_S(D\otimes_S D,I)_1=0. \tag{BG} \] This uses the torsion-free quotient only for maps to a domain. It does not assert that either tensor algebra is flat, or discard torsion in an Ext group.

2. The algebra action on the ideal is forced. Since \(I^2=0\), multiplication makes \(I\) a unital \(D\)-module. As an \(S\)-module it is a shift of \(B\), and \(\operatorname{End}_S(B)=B\): the finite normalization is birational onto its coefficient image, so an endomorphism is generically multiplication by its value at one, and the equality extends in the domain \(B\). This is the same argument used in the endpoint-connection lemma. The action is consequently an \(S\)-algebra map \(\alpha:D\to B\). Its \(B\)-linear extension kills the torsion kernel of the jet quotient and sends \(\epsilon\) to zero, since \(B\) has no nonzero square-zero element. Thus \(\alpha=\operatorname{ev}\), where \(\operatorname{ev}(s)=b+c\), \(\operatorname{ev}(v)=bc\). In particular \[ ai=\operatorname{ev}(\bar a)i\quad(a\in A,\ i\in I), \] where \(\bar a\) is the image in \(D\). The jet theorem also proves \(\delta_B\operatorname{ev}=\operatorname{ev}\delta_D\).

3. Subtracting the density forces a derivation. Let \(\nabla_A\) be the shifted module connection and put \(g=\nabla_A(1)\). It maps to \(-7s/2\). The kernel starts in weight \(N-1\ge4\), so \(s\) has a unique homogeneous lift \(\widetilde s\in A_1\) and \(g=-7\widetilde s/2\). Set \[ \partial_A(a)=\nabla_A(a)-ga. \] This is a degree-one connection for the coefficient derivation, sends one to zero, and induces \(\delta_D\) on the quotient. On \(I\), the evaluation action gives exactly \[ \partial_I=\delta_B-(N-2)c. \tag{ID} \] The Leibniz defect \[ \mathcal B(a,a')=\partial_A(aa')-\partial_A(a)a'-a\partial_A(a') \] is \(S\)-bilinear of degree one. For example the coefficient-derivation terms cancel when an argument is multiplied by any \(r\in S\). Its image lies in \(I\), since the quotient operator is a derivation. If one argument is \(i\in I\), (ID) and the evaluation identity imply \[ \partial_I(\operatorname{ev}(\bar a)i) =\operatorname{ev}(\delta_D\bar a)i+ \operatorname{ev}(\bar a)\partial_I(i), \] so \(\mathcal B(a,i)=0\). The square-zero condition covers two ideal arguments as well. Hence \(\mathcal B\) descends to a degree-one map \(D\otimes_S D\to I\). By (BG) it is zero. Therefore \(\partial_A\) is an algebra derivation, obtained without assuming multiplicative compatibility of \(\nabla_A\).

4. The normalization relations propagate to a splitting. The unique homogeneous lifts \(\widetilde s\in A_1\), \(\widetilde v\in A_2\) satisfy \[ \partial_A\widetilde s=-\widetilde s^2+2\widetilde v-2\kappa, \qquad \partial_A\widetilde v=-\widetilde s(\widetilde v+\kappa). \tag{LD} \] Indeed these identities hold in the quotient, while their errors would have weights two and three, below the first weight of \(I\). Thus the algebra map \(P=S[s,v]\to A\) defined by these lifts intertwines the derivation \(V\) given by (LD) and the coefficient drift. Let \(q(T)=1-sT+vT^2\), \(p^{\rm rev}(T)=\sum_{j=0}^N(-1)^jc_jT^j\), and \(E_j=[T^j]p^{\rm rev}/q^2\). The exact factorization presentation is \[ D=P/(E_{N-3},E_{N-2},E_{N-1},E_N). \] Here \(T\) is a formal variable fixed by \(V\). Direct logarithmic differentiation of the root factors, using trace zero for \(p\), gives \[ Vp^{\rm rev}=-(1+\kappa T^2)(p^{\rm rev})'+N\kappa T p^{\rm rev}, \quad Vq=-(1+\kappa T^2)q'-sq+2\kappa Tq. \] Consequently \[ V\left(\frac{p^{\rm rev}}{q^2}\right) =-(1+\kappa T^2)\left(\frac{p^{\rm rev}}{q^2}\right)' +\bigl((N-4)\kappa T+2s\bigr)\frac{p^{\rm rev}}{q^2}, \] so, coefficientwise with \(E_{-1}=0\), \[ VE_j=-(j+1)E_{j+1}+2sE_j+(N-j-3)\kappa E_{j-1}. \tag{TD} \] All these are polynomial identities; one may check them after adjoining roots, and the coefficient ring embeds in that splitting ring. The images of \(E_{N-3},E_{N-2}\) in \(A\) vanish: they belong to the kernel but have weights below \(N-1\). Apply \(\partial_A\) to the second identity and use (TD) at \(j=N-2\). It forces \((N-1)E_{N-1}\) to have zero image. Then apply (TD) at \(j=N-1\), forcing the image of \(NE_N\) to vanish. Both integers are invertible. Thus \(P\to A\) kills all four defining relations and factors through \(D\). The composite \(D\to A\to D\) fixes \(S,s,v\), hence is the identity. This is the promised graded algebra section.

Application to the actual extension. The endpoint-connection lemma proves that \(0\to L\to C/K_2\to M\to0\) is compatible and non-split for every \(N\ge5\). More explicitly, \(K_2\) begins in weight at least \(2N-1\), whereas every minimal generator of \(C\) has weight at most \(2N-4\). Thus \(K_2\subset S_+C\), and the quotient has the same minimal generators as \(C\), hence as \(M\). A split module \(M\oplus L\) would have extra generators from \(L\). The theorem therefore excludes the stated square-zero algebra structure on its shift. \(\square\)

Falsifying controls and limits. The split algebra \(D\oplus I\), with multiplication \((d,i)(e,j)=(de,\operatorname{ev}(d)j+\operatorname{ev}(e)i)\), does meet the hypotheses. The map \((d,i)\mapsto(\delta_Dd,\delta_Bi-(N-2)ci)\) is a derivation; adding multiplication by \((-7s/2,0)\) gives exactly the prescribed endpoint connections. Thus the category is nonempty; the theorem excludes its nonzero underlying module classes. The earlier general nonrigidity family has neither these normalizations nor this weight gap, so no blanket splitting statement follows. The first-jet theorem's explicit quintic torsion also persists: (BJ) is a quotient by relative torsion, never an assertion of flatness. No numerical computation was needed.

No mathematical correction was needed; its clarification about the role of the exact density coefficients is included in the statement. The medium pre-proof review distinguished this new category obstruction from the existing Hom theorem and required an explicit evaluation action and vanishing of mixed ideal terms; both are proved above. Exact normalization equations, endpoint densities and non-splitting, the global first-jet proof and their recorded dependency links were re-read. The review verdicts are retained.

Assessment and next step. This is a refutation of a sufficient reconstruction shortcut, not progress on the numerical upper bound in the module-extension rigidity conjecture. The admissible algebra-deformation category misses the actual nonzero class, even though the endpoint modules are algebras. Return to the full module Ext calculation: retain its polynomial torsion and correct connection, and test whether a horizontal class vanishing on the distinguished lowest relation must vanish. 27 September 2026 — Collision regularity leaves one generic horizontal extension direction

Working all-dimensional characteristic-zero proof: the generic image of compatible degree-zero extension classes is one-dimensional; horizontal torsion remains unresolved. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and outcome. Open statement 3 still needs the actual graded flag ideals. On the sufficient extension-reconstruction route, the missing upper bound is one on the compatible first-Ext class space. This cycle proves that bound on its generic image for every dimension, using local factorization, pole regularity and the actual connection. The remaining part of the rigidity conjecture is now precisely the vanishing of degree-zero horizontal classes in the relative torsion of the first Ext module. No torsion is discarded in making this reduction.

General statement. thm:cube-generic-horizontal-extension proves the generic-image dimension one for every characteristic-zero \(N\ge5\), not only the previously computed five- and six-root cases. It gives explicit rational coordinates for that line and a global reason why arbitrary cross-ratio multiples do not extend polynomially.

The generic image is a single constant line

Theorem (thm:cube-generic-horizontal-extension; working proof). In the centered characteristic-zero setup \(N\ge5\), let \(S=k[c_2,\ldots,c_N]\), \(D=D_{22}\), \(B=D_{32}\), \(M=D(-4)\), \(L=B(-N-3)\), with the actual endpoint connections. Set \[ T=\operatorname{Ext}^1_S(M,L),\qquad H=\ker(\mathscr E:T_0\longrightarrow T_1),\qquad F=\operatorname{Frac}B. \] Then the image of \(H\) in \(T\otimes_B F\) has dimension exactly one over \(k\). Consequently the full compatible-class rigidity conjecture is equivalent to \[ \ker(\mathscr E:(T_{\rm tor})_0\longrightarrow(T_{\rm tor})_1)=0, \tag{HT} \] where \(T_{\rm tor}\) is the \(B\)-torsion submodule. In particular the theorem does not assert that all of \(T\) is torsion-free.

1. The four generic coordinates. Label the \(m=N-5\) simple residual roots, so \[ p(Z)=(Z-b)^3(Z-c)^2\prod_{i=1}^m(Z-h_i). \] The resulting ring is a finite free extension of the normalization coefficient ring after its linear trace relation; this is the usual polynomial ring over its symmetric-polynomial subring, with the sum relation eliminating the first symmetric coefficient. Thus this passage is faithfully flat. Adjoin the mean when convenient to remove the trace relation; all rational coordinates below are invariant under simultaneous translation and have the stated homogeneous degrees.

At the generic triple-double locus, factor the universal polynomial into its separated cubic and quadratic blocks and its simple factors. The multiplication map on factor coefficients has invertible differential by Chinese remainders. It therefore gives formal local coefficient coordinates. Write the two blocks as \[ f_3(Z)=(Z-b)^3+\alpha(Z-b)+\beta, \qquad f_2(Z)=(Z-c)^2+\gamma. \] The selected normalization component has a marked double root \(x=b+t\) in the cubic and the double root \(c\) in the quadratic. Hence \[ \alpha=-3t^2,\quad\beta=2t^3,\quad\gamma=0. \tag{LC} \] Other normalization components have no generic support here. Let \(e_0,e_1\) map to \(1,t\). A free presentation for the cusp part has relations \[ r_a=\beta e_0+\tfrac23\alpha e_1,\qquad r_A=\tfrac13\alpha^2e_0-\tfrac32\beta e_1. \tag{CP} \] Indeed, first take the free rank-two algebra with \(t^2=-\alpha/3\), and then impose \(\beta+(2/3)\alpha t=0\); its products by \(1,t\) give (CP), up to an invertible constant. The determinant is nonzero in the polynomial coefficient ring, so this is a free resolution of length one. Tensor it with the two-term resolution for \(\gamma=0\). After applying Hom to the target, which kills \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\), every differential is zero. Thus generic first Ext has four coordinates \[ a=\phi(r_a),\quad A=\phi(r_A),\quad u=\phi(\gamma e_0),\quad v=\phi(\gamma e_1). \tag{EC} \] For a degree-zero class their weights are, respectively, \[ 4-N,\quad5-N,\quad3-N,\quad4-N. \tag{EW} \] These coordinates are on extension classes, so presentation coboundaries have already been removed. They are rational functions on the labeled normalization. Formal factorization is used to calculate their values, not to replace the polynomial extension problem.

2. The actual connection in these coordinates. Use centered drift \(r'=-r^2-\kappa\), \(\kappa=2c_2/N\). The centered cubic coefficients satisfy \[ \delta\alpha=-4b\alpha-3\beta,\qquad \delta\beta=-6b\beta+\tfrac23\alpha^2, \qquad\delta\gamma=-4c\gamma. \] The block means have \(\delta b=-b^2-\kappa+2\alpha/3\), \(\delta c=-c^2-\kappa+\gamma\). On (LC), \(\delta t=-2bt+t^2\). Put \(g=-7(b+c)/2\). The source connection therefore has the following free lift: \[ \nabla e_0=g e_0-\tfrac72e_1,\qquad \nabla e_1=\tfrac56\alpha e_0+(g-2b)e_1. \] Differentiating the four relations gives \[ \begin{aligned} \nabla r_a&=(g-6b)r_a+\tfrac{11}{3}r_A,\\ \nabla r_A&=(g-8b)r_A-\tfrac{13}{4}\alpha r_a,\\ \nabla(\gamma e_0)&=(g-4c)\gamma e_0-\tfrac72\gamma e_1,\\ \nabla(\gamma e_1)&=(g-2b-4c)\gamma e_1+\tfrac56\alpha\gamma e_0. \end{aligned} \] Subtract these from the target connection, whose density differs from \(g\) by \(-(N-2)c\), and set \(\alpha=\beta=\gamma=0\). Horizontality is exactly \[ \begin{aligned} 0&=\delta A+(8b-(N-2)c)A,\\ 0&=\delta a+(6b-(N-2)c)a-\tfrac{11}{3}A,\\ 0&=\delta v+(2b+(6-N)c)v,\\ 0&=\delta u+(6-N)c\,u+\tfrac72v. \end{aligned} \tag{HE} \] This calculation uses the full local coefficient presentation. It does not descend the drift through the noninvariant two-equation intermediate normalization algebra.

3. Polynomial classes impose different pole restrictions on the two pairs. Work in the labeled, uncentered polynomial ring \(k[b,c,h_1,\ldots,h_m]\). The generic coordinates of a polynomial Ext class satisfy \[ \begin{array}{c|c} \text{coordinates}&\text{possible finite pole divisors}\\\hline a,A&b-c=0\text{ or }b-h_i=0\\ u,v&b-c=0\text{ or }c-h_i=0. \end{array} \tag{PR} \] No order bound on these poles is needed. Here is a local proof, including the coordinate choices. Away from all root differences, factor coordinates are étale, the displayed finite resolution is defined over the local ring, and its specialized Hom differentials are zero. Thus there are no poles at any other prime. It remains to check the root-difference divisors that (PR) excludes.

At a generic divisor \(c=h_i\), the cubic centered at \(b\) remains separated from the entire residual factor. Factor only those two blocks. The normalization component is the tensor product of the cusp normalization in that cubic and the normalization of one marked double root in the residual polynomial. In its Hom complex, the cusp differential is identically zero because \(\alpha=\beta=0\) in the target. The cusp-degree-one summand in first cohomology is consequently two copies of Hom from that residual normalization to the target. This Hom is the coefficient ring itself, by evaluation at the marked double root: the base-changed algebra maps onto the target by evaluation and is generically rank one, so its kernel is relative torsion, killed by every map into the target domain. Evaluating those Hom maps at one gives precisely \(a,A\) in (EC). They are therefore regular at \(c=h_i\). This argument needs no quadratic factor separated from \(h_i\), and so does not invert \(c-h_i\).

At a generic divisor \(b=h_i\), instead separate the quadratic centered at \(c\) from the entire residual polynomial. Its normalization resolution is the two-term complex for \(\gamma\); its Hom differential is zero. The quadratic-degree-one summand is Hom from the normalization of one marked double root in that residual polynomial to the target. This time the residual polynomial has a persistent triple root at \(b\). Its global first-jet quotient sends the marked root to \(b+\epsilon\) and the remaining cubic root to \(b-2\epsilon\): \[ (Z-b-\epsilon)^2(Z-b+2\epsilon)=(Z-b)^3\pmod{\epsilon^2}. \] It is onto the dual numbers and generically an isomorphism, since the equations for a marked double root at the triple root give exactly length two. Its kernel is relative torsion. The same domain argument as in the global jet theorem gives Hom equal to the free span of evaluation and the first-jet coefficient. Evaluating a map at \(1\) and at the marked root minus \(b\) gives exactly \(u,v\). Both are regular at \(b=h_i\). The subtraction of \(b\) is in the target ring and requires no lift of a separated cubic center through this collision.

At \(h_i=h_j\), keep the cubic and quadratic separated from the entire spectator factor, without splitting that factor. The selected normalization component has the same resolution (CP) tensored with the quadratic resolution, with smooth spectator coefficients. Any extra marked-pair components from a new spectator double root are separated by their pair coordinates, so they do not change this component. Hence all four coordinates are regular there. These local factorizations can be made in completed local rings; invertibility of the factor resultants and faithful flatness of completion detect the same height-one pole orders in the rational coordinates. The coordinates are rational because the finite jets of the formal inverse to factor multiplication are obtained by linear equations over the root function field. No arbitrary formal power-series coefficient or analytic choice enters (EC). This proves (PR).

4. Horizontality and grading turn the pole restrictions into a dimension bound. Adjoin the mean \(\mu\), put \(e_1=3b+2c+\sum h_i=N\mu\), and extend each centered rational coordinate by simultaneous translation invariance. For a homogeneous scalar coordinate of weight \(q\), uncentered root drift \(D=-\sum r^2\partial_r\) acts as its centered drift minus \(2q\mu\). Each scalar coefficient in (HE), expressed in uncentered roots and then decreased by \(e_1\), differs from its centered coefficient by \(2q\mu\). Therefore (HE) is equivalent to the uncentered system with \(\delta\) replaced by \(D\) and \(-e_1\) added to each scalar coefficient. This derives the mean correction; it is not an assumed connection transfer.

For a scalar homogeneous equation \(Df+\sum d_r r f=0\), translation invariance and homogeneity give the rational covariance law \[ f\left(\frac{ar+b_0}{cr+d}\right) =\prod_r(cr+d)^{-d_r}f(r),\qquad ad-b_0c=1. \tag{MC} \] All weights used here are integers. To verify (MC), translations follow from invariance, diagonal matrices from \(2\deg f=\sum d_r\), and the lower unipotent substitution \(r\mapsto r/(1+tr)\) follows by differentiating: both sides solve \(\partial_t f_t=-\sum d_r r_t f_t\) with the same initial value. This is an identity of rational functions in characteristic zero. These substitutions generate the stated transformations, so no integrability assumption on an abstract representation is needed.

Set \[ H_c=\prod_i(c-h_i),\qquad v_0=\frac1{(b-c)H_c},\qquad \xi_i=\frac{h_i-c}{h_i-b}. \] The product for \(m=0\) is one. Direct differentiation gives \(\delta v_0+(2b+(6-N)c)v_0=0\) in centered coordinates. For the four homogeneous scalar equations, the weights \((d_b,d_c,d_{h_i})\) in (MC) are \[ \begin{array}{c|ccc} A&5&-m-5&-1\\ a\ (A=0)&3&-m-5&-1\\ v&-1&-m-1&-1\\ u\ (v=0)&-3&-m-1&-1. \end{array} \] Thus the ratios \[ P_A=\frac{A}{(b-c)v_0},\quad P_a=\frac{a}{v_0},\quad P_v=\frac{v}{v_0},\quad P_u=\frac{(b-c)u}{v_0} \tag{RP} \] are translation invariant, of degree zero, and rational functions of the \(\xi_i\). The transformations fixing \(b,c\) scale every \(\xi_i\) by the same factor. Formula (MC) says their respective homogeneous degrees in the \(\xi_i\) are \(-5,-4,0,1\), when the relevant equation is homogeneous.

For completeness the allowed rational functions in this step are constrained by both finite poles and infinity. Fix \(b=1,c=0\), so \(h_i=\xi_i/(\xi_i-1)\). By (PR), denominators of (RP) can involve only coordinate factors \(\xi_i\) or \(\xi_i-1\); there are no spectator-difference or other finite factors. Homogeneity under simultaneous scaling excludes every \(\xi_i-1\) pole: its infinitely many distinct scaled divisors could not all be pole divisors of a rational function. Hence these functions are Laurent polynomials. For \(P_A,P_a\), regularity at \(c=h_i\), and the additional factor \(H_c\) in their numerators, forbids negative exponents of every \(\xi_i\). Their negative total degrees force them to vanish. First this gives \(A=0\), and then \(a=0\).

For \(P_v\), regularity at \(b=h_i\) means regularity at each \(\xi_i=\infty\); \(v_0\) is a unit along that divisor. Thus every Laurent exponent is nonpositive. Total degree zero forces \(P_v\) to be a constant \(\lambda\in k\). The particular solution for the remaining equation is \[ u_0=\frac{7v_0}{2(b-c)}, \] since applying its homogeneous scalar operator to \(v_0/(b-c)\) gives \(-v_0\). The difference \(u-\lambda u_0\) has the same allowed poles as \(u\) and solves the homogeneous equation. Its \(P_u\) has only nonpositive Laurent exponents by the same infinity regularity, but total degree one, so it vanishes. For \(m=0\), all the rational functions in the empty list \(\xi\) are constants, and the same degree arguments apply. We have proved that every generic image lies on the constant line \[ (a,A,u,v)=\lambda\left(0,0, \frac7{2(b-c)^2H_c},\frac1{(b-c)H_c}\right),\qquad\lambda\in k. \tag{GL} \] The argument works after algebraic closure as well. The displayed line and coordinates are defined over \(k\), so descent gives the same bound over every characteristic-zero field. The pole argument is essential: arbitrary rational cross-ratio functions would otherwise give many solutions of the same scalar equations.

5. Nonzero image and the exact remaining obstruction. The actual generic formal extension is non-split. Its nonzero kernel line lies in \(\mathfrak mC\); in a split extension with that kernel annihilated by \(\mathfrak m\), its intersection with \(\mathfrak mC\) would be zero. The deeper kernel \(K_2\) has smaller support dimension, so disappears here. The actual compatible upper extension consequently has a nonzero generic image. This proves equality one, not only an upper bound.

The kernel of \(T\to T\otimes_B F\) is precisely \(T_{\rm tor}\). It is connection-stable: if \(rx=0\), then \(r^2\mathscr E x=0\) by the Leibniz rule. Restricting to horizontal degree-zero classes and using (GL) gives \[ 0\longrightarrow\ker(\mathscr E:(T_{\rm tor})_0\to(T_{\rm tor})_1) \longrightarrow H\longrightarrow k\longrightarrow0. \] The last map is onto because the actual class has nonzero image. This proves (HT) and identifies exactly what generic localization has left unresolved. \(\square\)

Checks and scope. The four local cochain coordinates have weights obtained directly from relations of weights three, four, two and three with endpoint shift \(1-N\). Their connection was differentiated before specialization. The two types of forbidden poles use different separated-factor presentations; neither presumes flatness of the normalization pullback. Constant degree-zero Laurent functions need individual regularity at infinity: ratios such as \(\xi_1/\xi_2\) would falsify the claim if that condition were omitted. The actual nonzero generic class supplies an independent existence control. No new root-count computation was run. Torsion may still occur on deeper collisions and cannot be deleted from the final rigidity question.

That same reviewer performed the consolidated correctness pass on the stable draft; no second reviewer was spawned. The review verdict is retained.

The remaining necessary implication for this reconstruction shortcut is (HT), rather than another root-count rank computation or an assumption that the Ext module is torsion-free. Analyze its torsion connection at deeper collisions and the vertex, beginning with the first possible support strata and the degree-zero range. 27 September 2026 — Extension torsion is detected by four divisor types

Working all-dimensional characteristic-zero proof: the remaining first-Ext torsion is a principal-parts dual, detected in codimension one. Horizontal vanishing remains open. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and outcome. The generic-image theorem reduced upper-extension rigidity to degree-zero horizontal torsion. This cycle determines what that torsion is and where it can be detected. It is the principal-parts dual of the relative torsion in the normalization pullback. After labeling spectator roots, four collision-divisor types suffice. A class confined to their deeper intersections cannot survive; in particular there is no independent vertex-supported contribution to this first-Ext torsion when \(N\ge6\). This concerns the Ext obstruction, not the essential residual vertex module of the original defect.

General statement. thm:cube-extension-torsion-principal-parts gives the full connection-compatible torsion identification and codimension-one detection for every characteristic-zero \(N\ge5\). It replaces an unspecified search over deeper supports by four geometric divisor types; it does not prove horizontal vanishing on those divisors.

The principal-parts description and divisor detection

Theorem (thm:cube-extension-torsion-principal-parts; working proof). In the actual centered normalization setup, let \(D=D_{22}\), \(B=D_{32}\), \(Q=\operatorname{Frac}B\), and put \[ A=B\otimes_S D,\quad U=A_{\rm tor},\qquad T=\operatorname{Ext}^1_S(D(-4),B(-N-3)). \] There are canonical graded isomorphisms \[ T_{\rm tor}\cong\operatorname{Ext}^1_B(A,B(1-N)) \cong\operatorname{Ext}^1_B(U,B(1-N)) \cong\operatorname{Hom}_B(U,(Q/B)(1-N)). \tag{PP} \] They intertwine the actual induced degree-one connections. On \(A\), use \[ \nabla_A(f\otimes d)=\delta_B(f)\otimes d+f\otimes(\delta_Dd-7sd/2); \] on the shifted target \(B(1-N)\) and on \((Q/B)(1-N)\), use \(\delta_B-7b/2-(N+3/2)c\). The Hom connection in (PP) is their commutator. The source torsion \(U\) is stable.

Moreover localization induces an injection \[ T_{\rm tor}\longrightarrow \prod_{\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak p=1}(T_{\rm tor})_{\mathfrak p}. \tag{CD} \] After the finite free extension labeling the \(m=N-5\) residual roots, the only necessary divisors are \[ b=c,\qquad b=h_i,\qquad c=h_i,\qquad h_i=h_j. \tag{DV} \] Their generic root patterns are respectively \[ (5,1^m),\quad(4,2,1^{m-1}),\quad (3,3,1^{m-1}),\quad(3,2,2,1^{m-2}); \] terms with unavailable spectators are omitted. In particular a nonzero element of \(T_{\rm tor}\) cannot be supported only in codimension at least two in \(\operatorname{Spec}B\). For \(N=5\), the vertex is itself the first divisor; for \(N\ge6\), it has codimension at least two and cannot support an independent such element.

1. Torsion in first cohomology comes from the zeroth tensor homology. Apply the endpoint shifts first, so the target is \(G=B(1-N)\) and the source is \(D\). Choose a finite graded free \(S\)-resolution \(F_\bullet\to D\), and set \(P_\bullet=B\otimes_S F_\bullet\). Its terms are free over \(B\), its zeroth homology is \(A\), and \[ T=H^1\operatorname{Hom}_B(P_\bullet,G). \] Write \(Z=\ker(d_1:P_1\to P_0)\) and \(R=\operatorname{im}d_1\). A cocycle \(\phi:P_1\to G\) represents a torsion cohomology class exactly when it becomes a coboundary over \(Q\). Such a cocycle kills \(Z\): after passing to \(Q\) it has the form \(\psi d_1\), so its value on \(Z\) is zero in \(G\otimes_BQ\), and the injection \(G\hookrightarrow G\otimes_BQ\) makes it zero already. It therefore factors through a map \(R\to G\).

Conversely every map \(R\to G\) yields a cocycle, because \(d_1d_2=0\). The resulting cohomology subgroup is \[ \operatorname{Hom}_B(R,G)/ \operatorname{im}\operatorname{Hom}_B(P_0,G) =\operatorname{Ext}^1_B(A,G), \] using \(0\to R\to P_0\to A\to0\) and freeness of \(P_0\). The inclusion into \(T\) is injective, since its coboundaries are precisely the displayed restrictions. This whole subgroup is torsion: after localization \(A\otimes_BQ\) is a vector space, so its first Ext over \(Q\) is zero. Localization commutes with these finite free complexes. Thus it is exactly \(T_{\rm tor}\), proving the first isomorphism in (PP). No assertion that tensoring the original resolution remains exact was made; the possibly nonzero higher tensor homology is retained in the full complex.

2. The free jet quotient removes the torsion-free part from this Ext. The global jet theorem gives the exact sequence \[ 0\to U\to A\to J=B[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)\to0, \qquad\deg\epsilon=1, \] with \(J\) free of rank two over \(B\). The Ext sequence yields an isomorphism \(\operatorname{Ext}^1_B(A,G)\to\operatorname{Ext}^1_B(U,G)\), since both \(\operatorname{Ext}^1_B(J,G)\) and \(\operatorname{Ext}^2_B(J,G)\) vanish. A module splitting exists, but no compatible connection splitting is assumed or needed.

The sequence \(0\to G\to Q(1-N)\to(Q/B)(1-N)\to0\) gives the third isomorphism in (PP). Indeed \(\operatorname{Hom}_B(U,Q)=0\), because \(U\) is torsion, and \(\operatorname{Ext}^1_B(U,Q)=0\): a resolution by finite free terms localizes to an exact resolution of zero over \(Q\). This proves the connecting-map isomorphism without requiring an injectivity assertion about arbitrary fraction-field modules. The grading on these Hom spaces is canonical even though the full fraction field is not graded: the finite graded torsion module \(U\) has a common nonzero homogeneous annihilator \(a\), so every map to \(Q/B\) lands in \(a^{-1}B/B\), which has its natural grading. Equivalently one may use the graded localization at nonzero homogeneous elements. All maps above preserve these degrees.

3. Compatibility with the actual connections. The formula for \(\nabla_A\) is balanced over \(S\), because both endpoint drifts restrict to the coefficient derivation. If \(ru=0\), then \(r^2\nabla_Au=0\), so \(U\) is stable. The source connection therefore descends to \(J\), though its splitting above need not respect it. The target connection extends by the quotient rule to \(Q(1-N)\) and preserves \(G\), hence descends to the principal-parts quotient.

Lift the source connection to \(F_\bullet\) as in the Ext-obstruction lemma and tensor the lifts with the coefficient drift on \(B\). The maps \(d_i\), the stable relation module \(R\) and all restrictions commute with the resulting connections. Thus factoring a cocycle through \(R\), and taking its class modulo restrictions from \(P_0\), commutes with the Hom commutator. This proves compatibility of the first map in (PP). The next two maps are induced by the stable short exact sequences just displayed; their Ext connecting maps commute with the same cochain commutator. Hence every isomorphism in (PP) is connection-compatible. This argument uses the canonical Ext operator, not a selected scalar connection on a presentation.

4. Codimension-one principal parts detect every element. Since \(B\) is a polynomial ring, it is a unique factorization domain and \[ B=\bigcap_{\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak p=1}B_{\mathfrak p} \quad\text{inside }Q. \] A fraction belonging to all those local rings has no uncancelled irreducible factor in its denominator, proving the equality directly. Consequently \[ Q/B\hookrightarrow\prod_{\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak p=1}Q/B_{\mathfrak p}. \] A map \(U\to Q/B\) is zero if each of its localizations is zero: every value then belongs to every \(B_{\mathfrak p}\), and hence is zero modulo \(B\). Localization of Hom here agrees with the corresponding local Hom since \(U\) is finitely presented. This proves (CD) via (PP). Only the finitely many height-one primes in the support of \(U\) matter. In particular, if a purported element has support of codimension at least two, all those localizations vanish and so does the element itself.

5. Four divisor types suffice. The labeled normalization ring \[ B'=k[b,c,h_1,\ldots,h_m]/(3b+2c+\sum_i h_i) \] is polynomial after eliminating one linear variable, and finite free over \(B\), by the symmetric-polynomial basis in the spectator variables. For \(m=0\) this is the usual quintic line. Flat base change commutes with the finite free Hom complex, its torsion kernel and the jet quotient: the latter has a free quotient, and its kernel becomes exactly the torsion after this extension. Thus the preceding proof applies equally over \(B'\), and faithful flatness detects zero classes over \(B\).

Invert all distinct-root differences in \(B'\). At every geometric point of this open set, the only monic quadratic \(Q_2\) whose square divides the polynomial is the selected pair of the triple and double roots. The off-diagonal equations \(p(x)=p'(x)=p(y)=p'(y)=0\) give exactly a first jet at the triple root and a reduced point at the double root. Thus every fibre of \(A\to J\) has source and target dimension two. The quotient \(J\) is free, so this sequence splits as modules and the kernel fibres are zero. Nakayama gives \(U=0\) on this open set. Its possible height-one support is therefore among the factors of those differences, namely (DV). This is only a support containment; the theorem does not assert that each divisor actually contributes torsion in every available dimension. Combining this with (CD) proves the stated detection and pattern list. \(\square\)

Controls and remaining limitation. In the quintic nonflat control, \(A\cong B\oplus B(-1)\oplus(B/(z^2))(-2)\), so \(U=(B/(z^2))(-2)\). With \(G=B(-4)\), its two-term resolution gives \(\operatorname{Ext}^1_B(U,G)\cong B/(z^2)\) with generator in weight zero. Thus the theorem does not silently force torsion to vanish; it detects a real degree-zero obstruction space. Its horizontality still depends on the actual connection. For \(N\ge6\), codimension-one detection excludes an independent first-Ext torsion element supported only at the vertex, but does not remove the vertex layer of \(C\), which is a different module and remains essential to the threshold problem.

No substantive gap or unused hypothesis remained. Its optional grading clarification using a common homogeneous annihilator is included above. The review verdict is retained. The proof includes the low-cohomology argument so that a universal-coefficient shortcut does not conceal higher tensor homology.

Assessment and next step. Upper-extension rigidity is still open, but any missing horizontal torsion class must now be visible at one of four generic collision-divisor types. Analyze the induced principal-parts connection there with the global polynomial compatibility retained; vanishing on every divisor would finish the upper-extension rigidity argument by (CD). A nonzero rational horizontal vector at a divisor need not extend to a global class. Deeper intersections can impose compatibility on divisor data, but cannot carry a separate invisible class. The residual extension and final flag ideals remain outside this upper-layer conclusion.

27 September 2026 — Explicit divisor modules exclude the extra marked-pair channels

Working all-dimensional characteristic-zero proof: four local torsion models and their connections; half-integral weights exclude the extra-pair horizontal components. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and outcome. The principal-parts theorem detects every remaining upper-extension obstruction at four collision-divisor types. This cycle computes their actual relative torsion modules and induced Ext connections. It excludes the entire triple-double-double divisor and the internal-pair component on the quadruple-double divisor. The main components of the quintuple, quadruple-double and triple-triple divisors remain; global polynomial compatibility is still required.

General statement. thm:cube-divisor-torsion-models gives the four generic divisor models for all characteristic-zero \(N\ge5\), with all available simple spectators. cor:cube-half-integral-torsion-exclusion rules out degree-zero rational horizontal classes in the extra marked-pair components uniformly. These are local formulas for whole collision types, not additional root-count rank tests.

The torsion modules and their induced connections

Theorem (thm:cube-divisor-torsion-models; working proof). Put \(A=B'\otimes_S D_{22}\), \(U=A_{\rm tor}\), where \(B'\) is the labeled-root normalization ring from the principal-parts theorem. At the generic point of any divisor below, complete its local discrete valuation ring to \(R\). Its fraction and residue fields retain all other generic root parameters. Let \(\nabla_U\) be the actual source connection, induced by root drift and density \(-7s/2\). The target is \(G=R(1-N)\), with density \[ g_L=-\tfrac72b-(N+\tfrac32)c. \] The following lists give every torsion summand of \(A\) over \(R\). Brackets record homogeneous generator weights; they are not lower bounds after localization.

Generic patternLocal parameter and torsion module
\((5,1^{N-5})\)\(a=(3b+2c)/5,\ z=(c-b)/5;\ U=R/(z^2)[2]\).
\((4,2,1^{N-6})\)\(d=h-b;\ U_{bc}=R/(d^2)[2]\), and \(U_{bb}=R/(d^3)[0]\).
\((3,3,1^{N-6})\)\(d=h-c;\ U=R/(d^2)[1]\oplus R/(d^2)[2]\).
\((3,2,2,1^{N-7})\)\(a=(h_i+h_j)/2,\ e=(h_i-h_j)/2;\ U_{ba}=R/(e^2)[0]\oplus R/(e^2)[1]\), and \(U_{ca}=R/(e^2)[0]\).

Subscripts identify the selected pair of clusters. The already-present pair \(b,c\) is the free jet component in the last row and contributes no torsion there. Components requiring unavailable spectators are omitted. In particular the lengths of \(U\) over these DVRs are respectively \(2,5,4,6\).

Write \(\mathscr E\) for the connection on \(\operatorname{Ext}^1_R(U,G)\). If \(\phi_i\) is the cochain coordinate dual to a generator \(q_i\) annihilated by \(r^a\), its degree for a degree-zero Ext class is \(\deg q_i+a+1-N\). In the order of the table, the exact operators are: \[ \begin{array}{ll} (5):&\mathscr E\phi=\delta\phi+ [(10-N)a+(\tfrac32-3N)z]\phi;\\[2pt] (4,2),bc:&\mathscr E\phi=\delta\phi+ [8b-(N-2)c+\tfrac{49}{8}d]\phi;\\ (4,2),bb:&\mathscr E\phi=\delta\phi+ [\tfrac{19}{2}b-(N+\tfrac32)c+\tfrac{19}{4}d]\phi;\\[2pt] (3,3):&\mathscr E\phi_0=\delta\phi_0+[(8-N)c+5d]\phi_0+\tfrac72\phi_1,\\ &\mathscr E\phi_1=\delta\phi_1+[2b+(8-N)c+5d]\phi_1;\\[2pt] (3,2,2),ba:&\mathscr E\phi_0=\delta\phi_0+ [\tfrac{15}{2}a-(N+\tfrac32)c]\phi_0+\tfrac72\phi_1,\\ &\mathscr E\phi_1=\delta\phi_1+ [2b+\tfrac{15}{2}a-(N+\tfrac32)c]\phi_1;\\ (3,2,2),ca:&\mathscr E\phi=\delta\phi+ [-\tfrac72b-(N-2)c+\tfrac{15}{2}a]\phi. \end{array} \tag{DC} \] All formulas are modulo the displayed annihilator power. The coefficient derivation is the actual root drift, so \(\kappa=2c_2/N\) includes the spectators and the transverse parameter. No connection is transported from an unfiltered formal module identification.

Separating pair components. Factor the polynomial into its separated cluster blocks by formal coefficient coordinates, as in the generic Ext proof. A selected quadratic square factor either takes one double root from each of two blocks, or lies wholly within a block of multiplicity at least four. These possibilities are distinct points of the finite normalization fibre, hence give idempotent components over the complete local base. A derivation kills idempotents, so both root drift and the source connection preserve these components. Spectators outside the displayed clusters have no repeated roots and supply no other choices. This proves that enumerating the indicated pair components is exhaustive.

The quintuple component. The selected five-root factor has roots \(a-2z\) three times and \(a+3z\) twice. Translate it by \(a\). If \(u\) is the centered sum of the two marked roots, the exact quintic pullback control gives \[ R[u]/\bigl((u-z)^2(u+2z),\ z^2(u-z)^2\bigr). \] Its free quotient is the jet algebra; its torsion is generated by \(q=(u-z)^2\), with \(z^2q=0\) and \(uq=-2zq\). This is the first row. The source pair sum acts on \(q\) as \(s=2a-2z\). Direct root differentiation gives \[ \delta z=-(2a+z)z,\qquad \delta q=(-4a-4z)q,\qquad \nabla_Uq=(-11a+3z)q. \tag{F5} \] For example, with \(t=u-z\), the specialized pair equations give \(tq=-3zq\) and \(\delta t=-2(a-2z)t+2t^2\); these imply the formula for \(\delta q\). The spectators affect \(\kappa\), which cancels in these root differences. Thus the connection calculation is valid for every \(N\), not only for an isolated quintic.

The quadruple-double components. Write the quartic block as \((Z-b)^3(Z-b-d)\). For the cross pair with the unchanged double root at \(c\), put \(t=x-b\) for the marked root in the quartic. The conditions that it be a double root are \[ t^3(t-d)=0,\qquad t^2(4t-3d)=0. \] They are equivalent to \(t^3=(3/4)dt^2\) and \(d^2t^2=0\). Hence this component is free on \(1,t\) plus \(R/(d^2)q\), \(q=t^2\). Since \(\delta t=-2bt-t^2\), its source connection is \[ \nabla_Uq= [-\tfrac{15}{2}b-\tfrac72c-\tfrac{33}{8}d]q, \qquad\delta d=-(2b+d)d. \tag{F42a} \] Indeed \(tq=(3/4)dq\), so \(\delta q=(-4b-3d/2)q\) and \(s q=(b+c+3d/4)q\).

For the internal pair in that quartic, set \(a=b+d/4\). The centered quartic is \[ (Z+d/4)^3(Z-3d/4) =Z^4-\tfrac38d^2Z^2-\tfrac18d^3Z-\tfrac3{256}d^4. \] It is the square of a monic quadratic exactly when that quadratic has zero centered sum, constant term \(-3d^2/16\), and \(d^3=0\); the constant-coefficient equation then follows from \(d^3=0\). Thus the entire component is \(R/(d^3)\), generated by one. Its pair sum is \(2a\), giving \[ \nabla_U1=(-7b-\tfrac74d)1. \tag{F42b} \] The two components have different pair coordinates even at the divisor, since \(b\ne c\), so their torsion modules sum directly.

The triple-triple component. Keep the triple root at \(b\), and write the other cubic block as \((Z-c)^2(Z-c-d)\). Let \(t=x-b\), \(u=y-c\). The double-root incidence equations reduce to \[ t^2=0,\qquad u^2=\tfrac23du,\qquad d^2u=0. \] Thus the free jet quotient is spanned by \(1,t\), and torsion is freely spanned over \(R/(d^2)\) by \(q_0=u,q_1=tu\). Root differentiation and the source density give \[ \begin{aligned} \nabla_Uq_0&=(-\tfrac72b-\tfrac{11}{2}c-3d)q_0-\tfrac72q_1,\\ \nabla_Uq_1&=(-\tfrac{11}{2}b-\tfrac{11}{2}c-3d)q_1, \qquad\delta d=-(2c+d)d. \end{aligned} \tag{F33} \] Here \(\delta t=-2bt\), \(\delta u=(-2c-2d/3)u\), and multiplication by the pair sum is multiplication by \(b+c+t+u\). These formulas give every displayed coefficient, including the off-diagonal term.

The triple-double-double components. The colliding spectators form \((Z-a)^2-e^2\). Selecting its double root imposes \(e^2=0\) and gives marked root \(a\). Pairing it with the triple root at \(b\) gives \((R/(e^2))[t]/(t^2)\), with source connection \[ \nabla_U1=-\tfrac72(b+a)1-\tfrac72t,\qquad \nabla_Ut=[-\tfrac72(b+a)-2b]t. \tag{F322a} \] Pairing it with the double root at \(c\) gives \(R/(e^2)\), with source density \(-7(c+a)/2\). The original pair \(b,c\) remains exactly the free jet algebra. Also \(\delta e=-2ae\). These prove the last row and exhaust the components.

Passing to the principal-parts connection. For a free list of torsion generators \(q_i\) killed by a common power \(r^a\), resolve their module by multiplication by \(r^a\). If \(\nabla_Uq_i=\sum_j H_{ji}q_j\), lift that matrix to the free generators. The relation generators \(r^aq_i\) have matrix \(H+a\delta(r)/r\). Thus a cochain vector has operator \[ \mathscr E\phi=\delta\phi+g_L\phi-\phi H -a\frac{\delta r}{r}\phi. \tag{DP} \] Changing lifts changes the result only by the annihilator ideal. Substitution of (F5), (F42a), (F42b), (F33), (F322a) and the scalar \(ca\) density gives exactly (DC). Each generator of weight \(w\) has relation weight \(w+a\); mapping it into \(R(1-N)\) gives the degree formula in the statement. This also agrees with the connection-compatible principal-parts identification. \(\square\)

Half-integral weights exclude every extra-pair component

Corollary (cor:cube-half-integral-torsion-exclusion; working proof). No degree-zero homogeneous horizontal class has a nonzero component in \(U_{bb}\)'s Ext summand on a quadruple-double divisor, or in either summand on a triple-double-double divisor. In particular the latter divisor type contributes zero to any globally compatible class. The components left to test are the quintuple, cross-pair quadruple-double and triple-triple ones.

A rational residue test. Suppose a nonzero rational function of independent distinct root variables is translation invariant, homogeneous of weight \(q\), and solves \[ -\sum r^2\partial_r f+\sum d_r r f=0, \qquad\sum d_r=2q. \] Substitute \(r\mapsto r/(1+tr)\). Its rational value \(f_t\) satisfies \[ \frac{\partial_t f_t}{f_t}=-\sum_r\frac{d_r r}{1+tr}. \] At \(t=-1/r\), the right side has residue \(-d_r\). Every logarithmic derivative of a nonzero rational function has integral residues, its zero and pole orders. Hence every \(d_r\) must be an integer. This proves the needed obstruction without interpreting nonintegral powers as rational group actions.

Apply this to the leading nonzero transverse layer of a putative horizontal vector in (DC). For layer \(r^j\), the scalar density gains \(j\delta r/r\); after restricting to the divisor this subtracts an integer multiple of twice its cluster root. Its cochain coefficient has the corresponding homogeneous degree lower by \(j\). Passing from centered roots to independent uncentered roots adds \(-e_1\) to the scalar density, exactly as in the mean-correction argument: the sum of the scalar coefficients minus \(N\) is twice that cochain degree. In the reduced divisor, \(e_1\) uses the new cluster multiplicities. Consequently the indicated half-integral weights persist in every transverse layer.

For \((4,2)\)'s internal-pair component, the scalar density on the divisor is \((19/2)b-(N+3/2)c\). Since \(e_1=4b+2c+\sum h_i\), the corrected weights at \(b,c\) are \[ \tfrac{11}{2}-2j,\qquad -N-\tfrac72. \] They are never integers. Thus the rational residue test excludes every possible leading layer, and the entire horizontal component is zero.

For \((3,2,2)\), use \(e_1=3b+2c+2a+\sum h_i\). The \(ba\) block is triangular. Its \(\phi_1\) equation has weights at \(c,a\) equal to \(-N-7/2\) and \(11/2-2j\), respectively. Thus \(\phi_1\) has no nonzero leading layer and is zero. The remaining scalar \(\phi_0\) equation has those same half-integral weights, so it too is zero. In the \(ca\) block the weights at \(b,a\) are \(-13/2\) and \(11/2-2j\), giving the same conclusion. The finite annihilator powers make leading-layer induction exhaustive. These are rational-function obstructions, so they hold before any global regularity restriction is imposed. They therefore exclude the images of all global degree-zero horizontal classes as well. \(\square\)

Controls and unresolved components. The fibre dimensions supplied by the tables are three at a quintuple point, four at quadruple-double and triple-triple points, and five at a triple-double-double point. These match the selected-pair incidence lengths: an off-diagonal pair contributes the product of the root multiplicities minus one in each factor, and the internal quadruple pair contributes one. At \(N=5\), \(a=0\), so (DC) recovers the torsion connection \(\delta\phi-(27/2)z\phi\) on \(k[z]/(z^2)\), whose weight-zero generator is not horizontal. The half-integral test does not apply to the three remaining components: their corrected weights are integral. This is a boundary of the test, not evidence of their horizontal vanishing. No numerical calculation was run.

A linear-weight denominator and an exact polynomial Hom problem

Theorem (thm:cube-horizontal-torsion-denominator; working proof). Let \(D=D_{22}\), \(B=D_{32}\), \(A=B\otimes_S D\), \(U=A_{\rm tor}\), and \(T=\operatorname{Ext}^1_S(D(-4),B(-N-3))\), with their actual connections. Write \[ p(Z)=(Z-b)^3(Z-c)^2H(Z),\quad \deg H=N-5, \qquad F=(b-c)^2H(b)^2H(c)^2. \tag{GD} \] Then \(F\) has weight \(4N-18\) and annihilates every degree-zero horizontal element of \(T_{\rm tor}\). This need not annihilate all of \(T_{\rm tor}\), or all of \(U\). There is a natural identification \[ \ker(\mathscr E:(T_{\rm tor})_0\to(T_{\rm tor})_1) \cong \ker\left(\mathscr E_F: \operatorname{Hom}_B\bigl(U,(B/(F))(3N-17)\bigr)_0 \longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}_B\bigl(U,(B/(F))(3N-17)\bigr)_1\right). \tag{GH} \] Here the source carries \(\nabla_A|_U\), while the target carries the induced derivation plus scalar density \[ g_F=(2N-\tfrac{47}{2})b+(N-\tfrac{35}{2})c, \tag{FD} \] and \(\mathscr E_F\) is their Hom commutator. The source \(U\) has a homogeneous \(B\)-generating family of at most \(\binom{N-2}{2}-2\) elements, with weights between two and \(2N-8\). Consequently the numerator images of all those generators have weights at most \(5N-25\). These are finite homogeneous polynomial spaces modulo \(F\); all source relations and the horizontal equation in (GH) must still be imposed.

Proof of the common denominator. Pass to the finite free extension labeling the roots \(h_i\) of \(H\). The codimension-one detection theorem identifies every torsion class with a principal-parts map and detects it at the four possible collision-divisor types. By the local models, the remaining main components are annihilated by the square of their divisor parameter. The half-integral theorem makes a degree-zero horizontal class zero on the internal quadruple-pair component, which required a cube, and on the entire triple-double-double type. Thus multiplying such a class by \[ (b-c)^2\prod_i(b-h_i)^2(c-h_i)^2 \] kills every height-one localization. Codimension-one detection kills the class globally. This product is exactly (GD), invariant under spectator permutations, so it belongs to \(B\). Faithful flatness descends its annihilation to \(B\). Its weight is \(2+4(N-5)=4N-18\). This argument uses the already-proved exclusions; replacing a cube by a square for arbitrary torsion would be unjustified.

Clearing denominators preserves the global maps and connection. Put \(Q=\operatorname{Frac}B\). The kernel of multiplication by \(F\) on \(Q/B\) is exactly \[ F^{-1}B/B\cong (B/(F))(\deg F),\qquad \overline p\longmapsto p/F+B. \] Hence a principal-parts map annihilated by \(F\) is exactly a \(B\)-linear map into this polynomial quotient. Applying the target shift \(1-N\) in the principal-parts theorem gives \(3N-17\), as in (GH). Conversely every such polynomial Hom map gives a global principal-parts map. If it is horizontal it is a horizontal torsion class, so this is an equality of kernels, not only a necessary condition on their dimensions.

The derivation preserves \((F)\), because each root difference is a Darboux factor. Since \(\delta(r-r')=-(r+r')(r-r')\), with \(m=N-5\) and \(3b+2c+\sum h_i=0\), \[ \frac{\delta F}{F} =-2(m+1)(b+c)-4\sum h_i =(20-2N)b+(16-2N)c. \] Differentiating \(p/F\) subtracts this polynomial from the target density \(g_L=-7b/2-(N+3/2)c\). The result is (FD). Thus division by \(F\) intertwines the exact target connections, and (GH) follows from the connection-compatible principal-parts theorem.

A bounded source for the numerators. Let \(t=s-b-c\). The jet map \(A\to B[\epsilon]/\epsilon^2\) has \(t\mapsto\epsilon\). It has a homogeneous \(B\)-linear section sending \(1,\epsilon\) to \(1,t\); this is not asserted to be an algebra or connection section. Writing the jet coefficients as \(\operatorname{ev},\tau\), the map \[ \pi(a)=a-\operatorname{ev}(a)\,1-\tau(a)\,t \tag{UP} \] is a homogeneous \(B\)-linear projection onto \(U\). The normalization free cover gives \(A\) a homogeneous generating family with weight polynomial \[ b_{22}(z)=\frac{(1-z^{N-3})(1-z^{N-2})}{(1-z)(1-z^2)}, \] of cardinality \(\binom{N-2}{2}\) and largest weight \(2N-8\). Its weight-zero and weight-one elements can be chosen as \(1,s\), and both project to zero in (UP). Projecting the others gives the stated bound on generators of \(U\). A generator of weight \(w\) maps under a degree-zero Hom in (GH) to a numerator of weight \(w+3N-17\), at most \(5N-25\). Negative weights contribute zero. The family may be redundant, but every source relation is kept; the projection is not a license to choose its images independently. \(\square\)

Explicit source and boundary of the conclusion. In \(P_B=B[s,v]\), the same source is the ideal quotient module \[ U=\bigl((s-b-c)^2,\ v-cs+c^2\bigr)/(E_{N-3},E_{N-2},E_{N-1},E_N), \] inside \(A\), where the \(E_j\) are the exact normalization tails after substitution in \(B\). The two displayed elements generate an ideal over \(P_B\), not generally a module over \(B\); the polynomial Hom in (GH) is \(B\)-linear. This distinction prevents reintroducing the refuted algebra-thickening shortcut. The theorem controls the denominators and unknown numerator weights, not the rank of their remaining global equations.

A local horizontal section can violate a global annihilator relation

Lemma (lem:local-horizontal-sections-do-not-globalize; working-proof control). Over any field and for any \(r\ge0\), let \[ R=k[x,y,z_1,\ldots,z_r],\quad \delta=x^2\partial_x+y^2\partial_y+\sum z_i^2\partial_{z_i}, \quad U_0=R/(x),\quad G=R(-2). \] Give \(U_0\) the induced derivation and \(G\) the connection \(\delta+y\). Then \[ V=\operatorname{Ext}^1_R(U_0,G)\cong R/(x)(-1), \] with generator \(e\) of weight one and connection \(\delta+y\). Its global degree-zero part is zero, but in \(V_{(x)}\) the nonzero degree-zero element \(e/y\) is horizontal. Thus codimension-one detection and local horizontal solutions do not imply existence of a global degree-zero horizontal class.

Proof. Resolve \(U_0\) by multiplication by \(x\). The relation connection adds \(\delta x/x=x\), so the induced Ext density is \(y-x\), which is \(y\) modulo \(x\). The shift gives generator weight one, so \(V_0=0\). Inverting \(y\) gives \[ (\delta+y)(e/y)=(-1+1)e=0. \] Under principal-parts duality, \(e/y\) at the prime \((x)\) sends the class of one to \(1/(xy)\) modulo \(R_{(x)}\). This is killed by \(x\) locally, because \(1/y\in R_{(x)}\). It is not killed by \(x\) in \(Q/R\): the product is the nonzero class of \(1/y\). More generally a global element killed by \(x\) is \(f/x+R\) with \(f\in R\), so matching this local section would require \(f\bmod x=1/y\), impossible in \(k[y,z_1,\ldots,z_r]\). The global source relation, not a missing local differential equation, obstructs the lift. \(\square\)

The line has made concrete uniform progress, but it has not yet produced a new odd-field threshold beyond the recorded ranges.

Comparing with the full flag theorem still leaves the actual residual extension uncomputed. Follow-up. Developed the obstruction test without deleting the known residual contribution.
