27 September 2026 — Two polynomial numerators force upper-extension rigidity in every dimension

Working all-dimensional characteristic-zero proof: horizontal first-Ext torsion vanishes, so the prescribed connections select one nonzero upper-extension class. The residual extension and threshold goal remain open. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and outcome. Open statement 3 still needs the actual graded threshold ideals. The current sufficient reconstruction route had reduced upper-extension rigidity to a bounded global horizontal-torsion kernel. This cycle eliminates that kernel. First, polynomial regularity excludes the cross-pair quadruple-double component. A smaller common denominator then bounds the images of two quadratic source elements so tightly that the triple-triple and quintuple restrictions are incompatible unless both vanish. Codimension-one detection completes the argument for all dimensions, without a new root-count computation.

General statement. lem:cube-cross-quadruple-torsion-exclusion excludes the remaining quadruple-double component for every available characteristic-zero dimension. thm:cube-horizontal-torsion-vanishing proves the full degree-zero horizontal torsion kernel zero for every \(N\ge5\). Together with the generic-image theorem, this proves the statement previously registered as conj:cube-normalized-extension-rigidity. Its stable ID is retained; the earlier conjectural record is not rewritten. This settles the upper normalized extension only, not the deeper residual extension or the original odd-field formula.

Regularity excludes the cross-pair quadruple component

Setup. Throughout, \(k\) has characteristic zero, \(N\ge5\), \(S=k[c_2,\ldots,c_N]\), \(D=D_{22}\), \(B=D_{32}\), and \[ p(Z)=(Z-b)^3(Z-c)^2\prod_{i=1}^{N-5}(Z-h_i). \] Root labeling is a finite free extension of \(B\). Put \(A=B\otimes_S D\), \(U=A_{\rm tor}\), and \(T=\operatorname{Ext}^1_S(D(-4),B(-N-3))\). We use the exact connections and principal-parts identification \[ T_{\rm tor}=\operatorname{Hom}_B(U,(\operatorname{Frac}B/B)(1-N)). \] A class in this proof is globally polynomial before this identification; its local rational coordinates are therefore subject to regularity, not arbitrary field solutions.

Lemma (lem:cube-cross-quadruple-torsion-exclusion; working proof). Every degree-zero horizontal element of \(T_{\rm tor}\) has zero cross-pair component at each divisor \(h_i=b\). Combined with the earlier half-integral exclusion, it is zero on the entire quadruple-double divisor.

A coordinate regular across the other cluster's collisions. Fix \(h_i=b+d\), and denote the other \(k=N-6\) spectators by \(h_j\). Separate the quartic factor \((Z-b)^3(Z-b-d)\) from the residual factor \((Z-c)^2\prod_j(Z-h_j)\). This requires only their resultant to be inverted; the residual factor is not split further. Bézout idempotents for these separated blocks select the cross-pair normalization component. Its pullback is the tensor product of the marked-double-root incidence algebras for the two factors.

In the quartic incidence algebra, \(t=x-b\) satisfies \[ t^3=\tfrac34dt^2,\qquad d^2t^2=0. \] Consequently \(q=t^2\), tensored with one in the residual algebra, defines a homogeneous map \((B/(d^2))(-2)\to U\) on this separated-factor open set. Pulling a global class in \(\operatorname{Ext}^1_B(U,B(1-N))\) back along this map gives a cochain coordinate \(\phi\) in the corresponding shifted \(B/(d^2)\). At the generic divisor it is exactly the cross-pair coordinate of the local model. This construction remains regular when \(c=h_j\) or \(h_j=h_l\): no resultant inside the residual factor was inverted. Equivalently one may make the factorization after étale extension and completion and use faithful flatness to detect the same pole orders.

Thus, on writing \(\phi=\phi_0+d\phi_1\pmod{d^2}\), both rational coefficients on the divisor can have finite poles only at \(b=c\) and \(b=h_j\). Taking the first two coefficients of the inverse block resultant introduces only further powers of those same factors. In particular they are regular at every \(c=h_j\) and \(h_j=h_l\). This is a property of the actual Ext coordinate, obtained by a polynomial pullback map, not an assumed extension of a generic trivialization.

The two transverse layers. The exact local connection is \[ \mathscr E\phi=\delta\phi+ \left(8b-(N-2)c+\tfrac{49}{8}d\right)\phi, \qquad\delta d=-(2b+d)d. \] The first coefficient \(\phi_0\) has weight \(5-N\) and solves \[ \delta\phi_0+(8b-(N-2)c)\phi_0=0. \] If it vanishes, \(\phi=d\phi_1\), where \(\phi_1\) has weight \(4-N\) and solves \[ \delta\phi_1+(6b-(N-2)c)\phi_1=0 \] on the divisor. Adjoin the mean and apply the homogeneous mean correction. Here \(e_1=4b+2c+\sum_jh_j\). The uncentered rational covariance weights \((d_b,d_c,d_{h_j})\) are respectively \[ (4,-N,-1),\qquad(2,-N,-1). \] Let \(V=1/((b-c)\prod_j(c-h_j))\), and \(\xi_j=(h_j-c)/(h_j-b)\). The translation-invariant degree-zero ratios \[ P_0=\phi_0/V,\qquad P_1=(b-c)\phi_1/V \] have homogeneous degrees \(-5\) and \(-4\) under simultaneous scaling of the \(\xi_j\), by the rational covariance calculation already proved in the generic-image theorem.

The pole restrictions above force both ratios to be polynomials in the \(\xi_j\). Explicitly fix \(b=1,c=0\), so \(h_j=\xi_j/(\xi_j-1)\). Their denominators can only involve \(\xi_j-1\), since they are regular at \(c=h_j\), and have no spectator-difference poles. Homogeneity excludes \(\xi_j-1\) as a pole divisor: scaling would produce infinitely many distinct pole divisors. Thus no finite pole remains. Negative homogeneous degrees force \(P_0=P_1=0\). When \(k=0\), the ratios are constants and the same nonzero degree characters force zero. Therefore \(\phi_0=0\), then \(\phi_1=0\), proving the lemma. \(\square\)

The remaining two divisor types cannot glue to a nonzero horizontal class

Theorem (thm:cube-horizontal-torsion-vanishing; working proof). For every characteristic-zero \(N\ge5\), \[ \ker(\mathscr E:(T_{\rm tor})_0\to(T_{\rm tor})_1)=0. \tag{TV} \] Hence \[ \dim_k\ker(\mathscr E:T_0\to T_1)=1. \tag{UR} \] The actual upper extension supplies its nonzero class. Thus the previously registered conj:cube-normalized-extension-rigidity is proved in all stated dimensions. With fixed endpoints, compatible connections were already unique; up to rescaling an endpoint, the nonzero compatible upper extension is now unique as well.

1. A smaller denominator. Let \(\eta\) be a degree-zero horizontal torsion class. The new lemma and the half-integral exclusions leave only quintuple and triple-triple divisors. Their local annihilators are squares. The same argument as in the denominator theorem now gives \[ F_2\eta=0,\qquad F_2=(b-c)^2H(c)^2, \quad \deg F_2=2N-8, \quad H(Z)=\prod_i(Z-h_i). \tag{SD} \] Codimension-one detection proves this globally; no assertion about annihilating nonhorizontal torsion is needed. Consequently \(\eta\) is represented by a global homogeneous \(B\)-linear map \[ U\longrightarrow (B/(F_2))(N-7). \] Only two of its values will be needed. They do not generate \(U\) globally as a \(B\)-module; their sufficiency will be proved using the local models at the end.

2. Translation gauge and the two polynomial values. Work in the labeled ring and put \(m=N-5\). Use coordinates relative to the double root: \[ x=b-c,\qquad y_i=h_i-c,\qquad \sigma=s-2c,\quad v'=v-cs+c^2,\quad t=\sigma-x=s-b-c. \] The centered labeled coefficient ring is the polynomial ring \(k[x,y_1,\ldots,y_m]\), because \(Nc+3x+\sum y_i=0\). Both \(t^2\) and \(v'\) lie in \(U\), by their zero images in the global first jet. Set \(M=\prod_i y_i\), with \(M=1\) for \(m=0\). Since \(F_2=x^2M^2\), their principal-parts values are \[ \eta(t^2)=\frac{P}{x^2M^2},\qquad \eta(v')=\frac{Q}{x^2M^2}, \tag{PQ} \] where \(P,Q\in k[x,y_1,\ldots,y_m]\) are homogeneous polynomials of degree \(m\). Indeed the two source weights are two, so numerator weight is \(2+N-7=N-5=m\). Since \(\deg F_2=2m+2>m\), these polynomial representatives are unique.

The connection in these relative coordinates must be specified, rather than simply setting a centered root to zero. Adjoin the mean \(\mu\). On translation-invariant homogeneous source elements, the uncentered source connection is the centered one minus \(2\mu E\) and minus \(7\mu\). On the target with shift \(1-N\), use uncentered density \[ -\tfrac72b-(N+\tfrac32)c-e_1, \qquad e_1=3b+2c+\sum h_i=N\mu. \] It differs from the centered density by \(-(2N+5)\mu\). For a degree-zero Hom map, the source and target polynomial weights differ by \(1-N\); therefore the two Euler corrections and the density difference cancel exactly in the Hom commutator. Thus a centered horizontal map is equivalently a translation-invariant uncentered horizontal map with this target density.

Now take the translation slice \(c=0\). The coefficient derivation and source density become \[ D=-x^2\partial_x-\sum_i y_i^2\partial_{y_i},\qquad \nabla_U=D_{\rm pair}-\tfrac72\sigma, \] where each marked pair root has the same drift \(-r^2\). The target density is \(-13x/2-\sum_i y_i\). Multiplication of the principal-parts map by \(M\) gives a horizontal map \(\psi=M\eta\) into the target with grading shift \(-4\) and density \(-13x/2\), because \(DM/M=-\sum_i y_i\). Multiplication by \(M\) is not assumed injective on torsion. Its two values are nevertheless the exact rational representatives \[ \psi(t^2)=\frac{P}{x^2M},\qquad \psi(v')=\frac{Q}{x^2M}. \tag{PPQ} \] They have weight \(-2\), so there is no homogeneous polynomial ambiguity in these representatives.

3. Triple-triple residues have constant coefficients. Fix a spectator \(i\) and localize at \(y_i=0\); write \(M_i=\prod_{j\ne i}y_j\). The local source torsion from the triple-triple model has generators \(u\) and \(a u\), where \(a\) is the displacement of the marked root from \(x\), and \[ a^2=0,\quad u^2=\tfrac23y_i u,\quad y_i^2u=0. \] Here the global pair elements satisfy \[ t^2=2au+\tfrac23y_i u,\qquad v'=xu+au. \tag{TT} \] Multiplication by \(M\) reduces the possible pole of \(\psi\) at this divisor to order one. Write its principal parts on these generators as \[ \psi(u)=f_0/y_i,\qquad \psi(au)=f_1/y_i. \] The leading parts of the actual source connection are \[ \nabla_Uu=-\tfrac72xu-\tfrac72au, \qquad\nabla_U(au)=-\tfrac{11}{2}xau \quad\pmod{y_iU}. \] Using target density \(-13x/2\), horizontality gives, for \(D_i=-x^2\partial_x-\sum_{j\ne i}y_j^2\partial_{y_j}\), \[ D_i f_1-xf_1=0,\qquad D_i f_0-3xf_0+\tfrac72f_1=0. \tag{TR} \] Their weights are \(-1,-2\), respectively. Formula (TT) and (PPQ) give explicitly \[ f_1=\frac{P|_{y_i=0}}{2x^2M_i},\qquad f_0=\frac{Q|_{y_i=0}-\tfrac12P|_{y_i=0}}{x^3M_i}. \tag{RF} \] Thus they have poles only on coordinate hyperplanes \(x=0,y_j=0\). This crucial global restriction follows from the polynomial numerators; it is not imposed on arbitrary local solutions.

Put \(r=1/x\), \(z_j=1/y_j\). Then \(D_i=\partial_r+\sum_j\partial_{z_j}\). A rational function with poles only on the coordinate hyperplanes that is invariant under simultaneous translation of all these reciprocal variables is a polynomial: any pole hyperplane would have infinitely many distinct translates. For the first equation in (TR), write \(f_1=rG\). Then \(D_iG=0\); \(G\) has reciprocal homogeneous degree zero and only coordinate poles. It is therefore a constant \(\lambda_i\in k\). Hence \(f_1=\lambda_i/x\).

The particular solution for \(f_0\) is \(7\lambda_i/(2x^2)\). A homogeneous difference solves \(D_i f-3xf=0\); writing \(f=r^3G\) makes \(G\) translation invariant of reciprocal degree \(-1\), again with only coordinate poles. It must be a polynomial of negative degree and is zero. Thus \[ f_1=\lambda_i/x,\qquad f_0=7\lambda_i/(2x^2). \] Substitution in (RF) proves the polynomial restrictions \[ P|_{y_i=0}=2\lambda_i xM_i,\qquad Q|_{y_i=0}=\tfrac92\lambda_i xM_i. \tag{PRQ} \] No symmetry assumption is needed to make the different \(\lambda_i\) equal.

4. Homogeneous degree forces a global form. The monomials \(M_i\) are linearly independent. Each polynomial \[ P-2x\sum_i\lambda_iM_i,\qquad Q-\tfrac92x\sum_i\lambda_iM_i \] vanishes on every coordinate hyperplane \(y_i=0\), by (PRQ), and therefore is divisible by \(M\). Its degree is \(m=\deg M\). Consequently there are constants \(a_0,b_0\in k\) with \[ P=a_0M+2x\sum_i\lambda_iM_i,\qquad Q=b_0M+\tfrac92x\sum_i\lambda_iM_i. \tag{GP} \] For \(m=0\), the sums are empty and this simply says that \(P,Q\) are constants.

5. The quintuple relation kills all triple-triple residues. At the generic divisor \(x=0\), all spectators are separated from the active five-root block. The exact quintic pullback algebra gives, on this component, \[ v'=\tfrac32t^2. \tag{QR} \] For clarity, with active mean \(a=3x/5\) and \(z=-x/5\), its centered pair sum is \(u\), \(t=u-z\), and its centered pair product is \((-15z^2+3u^2)/2\); substitution into \(v'\) gives (QR). The separated spectators do not enter this factorization equation. Since \(M\) is a unit at the generic quintuple divisor, (PQ) and (QR) imply that \(Q-3P/2\) is divisible by \(x^2\). Formula (GP) gives \[ Q-\tfrac32P=(b_0-\tfrac32a_0)M+ \tfrac32x\sum_i\lambda_iM_i. \] Its constant and linear coefficients in \(x\) must vanish. Thus \(b_0=3a_0/2\) and every \(\lambda_i=0\). The latter conclusion uses the linear independence of the \(M_i\); it holds for all \(m\ge1\) and is vacuous for \(m=0\).

6. The quintuple connection kills the remaining constant. We now have \(P=a_0M\), \(Q=3a_0M/2\), so (PPQ) gives \(\psi(t^2)=a_0/x^2\). On the quintuple source component, the exact connection from the divisor model is \[ \nabla_U(t^2)=(-11a+3z)t^2=-\tfrac{36}{5}x\,t^2. \] The target connection of \(\psi\) is \(D-13x/2\). Its Hom commutator on \(t^2\) is therefore \[ D(a_0/x^2)-\tfrac{13}{2}x(a_0/x^2) +\tfrac{36}{5}x(a_0/x^2) =\tfrac{27}{10}\frac{a_0}{x}. \] This principal part is nonzero at \(x=0\) unless \(a_0=0\). Horizontality forces \(a_0=b_0=0\), including \(m=0\). Thus both original numerators \(P,Q\) vanish. No injectivity of multiplication by \(M\) was used to infer this: it follows from their unique polynomial forms.

7. These two values detect the whole remaining class. At the quintuple divisor, \(t^2\) generates the source torsion. At each triple-triple divisor, (TT) expresses \(t^2,v'\) in the basis \(u,au\), with determinant \((2/3)y_i-2x\), a unit there. Thus vanishing of their two values makes the local principal-parts map zero on every remaining component. The quadruple-double and triple-double-double components were already excluded. Codimension-one detection now proves \(\eta=0\), establishing (TV). This explains why two elements suffice for detection even though they need not generate \(U\) globally over \(B\).

Finally the generic horizontal image theorem gives an exact sequence with kernel the space in (TV), image of dimension one, and a nonzero actual class. Therefore (UR) follows. Scaling the lower endpoint identifies any two nonzero classes on that line, proving the stated upper-extension uniqueness. The separate fixed-extension connection uniqueness remains compatible with this conclusion. \(\square\)

Checks and scope. The first exclusion retains the polynomial pullback of the actual Ext class across the residual collisions; generic connection weights alone would not suffice. The gluing proof uses the global numerator degree, coordinate pole restrictions and the exact factor \(3/2\) in the quintuple relation. Their mismatch with the triple-triple factors \(2,9/2\) is the decisive compatibility condition. The remaining constant is killed by \(27/10\), with the quintic control recovered when no spectators are present. No old rank certificate was rerun and no higher root count was computed. The proof remains characteristic zero and degree two. It does not identify the residual module \(K_2\), reconstruct its extension, or determine all odd-field thresholds.

Verification gate. The cycle's single fresh-context medium reviewer passed the full proof against the established dependencies. It checked the cross42 pullback and pole regularity, both covariance degrees, the smaller denominator, translation gauge and multiplication by M, all residue equations and weights, coordinate-only reciprocal poles, polynomial divisibility, the quintuple relation and coefficient 27/10, and detection by the two values. No substantive gap or unused hypothesis remained; one missing TeX backslash was repaired. The review verdict is retained. The full principal-parts theorem, all divisor models and exclusions, generic-image/covariance proof, global denominator theorem and exact quintic jet algebra were read. Named searches and reviewed dependency links distinguish this uniform proof from the older five- and six-root results.

Assessment and next step. The upper normalized extension is now rigid under its prescribed connection in every dimension. The next missing implication is the actual residual module and its extension to this upper quotient, or directly the intrinsic flag ideals that require that full graded information. Do not mistake a unique upper quotient for the full defect. On route cube-odd-characteristic, use the rigid upper module to isolate the first residual relation and determine what additional global data its extension needs; retain the known vertex contribution and the separate higher-saving and small-prime obligations.

27 September 2026 — The residual kernel has a quadruple-double component

Working characteristic-zero support theorem in every dimension: quintuple and quadruple-double residual components, with an exact quadratic-jet detector for the latter. Full residual reconstruction remains open. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and outcome. Upper-extension rigidity does not reconstruct the full graded defect. This cycle tests the general hypothesis that its residual kernel \(K_2\) is confined to the quintuple closure. It is false. At the first quadruple-double core, the complete first-order neighbourhood hides the residual, but the quadratic neighbourhood sees a two-dimensional image. A formal simple-spectator comparison transfers this obstruction to every larger dimension. The quintuple residual also persists, with generic transverse length sixteen. These are distinct required components, not a complete support or module classification.

General statement. lem:cube-simple-spectator-formal-stability compares complete defects and their dimension filtrations after adding separated simple roots. Combined with check:cube-six-root-residual-artin, thm:cube-residual-quadruple-double-support proves a quadruple-double residual component for all characteristic-zero \(N\ge6\), not merely one numerical root count. It refutes the proposed quintuple-only mechanism and changes the next reconstruction target.

Simple spectators preserve the complete defect and dimension filtration locally

Lemma (lem:cube-simple-spectator-formal-stability; working proof). Work in characteristic zero, with \(N\ge M\ge5\). At a geometric coefficient point, suppose exactly \(M\) roots belong to clusters of multiplicity at least two, while the other \(N-M\) roots are simple and distinct from all those clusters. Let \(p_M\) be the centered polynomial of those \(M\) active roots. After labeling separated factors and extending the residue field when necessary, formal coefficient coordinates identify \[ \widehat S_N\cong\widehat S_M[[t_1,\ldots,t_{N-M}]], \qquad \widehat C_N\cong\widehat C_M\widehat\otimes_{\widehat S_M}\widehat S_N. \tag{SS} \] The comparison respects the double-pair normalization quotient and its kernel \(K\), and identifies \(K_{2,N}\) with the corresponding extension of \(K_{2,M}\). These are complete coefficient-module and filtration statements. They are not isomorphisms of the original graded or Ore-filtered objects, or an identification of their connections, and carry no global degree bound.

Finite jets justify the pair decomposition. The global finite-jet theorem supplies powers for both sizes. Taking a common larger exponent gives finite presentations \[ J/J^{q+2}\xrightarrow{\mathcal L}P/J^q\longrightarrow C_0\longrightarrow0, \quad\mathcal L=\partial_s^2+s\partial_s\partial_v+v\partial_v^2+\tfrac52\partial_v. \] Completion is flat, so these presentations compute the completed modules. The argument used for the triple-double formal comparison applies to any union of separated pair-support points: if an idempotent representative satisfies \(e^2-e\in J^{q+2}\), its first pair derivatives lie in \(J^{q+1}\) and second derivatives in \(J^q\), since \(2e-1\) is a unit modulo those powers. The product rule gives \(\mathcal L(ef)=e\mathcal L(f)\pmod{J^q}\). Thus the cokernel itself splits by those pair supports. No ideal structure on \(\mathcal L(J)\) is assumed.

The active pair ideals are unchanged. Hensel factorization writes the universal polynomial as an active monic factor \(f_M\) times the separated simple factors. The differential of factor multiplication is invertible by Chinese remainders, giving formal coefficient coordinates. The root algebra splits accordingly. Its exterior square splits into the exterior square of the active root algebra, cross factors involving a simple root, and pairs of simple factors. On the active summand, the marked vector \(1\wedge Z\) is the same marked vector for \(f_M\). Therefore the kernel of the pair map \(P\to\bigwedge^2(S[Z]/p)\), restricted to that summand, is exactly the active pair ideal. This follows from the proved cyclic pair-algebra identification and handles internal diagonal pairs too; division by a root difference is not used on those pairs. Equivalently Bézout idempotents for the separated root factors identify their pair quotient maps and kernels.

Every other pair piece has zero central defect, since a pair involving a simple cluster has the factor \((m_i-1)(1-1)=0\), and an internal simple cluster contributes none. The support-preserving Galois finite-jet identification transports these pair-block harmonic deficits to the EPD cokernel pieces. Thus this step does not presume the EPD isomorphism is pair-multiplication linear. Each piece is a finite coefficient module, so Nakayama kills the pieces with zero central fibre. The active EPD pieces retain precisely the same ideals and the same operator \(\mathcal L\) as for \(f_M\).

Translate the active roots by their own mean. This is a coefficient-dependent translation, but its coefficients are constant for the pair-variable derivatives; \(\mathcal L\) is invariant under it. The global trace determines the active mean from the simple spectator roots, because \(M\) is invertible. There are \(M-1\) centered active coefficient coordinates and \(N-M\) independent spectator coordinates, totaling \(N-1\). This proves (SS). Constant rescaling of a nonzero active root separation multiplies \(\mathcal L\) by a coefficient-field unit and permits the canonical six-root point used below.

Normalization and the residual dimension layer. On an active pair component, the simple spectator factor is a unit modulo the square of its marked quadratic. Divisibility by that square is therefore equivalent for the full polynomial and for \(f_M\). Hence the normalization incidence algebra and the EPD quotient map agree, including diagonal pairs, so the comparison identifies \(K_N\) with the extended \(K_M\).

The normalized lower quotient, whose review gate was closed in the bounded-source record, identifies \(K_2\) as the largest submodule below the dimension of the triple-double layer. This characterization survives the present extension. To see it without assuming arbitrary filtration/base-change commutation, the completed normalizations are finite products of completions of their polynomial normalization rings. Each nonzero factor is a power-series domain of dimension \(M-3\) or \(M-4\), respectively; a nonzero coefficient submodule has that same dimension. After adjoining \(N-M\) formal variables these dimensions become \(N-3,N-4\), with no lower-dimensional submodules. The extension of \(K_{2,M}\) has dimension at most \(N-5\), while its quotient in \(C_N\) is an extension of the two just-described unmixed layers and has no submodule of dimension at most \(N-5\). It is consequently exactly the maximal such submodule, namely \(K_{2,N}\). Empty normalization fibres cause no exception. This proves the filtration assertion. \(\square\)

The first unchecked quadratic layer detects the residual

Exact certificate (check:cube-six-root-residual-artin; finite computation over \(\mathbb Q\)). Let \(\mathfrak m_a\) be the coefficient maximal ideal at the indicated centered six-root polynomial and \(R_j=S_6/\mathfrak m_a^{j+1}\). Write \(E=C_6/K_{2,6}\) for its actual upper quotient. The two retained certificates give:

The quadruple-double point is \(p=(Z+1)^4(Z-2)^2\), with \((c_2,c_3,c_4,c_5,c_6)=(-6,4,9,-12,4)\). The triple-triple control is \(p=(Z+1)^3(Z-1)^3\), with coefficients \((-3,0,3,0,-1)\). Jet order two means the quotient by \(\mathfrak m_a^3\), not a proof that all primary nilpotence has exponent two. The residual image is the image of \(K_{2,6}\) in \(C_6/\mathfrak m_a^{j+1}C_6\), by right exactness of the known quotient sequence. Why the full defect calculation terminates exactly. Use the actual centered pair target \(F=\bigwedge^2(S_6[Z]/p)\), of rank fifteen, marked by \(v=1\wedge Z\), with its proved connection \(\nabla\). If \(\mathcal E\) is the grading Euler connection, then \(\widetilde\nabla=\nabla+\lambda\mathcal E\) generates the same coefficient submodule from the homogeneous marker: on \(\nabla^jv\), the added term is \(\lambda(\deg v+j)\nabla^jv\), so the change of iterates is triangular with diagonal one. At a centered two-cluster point with values \(b,c\), the coefficient drift is \(- (b+c)\mathcal E\), since \(\kappa=bc\). Thus \(\lambda=b+c\), namely one or zero in the two controls, makes the modified coefficient derivation vanish at the point. It preserves every power of \(\mathfrak m_a\), so the entire connection descends to \(R_j\).

The first driver builds this finite rational operator and the coefficient-multiplication operators on \(F\otimes R_j\). Local elimination reduces the quadratic calculation. Eleven consecutive cyclic columns are independent on each closed fibre. Complete their constant vectors to a basis and lift it over \(R_j\). Indeed write any vector as a sum of a combination of the eleven columns and \(Lr\). Differentiating the first ten columns stays in that free span; differentiating the last has projected value \(w\). Hence the projected cyclic image is stable under the induced connection and contains \(w\), while induction on the original iterates puts it in the cyclic submodule of \(w\). Two necessary components of the residual support

Theorem (thm:cube-residual-quadruple-double-support; working proof). Let \(\Delta_5\) be the closure of polynomials with a root of multiplicity five, and \(\Delta_{42}\) the closure of the exact quadruple-double pattern. In characteristic zero, \[ \Delta_5\subseteq\operatorname{Supp}K_{2,N}\quad(N\ge5), \qquad \Delta_{42}\subseteq\operatorname{Supp}K_{2,N}\quad(N\ge6). \tag{RS} \] They are distinct irreducible components of dimension \(N-5\) when both are present; in particular \(\dim K_{2,N}=N-5\). The generic transverse length on \(\Delta_5\) is sixteen. At every geometric point of exact pattern \((4,2,1,\ldots,1)\), with coefficient maximal ideal \(\mathfrak m\), \[ K_2\subseteq\mathfrak m^2C,\qquad \dim_{\kappa}\bigl(K_2/(K_2\cap\mathfrak m^3C)\bigr)=2. \tag{QJ} \] This two-dimensional image does not determine the full transverse length, minimal resolution, connection or graded normalization map of that component. No completeness of the support list (RS) is asserted.

Proof. At an exact quintuple point apply (SS) with \(M=5\), active polynomial \(Z^5\) after translation. The known five-root residual is the length-sixteen vertex module. Its extension by the simple spectator parameters is nonzero and has transverse length sixteen. Thus every exact quintuple point lies in the residual support, and closedness gives the first inclusion.

At an exact quadruple-double point, apply (SS) with \(M=6\). Centering and a nonzero constant scaling identify its active roots with \(-1\) four times and \(2\) twice. The exact certificate shows that the six-root residual has zero images at jet orders zero and one and a two-dimensional image at order two. Ranks of rational matrices are unchanged under characteristic-zero field extension. A formal coordinate isomorphism preserves maximal-ideal powers.

Adjoining \(s=N-6\) formal spectator variables preserves those first nonzero image data. More explicitly, for a finite module \(M_0\) over a complete local ring with maximal ideal \(\mathfrak n\), the length after adjoining \(s\) formal variables and quotienting by the \((j+1)\)-st power of the new maximal ideal is \[ \sum_{a=0}^j\binom{s+a-1}{a} \operatorname{length}(M_0/\mathfrak n^{j+1-a}M_0), \] with coefficient one at \(a=0\) and zero for \(a>0\) when \(s=0\). This follows by grouping the formal-variable monomials by degree. Apply it to \(C_6\) and its upper quotient and subtract. Since their differences are \(0,0,2\), the enlarged differences remain \(0,0,2\). The filtration comparison in (SS) identifies the kernel with the actual \(K_{2,N}\), proving (QJ), and hence the second inclusion in (RS).

The parameter spaces for the generic patterns are irreducible, with dimensions \(N-5\): count the distinguished root values and the residual monic coefficients, then impose trace zero. Their coefficient maps are finite and generically birational onto the corresponding multiple-root loci. The two loci are distinct because an exact quadruple-double polynomial has no quintuple root, and an exact quintuple-plus-simple polynomial has no quadruple-double pair. The previously proved upper bound \(\dim K_2\le N-5\) therefore makes each a support component and gives equality of dimension. This refutes the quintuple-only hypothesis for every \(N\ge6\). \(\square\)

A polynomial connection on a fixed-centre transverse slice

Lemma (lem:cube-fixed-centre-cross-connection; working proof). Let \(k\) have characteristic zero, \(m,l\ge2\), and fix \(b\ne c\) in \(k\). Set \[ R=k[a_2,\ldots,a_m,d_2,\ldots,d_l],\quad f(X)=(X-b)^m+\sum_{j=2}^m(-1)^ja_j(X-b)^{m-j},\quad g(Y)=(Y-c)^l+\sum_{j=2}^l(-1)^jd_j(Y-c)^{l-j}. \] Use \(a_0=d_0=1\), \(a_1=d_1=a_{m+1}=d_{l+1}=0\), and put \[ \alpha=b+c-\frac{2a_2/m-2d_2/l}{b-c},\qquad \beta=b^2-2a_2/m-\alpha b, \] \[ \delta a_j=(j+1)a_{j+1}+j(\alpha-2b)a_j-\frac{2a_2}{m}(m-j+1)a_{j-1}, \quad \delta d_j=(j+1)d_{j+1}+j(\alpha-2c)d_j-\frac{2d_2}{l}(l-j+1)d_{j-1}. \] On \(F=R[X,Y]/(f(X),g(Y))\), of rank \(ml\), define \[ \nabla=\delta+(-X^2+\alpha X+\beta)\partial_X +(-Y^2+\alpha Y+\beta)\partial_Y +\alpha-\tfrac12(X+Y). \tag{FC} \] This is well-defined and its cyclic coefficient submodule generated by \(Y-X\) is the image of all universal pair columns. At the coefficient origin, its completed cokernel is the cross-pair summand of the full defect on this fixed-centre slice. No global graded or marked-order identification is claimed.

Proof. A root moving by \(r'=-r^2+\alpha r+\beta\) preserves both chosen means: its average on the first factor is \(-b^2+2a_2/m+\alpha b+\beta=0\), and on the second factor it is \(-c^2+2d_2/l+\alpha c+\beta=0\). Subtracting gives the displayed \(\alpha\). In centred factor coordinates the drifts are \(-u^2+(\alpha-2b)u-2a_2/m\) and its second-factor counterpart. Differentiating elementary symmetric functions gives the two coefficient formulas. The total derivation preserves each monic factor ideal; the scalar multiplication part does so too.

Before reducing by those factors, write the universal alternating series as \[ \sum_{j\ge0}g_jT^j=(Y-X)((1+XT)(1+YT))^{-3/2}. \] The proved free-polynomial identities give quadratic drift \(g_j\mapsto(j+1)g_{j+1}\), translation \(g_j\mapsto-(j+2)g_{j-1}\), and the grading Euler operator \(g_j\mapsto(j+2)g_j\). Consequently \[ \nabla g_j=(j+1)g_{j+1}+\alpha(j+2)g_j-\beta(j+2)g_{j-1}. \tag{TC} \] These columns have no coefficient dependence before reduction; factor preservation justifies reducing afterward. The recurrence is triangular with invertible leading coefficients. It proves equality of the two coefficient spans, even though \(\alpha,\beta\) vary with the parameters. It does not claim that translation alone acts on the factor quotient.

For the completed cross-pair assertion, use the finite EPD presentation and its proved pair-support decomposition. On the selected cross pair the exact pair ideal is \((f(X),g(Y))\), and \(Y-X\) is a unit. The harmonic-column cokernel is therefore this cross EPD summand, by the support-preserving adjoint identification. Equivalently, modulo any coefficient-ideal power the two-root series expands into finitely many rational functions times the square character of the two distinct central linear factors. That character separates it from internal pieces and other cross pieces; the coefficient spans split, not merely their residue-field ranks. Passing to the inverse limit is legitimate for the finite cokernels. This proves the claim. \(\square\)

The complete residual module at a quadruple-double point

Theorem (thm:cube-quadruple-double-transverse-residual; working proof with exact rational certificate). In every characteristic-zero \(N\ge6\), at an exact geometric root pattern \((4,2,1,\ldots,1)\), the completed transverse coefficient ring can be written \[ T=\kappa[[A,B,C,D]],\qquad f(X)=(X+1)^4+A(X+1)^2-B(X+1)+C,\quad g(X)=(X-2)^2+D. \] The actual residual module has transverse form \[ K_{2,\mathrm{tr}}\cong T/(B,C,D,A^2)\ \oplus\ T/(A,B,C,D). \tag{K42} \] Thus its generic transverse length is three, its annihilator is \((B,C,D,A^2)\), and its nonzero maximal-ideal multiple has length one and square zero. Formal smooth variables extend this statement along the stratum and for simple spectators. The isomorphism is a coefficient-module statement; it does not assign global generator degrees, transfer the original connection or describe the global residual extension.

The transverse coordinates. Formal factorization first separates the quartic and quadratic. Their means are independent smooth coordinates before centering. Translation removes the total mean. Their nonzero separation gives a further smooth coordinate; coefficient-dependent affine scaling fixes the means at \(-1,2\). The harmonic series transforms by an invertible triangular prefix change under translation and scaling, or directly the EPD operator changes by a coefficient unit. Thus the defect and its normalization filtration are extended from the four transverse coefficients. The simple-spectator lemma supplies the other \(N-6\) smooth coordinates. No root-ring ramification is introduced.

Complete polynomial computation. For \(m=4,l=2,b=-1,c=2\), (FC) has \[ \alpha=1+A/6-D/3,\quad \beta=2-A/3-D/3, \] \[ \delta A=3B+2(\alpha+2)A,\quad \delta B=4C+3(\alpha+2)B-A^2,\quad \delta C=4(\alpha+2)C-AB/2,\quad \delta D=2(\alpha-4)D. \] The driver constructs the eight-row tensor basis, verifies preservation of both factor equations, and computes the exact coefficient span of successive iterates by rational Gröbner bases. At order twelve the next column lies in the preceding span; applying the connection to every final Gröbner generator also reduces to zero. These are terminating invariant-module checks, so the retained thirty-five-column presentation gives the entire cyclic quotient \(M\), not a jet approximation. Its closed fibre has dimension three, matching the general cross-cluster formula.

Write \(I\subset R^8\) for that image and \(\mathfrak m=(A,B,C,D)\). Saturation gives \[ H^0_{\mathfrak m}(M)=(I:\mathfrak m^\infty)/I. \] The complete certificate retains the connection, cyclic presentation, saturation generators, residual presentation and basis. It gives dimension zero, length three, and annihilator \((D,C,B,A^2)\). Since this quotient is a three-dimensional vector space killed by \(B,C,D,A^2\) but not by \(A\), the action of \(A\) has exactly one Jordan block of size two and one of size one. This proves (K42) for the computed finite-length submodule.

Why this is the actual residual. The internal quartic summand is exactly its normalization module, by the quartic comparison; on this slice it is \(T/(B,4C-A^2)\), with \(D\) free, and has no finite-length submodule. The internal quadratic summand is zero. In the full defect, \(K_2\) is the maximal submodule below the triple-double layer, and the two normalization layers have no smaller-dimensional submodules. At the six-root quadruple-double point, fixing the smooth separation coordinate makes that dimension threshold zero. Hence the finite-length submodule of the cross summand is precisely \(K_{2,\mathrm{tr}}\). Completion and characteristic-zero field extension preserve the exact presentation, saturation quotient and its length. The formal spectator comparison then proves (K42) in every stated dimension. \(\square\)

27 September 2026 — A global polynomial jet detector for the quadruple-double residual

Working all-dimensional characteristic-zero graded detector: finite polynomial target, no root-difference inversions, and generic injection on the length-three residual component. Global reconstruction remains open. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and outcome. The previous transverse module was obtained after separating factors and fixing their means, with no global grading assertion. Open statement 3 needs polynomial maps and their actual degree costs. This cycle constructs a homogeneous map from the original full defect to an explicit finite module on a thickened quadruple-double normalization. It detects the entire residual at that component's generic point. Its target has a constant-size free coefficient-jet ambient module over the normalization parameter ring; its image still needs to be computed, and it does not reconstruct the full residual or its extension.

General statement. thm:cube-quadruple-polynomial-jet-detector constructs this actual polynomial map for every characteristic-zero \(N\ge6\), with explicit target generator and relation-source weights. It uses the completed local theorem only to prove generic injectivity, not to assert that a formal isomorphism preserves global grading.

An explicit homogeneous detector on a finite thickening

Theorem (thm:cube-quadruple-polynomial-jet-detector; working proof). Let \(k\) have characteristic zero and \(N\ge6\). Write \(r=N-6\). For \(r\ge1\), set \[ \mathcal B_{42}=k[b,c,h_2,\ldots,h_r],\quad H(Z)=Z^r+(4b+2c)Z^{r-1}+\sum_{j=2}^r h_jZ^{r-j}; \] for \(r=0\), set \(\mathcal B_{42}=k[b,c]/(4b+2c)\) and \(H=1\). Give \(b,c\) weight one and \(h_j\) weight \(j\). Define \[ \mathcal T=\mathcal B_{42}[a_2,a_3,a_4,d_2]/(a_2,a_3,a_4,d_2)^4, \quad \deg(a_2,a_3,a_4,d_2)=(2,3,4,2), \] \[ f(Z)=(Z-b)^4+a_2(Z-b)^2-a_3(Z-b)+a_4, \qquad g(Z)=(Z-c)^2+d_2. \tag{JT} \] The centered coefficient map \(S_N=k[c_2,\ldots,c_N]\to\mathcal T\) is defined by \(p_N(Z)=f(Z)g(Z)H(Z)\).

Let \(Q_6\) be the fixed, finite recursive bound supplied by the six-root endpoint corollary. In the free \(\mathcal T\)-module \[ W=\bigl(\mathcal T[X,Y]/(f(X),g(Y))\bigr)(-1) \] use the basis \(X^iY^j\), \(0\le i<4,0\le j<2\), with weight \(i+j+1\), and let \(G_j\) be the coefficient of \(z^j\) in \[ (Y-X)((1+Xz)(1+Yz))^{-3/2}. \] Set \[ M_{42}=W/\sum_{j=0}^{Q_6}\mathcal T G_j. \tag{PD} \] There is a canonical homogeneous degree-zero \(S_N\)-linear map \[ \Phi_{42}:C_N\longrightarrow M_{42},\qquad [u(Z)\wedge v(Z)]\longmapsto [u(X)v(Y)-v(X)u(Y)]. \tag{PM} \] At the generic point of \(\Delta_{42}\), its restriction to the actual \(K_{2,N}\) is injective and its image has transverse length three.

The algebra \(\mathcal T\) is finite over \(S_N\) and free of rank thirty-five over \(\mathcal B_{42}\). Thus (PD) is a polynomial quotient of a rank-280 free module over \(\mathcal B_{42}\). More explicitly, \(M_{42}\) has an \(S_N\)-generating family of at most \(4480N^2\) elements, all of weights at most \(8N+15\). Its presentation over \(\mathcal T\) uses the eight target weights \(i+j+1\) and the relation-source weights \(j+2\), \(0\le j\le Q_6\); the coefficient-jet weights are at most twelve. This is not a bound on all first syzygies over \(S_N\). The image \(\Phi_{42}(K_{2,N})\) is generated by the images of the known residual source, at most \((N-3)(3N-10)\) elements in weights \(2N-1,\ldots,4N-6\).

The construction is polynomial everywhere. The coefficient of \(Z^{N-1}\) in \(fgH\) is zero by the definition of \(H\), including the separate \(N=6\) trace relation. Therefore the displayed coefficient map exists and preserves weights. Reduction modulo monic \(f,g\) proves that \(W\) is free of rank eight over \(\mathcal T\), with the stated homogeneous basis. The jet algebra has the thirty-five monomials of ordinary total exponent at most three in four variables; their weighted degrees are at most twelve. Every construction still makes sense when \(b=c\), when \(H(b)H(c)=0\), or when \(H\) has repeated roots. No resultant or root difference is inverted.

All pair columns are killed by the finite relation list. In the universal six-root polynomial \(p_6=fg\), translate by its mean \((4b+2c)/6\). The polynomial triangular translation formula identifies every prefix of its pair columns with the corresponding centered prefix. Its generating-series proof is an identity before quotient reduction, so this use does not require an anchored root at zero. The centered six-root monic bound implies that all columns lie in the span of a prefix of length at most \(Q_6\); using indices \(0,\ldots,Q_6\) is a harmless larger prefix. This follows from the original-to-pair order shift and the unitriangular recurrence. The relations hold before any factor specialization.

Project the exterior square of the universal six-root algebra to its quartic/quadratic tensor product. Every polynomial column relation projects to the same relation among the \(G_j\). Specializing its coefficients to \(\mathcal T\) proves that the finite list in (PD) spans every \(G_j\). Surjectivity of the exterior projection at colliding factors is not required: only its effect on these columns is used. Thus (PD) is explicit and finite even though the deliberately coarse constant \(Q_6\) is not numerically evaluated.

The same exterior projection exists for \(p_N\), since \(f\) and \(g\) divide it over \(\mathcal T\). It is independent of polynomial representatives: a multiple of \(p_N\) is zero in each selected root algebra. The universal generating series sends the original pair marker and every polynomial column to \(G_j\). The centered recurrence identifies their span with the original full cyclic image. Hence the projection kills every defining relation of \(C_N\) and descends to (PM). Each wedge basis element and its image have weight \(i+j+1\); monic reductions preserve weight. The map is genuinely homogeneous of degree zero, not merely a rational map with an unrecorded denominator.

Finiteness over the original coefficient ring and the degree ledger. Monic division of \(p_N\) by \(fg\) expresses all coefficients of \(H\) polynomially in \(c_2,\ldots,c_N,b,c,a_2,a_3,a_4,d_2\). Thus \(\mathcal T\) is generated over \(S_N\) by those six displayed extra variables. Evaluation gives \[ p_N(b)=a_4g(b)H(b),\qquad p_N(c)=d_2f(c)H(c), \] so \(p_N(b)^4=p_N(c)^4=0\) in \(\mathcal T\). These are monic polynomial relations of degree \(4N\) in \(b,c\), with coefficients in \(S_N\). Together with the fourth-power jet relations they reduce every element to the span of \[ b^ic^j a_2^{e_2}a_3^{e_3}a_4^{e_4}d_2^{e_d},\quad 0\le i,j<4N,\quad e_2+e_3+e_4+e_d<4. \] There are at most \(560N^2\) such monomials, of weights at most \(8N+10\). Multiplying by the eight pair basis elements gives \(4480N^2\) and maximum weight \(8N+15\). Relations may make this cover highly redundant. The degree-zero restriction of (PM) transports the already-proved residual free cover without increasing its weights; no submodule-generator bound is inferred just from the target cover.

Generic detection of the actual residual. At an exact quadruple-double point with simple spectators, formal factorization uniquely separates the quartic, quadratic and residual factors. Its multiplication Jacobian is invertible by Chinese remainders. Their coefficients are formal coordinates, with the trace relation removing one mean. The two means and residual-factor coordinates give \(N-5\) smooth directions; the four centred factor coefficients are transverse coordinates. Consequently (JT), at the generic point of this stratum, is exactly the fourth-power transverse coefficient neighbourhood, after the same harmless residue-field extension used in the local theorem.

On this separated locus the projection in (PM) selects the cross-pair summand. The internal quartic summand has no residual, and the other pair pieces involving simple spectators vanish. The complete transverse theorem therefore identifies the restriction with \[ K_{2,\mathrm{tr}}\longrightarrow C_{\mathrm{cross},\mathrm{tr}}/ (a_2,a_3,a_4,d_2)^4 C_{\mathrm{cross},\mathrm{tr}}, \] which is injective and has image of length three. Faithfully flat completion detects this injection. This proves the generic assertion in every stated \(N\). Falsification and decision. The exact weight-twelve witness shows that the detector image is not closed under normalization multiplication in any dimension. General statement. lem:cube-two-cluster-coefficient-basis proves a finite free coefficient basis for every ordered two-cluster multiplicity family in characteristic zero. thm:cube-detector-coefficient-ring-reduction applies it to the actual quadruple-double jet target and gives an exact coefficient-ring image-closure procedure for all \(N\ge6\). The general proof precedes the single smallest-core control.

A finite free basis over the first coefficient parameters

Lemma (lem:cube-two-cluster-coefficient-basis; working proof). Let \(k\) have characteristic zero, \(m,l\ge1\), \(N\ge m+l\), and \(r=N-m-l\). Let \(B_{m,l}\) be the parameter algebra of centered factorizations \[ p(Z)=(Z-b)^m(Z-c)^lH(Z),\qquad \deg H=r. \] For \(r\ge1\), it is \(k[b,c,h_2,\ldots,h_r]\), with \(H=Z^r+(mb+lc)Z^{r-1}+\sum_{j=2}^rh_jZ^{r-j}\). For \(r=0\), it is \(k[b,c]/(mb+lc)\). The factors are ordered; when \(m=l\), no quotient by their interchange is taken. Set \(\deg b=\deg c=1\), \(\deg h_j=j\), and use the actual coefficient functions \(c_j\) of \(p\). Then \[ A_{m,l}=k[c_2,\ldots,c_{r+2}]\ \hookrightarrow\ B_{m,l} \] is a polynomial subring, and \(B_{m,l}\) is graded free over it with basis-weight polynomial \[ b_r(t)=\frac{(1-t^{r+1})(1-t^{r+2})}{(1-t)^2} =(1+t+\cdots+t^r)(1+t+\cdots+t^{r+1}). \tag{NB} \] Its rank is \((r+1)(r+2)\), and its largest basis weight is \(2r+1\).

Proof, including the zero fibre and freeness. This generalizes the finite-free argument for the two earlier normalization resolutions; it is not a novelty claim about Noether normalization. Write \[ H_j(b,c)=[z^j](1-bz)^{-m}(1-cz)^{-l}. \] Logarithmic differentiation gives \[ (j+1)H_{j+1}=((j+m)b+(j+l)c)H_j-(j+m+l-1)bcH_{j-1}. \tag{TR} \] After setting \(c_2,\ldots,c_{r+2}\) to zero, truncated monic division determines the residual-factor coefficients and leaves exactly \(H_{r+1}=H_{r+2}=0\). Thus the zero fibre is \(k[b,c]/(H_{r+1},H_{r+2})\). For \(r=0\), its first equation is the trace relation \(mb+lc=0\); it is not elimination of a nonexistent \(c_1\).

If \(bc\ne0\), (TR) propagates the two consecutive zero values backwards to \(H_0=0\), impossible. If \(b=0\), then \(H_j=\binom{l+j-1}{j}c^j\), and similarly when \(c=0\); the first relevant index is positive and all coefficients are nonzero in characteristic zero. Hence the common zero locus is the origin. The two homogeneous equations are a regular sequence in \(k[b,c]\), giving the finite zero-fibre Hilbert polynomial (NB).

Lift its homogeneous basis to \(B_{m,l}\). Induction on weight, subtracting a residue-field expression and then multiples of the positive-weight coefficient parameters, shows that these lifts generate over the formal polynomial ring on \(c_2,\ldots,c_{r+2}\). This is actual finiteness, not just a fibre dimension. That polynomial ring has \(r+1\) variables, equal to the dimension of the integral parameter algebra, so its map has zero kernel. Finally, the parameter algebra's explicit weighted Hilbert series gives \[ H_{B_{m,l}}(t)=H_{A_{m,l}}(t)b_r(t), \] including \(b_0=1+t\) when the trace eliminates one of \(b,c\). The graded free cover from the lifted fibre basis has this same Hilbert series, so its kernel is zero. This proves all claims. \(\square\)

The jet target over the original coefficient subring

Theorem (thm:cube-detector-coefficient-ring-reduction; working proof). Use the polynomial jet detector \(C_N\to M_{42,N}\), its coefficient algebra \(\mathcal T\), and its eight-generator ambient module \(W\), for characteristic-zero \(N\ge6\). Put \[ A_N=k[c_2,\ldots,c_{N-4}],\quad \rho_N=(N-4)(N-5),\quad J_4(t)=\sum_{e_2+e_3+e_4+e_d<4}t^{2e_2+3e_3+4e_4+2e_d}. \] The actual, deformed coefficient map embeds \(A_N\) into \(\mathcal T\). Both \(\mathcal T\) and \(W\) are graded free over \(A_N\), with basis-weight polynomials \[ \tau_N(t)=b_{N-6}(t)J_4(t),\qquad w_N(t)=\tau_N(t)\,t(1+t+t^2+t^3)(1+t). \tag{CF} \] Their ranks are \(35\rho_N\) and \(280\rho_N\), and their largest basis weights are \(2N+1\) and \(2N+6\). Expanding the finite column presentation \(G_0,\ldots,G_{Q_6}\) in these bases gives a finite homogeneous \(A_N\)-presentation of the actual target, with source basis weights at most \(Q_6+2N+3\).

The four multiplication maps by \(c_{N-3},c_{N-2},c_{N-1},c_N\) commute, are homogeneous and \(A_N\)-linear, and preserve the target relations. If \(L_0\) is the \(A_N\)-span of the images of the known finite residual source and \[ L_{q+1}=L_q+\sum_{j=N-3}^{N}c_jL_q\subseteq M_{42,N}, \tag{AC} \] then this chain stabilizes at exactly \(I_N=\Phi_{42}(K_{2,N})\). Its generic \(A_N\)-rank is \(3\rho_N\). No freeness of \(I_N\), iteration bound, original connection reduction or sharp first-syzygy bound is asserted.

Proof. The preceding lemma gives the assertion for the reduced marked-factor algebra \(\mathcal B_{42}\). Filter \(\mathcal T\) by powers of its four-variable coefficient-jet ideal. On every associated-graded piece, the action of \(c_j\) is its reduced action: the difference between the deformed and reduced coefficients raises that filtration. Each piece is a direct sum of shifted copies of \(\mathcal B_{42}\), one per jet monomial of the relevant ordinary exponent degree. These are free graded \(A_N\)-modules. Successively lifting their homogeneous bases splits the finite filtration as graded \(A_N\)-modules, proving (CF). Reduction already proves injectivity of the map from \(A_N\); no nilpotent flatness assumption is substituted for this filtration argument.

The highest jet weight is twelve and the reduced basis maximum is \(2N-11\), so the maximum for \(\mathcal T\) is \(2N+1\). The pair basis adds at most five. The relation column \(G_j\) has weight \(j+2\); expanding its \(\mathcal T\)-multiples therefore gives the stated source bound. All weights are the original coefficient weights. Multiplication by the four remaining coefficients descends because the target relations form a \(\mathcal T\)-submodule. Since \(S_N=A_N[c_{N-3},\ldots,c_N]\), the union of (AC) is exactly the original coefficient span of the source images. It stabilizes by Noetherianity of the finite \(A_N\)-module \(M_{42,N}\).

An exact generic \((4,2,1,\ldots,1)\) polynomial uniquely determines its marked quadruple and double factors, so the fraction field of the reduced parameter algebra is the residue field of \(\Delta_{42}\). This domain has degree \(\rho_N\) over \(A_N\). The actual image has generic transverse length three on its sole maximal-dimensional support \(\Delta_{42}\), by the detector theorem. Localizing at the fraction field of \(A_N\) therefore gives dimension \(3\rho_N\); smaller-dimensional boundary contributions disappear there. This is a rank computation, not removal of those contributions from the image. \(\square\)

Falsifying controls. At \(N=6\), \(A_6=k[c_2]\). With \(t=c_2\), the deformed zero fibre has the presentation \[ k[b,A,B,C,D]/((A,B,C,D)^4,\ 6b^2-A-D). \] The exact control gives length seventy, maximum basis weight thirteen, and \(b^7\ne0,b^8=0\). Thus it retains the deformation of the coefficient action: replacing it by the reduced action would incorrectly make \(b^2=0\). The ambient module has rank 560 and maximum basis weight eighteen. The predicted generic image rank is six. Its normalization span has the same generic image: at the generic quadruple-double point the target coefficient algebra is a quotient of the localized coefficient ring by the fourth transverse power, so normalization scalars already come from that ring. Both spans are finite graded coefficient modules, hence their quotient at six roots is supported at the vertex and has finite length. This justifies the finite boundary-quotient target of the next test, without computing its length. In characteristic three the ordered \((3,2)\), \(N=5\) control instead has \(p=(Z-b)^3Z^2=Z^5-b^3Z^2\), so \(c_2=0\) and the proposed zero fibre is a line. The characteristic-zero hypothesis cannot simply be dropped; this is not a counterexample to odd-field cube normality.

Working characteristic-zero image and boundary theorems: complete six-root graded presentation with first relations through weight twenty, and a rank-four reduced sixfold boundary module in every dimension. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

General statement. thm:cube-six-root-detector-image is an exact polynomial-module calculation over the full coefficient ring, not a pointwise rank sample. thm:cube-sixfold-normalization-boundary proves the resulting reduced rank-four boundary component for every characteristic-zero \(N\ge6\). The complete six-root image over the original ring

Theorem (thm:cube-six-root-detector-image; working proof with exact rational certificates). Let \(S=k[c_2,c_3,c_4,c_5,c_6]\) in characteristic zero, with the original weights, and let \(I_6=\Phi_{42}(K_{2,6})\) be the actual image in the polynomial jet target. Put \(t=c_2\), \(u=c_3\), and \[ \Delta=u^2+\tfrac{2}{27}t^3. \] Then, as graded \(S\)-modules, \[ I_6\cong F\oplus k(-14). \tag{CI} \] On \(F\), the other coefficients act by \[ c_4=t^2/4,\qquad c_5=tu/2,\qquad c_6=u^2/4. \tag{SG} \] As a \(k[t,u]\)-module, \(F\) is the cokernel of the following matrix, whose row-generator weights are \((14,13,14,12,13)\) and column-relation weights are \((16,16,17,17,18)\): \[ P=\begin{pmatrix} t&0&\frac{2547}{694}u&0&\frac{3572100}{120409}t^2\\ u&0&\frac13t^2&0&0\\ 0&t&u&27u&\frac{566}{347}t^2\\ 0&t^2&0&27tu&27u^2\\ 0&u&0&-2t^2&-2tu \end{pmatrix}. \tag{CP} \] This rational basis is not canonical. The complete annihilator is \[ \operatorname{Ann}_S I_6= (c_4-t^2/4,\ c_5-tu/2,\ c_6-u^2/4,\ \Delta^2). \tag{AN} \] In particular the image lies on the squared-cubic locus, with a doubled cusp condition; it is not replaced by the reduction of that locus.

Over \(A=k[t]\), \[ I_6\cong A(-12)\oplus A(-13)^2\oplus A(-14)^2\oplus A(-15) \oplus(A/(t))(-14). \tag{AI} \] The original \(S\)-minimal generator and first-relation polynomials are \[ \beta_0(I_6;z)=z^{12}+2z^{13}+3z^{14},\qquad \beta_1(I_6;z)=4z^{16}+6z^{17}+7z^{18}+5z^{19}+3z^{20}. \tag{IB} \] Thus the largest first-relation weight of this image is exactly twenty. This is not a relation bound for the full \(K_{2,6}\) or a value of the original monic cutoff.

Let \(\overline I_6=k[b]I_6\) denote its normalization span inside the same target, where the marked double root is \(-2b\). Then \[ \overline I_6=I_6+bI_6+b^2I_6,\qquad \overline I_6/I_6\cong k(-13)\oplus k(-14)^3 \tag{BD} \] as graded \(S\)-modules. The quotient is not asserted to inherit multiplication by \(b\), since \(I_6\) is not closed under it.

Exact finite coefficient encoding. The coefficient-ring theorem identifies \[ \mathcal T_6= k[t,b,A,B,C,D]/((A,B,C,D)^4,\ 6b^2+t-A-D) \] as free of rank seventy over \(k[t]\), with basis \(b^iA^{e_2}B^{e_3}C^{e_4}D^{e_d}\), \(i\in\{0,1\}\), \(e_2+e_3+e_4+e_d<4\). The pair target adds \(X^iY^j\), \(0\le i<4,0\le j<2\), giving rank 560. This is the actual deformed coefficient action, not the reduced substitution \(t=-6b^2\).

The complete driver builds the \(\mathcal T_6\)-linear span of the universal pair columns. The next column at order thirteen lies in the preceding span, whose \(A\)-rank is 482. Completeness follows from the centered connection recurrence, not from the stabilized rank. Explicitly, the coefficient derivation has \[ \delta b=b^2+A/6-D/3,\quad \delta A=3B-4bA,\quad \delta B=4C-6bB-A^2, \] \[ \delta C=-8bC-AB/2,\quad\delta D=8bD,\quad\delta t=3c_3. \] It preserves the jet ideal and the relation \(6b^2+t-A-D\), the latter checked exactly. These are the centered root drifts of the two factors, so they preserve their root ideals as well. Therefore dependence of the next column makes the whole \(\mathcal T_6\)-span connection-stable, and every later column lies in it. The target quotient has generic \(A\)-rank 78, agreeing with the two normalization sheets times the known transverse cross length thirty-nine.

The full original coefficient image. The reviewed polynomial residual source is generated in weights eleven through eighteen. In each of those weights the driver takes the complete kernel of the normalized \(\chi\)-map on representatives \(a_5u+a_6w\). The previous exact dictionary proves these kernels cover every actual residual class. Each representative is mapped by a verified polynomial EPD primitive and then the original exterior projection. This retains all source relations; no ideal closure is substituted.

Their \(A\)-span, modulo the complete target relations, is already stable under \(c_3,c_4,c_5,c_6\) at the first full module check. Thus it is precisely \(I_6\). Generic image rank is six, as predicted, but stability is checked by module remainders, not rank. Successive closure under \(b\) adds \(bI_6\) and \(b^2I_6\); the third check adds nothing. Its generic rank remains six. The previously saved weight-twelve witness lies in \(I_6\), while its product by \(b\) still does not, providing a nonvacuous control on which coefficient ring is used.

The complete PID certificate retains the target, original image and normalization-span preimages, all scalar coefficient operators, and graded presentations. Saturating the target-relation module by \(t\) identifies torsion; its intersection with the image gives exactly one torsion class in weight fourteen. The torsion-free quotient has basis weights \(12,13,13,14,14,15\). The normalization quotient has four basis vectors, one of weight thirteen and three of weight fourteen, and is killed by \(t\). This proves (AI) and the \(A\)-module form of (BD).

Recovering the actual \(S\)-action. The action extractor uses the recorded embedding and a homogeneous pruning isomorphism, then lifts each ambient coefficient action back to the seven-generator minimal \(A\)-presentation. It verifies the lift, the source relation, every degree, and all pairwise commutators. Its certificate gives four small matrices. Their vertex row and column vanish. Equivalently, any homogeneous \(A\)-splitting in (AI) is \(S\)-linear here: the other coefficients have degree at least three, and cannot map a free generator of minimum weight twelve to the lone torsion weight fourteen. They kill that torsion. Thus (CI) is an \(S\)-splitting, not only an ungraded PID decomposition.

On the six-generator free part, the matrices satisfy (SG). If \(U\) is its \(c_3\)-matrix, exact checks give \[ (U^2+\tfrac{2}{27}t^3)^2=0,\qquad U^2+\tfrac{2}{27}t^3\ne0,\qquad \operatorname{rank}_{k(t)}(U^2+\tfrac{2}{27}t^3)=2, \] and \(\det(uI-U)=\Delta^3\). The structural extraction gives a minimal five-by-five presentation over \(k[t,u]\), followed only by homogeneous invertible constant row and column changes to obtain (CP). The full certificate retains those changes. Since \(\Delta\) is irreducible over \(k(t)\) by the odd \(t\)-valuation of \(-2t^3/27\), the minimal polynomial of \(U\) is \(\Delta^2\). Division by this monic polynomial in \(u\) proves \(\operatorname{Ann}_{k[t,u]}F=(\Delta^2)\). Equation (SG), and the vertex summand annihilated by every positive coefficient, give (AN).

Original-ring minimal relations. The determinant of (CP) is a nonzero scalar times \(\Delta^3\), so its square presentation is injective on its relation module. All entries have positive weight, hence it is a minimal two-variable resolution. Adjoin \(c_4,c_5,c_6\) with the three monic graph relations (SG). Their Koszul complex is exact on the extended module: successively, a monic new variable minus an existing endomorphism is injective by its highest variable coefficient. Its tensor product with the two-variable resolution is minimal over \(S\), since every differential entry has positive weight. Adding the vertex Koszul resolution gives the full Betti generating polynomial \[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal B_{I_6}(v,z)={}& (z^{12}+2z^{13}+2z^{14}+v(2z^{16}+2z^{17}+z^{18})) \prod_{j=4}^{6}(1+vz^j)\\ &+z^{14}\prod_{j=2}^{6}(1+vz^j). \end{aligned} \] Its first two coefficients are (IB), also extracted from the retained presentation. The four boundary classes have only weights thirteen and fourteen, whereas every \(c_j\) has weight at least two, so all of \(S_+\) kills them. This upgrades (BD) to the stated \(S\)-module identity. For any basis \(z_1,z_2\) of \((I_6)_{13}\) and nonzero \(z\in(I_6)_{12}\), the classes of \(bz,bz_1,bz_2,b^2z\) give a boundary basis, by the span identity and the recorded dimensions. \(\square\)

A rank-four reduced boundary component in every dimension

Theorem (thm:cube-sixfold-normalization-boundary; working proof). For every characteristic-zero \(N\ge6\), let \[ I_N=\Phi_{42}(K_{2,N}),\qquad \overline I_N=\mathcal B_{42}I_N\subset M_{42,N},\qquad Q_N^{\mathrm{bd}}=\overline I_N/I_N. \] The notation \(Q_N^{\mathrm{bd}}\) is unrelated to the old monic cutoff \(Q_N\). At every exact geometric pattern \((6,1,\ldots,1)\), after the usual separated-factor coordinates and residue extension, the completed boundary module is \[ \widehat{Q_N^{\mathrm{bd}}}\cong k[[t_1,\ldots,t_{N-6}]]^{\oplus4}, \tag{SB} \] with all five transverse active-six-root coefficient parameters acting by zero. Consequently the sixfold closure \(\Delta_6\) is a support component of dimension \(N-6\), with generic transverse length four and reduced transverse action, and \(\dim Q_N^{\mathrm{bd}}=N-6\). No complete support list or global graded trivialization is asserted.

Proof. The natural formal detector comparison identifies the completed source residual, target and actual image near this pattern with their six-root versions and \(N-6\) smooth variables. It also identifies normalization spans. After Hensel removal of the simple spectator factor, its coefficients and the active mean \(\mu\) belong to the completed coefficient ring. The normalization coordinates satisfy \(b=b_6+\mu\), \(c=-2b_6+\mu\). Thus their action and every residual-factor coefficient action enlarge the image by exactly the scalar extension of \(k[b_6]I_6\). Flat completion commutes with the image and this finite span inside the finite target. Formula (BD), forgetting its six-root global weight labels, gives (SB).

Globally, the boundary is finite over \(S_N\) and supported on \(\Delta_{42}\). At its generic point the marked factors are unique and the jet coefficient algebra is the fourth-power transverse quotient of the localized coefficient ring. Its normalization scalars therefore already act through that ring, so \(\overline I_N=I_N\) generically. Hence the boundary support has dimension at most \(N-6\). The sixfold parameterization \(p=(Z-a)^6H\), with trace zero, is finite and generically one-to-one on the exact stratum; its irreducible image has dimension \(N-6\). Formula (SB) makes this locus nonzero in the boundary support, and closedness plus the upper dimension bound proves that it is a component and gives equality of dimension. The formal coefficient comparison carries no global weight bound, so the labels thirteen and fourteen are not transferred to higher \(N\). \(\square\)

27 September 2026 — Three collision loci suffice, and the missing kernel is finite over the original parameters

Working characteristic-zero support and parameter theorems in every dimension: the detector kernel is confined to quintuple and triple-triple collisions; the full residual is finite over the first coefficient parameters. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and outcome. Open statement 3 needs the relations of the full residual, whereas the last cycle presented only a detector image. The pair decomposition confines the full residual to three collision loci and the detector kernel to two. All three loci are finite over the same original coefficient parameters. This extends the coefficient-ring method to the full residual, without making it free or bounding its relations. One universal unknown transverse length remains on the triple-triple locus.

General statement. thm:cube-residual-three-locus-support locates both modules for every characteristic-zero dimension, including configurations with arbitrarily many repeated spectator clusters. thm:cube-full-residual-coefficient-finiteness proves actual module finiteness and a rank formula over original coefficient parameters. The next complete triple-triple local-module calculation will decide the remaining term in that formula; no additional root-count series is proposed.

Support of the full residual and of the unseen detector kernel

Theorem. Work over a characteristic-zero field, with the established centered coefficient ring \(S_N=k[c_2,\ldots,c_N]\), defect \(C_N\), and residual dimension layer \(K_{2,N}\). Write \(\Delta_5,\Delta_{42},\Delta_{33}\) for the reduced closures of the indicated multiple-root patterns, allowing distinguished roots to coincide. For \(N\ge6\), let \(H_N=\ker(\Phi_{42}|_{K_{2,N}})\). Then \[ \Delta_5\cup\Delta_{42}\ \subseteq\ \operatorname{Supp}K_{2,N} \ \subseteq\ \Delta_5\cup\Delta_{42}\cup\Delta_{33}, \] \[ \Delta_5\ \subseteq\ \operatorname{Supp}H_N \ \subseteq\ \Delta_5\cup\Delta_{33}. \tag{KS} \] The first upper inclusion also holds at \(N=5\), with the two six-root loci absent. These are support inclusions, not annihilator identities. The status of \(\Delta_{33}\) as an additional component is not decided here.

Local pieces and their dimension layers. Use the exact formal pair decomposition in the normalization-kernel support proof, whose provisional review gate was subsequently closed. At a geometric point, factor \(p=\prod f_i\) into separated monic factors of degrees \(m_i\). The factor coefficients, with one trace relation, are formal coordinates. Compatible idempotents at jet orders \(q+2,q\) split the actual EPD cokernel, since their first derivatives lie in \(J^{q+1}\), second derivatives in \(J^q\), and \(\mathcal L(ef)=e\mathcal L(f)\pmod{J^q}\). The cross piece has exact ideal \((f_i(x),f_j(y))\), with \(x-y\) a unit; an internal piece has the alternating pair ideal for \(f_i\), without division by a root difference. Unselected factors are units on this piece, even when they have repeated roots of their own.

The normalization map decomposes into the corresponding squared-quadratic incidence maps. Translate the selected factors by their joint mean; the pair derivatives regard this coefficient function as a scalar, and the EPD operator is translation invariant. The unselected factor coefficients then supply smooth independent variables. For each selected piece this is a comparison of the entire cokernel and normalization map, not only of their reduced fibres. Internal sizes at most three and cross pieces involving a simple root vanish by the support-preserving adjoint lemma and Nakayama. Internal size four and a cross pair of doubles have no normalization kernel, by the exact quartic comparison.

A selected triple-double piece has only the top and middle layers: the latter is a smooth extension of the known length-one transverse kernel, and has dimension \(N-4\). The completed top normalization branches are domains of dimension \(N-3\). Each nonzero coefficient submodule of these layers has the same dimension as its branch: their finite parameter-ring maps have prime kernels, and a nonzero ideal in the branch domain has full dimension. Thus an extension of these layers contains no submodule of dimension at most \(N-5\). This verifies the needed dimension-filtration comparison even with repeated spectators; it does not assume arbitrary base change commutes with dimension filtrations.

First upper inclusion. Outside the three stated loci every cluster has size at most four, no cluster of size four coexists with another repeated cluster, and at most one cluster has size three. The surviving pair types are therefore internal four, cross double-double, and cross triple-double. Their preceding descriptions leave no residual dimension layer. This includes \((3,2,2,\ldots,2)\) and arbitrarily many double clusters. Hence \(K_2\) vanishes there. Completion and geometric field extension are faithfully flat, so this proves the first upper inclusion over \(k\).

Injection outside the two kernel loci. Outside \(\Delta_5\cup\Delta_{33}\), every cluster has size at most four and at most one has size at least three. If that cluster has size at most three, the preceding argument kills \(K_2\). Otherwise, the only pieces with a residual are its cross pairs with double clusters. Each is a smooth extension of the complete quadruple-double module, of transverse length three. The internal quartic and double-double pieces add no residual.

The finite detector algebra above this point has one completed factor for each choice of that quartic and a double cluster: these exhaust its reduced marked factorizations. For any such choice, the selected quartic, quadratic and remaining factor are pairwise coprime at the central point. Formal factor multiplication is therefore invertible, regardless of repetitions inside the remaining factor. Its local jet algebra is exactly the quotient by the fourth power of the four selected transverse parameters, with all other factor coefficients retained as smooth variables. The exterior projection defining \(\Phi_{42}\) selects the corresponding cross piece and kills the other exterior blocks. The support-preserving EPD comparison identifies this with the same cross-cokernel quotient. The complete transverse theorem proves that its intersection with the residual is zero. Extending by smooth variables preserves that injection; the ideal is the extended transverse ideal, not the full coefficient maximal ideal.

Taking all choices yields a diagonal collection of injective maps on all nonzero residual pieces. Thus \(\Phi_{42}\) is injective throughout this complement, proving the second upper inclusion. This strengthens generic injectivity: it covers arbitrarily many additional double clusters without treating them as simple spectators.

The proved nonzero components give the first lower inclusion, with generic transverse lengths sixteen on \(\Delta_5\) and three on \(\Delta_{42}\). The detector target is supported on \(\Delta_{42}\), which omits the generic quintuple-plus-simple point. Hence the generic quintuple residual lies in \(H_N\), and closedness gives \(\Delta_5\subseteq\operatorname{Supp}H_N\). At \(N=5\) the full residual is the already-known length-sixteen vertex. \(\square\)

The same parameters control the full residual

Theorem. For every characteristic-zero \(N\ge5\), put \[ A_N=k[c_2,\ldots,c_{N-4}], \] with \(A_5=k\). The actual \(K_{2,N}\) is a finite graded \(A_N\)-module. For \(N\ge6\), the actual kernel \(H_N\) and image \(I_N\) are finite graded \(A_N\)-modules as well, in an exact sequence \(0\to H_N\to K_{2,N}\to I_N\to0\).

Let \(\lambda\) be the generic transverse length of \(K_{2,6}\) on \(\Delta_{33}\), taking \(\lambda=0\) if that locus is not a support component. This is a finite nonnegative integer, independent of \(N\) after adding simple spectators. Set \(\rho=(N-4)(N-5)\). For every \(N\ge6\), \[ \operatorname{rank}_{A_N}K_{2,N}=16(N-4)+3\rho+\tfrac12\lambda\rho, \qquad \operatorname{rank}_{A_N}H_N=16(N-4)+\tfrac12\lambda\rho. \tag{KR} \] In particular the six-root kernel has rank \(32+\lambda\), while its already-presented image has rank six. No freeness, bound on parameter-basis weights, nilpotence exponent or syzygy degrees is asserted for these modules.

Finiteness of the reduced loci. The two-cluster coefficient-basis lemma, applied to \((4,2)\) and \((3,3)\), gives finite free ordered parameter algebras over this exact \(A_N\), of rank \(\rho\). Their reduced image coordinate rings are \(A_N\)-submodules of those finite modules and hence finite, since \(A_N\) is Noetherian. Ordering matters: the \((4,2)\) parameterization is generically one-to-one, while the \((3,3)\) parameterization has generic degree two from interchanging the distinct triple roots. Thus the function-field degrees of the reduced loci over \(\operatorname{Frac}A_N\) are \(\rho\) and \(\rho/2\), respectively. No ordered cover is identified with the unordered normalization.

For \(\Delta_5\), write \(p=(Z-b)^5H\), with \(r=N-5\) and monic \(H\) of degree \(r\). If \(r\ge1\), its trace-zero parameter ring is \(B_5=k[b,h_2,\ldots,h_r]\), with the next coefficient of \(H\) equal to \(5b\). Working characteristic-zero obstruction for every \(N\ge6\): a small Hilbert budget forces vertex torsion, and formal spectator transfer preserves it. The residual degree bound remains open. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, high reasoning).

Question and outcome. Open statement 3 needs original graded residual relations and their intrinsic syzygy flag. The tested sufficient mechanism was that \(K_{2,N}\) might be free over \(A_N=k[c_2,\ldots,c_{N-4}]\). Such freeness would replace unknown parameter relations by the four remaining coefficient actions. It fails: one six-root Hilbert count forces a deeper layer, and the exact spectator comparison transfers the obstruction to every \(N\ge6\). This is a proof for all larger dimensions, not a sweep through them.

General statement. thm:cube-residual-sixfold-torsion proves non-Cohen–Macaulayness at every exact sixfold-plus-simple geometric point, hence nonfreeness over the proposed original coefficient parameters, for all characteristic-zero \(N\ge6\). The known non-Cohen–Macaulayness of the full defect did not establish this assertion about its residual. Likewise, torsion in the earlier detector image did not imply torsion in its source.

The full residual has a nonzero sixfold embedded layer

Theorem. Work over a characteristic-zero field \(k\), with the established centered degree-two defect \(C_N\) over \(S_N=k[c_2,\ldots,c_N]\), \(\deg c_j=j\), and its actual residual dimension layer \(M_N=K_{2,N}\). At \(N=6\), put \(t=c_2\), \(\mathfrak m=(c_2,\ldots,c_6)\). Then \[ \dim_k M_6/tM_6\ge60>54=\operatorname{rank}_{k[t]}M_6. \tag{HF} \] Its \(k[t]\)-torsion submodule \[ T_6=H^0_{\mathfrak m}(M_6) \] is nonzero, finite-dimensional, and satisfies \(\dim_k T_6/tT_6\ge6\), hence \(\dim_kT_6\ge6\). These are lower bounds, not an exact length or an exact graded presentation.

For every \(N\ge6\), at every exact geometric root pattern \((6,1,\ldots,1)\), the complete residual has a nonzero submodule obtained by extending \(T_6\) by \(N-6\) smooth variables. Its dimension is \(N-6\), while the complete residual has dimension \(N-5\). In fact its depth is \(N-6\), so it is not Cohen–Macaulay there. Consequently \(M_N\) is not a graded free \(A_N\)-module for any \(N\ge6\). No original global weight or connection is transferred by the formal comparison.

Exactness of the parameter fibre. Let \(E_6=C_6/M_6\). The two normalization sequences, whose verification gate was subsequently closed, give \[ 0\longrightarrow D_{32}(-9)\longrightarrow E_6 \longrightarrow D_{22}(-4)\longrightarrow0. \] Here \(D_{22}=k[s,v,r_2]\) with weights \(1,2,2\), parameterizing \[ p=(Z^2-sZ+v)^2(Z^2+2sZ+r_2),\qquad c_2=2v+r_2-3s^2. \] Also \(D_{32}=k[b,c]\), both weights one, parameterizing \[ p=(Z-b)^3(Z-c)^2(Z+3b+2c),\qquad c_2=-6b^2-6bc-3c^2. \] Thus \(t\) is a nonzero element in each polynomial domain and multiplication by \(t\) is injective on each layer and on their extension \(E_6\). Tensoring \(0\to M_6\to C_6\to E_6\to0\) with \(k[t]/(t)\) stays left exact, because the length-one resolution of \(k[t]/(t)\) identifies its first Tor with the kernel of multiplication by \(t\) on \(E_6\). In particular \[ H_{\overline M_6}(z)=H_{\overline C_6}(z) -\frac{z^4}{(1-z)(1-z^2)}-\frac{z^9(1+z)}{1-z}, \qquad \overline{(\cdot)}=(\cdot)/t(\cdot). \tag{EF} \] The displayed upper-layer series also follow from the normalization formulas. Exact fibre injection, rather than a rank subtraction after an arbitrary specialization, is essential.

A relation-count lower bound is enough. The exact marked deflation gives \(C_6=F/\Gamma\), where \(F\) has six basis weights \(4,5,6,6,7,8\) and \(\Gamma=S_6\{D^iv:i\ge0\}\), \(\deg D^iv=11+i\). After setting \(t=0\), write \[ R=k[c_3,c_4,c_5,c_6],\qquad p_d=[z^d]\frac1{(1-z^3)(1-z^4)(1-z^5)(1-z^6)}, \quad p_d=0\ (d<0). \] In weight \(d\), the free target has \(f_d=p_{d-4}+p_{d-5}+2p_{d-6}+p_{d-7}+p_{d-8}\) rows; all cyclic relation columns number at most \(g_d=\sum_{a=0}^{d-11}p_a\), with an empty sum zero. No independence of those columns is presumed. Right exactness of specialization gives \(\dim\overline C_{6,d}\ge f_d-g_d\). We specialize the universal columns; we do not iterate a specialized derivation, since the ideal \((c_2)\) is not connection-stable.

Let \(e_d\) be the coefficient of the two upper series in (EF). For \(d\ge11\), \(e_d=\lfloor(d-4)/2\rfloor+3\). Therefore \(\dim\overline M_{6,d}\ge\max(0,f_d-g_d-e_d)\). The complete useful part of the integer calculation is:
